Chicago Chess Center

weekly on Friday, starting from Friday, January 16, 2026, forever

Event Overview

Rated Blitz at the Chicago Chess Center!
Some days will be skipped in order to not conflict with bigger tournaments in the area. Please check kingregistration.com/affiliate/chichess to confirm registration.
Equipment:  Chess sets and clocks are provided by the CCC.
Location:   166 W Washington St, Chicago, IL 60602, Unit # 600
Section & Format: Open; 5 double-rounds (10 games) SS G/3, inc/2.
Schedule:  Round 1 at 6:30 PM
Registration : Free; Online or onsite 6:00 PM to 6:15 PM.
Registration closes 15 minutes before the first round. Any players not registered before then will receive a round 1 bye.
All children who score higher than 50% will receive a medal!
Transportation:  Conveniently located within 10 minutes of multiple L stations (Washington and Wells, Clark and Lake, Washington, and Lake), Ogilvie, Union Station, and the Kennedy.
Parking:  There is street parking, lots, and garages nearby.

Fayetteville Chess Society Classical

The Green Dragon

weekly on Sunday, starting from Sunday, January 25, 2026, forever

Event Overview

Fayetteville Chess Society (FCS) Sunday Classical
USCF-Rated Classical Event Series
Website Link

Fayetteville Chess Society hosts a recurring USCF-rated Sunday Classical event series in Fayetteville, North Carolina. These events are designed to provide consistent, over-the-board classical rated play in a structured tournament environment for players of all strengths. The series emphasizes regular rated competition, rating development, and a professional yet welcoming club atmosphere. Events are held 2–3 times per month on Sundays. Specific dates — check calendar for current and upcoming events.

Event Details (Quick Reference)

What:
• USCF-rated classical chess

Who:
• Open to all USCF members
• All ratings welcome

When:
• Sundays
• 2–3 times per month
• Sundays exact dates vary — check calendar
• Start time: 10:00 AM
• Registration by: 09:45 AM

Where:
• Fayetteville, North Carolina
• The Green Dragon 6111B Yakin Rd

Format / Time Control:
• 2–3 rounds
• G/45 with 10-second delay
• Sections and pairings based on entries

Notes:
• USCF membership required
• Casual play and blitz available after
• All registration details and updates — check calendar

MCC Monthly Club Night Tournaments: Blitz RR or Quick Swiss

First Cumberland Presbyterian Church

monthly on Thursday, but only the last instance of this set, starting from Thursday, January 29, 2026, forever

Event Overview

- Schedule: Last Thursday of each month, rescheduled for holidays.

- Event Alternates: Blitz RR on odd numbered months (January, March, etc.), Quick Swiss on even numbered months (February, April, etc.).

- Required: Must be a current US Chess Member.

- Registration: 6:00 PM to 7:15 PM

- Rounds: Round 1 @ 7:30 PM, subsequent rounds a.s.a.p.

- Entry Fee: $10.00 Cash or $12.00 PayPal https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/mborochessclub

- Prize Fund: 70% returned (remaining for expenses and church donation).

- Sections & Pairings: TD has complete control over both.

- Noise Disclaimer: Beware, some casual chess and talking are to be expected on club nights.

Blitz:
Time Control: 3+2
Format: Round Robin Section(s)
Quick:
Time Control: 15+3
Format: 3-Round Swiss Section(s)

Dragon Knight Chess Saturday Scholastic Pizza Quads (Holly Springs)

New School Montessori Center

weekly on Saturday, starting from Saturday, January 31, 2026, forever

Event Overview

Each Saturday at 1:30pm
A 3-6 round "quad" US Chess rated tournament open to all scholastic (K-12) players. Quads group players by their skill level. This is a chance to play 3-6 quick rated games each Saturday afternoon, with free pizza included!
New School Montessori Center
5617 Sunset Lake Road
Holly Springs, NC 27540
(919) 422-2535
3-6 round (Single or Double) Quad Round Robin sections
First place trophy in each 4 player section. Team trophy to top school overall. Other prizes will also be awarded.
Registration and Entry Fee:
$19 online mid-day before the event (Noon Friday), or
$29 onsite registration 12:30-1pm day of tournament.
Players currently rated 1200+: Free Entry
Free Entry Policy:
Free entry is offered to scholastic (K-12) players who have a current "live Over The Board (OTB)" US Chess rating of 1200+. No exceptions.
To get free entry, players must register online mid-day before the event (Noon Friday).
If you register for free but must cancel, email [email protected]
or text (919) 422-2535 by 12:30pm (one hour before Round 1 of the quad).
Players receiving free entry are not permitted to withdraw mid-quad, without permission from all other players in their quad. Free entry players who withdraw mid-quad (without permission) will not be eligible for free entry in future Dragon Knight Chess quads.
US Chess membership required; Dragon Knight Chess will use vouchers to create new scholastic memberships. US Chess is the governing body of chess in the United States. US Chess conducts all rating calculations for players.
Time Control:
G/24; delay 4 (3-6 games):  Each player receives 24 minutes (plus a 4 second delay each move) to complete each game.
Onsite registration 12:30-1pm day of tournament.
Round Times:
1st Round 1:30pm;
Round 2: ASAP;
Round 3: ASAP
End Time: Between 3-4pm, depending on quad.
How it Works:
Players must register weekly.
Quads: Players are placed into groups of 4 by their most recent "live" US Chess rating. (Minor section shifts are possible, to avoid family member pairings.)
3-6 rated games each Saturday afternoon
Each Saturday afternoon is limited to the first 50 players to register.
Entries are first registered, first served.
Quads are for K-12 students only.
IMPROVE - Game analysis and blitz with Dragon Knight Chess coaches
SIDE EVENTS - Free USCF rated blitz tournaments can start as early as 1:30pm.
For questions, concerns, and withdrawals prior to the event email:  [email protected]
For contact during the event email (above) or text (or call) ( 919) 422-2535
Trophies awarded
Handicap Accessible

NO Residency Restriction: Open to all scholastic players!
Live OTB event

Western Illinois University QC Campus

monthly on Tuesday, but only the first and the third instance of this set, starting from Tuesday, February 3, 2026, forever

Event Overview

Western Illinois Chess Club USCF Rated, 4-Round Rapid Play Tuesday Chess Tournament
Open to all ages. USCF membership required.
♟️♟️♟️
When: The 1st Tuesday and the 3rd Tuesday of every month, 5:30pm - 8:30pm
Type: 4 Round Swiss USCF Quick Rapid Rated G/15; d2
Where: Western Illinois University - Quad Cities Campus, Riverfront Building, rooms 103/104, 3300 River Drive Moline, Illinois, 61265
Registration: 5:30pm - 5:55pm
♟️♟️♟️
Rounds:
1st round: 06:00pm
2nd round: 06:35pm
3rd round: 07:10pm
4th round: 07:45pm
♟️♟️♟️
Entry Fee: $4 cash in person
♟️♟️♟️
Sections: Open Section & Under 1200 Section
Open Section Prize: $25 Gift Card
Youth Section Prize: $10 Gift Card
♟️♟️♟️
Additional info:
-US Chess Federation (USCF) membership required. On Site Registration Available. We have some vouchers for free USCF membership for those 17 and under. $3 off for adults.
-Parents/Guardians of young chess players are responsible for their children. Parents/Guardians must be present at all times of the tournament and may enjoy some light snacks or drinks in waiting area while games are in progress.
-Boards and clocks will be provided.
-By registering for this event, you also agree to have your photo taken to be used on our facebook page for promo purposes. Sometimes the local news stations show up as well.
♟️♟️♟️
For questions: Contact Luis Peralta or Mariela Treviño at [email protected] or (309) 737-2890
♟️♟️♟️
Tournament Director: Mariela Trevino
♟️♟️♟️
♟️♟️♟️
Key Rules, Procedures, Cheating & Etiquette:
Contacting the TD: Stop the clock and immediately call the Tournament Director for any rule violation, illegal move, or dispute.
Touch-Move Rule: If you touch one of your pieces, you must move it if it has a legal move. If you touch an opponent's piece, you must capture it if possible.
One-Hand Rule: Use only one hand to move a piece and press the clock.
Clock use: Make your move then press the clock to stop your time until it is your turn again. You will have 15 minutes plus a 2 second delay in each turn. Running out of time before checkmate means you lose the game automatically.
Illegal Moves: If you make one, your opponent stops the clock, shows the TD the illegal move, and you get a time penalty (2 minutes extra time will be added to your opponent).
Castling: Touch the King first, then the Rook, using one hand.
"J'adoube" (I adjust): Say this before touching a piece to adjust it, not to move it.
Pawn Promotion: The pawn is considered "touched" when it reaches the promotion square and must be promoted immediately to the piece you place on that square.
No Outside Help: No computers, phones (strict penalties), books, or talking to others about the game during play.
Communication: Only talk to your opponent or the TD. Be courteous. Be curteous of the players and their ongoing games around you. Whisper if talking must happen.
Cell Phones: Keep them off and away; penalties are severe.
Disputes: Handle calmly; argue with the TD, not your opponent.
Where to Find More rules: The full rules are in the US Chess Federation's website under Official Rules of Chess section.

weekly on Friday, starting from Friday, February 6, 2026, 8 times

Event Overview

Albany Chess Center Online Blitz is a weekly 9-round Swiss tournament held on the Albany Chess Center Team on lichess.org.

Rounds are played every Friday from 6:00 pm to 8:00 pm Eastern Time. The time control is 3 minutes with a 2-second increment (3+2) for each game.

Pairings and results are handled automatically by lichess, and players should join the Albany Chess Center team page in advance to participate.

There is a 25 dollar gift card awarded each month to the best overall performer across that month’s Friday events; tie-breaks, eligibility, and fair-play decisions are at the discretion of the tournament director.

Sixty Four Squares Online Quick Round Robin

weekly on Sunday, starting from Sunday, February 15, 2026, 12 times

Event Overview

Sundays @12pm Central Time
Sign up here
We will be using a discord server for all of our communications.  CLICK HERE TO JOIN   https://discord.gg/hDa8PyeVmX
This tournament will use Swiss pairings.
The time control will be  game in 10 minutes with a 5-second increment . There will be four rounds. Each round will begin 30 seconds after all the games from the previous round have finished. The tournament will last for approximately 2 hours.
This event will be  rated under the USCF online quick rating system . The tournament will be run on chess.com
This tournament is open to both children and adults of any age or rating.
Before signing up for the tournament, please register for a chess.com account
There will be one section for this tournament which is open to all players.
All participants must be active members of the US Chess Federation.
Players can withdraw from the event at any time by pressing the "withdraw" button.
Tiebreaks are calculated based on the Sonneborn–Berger method, after which we use chess.com performance ratings as a secondary tiebreak.
There will be a group town hall Q&A session at 11:40am in the discord server to ask any questions you have and fix any issues that have occurred before the game starts.
Players will not be required to be in the voice chat or stream your screen while the games are going on, but we will monitor the games very closely to ensure fair play. Chess.com has an excellent algorithm for detecting cheating, and we will also do a post-tournament fair-play inspection. If a participant's account is flagged for cheating by chess.com, we have the prerogative to submit the player's games as losses for USCF-rating purposes, or (in rare cases) annul the games.
The entry fee is $15 by 11:59 am CT on Sunday
For questions please email [email protected]

BayAreaChess REAL-FIDE 2026 February Championship

Courtyard by Marriott Fremont Silicon Valley

Friday, February 20, 2026
- Sunday, February 22, 2026

Event Overview

Take your game to the next level with BayAreaChess REAL-FIDE tournaments — tailored for players seeking FIDE ratings and serious competition! Whether you're chasing norms or climbing the international ladder, the BayAreaChess REAL-FIDE offers a professional chess environment, perfect for ambitious scholastic and adult players alike.
Register here

- You must  log in or sign up before you can register.

- Online registration closes at  12:00 a.m. the day of the tournament.

- Onsite registration is subject to availability (additional fee incurred).

- Late fee ($30) applied on February 19 or when reaching capacity.

Schedule

- 2 schedules available ( More info )
- 3-day option:
- Rounds: 6

- Time Control: 6x G/90 +30

- Round Times:
‣ Fri, Feb. 20 - 6:30 p.m.
‣ Sat, Feb. 21 - 9:30 a.m., 1:50 p.m., 6:10 p.m.
‣ Sun, Feb. 22 - 9:30 a.m., 2:00 p.m.

- 2-day option:
- Rounds: 6

- Time Controls: 2x G/55 d5, 4x G/90 +30

- Round Times:
‣ Sat, Feb. 21 - 9:00 a.m., 11:20 a.m., 1:50 p.m., 6:10 p.m.
‣ Sun, Feb. 22 - 9:30 a.m., 2:00 p.m.

- ½-point byes are available for any round (Max byes: 3; byes must be requested  at least 30 min before that round's start except last round byes; last round bye must be requested latest before Round 3)

- 0-point byes are available for any round (player must play  at least half the rounds to be eligible for prizes)

Sections

- Players will be placed into one of the three sections based on February 2026 Published Supplement rating:
- Open (1800+) FIDE-rated

- AB (1400-1799) FIDE-rated

- CDEu (unr. & u1400)

- A player may pay to play up one higher section, double play up is  NOT allowed.

- Players must be within 300 points of the rating cutoff to play up, and within 200 points in highest section.
(Note: The rating used to determine if a player may play up is their  February 2026 Published Supplement rating.)

Prizes

- Prize Fund: $4,000 Guaranteed! ( More info )

- Regular entry winners get full prize, Econ entry winners get 50% prize.

- Unrated winners: Max $200 (except in the top section)

- A player who withdraws during the tournament is  not eligible for prize money.

- Prizes will be paid out by check (mail), PayPal or Zelle.

Fees

- Regular entry: $148

- Econ entry: $111

- Play up fee: +$28

- Discount for BayAreaChess Membership Subscribers ( More info )

- Onsite fee: +$33 (membership discounts are  not  redeemable onsite)

Withdrawals

- Withdrawals are eligible for a partial refund, subject to a 4% processing fee.

- Only withdrawals made  before the tournament day are eligible for refund.

Change requests

- After registration, changes can be requested at  bayareachess.com/changeform and are subject to the following fees:
- until Feb. 18, $7 change fee.

- on Feb. 19, $15 change fee.

- The following requests are exempt from the change fee:
- playing up to a higher section.

- requesting byes.

Other requirements

- USCF membership must be active.

More information available  here .

Fremont , CA 94538

2026 U.S. Amateur Team-North

National Championship Event

Hyatt Regency Schaumburg

Friday, February 20, 2026
- Sunday, February 22, 2026

Event Overview

2026 U.S. Amateur Team North
February 20 - 22, 2026
Chess Weekend and US Chess present
2026 U.S. Amateur Team North
PRIZES • FUN • FRIENDS • US CHESS RATED NATIONAL EVENT
February 20 - 22, 2026 • Schaumburg, Illinois
Early entry ends February 7
Hyatt Regency Schaumburg
1800 E. Golf Rd., Schaumburg, Illinois 60173
$119 single-quad , free wifi included with room
Please reserve early  at this link  or call 847-605-1234 and use code GCHE5
OPEN and RESERVE SECTIONS (see box below for one-day U1000 Section)
5 round Swiss, open to 4 player teams with one optional alternate.
Choice of 2-day or 3-day schedules.
Team average  (4 highest ratings – January 2026 Rating List) must be

- under 2200 for Open (Maximum rating difference between board 3 and board 4 is 1000; rating of board 4 will be adjusted accordingly)

- under 1600 for Reserve

An entire team may take up to two byes in any rounds; byes must be requested by end of round 2 and are irrevocable after the end of round 2.
Time Controls
Game/90 +30 sec increment from move 1. Rounds 1 and 2 in the 2-day schedule play Game/60, d5.
Entry Fees

- $200 per team if received USPS or online by 6pm on Feb. 7

- $220 per team if received USPS or online by 6pm on Feb. 14

- $240 per team online until 9:30am Feb. 20 and onsite.

Team changes onsite or after 6pm on Feb. 20, $20.
Individuals
…wishing to play, send $60 by USPS or online by 6pm on Feb. 14 or $70 thereafter, and request to be put on a team. Note: we guarantee you will play, but can’t guarantee which schedule, which section, which board you will play, or the ratings of your teammates. Teams are formed the day of the event.
Schedule

- 3-DAY:  onsite registration/check-in  Friday,  5:30pm-6:30pm; Round 1, 7pm.  Saturday , Round 2 10am; Round 3, 4pm.  Sunday , Round 4, 10am; Round 5, 3:30pm.

- 2-DAY:  onsite registration/check-in  Saturday , 8am-9:30am; Round 1, 10am; Round 2, 1pm then merge with 3-day schedule for Round 3.

Prizes
Winning Open Section team qualifies for national playoffs.
Open Section Prizes

- Top three teams

- Top teams with average rating Under 2000, Under 1800

- Top college team (all players in college)

- Top high school team (all players in high school)

- Top team composed of juniors (high school and younger)

- Top mixed doubles team (two women and two men)

- Top senior team (all players 50 and over)

- Top individual score on each board

Reserve Section Prizes

- Top three teams

- Top teams Under 1400 and Under 1200

- Top K-8 team

- Top high school team

- Top female team

- Top individual score each board

Special Prizes

- Best team name

- Best costume or theme (This will be held on Saturday.)

Prizes are clocks or bookstore credit. Books and equipment by Rochester Chess.
_____________
One-Day Booster Section
Saturday, February 21 , one day only
Time control:  4/SS G/60, d5
Four-player teams  with one optional alternate
Team average  (4 highest ratings – January 2025 Rating List) must be U1000
Round Times:  10:00am, 1:00pm, 3:30pm, 6:00pm
A team may take a bye in any round, byes must be requested by end of round 2 and cannot be changed after the end of round 2.
Entry Fee:

- $120 per team if received USPS or online by 6pm on Feb. 7

- $140 per team if received USPS or online by 6pm on Feb. 14

- $160 per team online until 9:30am Feb. 21 and onsite.

Prizes
Top three teams
Top individual each board
Prizes are clocks or bookstore credit.
______
Register online here for all sections:
… or by mail:  Make checks payable to and send to: Chess Weekend, 21694 Doud Ct., Frankfort, IL 60423. Please include Team’s name and roster (plus ID#), captain’s email and phone number, and desired schedule.
A town hall for USAT-N Team captains will be held on Zoom the evening of Wednesday 2/18, and team captains will receive an email invitation.
Information
Email: [email protected]
Other team tournament rules are here
Boards and sets provided. PLEASE BRING CLOCKS!

_______
Northern Blitz Championship
$1000 Guaranteed!  5-round double Swiss (two games with each opponent) Game/3, 2-second increment. US Chess rated. Will be held Saturday night at 8 p.m. or after USAT Round 3 (which begins at 4pm).  More information and registration here .

All special rules, details, and tournament conditions are subject to change without notice; changes will be posted ASAP at the tournament site, at chessweekend.com, at il-chess.org, and at kingregistration.com.

2026 Charlotte February Open

Grand Prix

Hilton Garden Inn - Southpark

Friday, February 20, 2026
- Sunday, February 22, 2026

Event Overview

https://www.charlottechesscenter.org/events/febopen

OVERVIEW
The Charlotte February Open is a classical event with a $6,000 guaranteed total prize fund - $5,500 in the main event plus a free $500 Saturday evening blitz tournament.

All sections are US Chess and FIDE rated. There is a minimum rating of 1200 and registration cap of 140 players.

WHEN
February 20-22, 2026
3-day and 2-day schedules available
​

WHERE
Beautiful Venue in the Heart of Southpark! Walk to Starbucks, Whole Foods and more!

Hilton Garden Inn - Southpark
4808 Sharon Road
Charlotte, NC 28210
(704) 362-5080

Free internet, free parking
​

​ HOTEL BOOKING
Both hotel options attached to the playing venue.

Hilton Garden Inn - Southpark
$134/night for King or $149 for 2 Queens
Booking Link - Reserve ASAP

Homewood Suites - Southpark
$152/night for King suite with sofa bed
Booking Link - Reserve ASAP

ELIGIBILITY

- There is a strict minimum rating of 1200 to enter, based on February US Chess ratings or a peak rating achieved between January 1 - February 20.

- See events schedule for other options this weekend.

- Registration Cap:  140 players. The organizer may continue to accept registration past 140 players based on specific space constraints.

REGISTRATION

- Online registration only - no on-site registration.

- All registration closes 90 minutes before round 1 start time.

- On-site check-in is not necessary .

TIME CONTROLS
3-Day Schedule: G/110; inc/10
Rounds 1-2 of 2-day: G/30, inc/10

PRIZES & SECTIONS
$5,500 Guaranteed Prize Fund in 3 Sections .

Championship Section  - FIDE Rated
$1000 – $700 – $400
Top U2200: $400
40 US Chess Grand Prix Points
​
Under 2000 Section  - FIDE Rated
$700 – $400 – $200
Top U1800: $300

Under 1600 Section  - FIDE Rated
$600 – $300 – $200
Top U1400: $300

Minimum rating of 1200.

100-point Rule  applies for "playing up" - see Special Notes below.

Plaques to first place in all sections.

SCHEDULE
3-Day Schedule - 5 Rounds
Friday: 6:30pm
Saturday: 10:30am & 4:00pm
Sunday: 10:00am & 3:00pm
​
2-Day Schedule - 5 Rounds
Saturday: 10:30am*, 1:00pm*, 4:00pm
Sunday: 10:00am & 3:00pm
​
* Rounds 1-2 of 2-Day Schedule played at G/30; inc/10 time control, then merge with 3-day schedule, Saturday 4:00pm

FREE FEBRUARY OPEN BLITZ

- Saturday 8:45pm

- Blitz Registration On-site only, Saturday 4:00-8:30pm

- No online or emailed blitz registration

- Free blitz entry for players in the February Open

- Open to all players - $30 on-site blitz entry for those not in the February Open

- 6 (single) Rounds – US Chess regular ratings used for pairings/prizes.

- US Chess and FIDE blitz rated. US Chess membership required.

- $500 guaranteed prize fund in one section:
- $200 - $100 - $60. Top U2000: $80, Top U1700: $60.

ENTRY FEE
$135 by February 9
$150 after February 9

GM/IM/WGMs : Free online entry, no deduction from prize if registered by January 20, otherwise $135 deducted from prize.

Re-entry: $60. See information under "Special Notes" below.

CONTACT

Caveman February 3x3 Open Sans Prix 14+

Signature Regus

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Caveman February 3x3 Open Sans Prix
Saturday, February 21st, 2026.
Signature 222 South Prospect, Floor R, Park Ridge, IL 60068
3 Sections: Open (1800 and up), Reserve U1800 (1799 - 1400), and Booster U1400 (below 1400). Play-up fee: $20.
Rounds/Style: 3-round Swiss System
No tournament check-in at the site is needed. Just verify your registration online before the tournament. If there are issues that require making changes to your registration, please visit cavechess.cc/change .
Time Control:  G/60
Schedule:  9:00 AM, 12:00 PM, 3:00 PM.
Entry Fee:

- $15 online until the week before the event.

- $20 online until day of event.

- $10 off for Caveman Chess members.

- Online entries only, no entries onsite.

Byes: One ½-point bye available for any round, committed by the end of round 1. No byes may be added or rescinded after round 1.
ENT: Register online at   Caveman Chess Registration
Mem Req'd:  US Chess membership is required,  please obtain before the event. Discounted scholastic (ages 5-18) memberships are available at  cavechess.cc/voucher . Free US Chess membership to Park Ridge students (ages 5-18).
Chess Equipment: Boards, sets, and clocks provided by Caveman Chess, LLC.
Parking:  Free parking. Visitors' parking behind the building and the SW corner lot @ Garden & S. Fairview Streets, also street parking.
Questions:  Click here to show mail address .
Ratings: January supplement. All sections are US Chess-rated.
Watch for additional information on upcoming events at
1.  https://www.cavemanchess.com/new-events
2.  Caveman Chess Registration  at  https://register.cavemanchess.com

2nd Annual B-Town Blizzard Scholastic & Open!

Faith Lutheran Church

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

2nd Annual B-Town Blizzard Scholastic & Open!
$1,000 projected prize fund! Part of weekend festivities w/special guest! Free pizza & cocoa!

- Saturday, February 21, 2026

- Faith Lutheran Church, 2200 S High St, Bloomington, IN

Onlineregistration.cc registration:
https://onlineregistration.cc

- Sections and prizes:
- Scholastic sections:
- 3rd Grade/Under Scholastic - trophy prizes

- 8th Grade/Under Scholastic - trophy prizes

- 12th Grade/Under Scholastic - gift card prizes

- Open sections:
- Master/Expert Open (2000+) - $350 prizes

- Upper Open (1500-1999) - $300 prizes

- Lower Open (1000-1499) - $200 prizes

- Novice Open (<999) - $150 prizes

- Note: We may combine sections due to turnout if necessary

- Scholastic round times, arrival times, and time control:
- Round times: 9:30AM, (lunch break), 12:00PM, last two rounds will start as soon as the last game finishes

- Arrival time: Arrive between 8:00-9:15AM (inc. on-site registration)

- Time control: G45;d5 (each side has 45 minutes to make moves with a five-second delay before the clock ticks down each move)

- Open round times, arrival times, and time control:
- Round times: 9:00AM, (lunch break), 12:30PM, 3:30PM, 6:30PM

- Arrival time: Arrive between 8:00-8:45AM (inc. on-site registration)

- Time control: G60+5 (each side has 60 minutes to make moves with a five-second increment after each move)

- NOTE: Open sections begin 30 minutes BEFORE the scholastic sections! Plan accordingly!

- Equipment: Open section players, please bring boards, pieces, and clocks!

- Byes: Up to 2 half-point byes can be requested. Let us know ASAP. We do not want to forfeit you!

- Entry fee for all sections: $5 until December 31, $20 till January 31, $40 after/on-site. Free entry upon proof of public assistance. Full refunds available between January 1 and February 18.

- Perks:
- Cozy concessions and free pizza available!

- Scholastic players earn 400 HCA points and join/climb up our participation leaderboard! Visit our website to learn more

- This tournament is just one of many exciting chess activities all weekend, Saturday and Sunday! Stick around to meet a special guest…

- Awards:
- Scholastic players will receive trophies at each section’s awards ceremony once all fourth-round games finish. Let us know if you need to skip the ceremony, and we can ship trophies to your address.

- Open section players who need to leave before cash prizes are handed out will receive their payouts electronically via PayPal, Venmo, or check.

- Contact: Click here to show mail address , 812-318-2875

- Full tournament policies and procedures: Visit our website to read

- Follow us on Facebook! @Hoosier Chess Academy

- Check out our website: hcachess.org

Tri-Valley Feb Open (youth and adults, cash prizes and trophies)

John Green Elementary MPR

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Emerald Hills Chess , the  Tri-Valley Chess League , and the  Emerald Knights Chess Club  present the Tri-Valley Feb Open, for players of all levels and ages, including youth and adults!
Our  low-cost half-day tournaments  consistently  attract 150 or more players (such as  January’s 169-player tourney ), from nationally-age-ranked competitors, to adult improvers and returning tournament players, to after-school chess club members trying out their first tournament!
Flex your chess skills, boost your rating, win one of 50+ trophies and ~$700 in cash prizes, and have fun!
Register and more info here
When: Sat Feb 21 2026, 9-1:30 PM (on-site registrants allowed before 9 AM but not guaranteed 1st round pairing); trophy ceremony start ~1:30 PM
Where: John Green Elementary School,  3300 Antone Way, Dublin
Rounds and Time Control
Championship: 3-round USCF-rated quads with Game in 40 min/5 sec delay
Experts, Premier and Challenger: 4-round rated Swisses with Game in 25 min/5 sec delay
Novices: non-rated 5-round Swiss with 15 minutes and 3 seconds delay per move per player
Sections (based on Feb 2026 published rating -  check here )
Championship Quads for USCF/FIDE 1200+ players
Free entry for 1) All USCF and FIDE titled players (including GMs, WGMs, IMs, WIMs, FMs, WFMs, and NMs) 2) Chess teachers and parent organizers/coaches (any section) bringing students
Prizes: $80 first prize and trophy per quad (split in case of ties); $100 for quads with 1400-1499 average rating; $120 for 1500-1599 avg. rating, etc. Add (subtract) $20 for groups larger (smaller) than 4 (i.e. $100 for 5 players, $120 for 6 players)
Register here
Experts for 800-1199/unrated players of all ages including adults
Guaranteed Prizes: $100 1st place, $50 2nd place. Trophies to Top 6, Top 3 U1000/unrated, and any other Outstanding Performers scoring 3 or more.
Premier for U800/unrated players of all ages including adults
Prizes: Trophies to Top 6, Top 3 U600/unrated, and any other Outstanding Performers scoring 3 or more.
Register here
Youth Challenger for K-12 players under 400 rating or unrated
Prizes: Trophies to Top 6, Top 3 U200/unrated, and any other Outstanding Performers scoring 3 or more.
Register here
Non-Rated Youth Novices for K-12 players that 1) are unrated, or 2) have provisional (under 25 games) USCF rating under 300; 3) have not won a trophy in a prior Novices tournament.
No USCF membership required.
Prizes: Trophies for Top 5, Top 2 K-2, plus all other Outstanding Performers scoring 3.5 or more.
***
Emerald Hills Chess provides professionally-led after-school chess clubs and tournament training classes serving 300+ kids in the Tri-Valley, including our  high-performance (1300+) class led by GM Enrico Sevillano .
Learn more and register now for Spring 2026.
The  Tri-Valley Chess League is a student-led non-profit that holds tournaments and classes.
The  Emerald Knights Chess Club  is a student-led organization that holds tournaments and classes.

Dublin , CA 94568

United States

OC Mess Hall Market

Event Overview

February Open – Day Knight Chess Free USCF-Rated Tournament
Welcome to the Day & Knight Chess February Open! This free community event is designed to help players of all levels gain experience in a competitive tournament environment.
https://www.kingregistration.com/event/Feb26
Location: OC Mess Hall
Address: 1705 Flight Way, Tustin, CA 92782
Date: Saturday, February 21st, 2026
Player Capacity: Limited to 100 participants.
Entry: FREE for all participants!
Sections & Schedules
All sections are USCF rated. If you are unrated, please join the U600 or U1000.
Open Section (4 Rounds | G/45; d5)

- Minimum rating: 1300+ required .

- Check-in: 8:30 AM

- Round 1: 9:00 AM

- Round 2: 11:15 AM

- Lunch (All): 1:30 PM – 2:00 PM

- Round 3: 2:00 PM

- U1400: Ratings 900–1399.

- U1000: Ratings 500–999.

- Check-in: 10:30 AM

- Round 1: 11:15 AM

- Round 2: 12:15 PM

- Lunch (All): 1:30 PM – 2:00 PM

- Round 3: 2:00 PM

- Round 4: 3:00 PM

Trophies for the Top 3 in each section and a Gift Raffle for all participants. Raffle from 1:45 - 2:00 PM

Equipment & Logistics
Players must bring everything. Please bring your own:

- Chess board and pieces

- Chess clock

- Notation sheets and pencils

HCC Feb Game-in-45 Challenge (Prizes: $600, b/24)

Play More Chess Academy - Home of the Hamden Chess Club

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

HCC February Game-in-45 Challenge ($600 in prizes 70% Gtd; 2 sections)
DATE & TIME:  Saturday, February 21, 2026;  1:00PM~6:00PM  (Round 1 at 1:00PM, subsequent rounds ASAP) .
LOCATION:  Play More Chess Academy, Home of the Hamden Chess Club,  1227 Whitney Ave., Hamden, CT 06517
EVENT FORMAT:   G/45, d5;  3-SS; Two Sections:  Open and U1600   (PLAY UP LIMIT:   200 POINTS. i.e. player with rating 1400-1599 may choose to play in either section).
ELIGIBILITY:  A current USCF membership is required to play in this tournament (see link in notes below to join or renew. This tournament is open to all adult players ages 13+ of any rating, including Unrated.   (Players who are under age 13, but have a USCF rating of 700+ are also eligible for this tournament).
BYES:   One irrevocable half-point bye available any round; Must be declared by end of registration.
ENTRY FEE:
Early entry (by 11:59PM Tuesday prior):   $40; (Non-HCC Member: Additional $10 Fee);  Free Early entry for titled players (GMs, IMs and NMs) with no entry fee deducted from prize; then
Early entry (by 11:59PM Thursday prior): All players $50, then
Regular entry (by 11:00AM day of tournament):  All players $60
PRIZES:  $600, based on 24 paid entries (70% Gtd);  (Open Section: $150-100, Top Female $50;  U1600 Section: $125-75, Top Female $50;  Biggest Upset in tournament $50.  Prizes adjusted on pro rata basis based on actual entries. Players with tie score within section share prizes equally.
PRIZE LIMITS:  Unrated player: $100 limit.  Unrated player not eligible for Biggest upset prize and place prize is limited to $100 for unrated player.
PLAY UP LIMIT:  200 POINTS. i.e. player with rating 1400-1599 may choose to play in either section.
REGISTRATION AND CURRENT ENTRIES:   https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8303/
ENTRY DEADLINE:  11:00AM day of tournament (the registration closes two hours before tournament start time) or player limit of 36 whichever is first.
SCHEDULE OF ROUNDS:  Rd. 1: 1:00PM, then asap.  (The Playwright Irish Pub & Restaurant, across street, offeres free beverage with Entree/Burger purchase (show copy of flyer).
Join the HCC and Save  - discounts on OTB tournaments, free weekly online tournaments with prizes, free casual play evenings each week!
Adults only $130/year;  Scholastic (K-12) and Senior Citizens (65+) only $110/year!    Join HCC today at PlayMoreChess.com!
PARKING AND TRANSPORTATION:  Free parking is available on behind the Academy, including free street parking on Putnam/Lake Drive that goes behind the Academy; additional free parking at 60 Putnam Ave (one block West) ( See Parking Map ).  CT Transit bus stop is adjacent to Academy at intersection of Putnam/Whitney Ave.
ADDITIONAL NOTES:  All players must be current members of US Chess (go to  USCHESS.org  to join or renew your USCF membership/membership ID number. HCC Affiliate # is A6054128.  Chess sets, boards, DGT clocks provided (must use our equipment).  Score sheets and pens are also provided.  Games on top two boards broadcast live at:  https://playmorechess.com/livegames.htm .

Jenks K-12 Open

Jenks Middle School

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Schedule

8:30 Doors open. There is no check-in; all registered players will be paired.
9:30 Round One for all sections will begin following announcements in the playing hall.
​Subsequent rounds are paired back to back with a break for lunch. Awards ceremonies take place for each section after that section's final round is complete.
​For late arrivals or last-minute cancellations, send a text to 918-978-1899. This helps us start on time and avoid pairing players with no-shows.
​
​Sections & Prizes
1: Grades K–3 rated under 600

- Five rounds, G/30

- 🏆 Trophies for first, second, and third-place individuals. Outstanding Performance trophies for players scoring 4.0+ who did not place in the top three. Trophies for first, second, and third-place school teams and for first-place club team.

- 🏅Medals for players with scores of 3.0–3.5​​.

​ 2: Grades 4–6 rated under 600

- Five rounds, G/30

- 🏆 Trophies for first, second, and third-place individuals. Outstanding Performance trophies for players scoring 4.0+ who did not place in the top three. Trophies for first, second, and third-place school teams and for first-place club team.

- 🏅Medals for players with scores of 3.0–3.5​​. ​

​ 3: All grades rated under 900
K-6th graders rated under 600 may play in either section 1 or 2 according to their grade.

- Five rounds, G/30

- 🏆 Trophies for first, second, and third-place individuals and Outstanding Performance trophies for players with 4.0 or higher who did not place in the top three. Trophies for first, second, and third-place school teams and for first-place club team.

- 🏅Medals for players with scores of 3.0–3.5​​

4: All grades rated under 1300

- Four rounds, G/40;d5

- Clocks required

- Notation strongly encouraged

- 🏆 Trophies for first, second, and third-place individuals. Trophies for first-place school team and club team.

- 🏅Medals for players with scores of 2.5 or higher.

5 (Premier): All grades rated 1300+*

- Four rounds, G/40;d5

- Clocks and notation required

- 🏆 Trophies for first, second, and third-place individuals. Trophy for top U1600. Trophies for first-place school team and club team.

- 🏅Medals for players with scores of 2.5 or higher.

​*Players with a rating of 1200+ may play up to Premier. ​
​

Equipment

Sets are provided for tournament games, but players are encouraged to bring their own for skittles (waiting area).
​Scoresheets and pencils are provided.
Clocks are provided for sections 4 & 5 only. Players in other sections may bring their own. A good selection of tournament-suitable clocks can be found here .​
Membership

A current US Chess membership is required for all players. OSCO offers discounted memberships to all registered players, including non-Oklahoma residents. If your player has never had a US Chess membership, or if their membership will have expired by the date of the tournament, visit the appropriate link below after you register.
This is NOT an automatic process. Our volunteers will use the information you provide in the forms below to get a US Chess ID for you child or renew their membership.

New players: Grades K–3 rated under 600
​ Oklahoma residents: First-time membership, Section 2 or higher
All players: Renew an expired membership
​ Other states: First-time membership, Section 2 or higher
​Not sure if your player's membership is still current? Please check before you register: US Chess Player Search (Link opens in a new window.)
Read before you register

When you register, you will be asked to agree to OSCO's terms & conditions. You will also be asked to affirm that you will make sure your player understands our tournament rules and code of conduct. Please take a moment to read them now. (Each link opens in a new window, so you won't lose your place.)
Terms & conditions
Tournament rules

​If you or your player have a question about OSCO's rules, please contact us at Click here to show mail address   so we can answer it before the tournament.
​Registration
Registration is on our website HERE and ends February 19. No registrations will be accepted after the deadline.
Entry is $25/player. Parents registering three or more siblings at the same time: $20/player.
​​Questions?
For general tournament or registration questions, requests to change section or team affiliation, or cancellations before the registration deadline, send an email to  Click here to show mail address .
For payment questions or refund requests made before the registration deadline, send an email to  Click here to show mail address . Refunds do not include online processing fees.

2026 GREATER CHICAGO K-12 CHAMPIONSHIPS!

McCormick Place South Building

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

GREATER CHICAGO K-12 CHAMPIONSHIPS!
Open to all players in grades 12 & below
McCormick Place South Building 2301 S Martin Luther King Dr, Chicago, IL 60616  – we will be on the 4 & 5th floor

Presented by Renaissance Knights Foundation, Kasparov Chess Foundation, & Chicago Public Schools; sponsored by SBB Research Group

DETAILS
Championship Sections:  4-SS, G/40,d5 Rounds : 10:00, 12:30, 2:30 & 4:30
Reserve & Novice Sections: 5-SS, G/25,d5 Rounds : 10:00, 12:00, 2:00, 3:30 & 5:00.
Awards Ceremony: 6:30 pm.
Entry Fee: $50 by 1/19; $65 by 2/9; $85 by 2/19, No entries allowed after 2/19 or onsite
Online Entries / info:   www.greaterchicago.rknights.org
Section Changes: $20 after 2/11, request online only by 2/19, onsite takes effect in round 2.
Refunds: $20 fee per registered player if requested by 2/19.
Byes:  One ½-pt bye available, to include the final round, see website for details.

SECTIONS / AWARDS:
PRIMARY (K-4): Championship: open to all. Awards: top 5 players, top 2 schools.
Reserve U600:  open to players rated Under 600. Awards: top 8 players, top 3 schools.
Novice U300: open to players rated Under 300 / Unrated. Awards: top 8 players, top 3 schools.

ELEMENTARY (K-6): Championship: open to all. Awards: top 5 players, top 2 schools . Reserve U800:  open to players rated Under 800. Awards: top 8 players, top 3 schools.
Novice U400: open to players rated Under 400 / Unrated. Awards: top 8 players, top 3 schools.

JUNIOR HIGH (K-8): Championship: open to all. Awards: top 5 players, top 2 school. Reserve U1000:  open to players rated Under 1000. Awards: top 8 players, top 3 schools. Novice U500:  open to players rated Under 500 / Unrated. Awards: top 8 players, top 3 schools.

HIGH SCHOOL (K-12): Championship: open to all. Awards: top 5 players, top 2 school. Reserve U1100:  open to players rated Under 1100 / Unrated. Awards: top 5 players, top 2 schools.
Any player who scores 4 or more points and doesn’t win an award will receive a medal!

CHICAGO’S OFFICIAL SCHOLASTIC CHAMPIONSHIP
The City of Chicago will recognize the top individual & team from Chicago in each Championship section as the City Champion

The official version of the tournament rules & regulations is posted on the event website and are subject to change:  www.greaterchicago.rknights.org

Chicago , IL 60616

United States

Kleptz YMCA

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

This is a USCF-rated event for the Kleptz YMCA of Englewood Chess Club. (Non-members from the community pay $5 to the YMCA at the site.) ONLINE REGISTRATION ONLY. Cost: $15 (payable online).
Prize Fund. Guaranteed $400. 7 Categories— one prize per category. First overall $100; Categories A/B/C/D/E/Under 1000 & Unrated $50. Any profit will go to the Brethren Youth Group.
It starts at 9 am sharp.
Limited to the first 36 to register online.
Registration Link:
http://www.chessregister.com/register?event_key=xjCTlCkxjZOd3DXXxGyFZ81V04Ucuw73-2nkGVypuPY%3D
The time control is G25+5. New or first-time players must obtain a USCF membership by going to
Join US Chess
Bring a clock and a regulation chess set. Some supplied. Clocks without an increment time, e.g., delay or analog, will be adjusted by adding 5 minutes.
The event is expected to conclude by 1:15 pm. Kids under 16 should have a parent present.
The tournament will take place in the Heritage Room. An alternative room is available for kibitzing and parents.

Mohar February Chess Tournament

Holiday Inn

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Team Trophies!
Three players in the rated sections attending the same school (as of the spring 2026 semester). Teams have no upper limit;
the more players on a team, the higher the chances for a good result, but only the top 3 players’
results count for the team total. The team gains points by winning or drawing rated games. Points are
weighted, with results in higher sections worth more.
-------------------------------------------------
Mohar February Chess Tournament – Scholastic and Open Chess Tournament
February 21, 2026
Holiday Inn, 909 Holcomb Bridge Rd Roswell, GA 30076
4SS, G/25;d5
5 sections – An Open section for adults and advanced scholastic players, 3 Rated Scholastic-only
sections for K-12 players and a Nonrated Scholastic practice section for new and young players.
ROUND TIMES:  First round is at 10:00AM, rounds 2-4 will start ASAP after the preceding rounds finish
with a slightly longer break for lunch between rounds 2 and 3. We are usually done around 4 – 4:30
PM.
NONRATED SECTION:  The Nonrated section is for new/unrated players and players rated below 300
who need practice. While the rules of chess still apply, this is a more relaxed game designed to let new
and young players experience chess without worrying about ratings. New players may choose to play
in the Under 400 section if they want to become rated.
3 SCHOLASTIC-ONLY RATED SECTIONS: Under 400, Under 800 and Under 1200: These sections require
an active US Chess Federation membership (https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess). New players
wanting a rating play in the Under 400.
OPEN SECTION:  This Section is available to both adults and scholastic players. Scholastic players rated
over 1199 must play in this section; however, any scholastic player rated 1000+ may choose to play in
either the Open or kids-only Under 1200 section.
Players will be placed in the section that matches their rating unless granted an exemption by the
Tournament Director. Rated sections may be combined at TD discretion.
ENTRY FEE:  Early entry received through 10th February is $35. Registration is $40 from February 11 - 19.
Late registration begins February 20th and is $45.
Same day, onsite registration is $50 and must be completed by 9:00AM to be paired for Round 1. Late
sign ups may receive a ½ point round one bye.
REGISTRATION:   CLICK HERE , fill out the form, and pay via Zelle to  [email protected]
BYES:  If you have a scheduling conflict and plan to skip one or two rounds, 1/2 Point Byes are available
and should be requested at the time of registration.
INDIVIDUAL PRIZES:  Trophies for 1st, 2nd, 3rd place in each SCHOLASTIC section and cash or gift cards
for the Open section.
TEAM PRIZES:  Team Trophies to top 3 schools based on weighted points of 4 players. Must have a
minimum of 3 players from the same school playing in the USCF Rated Sections to qualify for Team
Prizes.
FOOD  – We plan to have food vendors to supply snacks and lunch.
Sets, boards and notation sheets supplied. Please bring chess clocks if possible.
CONTACT:   [email protected]  or 7708158221 FOR QUESTIONS

Address: 909 Holcomb Bridge

Rosewell , GA 30076

United States

Open Section at 2026 Greater Austin Scholastic Championships

NYOS Charter School

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

USCF rated chess tournament on February 21, 2026 for adults and more advanced scholastic players. 4 round Swiss at G/45 +5.
Full pairings and standings can be found at the registration link below (click on the blue “Live” text to get to them).
Register  HERE ! When you click the link, scroll to the bottom for registration.
See Preregistration List  HERE

Basics
This is a Swiss-system tournament, so everyone plays all day—there is no “elimination.” Players must know how to play the game of chess! We follow  USCF rules  including: touch-move, mandatory clocks (bring your own if at all possible), and mandatory notation. If registrations exceed 32, we reserve the right to split into two sections.
Location
NYOS Charter School
12333 N Lamar Blvd
Austin, TX 78753
Eligibility
All adults
Any youth who have reached at least 1300 by the February 2026 USCF supplement.
Ineligible entries will be moved to the appropriate scholastic section of the  2026 Greater Austin Scholastic Championships .
This is a rated tournament.  You must have a USCF ID and your membership (can be purchased/renewed at check out or  online with the USCF  in advance of registration) . You can verify your USCF membership ID and expiration by visiting the  USCF’s Member Services Area . Anyone can become a USCF member. Players new to tournament chess are welcome to play. Your USCF membership cannot expire before February 28, 2026.
Schedule
No check-in necessary for preregistrations. We will make every attempt to contact you in advance if we see a problem with your registration.  Verify your entry ONLINE!
9:00 a.m. Open section begins.  Open has 4 rounds, all rounds are are G/45, +5.
No changes for round 1 (bye or section) allowed after online registration closes. Requests for byes, withdrawals, player info edits be made onsite with your chief TD and go into effect as of round 2.
Approximate Round Times

Open Section:
rd 1 – 9:00am, rd2 – 11:00am, rd3 – 1:30pm, rd4 – 3:30pm
Notes
There will be some down time between rounds since many games will finish early. We will provide an area (outside the tournament room) for casual  “skittles”  chess and/or other indoor activities.
Concessions TBA.  Only water bottles allowed at the chess board.
Awards
Cash prizes  (to winners in both sections, in the case of multiple sections), based on number of entries.  Special trophies  will be awarded to the highest scoring  Family & Child  teams  (Uncles, Aunts, Adult siblings, Parents, or Grandparents paired with at least one scholastic aged player.).
Registration Information

Entry fee pricing is staggered and based on date of entry/payment.
*youth – $35/adult – $25 through Saturday, 1/31/2026.
*youth – $45/adult – $35 through Saturday, 2/14/2026.
*Late entry youth-$50 / adult – $40 begins Sunday, 2/15/2026 and ENDS at midnight on Wednesday 2/18/26, at which time online entry closes.
*If space permits, onsite registration on Saturday, 2/21/26 will be permitted, $50 regardless of age. Cash or venmo only. First round play requires registration and payment before 8:45am.
Withdrawals requested via email before  midnight  on  Wednesday 2/18/26 are eligible for a refund (minus a $10 service fee). No exceptions. NO email/phone entries.
If you need byes, request them by adding a note when you register. First bye receives 1/2-point. Further byes receive 0-points. Email the registrar to make changes to your requested byes. Deadline to add or remove a 1st round requested bye is 9am Friday 2/20/2026. All 1/2-point byes must be requested/removed before the end of round 2.
Email Sarah Brauner ( Click here to show mail address ) with other questions.  No phone calls, please.  Emails will be returned promptly.
Organized by Rocks & Rooks

2026 Greater Austin Scholastic Championships

NYOS Charter School

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Would you like to be an Austin area scholastic chess champion? Here’s your chance!
Scholastic chess tournament in multiple sections to be held on February 21, 2026. G/25, +5 inc. Trophies and medals awarded.
Full pairings and standings can be found at the registration link below (click on the blue “Live” text to get to them).
Register  HERE ! When you click the link, scroll to the bottom for registration.
See Preregistration List  HERE

Basics

USCF rated chess tournament in multiple RATED scholastic sections: K-3 U400, K-3 U700, K-5 U600,  K-5 U1000,  6-12 U600, 6-12 U1000, and K-12 Elite (for players rated 950-1399). Please note: all scholastic players rated 1400 and over must play in the   Open section . Please note, at the event pairings will be posted only  online .

This is a Swiss-system tournament, so everyone plays all day—there is no “elimination.” Players must know how to play the game of chess! We follow  US Chess rules  including: touch-move, mandatory clocks if available, and notation. K-3 and younger sections are excused from taking notation. Please review the  Parent/Coach Responsibilities  before registering.

Location

NYOS Charter School
12333 N Lamar Blvd
Austin, TX 78753

Eligibility

This is a rated tournament.  You must have a USCF ID and your membership can be purchased/renewed  online with US Chess  in advance of registration. You can verify your US Chess membership ID and expiration by visiting the  US Chess Member Services Area . Anyone can become a USCF member. Players new to tournament chess are welcome to play. Your US Chess membership cannot expire before February 28, 2026.  (New players in 3rd grade and below may request a non-member ID as a part of USCF’s   Junior Tournament Player  program during registration. JTPs ok in  K-3 sections only .)

“Under” sections are only for students meeting the rating criteria. All players who are new to tournaments are eligible for their age appropriate ‘under’ section. ( Look up your player’s rating here .  Please email the registrar or ask your chess coach for placement information.
If your 6th grader attends an Elementary School, please contact the registrar for options.  With enough registrations, any section may be divided into two sections so we can offer more prizes. Sections with fewer than 20 entries may be merged into a similar section to provide optimal pairings and competition.

Please note: February 2026 ‘Regular’ OTB ratings will be used for pairing purposes. If no regular rating is available, then other USCF ratings (quick, blitz, online) can and will be considered for section placement.  Requests to play down will not be honored.  FYI:   Any event that is rated after January 21st will not affect your February supplement rating, as those events takes place after February ratings are calculated.

All players in this event must be in 12th grade or lower.

Schedule

No check-in necessary for preregistrations. We will make every attempt to contact you in advance if we see a problem with your registration.  Verify your entry online!
8:00 a.m. Chess Control opens for onsite registration.  Onsite registrations  before 9:30am accepted, but must start play in round 2.
8:30 a.m Announcements  begin in all scholastic playing rooms.
Players and coaches should be present.
9:00 a.m. Rd 1 begins.  Scholastic sections have 5 rds, G/25, +5.
9:00 a.m. Open section  (different event allowing adults)  begins.  Open has 4 rounds, all rounds are are G/45, +5.
9:15 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Chess control open for event issues.  No changes for round 1 (bye or section) allowed after online registration closes. Requests for byes, withdrawals, and player or school information edits go in effect immediately if made via email before the close of online registration. Changes requested onsite go into effect as of round 2.

Approximate Round Times

Scholastic Sections:
round 1 – 9:00am, rd 2 – 11:00am, rd 3 – 12:45 pm, rd 4 – 2:30 pm, rd 5 – 4:00 pm
Awards in the cafeteria as each section finishes.

Notes

There will be some down time between rounds since many games will finish early. We will provide an area (outside the tournament room) for casual  “skittles”  chess and/or other indoor activities. Parents and/or coaches, please provide age-appropriate activities during the time between rounds. The organizers cannot baby-sit.  No child should be left unattended!

Concessions details coming soon.  Only water bottles allowed at the chess board.

Awards

Trophies & Medals  to Top Contenders!  Ribbons  to all participants!
Trophies to the  top individuals  in each scholastic section. Trophies to the  top teams  in all sections. Number of individual and team trophies will depend on number of entries. Chess medals will go to all players (excluding Open section) that finish the tournament with a positive score (3.0 & 3.5 points). Trophies to players scoring 4.0 and above. No teams in Open section, but special trophies will be awarded to the highest scoring  Family & Child  teams (Uncles, Aunts, Adult siblings, Parents, Grandparents, or coach paired with at least one scholastic aged player.)

Registration Information

*$35 thru Saturday, 1/31/2026.
*$45 thru Saturday, 2/14/2026.
*Late entry $50 begins Sunday, 2/15/2026 and ENDS at midnight on Wednesday, 2/18/2026, at which time online entry closes.
*$60  Onsite entry  receives 1/2pt bye in round 1, and begins play in round 2.

Withdrawals requested via email before online registration closes ( midnight  on  Wednesday 2/18/26) are eligible for a refund (minus a $10 service fee). No exceptions. No refunds for USCF memberships after purchased from the USCF. NO email/phone entries.

Please request byes by adding a note when you register. First bye receives 1/2-point. Further byes receive 0-points. Email the registrar to make changes to your requested byes. Deadline to add or remove a 1st round requested bye is 9am Friday 2/20/2026. All 1/2-point byes must be requested/removed before the end of round 2.

Email  Click here to show mail address  with other questions.  No phone calls, please.  Emails will be returned promptly.

Austin , TX 78753

United States

Tunnelvision XLI

Columbia Chess Club

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

The Columbia Chess Club Presents Columbia Tunnelvision XLI
February 21, 2026
$1000 Guaranteed
10:30 a.m. 4-Round G/45;inc.5
Columbia Chess Club
6169 St. Andrews Rd.
Columbia, SC 29212
Register
Registration
Standard registration is $40 until the day before the tournament.  $50 late registration the day before/morning of.  Registration online only, registration limited to first 74 players.
Entry for titled players (National Master and above) is free, standard entry fee deducted from prizes.  If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout.
Considering Tunnelvision as your first chess tournament?  Great!  We've put together a guide to help first-time players .
Register Now
Pre-Registered Players
Format
4 Round Swiss. Time control is G45/inc.5 (45 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment ), which will be USCF dual-rated under both Quick and Classical. All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. Tournament has three sections: Championship (1600+), Under 1600, and Under 1000. Players may register for a higher section if they are within 100 USCF rating points of the cutoff.
If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit  https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess.
Live Standings/Pairings/Boards
The top board of each section will be live streamed to the DGT LiveCloud along with real-time updates to Lichess.org and Chess.com.  A live video stream of the top Championship board will also be available on the club's Twitch page.  See this site's "Live" menu for links.
Live standings (including current pre-registration information) and pairings are also available below.
Live Standings
Prizes
$1000 Prize Fund Guaranteed.
Championship (1600+)
$400 Fund. 1st: $200; 2nd: $130; 3rd: $70
Under 1600
$300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50
Under 1000
$300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50
Schedule

- Round 1: 10:30 a.m.

- Round 2: 12:50 p.m.

- Round 3: 2:40 p.m.

- Round 4: 4:30 p.m.

Byes
A single half-point bye is available any round, including the final round.  The half-point bye may be requested as a part of the advance entry or on site before the tournament starts.  Thereafter the only bye available is a zero-point bye.  The chief tournament director shall have the ability to grant a half-point bye for any round on unusual circumstances.
Location
Columbia Chess Club
6169 St. Andrews Rd., Ste A
Columbia, SC 29212
Questions?
Email  [email protected] or call/text James Brandmair at 803.569.0938.
Parking
The Columbia Chess Club is located in a shopping center with ample parking.
Food
The Columbia Chess Club offers on-site concessions, including drinks and snacks.  By the Fire Pizza and Zorba's Restaurant are located in the same shopping center and will be open during the tournament.  Many other restaurants are available close by!

Address: 214 Wilton Hill Rd

Columbia , SC 29212

United States

Sections: 3
Grand Prix Points:
Prize Fund: $1,000

Handicap Accessible: No
Residency Restriction: No
Online Event: No

Columbia Chess Club

Phone: 8035690938

Arlington Classics Academy Middle School Campus

Event Overview

Sections

- One Section, but in the case of a large turnout, sections will be assigned at the discretion of the tournament director.

Details
Rounds:  The first round begins at 9:00 am. All other rounds as soon as possible.
Keeping Score:  No time penalties will be issued for failing to keep score, but an adequate score sheet is still required for some claims.
Trophies:  Trophies will be awarded to top individual finishers in all sections. There are no team prizes.
No Lunch:  There will be no lunch break, but players may bring a snack or lunch.
Early Registration is $20; Day-of registration is $40. Four rounds with a time control of G/25;d5.

Farmers Branch Chess Club Tournament #45_February 21, 2026

Farmers Branch Chess Club

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Tournament Location :
Farmers Branch Chess Club

1804 Mindehall Drive, Farmers Branch Texas 75234

IMPORTANT :

Participants MUST bring their own Tournament Clocks & Scoresheets.
Tournament will be initially limited to 30 players.

United States Chess Federation Memberships Required for all sections - Can Be Purchased using this online registration form

Open to All the players

USCF Rated.

Date : 2/21/2026

Sections : U600, U1200, Championship.(Live USCF rating might be considered)

In the event of low turnout , sections MAY be merged.
Entry Fee :  $30

Format:
4 Round Swiss, non-elimination
Time : 9 AM CST

Round 1 starts at 9:00 AM.
Lunch break for 30 minutes after Round 1. All others ASAP.
All rounds G/30; D5 Second Time Delay.

Awards : Trophy

Blitz :

Section : Open
Entry Fee :  $15

Format:
5 Round Swiss, non-elimination
Time : Immediately upon Regular Rounds completion

All rounds G/5; 0 Second Time Delay.

Awards : Trophy

Registration:  On-line  - https://www.farmersbranchchessclub.com/
Mandatory to Submit this form online AFTER making the Zelle Transfer - Registration ends at 11:00pm the day before the event.

Payment  : Zelle Transfer to [email protected] .(Include  Participant   Full name in the Memo Field during Zelle Transfer)

Inquiries  : [email protected]
Lunch\Drinks  : Not available at Location - Participants may bring sack lunches. Please plan accordingly

Tournament Policy :

Refunds: A player can receive Tournament credits if notified in an email by 11:00pm the day before the event. Players that no-show do not receive a refund. No exceptions.
Photography: Photos will be taken of the tournament

Note :

Parents/Guardians of Minors

We welcome children to play in our tournament, but please be aware of the following:
Your child will play against adults, will be treated like an adult, and will be expected to interact like an adult. Your child will not be supervised by us. If a child is under 16 years old, a parent/guardian must remain in the building.

Rule Variations in Effect at the Tournament

1H1. Director as witness only.  In an event in which most games are not watched by directors, a director may refrain from correcting all illegal moves he or she may notice but simply serve as a witness should one of the players point out the illegal move before any moves have been made.
15A. Paper scoresheet variation.  The player using a paper scoresheet may first make the move, and then write it on the scoresheet, or vice versa.

United States

SACA-Wakefield Open

Wakefield Middle School

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

SACA-Wakefield Open
Saturday, February 21, 2026
Wakefield Middle School
Open to all ages and skill levels!
Join us for our first-ever tournament at Wakefield Middle School! It's a perfect chance to try competitive chess and help us grow more events like this in the future.

FLYER
LOCATION:
Wakefield Middle School, 101 W. 44th Street, Tucson, AZ 85713 .
DESCRIPTION:
4-round Swiss tournament in 3 rated sections: Open, K – 8th Grade, K – 3rd Grade
and 2 not-rated sections: Not-Rated 4th – 8th Grade, Not-Rated K – 3rd Grade.
Ratings based on February Supplement. Tournament is open to all ages and skill levels.

The Open , K – 8th Grade , and K – 3rd Grade sections will be US Chess Federation rated.
(See REGISTRATION below for US Chess Federation membership requirements.)

The Not-Rated 4th – 8th Grade , Not-Rated K – 3rd Grade are not US Chess Federation rated.

EQUIPMENT:
Players are responsible for boards/set, scoresheets, pencils/pens, bringing/setting their own clocks.

TIME CONTROL:  Time control: G/30;d5.

REGISTRATION:
For the Open and K – 8th Grade section US Chess Federation membership is required. Annual membership is available on uschess.org. If you have not joined US Chess or renewed your membership by February 20, please renew onsite through SACA before the 1st round. Players that cannot show proof of paid membership before the 1st round will not be paired.

Registration is online at https://www.kingregistration.com/event/wakefield .
Online registration closes Friday, 2/20 at 7 pm.
Onsite registration: Saturday, 8:30 am – 9:00 am. Registrations after 9:00 am may receive a ½ point bye for round 1 and be paired for round 2.
There will be a $5 processing fee for any refunds (must be requested before 8 pm Friday, 2/20).

ENTRY FEES:
$20 if received by Thursday, 2/12. $25 if after Thursday, 2/12 or $30 at the site.

SCHEDULE:
9:30 am, 10:45 am, 12:30 pm, 1:45 pm.
Please arrive by 9:15 am for pairings and announcements. There is no tournament check-in.
Byes: ½ point byes are available for all rounds if requested prior to start of round two .

PRIZES:
Open : 1st, $75; 2nd, $60; 3rd, $40
Other Sections : 1st, Trophy; 2nd, Large Medal; 3rd, Small Medal; 4th, Ribbon
Additional prizes may be awarded based on entries. Prizes are 100% guaranteed.

CONTACT:
Michelle Martinez, (520) 615-1308 (TEXT); sazchess.org; Click here to show mail address

Tucson , AZ 85713

United States

Loudoun Chess Tournament 2/21/26

Executive Conference and Training Center

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Register at  chessacademy.com/tournaments !
This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience.  We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games.
Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating.  Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy.
This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare).
Everyone will use a clock!  We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player.
Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both!

- All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds

- If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it.  If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!).  If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up  here

- Please arrive 15 minutes before games start.  Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads.

- Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament.

Questions?  Please let us know at  Click here to show mail address !

Three rounds, USCF rated
Three major sections by age; subsections in groups of 8 by rating.

Escuela Vieau Public School

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

When
Saturday, February 21, 2026
On-site registration: 8:15-9:00 AM
Round 1: 10:00 AM - Round 2: 11:15 AM. Subsequent rounds start shortly after the completion of the prior round.
Where
Vieau School
823 S 4th St Milwaukee, WI 53204

Byes  Limit one half-point bye. Additional byes are OK but are zero points. Final round byes are zero points unless requested before the first round. Contact the organizers at  [email protected]  to arrange byes.

Bring Pencils. Sets provided on-site.

Lunch Concessions on site.

Supervision Players in K-8th grade MUST have adult supervision at all times.

E-mail questions to [email protected]

Scholastic Tournament

4 SECTIONS

K-8 Non-Rated: 5 Rounds
K-4 Rated: 5 Rounds
K-8 Rated: 5 Rounds
K-12 Rated: 4 Rounds

Time Control

K-8 NR, K-4 Rated & K-8 Rated: G/30
K-12 Rated: G/45
All sections 5-second delay

Awards
K-8 Non-Rated

Top 3 Team  Top 8 Individual  Participation Awards to all.

K-4, K-8 & K-12 Rated

Top 3 Team  Top 8 Individual  Medals to those with a plus score (3+ in K-4, K-8 and 2.5+ in K-12)

ENTRY FEE

$30 Online on or before Saturday, February 14th, $35 after. Register online here: Register for 2026 Vieau School Charge into Chess
Refund Policy: If you register for the tournament and are unable to make it, please notify us at least one hour in advance of the start of round one. If this is done, then the IAC will refund your entry fee less the cost of online registration ($1) and payment processing ($0.30 + 2.9% of the entry fee.)

Grupology February Rapid Scholastic Tournament

Grupology HQ

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Tournaments take place every month at Grupology HQ in Downtown Burlingame.
Location

- Grupology HQ: 1419 Chapin Ave. Suite 101, Burlingame CA 94010

Eligibility

- Players must have an active (paid) US Chess Federation membership to compete in the rated sections.

- Expiration date of US Chess membership must be later than the day of the tournament.

- Check membership status

- Become a member or renew your membership

Rapid Tournaments

Sections

- K–12th Rated (4 games)
- 2 or 3 sections depending on number of registrations: 600+, under 600

- TDs reserve the right to adjust the sections based on the players signed up to better serve them.

- K–5th Non-Rated (4 games)

Schedule

- Doors Open: 8:50am

- Start Time: Game 1 starts promptly at 9:00am.

- Rounds: All sections will play 4 games. This is not an elimination competition.
- Round 1: 9:00am

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids

Kings & Queens Chess Academy

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30.  Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00.  The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play.  Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections.  The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment.  Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $30.  Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information:  Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).

World Chess Fair #167

Shelly Studio of Bridge and Games

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Four Rounds: G/25, d5
Registration: 5:30 p.m. - 5:55 p.m.
Round Times : 6, 7, 8, 9pm. Event ends around 10:15 p.m.
Entry Fee: $5
Three Sections with Three Separate Prizes (Open to ALL ages)
Qualified (All Ratings Over 1200): Standard and Quick (Dual) USCF Rated.
Youth Open (Under 1201/Unrated): Standard and Quick (Dual) USCF Rated.
Adult Open (Under 1201/Unrated): Standard and Quick (Dual) USCF Rated.

$120 GUARANTEED PRIZE FUND: Prize for First Place. Two-way tie splits cash evenly. More than two players/teams tie, no prize awarded.
Qualified Section (All Ratings Over 1200): First Place $60
Youth Open Section (Under 1201/Unrated): $20
Adult Open Section (Under 1201/Unrated): $20
Family Team Prize: $20 (The scores of two family members will be combined. Can be in different sections. If more than two family members play, then the highest two scores will be used. Family members won't ever be paired against each other. Two way ties split money evenly; if three or more tie, then no one wins. Family teams are: parent(s)/children; siblings; adult couples. Maximum score is: 8 points [4 + 4])
Within all sections, some pairings may be adjusted for competitive matches and greater opportunity for both players to gain rating points, regardless of tournament score.
Minimum four players or section will be merged with lower section. Prize eligibility remains the same; all prizes guaranteed.
Playing up sections is not allowed by request. Playing down one section by request is allowed. Tournament Director has full discretion with pairings and moving players into different sections if necessary. The objective is for all players to have competitive matches all rounds with minimal byes and mismatches.
Late-Entries Welcome - Show up before any round begins, and you'll be paired against a similar-rated opponent. $5 entry even if playing one game.
Free Bottled Water/Snacks
Boards/Sets/Clocks/Scoresheets/Pens Provided - No Equipment Needed.
Annual USCF membership REQUIRED to participate. You can join/re-new USCF membership at club BEFORE ROUND ONE if needed.
The most efficient way to gain rating points is Action Chess. Why play a six-hour game when you can play a one-hour game for the same rating points? With modern computer analysis, chess growth happens away from the board, reviewing played games. FOUR COMPLETE GAMES in the same time of one traditional tournament game means FOUR times the learning opportunity and FOUR times the potential rating point gain - all in one evening.
Action Chess is the most competitive and most fun form of standard-rated chess! If you're trying to become an Expert, Master, or scholastic player trying to move up the age lists, Action Chess is your best way to achieve your goals.

Suite 103 - D

Latham , NY 12110
