TEXAS ACTION CHAMPIONSHIP 2026

Grand Prix, State Championship Event

THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Texas Action Championship 2026
A US Chess Grand Prix and State Championship Event
At The Houston Chess Studio
Saturday, Feb. 21 2026
REGISTRATION:   https://www.kingregistration.com/event/ACTION_CHAMP_2026
Event Overview:
A one-day event.  5 Round Swiss, G/30, d5.
3 Sections: Open, U1600, U800
Projected Prizes: $900.00
Including $300 Guaranteed 1st Place , Grand Prix Points and 2026 Texas Action Chess Champion title and trophy for First Place in the Open Section
Benefits:
1. State Championship Status
Do you want to be known as the best chess player in Texas for one-hour games? As an official US Chess state championship, sponsored by the Texas Chess Association, we have the honor of making this possible by awarding the title of “2026 Texas Action Chess Champion.”
2. Grand Prix Event
This tournament is one of the very few upcoming events in Texas that qualify as a US Chess Grand Prix event.  In case you are not familiar with the US Chess Grand Prix, it is a US Chess program that recognizes the ten players who win the most points in qualifying Grand Prix events. Essentially, if you make it into the top ten, it is proof that you are among the best of the best. It also means that you receive a substantial cash prize from US Chess.
3. Beginners Are Welcome
This tournament is not just for high-rated players. There will be two under sections (U1600 & U800) so that players can compete against other players of similar ability and are not crushed by opponents they have no chance of defeating anytime soon. But if you want to ‘play up’ into the Open Section you can do so for no additional charge. The Texas Action Championship will also be one of the very few cash prize events that offers a U800 section.
4. Savings Potential
We recognize the hardships of inflation. Accordingly, our starting entry fees ($45 for the Open and $35 for all other sections) are much lower than the entry fees that are charged as we move closer to the event. If you want a deal, register now. Not sure if you can come yet? No need to worry. Your entry fee is fully refundable until seven days before the event. No questions asked. No hassle. Just ask for a refund by the deadline and your refund will be on its way in no time. If you cancel within 7 days of the event you will be refunded the entry fee minus $15 OR you may apply the entire entry fee to a future event, within 90 days, at The Houston Chess Studio.
The Fine Print:
Qualifications : All chess players, regardless of residence, are welcome as long as they meet the membership requirements. You must have an unexpired USCF and TCA membership in good standing on the day of the tournament. If you do not have these memberships at the moment, you can still register but you will need to purchase/renew them before the tournament. Please note, however, that while residents of other states may participate and win cash prizes, the state champion title and trophy are for Texas residents only.
Entry Fees : For the Open Section, $45 by Jan 3rd; $55 by Feb. 7th; $65 thereafter. For all other sections, $35 by Jan. 3rd; $45 by Feb. 7th; $55 thereafter.
Byes:  Every player is entitled to one half point bye if requested before the close of online registration. All last round byes are for zero points.
Draws:  Draws prior to 30 moves and both players are barred from any cash prizes and the state champion title.
Schedule :  Round 1, 10:00-11:00am; Round 2, 11:15am-12:15pm; Lunch Break; Round 3, 1:00-2:00pm; Round 4, 2:15-3:15pm; and; Round 5, 3:30-4:30pm.
Prizes : For the Open section, $300 for first place plus a trophy, $150 for second place. $300 First Place in the Open Section is guaranteed , all other cash prizes based on 50 total paid entries . For all other sections, $150 for first place, $75 for second place. In the event of ties, prizes will be equally divided between the tying players in conformity with the Official Rules of Chess. However, if two or more Texas residents tie for first place in the Open Section, all of them will be recognized as co-champions, but tie breaks will determine who takes home the trophy. All cash prizes paid via PayPal.
Notation:  Absent a physical or developmental disability rendering a player unable to notate, notation is required in all sections except the U800 section.
Equipment : Bring your own chess boards and pieces and clock if you have them.  Some will be provided by the organizer but maybe not enough for everyone. You can still play even if you do not own a chess clock. Electronic notation approved by US Chess will be allowed and notation sheets will be provided free of charge as well.
Section Assignment : You may ‘play up’ if you want, at no additional charge. If you initially register for an under section and then move to the Open section, you will be charged a $10 section adjustment fee because the entry fee for the Open is higher to allow for larger prizes. However, this fee will not apply if you were allowed to play in an under section when you registered but later are required to play in the Open section because your rating increased after registration.  The tournament Director reserves the right to merge sections if necessary.
Rating : This tournament will use your regular rating as shown on the February Supplement for the purposes of section qualification and pairings. Players with foreign ratings are required to disclose such ratings and the tournament director may make such adjustments to the deemed rating of said players as he thinks proper.
Unrated Policy : Unrated players may win a maximum of $100, unless they are playing in the Open Section, in which case there are no limitations to how much they can win. If no rating is assigned, an unrated player may choose any section.
Illegal Moves:  As a variation of the Official Rules of Chess, an illegal move that is not corrected within three moves shall stand. The default rule is that illegal moves may be corrected up to ten moves away. The organizer believes that a lookback of up to ten moves is impracticable for events with shorter time controls like the Texas Action Championship.
Spectators:  No spectators will be allowed in the Tournament Hall while games are underway.  However, there is a skittles room/lounge right next door inside the Houston Chess Studio.  Many of the ongoing games, and views of the entire tournament hall, will be visible on one of the many screens on display in the lounge.
Food :  There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway, and Patron Pizza.  Several others are within walking distance.  There are also vending machines located in the skittles room/lounge of The Studio. Food and beverages are allowed at the playing boards.  Just be sure to clean up after yourself.
Venue:  THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO   provides a  quality chess playing experience for players of all levels, and their parents and spectators . Centrally and conveniently located at 250 Patton St., Suite H, Houston TX 77009.  Just inside North Loop 610 and just 2 blocks off North I-45. There is always plenty of  FREE  parking at The Studio.

The Baton Rouge Dual

Grand Prix

Baton Rouge Bridge Center

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Registration:  Click register to secure your spot! On site registration first come, first serve.
Tournament details: Five round, two-section, swiss system, G/40;d5, USCF dual-rated tournament.
Date: Saturday, February 21, 2026. Registration 9:15 AM-9:45 AM, first round pairs for 10:00 AM. Please do not enter the building prior to 9:15 AM!
Venue: Baton Rouge Bridge Center, 3033 Old Forge Dr, Baton Rouge, LA
Round times: 10:00 AM, 11:45 AM, 1:25PM, [meal break],  3:45 PM, 5:25 PM, prizes at 7:00 PM. Round times are tentative and subject to change. If we can move quicker, we will!
Prize fund: Prize fund is $1,000 b/60, 50% guaranteed. Prize fund breakdown as follows:
1st in open/unrated, $400
2nd in open/unrated, $200
1st in u1400, $250
2nd in u1400, $150
Sections: Open and U1400. Open section is FIDE rated and directed according to FIDE rules.  Players should familiarize themselves with the most common FIDE rules differences . TD reserves the right to adjust sections to match turnout. TDs reserve the right to use accelerated swiss pairing if one section contains more than 32 players.
Pairing: Highest of quick or regular rating to be used for pairing and prizes. If you are rated under 1400 but would like to play in the open, you may register for the open at no extra charge. Unrated players may play in either section, but are prize eligible in the open only. Ratings determined by this month's official USCF rating. 100 elo may be added to those with provisional ratings.
Entry fee: $35 early entry fee if purchased by one week prior. $40 standard entry if purchased by two days prior. $45 thereafter and on-site. Capacity limited to first 80 registrants.
Eligibility: Current USCF membership required. FIDE membership required for open section. FIDE membership is free if you already have a USCF membership (we will register you). No FIDE rated players 2400 or above, due to time control and format.
Bye policy: Two 0.5 point byes for any round available upon request, must be made prior to pairing round three in non-emergency situations. Bye requests cannot be cancelled following the start of round 3.
Equipment: A small amount of chess equipment will be provided. If you have a chess set and clock, please bring it.
Tiebreaks: Cash prizes to be split among all tied entrants.
Late arrivals: Games are forfeited 30 minutes after the round start time if a player has not arrived.
Refunds: Players who withdraw 60 minutes before round one are eligible for a refund of their entry fee, minus any applicable payment-processor fees (typically 5-7%).
FIDE rated: Top section played in accordance with the FIDE Laws of Chess. Entrants from other federations must provide FIDE ID; any player without an IM or higher title must also provide a valid USCF member ID. No FIDE norms will be awarded.
Unrated players with foreign ratings: For unrated USCF players with established foreign ratings, the most  current USCF conversion will be used (with preference toward their FIDE rating, if available) for all sections.
Check  downriverchess.com/tournaments for all our upcoming tournaments!

Baton Rouge , LA 70808

United States

Prize Fund: 1000

Rising Star February Grand Prix

Mesa DoubleTree by Hilton

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

Rising Star February Grand Prix
Saturday, Feb 21st, 2026
Location:
Mesa DoubleTree by Hilton
1011 West Holmes Ave
Mesa, AZ 85210
Format:  4-round Swiss tournament
Time Control : G/45;+10

Six Sections:
Open (2000 and up)
Class A (1800-1999)
Class B (1600-1799)
Class C (1400-1599)
Class D (1200-1399)
U1200 (1199 and Under)
Players within 100 points of rating floor of a higher section may play up for an additional $5.
Important:
• All sections USCF dual-rated.
• USCF membership required (may join or renew here: USCF join or renew or on site).
•  The official published February 2026 USCF Regular ratings will be used for section eligibility, pairings, and
prize eligibility. Higher unofficial USCF ratings might be used for playing up, or for other purposes.
• A maximum of two half-point byes are available. Half-point byes must be requested no later than
30 minutes before the round starts for rounds 1-2. Half-point byes for rounds 3-4 must be requested
before the start of round 2 and may not be revoked after round 2 starts.
• Boards, sets, clocks AND pens will be provided for all sections.

Prizes: $1000 Prize Fund (based on 80 paid paid entries):
Open:    1st -- $120, 2nd -- $90, 3rd -- $60, 1st U2200: $30
Class A: 1st -- $90, 2nd -- $60, 3rd -- $45
Class B: 1st -- $60, 2nd -- $45, 3rd -- $30
Class C: 1st -- $60, 2nd -- $45, 3rd -- $30
Class D: 1st -- $60, 2nd -- $45, 3rd -- $30
U1200:   1st -- $40, 2nd -- $30, 3rd -- $15, 1st U800: $15

All players earn Rising Star Grand Prix points. See  Rising Star Grand Prix Policy  for details.
Schedule: Round times: Rd 1: 9:00 am, Rd 2: 11:10 am, Rd 3: 1:35 pm, Rd 4: 3:45 pm

Entry Fees: $30 on or before Fri, Feb 13; $35 on or before Wed, Feb 18, $40 on or before Fri, Feb 20, $45 on-site Sat, Feb 21
Free entry for any GM/WGM/IM/WIM/FM/WFM
No prize deduction for FIDE-titled players if entered on or before Fri, Feb 13, 2026
$30 deducted from FIDE-titled players' prize winnings if entered after Fri, Feb 13, 2026
Re-entry: Players may re-enter after 1st or 2nd round with half-point byes for previous rounds.
Re-entry fees: $5 after round 1, $10 after round 2.
Online Registration: Rising Star Febuary Grand Prix Registration
Online registration is available until 11:59 pm MST Fri, Feb 20th
On-site registration is available until 8:30 am on Sat, Feb 21 before round 1.

Phoenix Saturday Action

Phoenix Chess Academy

Saturday, February 21, 2026

Event Overview

4 round Swiss. Time control: Game in 25 minutes with 5 sec delay. Boards, sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided.
Registration: Go to www.phoenixchessacademy.com. USCF membership is required. New or renewing USCF members are welcome. Highest rating will be used for Swiss pairings and prize purposes.
Sections: Open, Under 1700 & Under 1200 (No playing up allowed). Sections will be combined in case a section has less than 4 players registered.
Schedule: Round 1- 9:00 AM, Round 2- 10:05 AM, Round 3- 11:10 AM, Round 4- 12:15 PM. Awards Ceremony will start right after last game is over. Half point Byes are available in all 4 rounds and (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. Requesting a zero-point bye late in the tournament is considered the same as withdrawing.
Entry Fee: $25.00 by 02/18; $30 by 02/20; $35 same day. Full refund will be issued to players who withdraw at least an hour before the first round. In cases where a registered player does not show up for the tournament without prior notice, they will not be eligible for a refund.
Prizes: Trophies for top three in each section.
A player will automatically forfeit the game if going in the bathroom with a cellphone.

Katy After School Chess Camp-Houston International Table Tennis

monthly on Sunday, but only the last instance of this set, starting from Sunday, February 22, 2026, forever

Event Overview

Katy Kids Chess Monthly Rated Chess Competition
Chinese New Year Competition
Hosted by Katy Kids Chess & Houston International Table Tennis

Event Overview
Katy Kids Chess and Houston International Table Tennis are excited to invite young chess enthusiasts and their families to our upcoming Kids Monthly Rated Chess Competition in Katy Texas! This event is designed to offer a fun, competitive, and supportive environment for players to improve their skills, meet new friends, and enjoy the game of chess.

Event Details
• Date: [2.22.26]
• Time: [11am] – [4pm]
• Location: [923 S Mason Rd, Katy, TX 77450] Eligibility
• Open to all chess players with an ELO rating of 1200 and below
• Active USCF membership is required to participate Competition Format
• 5 rounds of play • Each round uses a 15-minute time control per player (G/15)
• Swiss-system pairing (no elimination – everyone plays all rounds) Entry Fee and Prizes • Entry Fee: [$20] per participant
• Prizes: Trophies for top finishers and medals for all participants

Registration
1. Visit our registration website: [ Register Here ]
2. Fill out the online registration form
3. Submit your entry fee payment online
4. Be sure your USCF membership is current before the event

Note: Bring your own board and clock if you have it.
Link to sign up for USCF.

Dr. David Ostfeld Memorial ICA Championships

Community Church of Glen Rock Education Building

Sunday, February 22, 2026

Event Overview

Rounds:  The event is four rounds (ie; win or lose, all players play four games each).  Pairings are determined Swiss-style.

Time control:  G30;d5 for all sections

Byes:  Up to two half-point byes are available per player.  They must be requested prior to the start of round one.  Late entrants will receive a half-point bye for round 1.

Schedule:  First round starts at 2pm for all sections. Tournament should finish no later than 7pm.

Entry fee:  $40 (until February 15), $50 after.

Registration link :  https://ica.jumbula.com/ICATournaments2026/DrDavidOstfeldMemorialICAChampionshipsFebruary22
Equipment:  Boards, sets, and clocks are provided for all sections.
For parents:  ICA kindly reminds parents this is a large event that does not include free babysitting.  Event staff will supervise children during games in priogress, but cannot manage children between games.  The overwhelming majority of children are well behaved, but there are an occasional few who become bored and engage in dangerous or destructive behavior. Click the following URL for more information on our tournament rules: https://icanj.net/files/2025/03/25/tournament_rules.pdf
Section 1 -- (K-2, unrated games)
Restricted to unrated players; K through 2nd grade.
Round 1 starts at 2:00 PM (tournament will end at approximately 5:00PM)
All players with 2.5 or more points will receive a trophy.  All players with 2 or more points will receive a medal. Trophies also awarded to the top three finishers.
No USCF membership required.  This section is not rated.

Section 2 -- (K-6, unrated games)
Restricted to unrated players; K through 6th grade.
Round 1 starts at 2:00 PM (tournament will end at approximately 6:00 PM)
All players with 2.5 or more points will receive a trophy.  Trophies are also awarded to the top three finishers.
No USCF membership required.  This section is not rated.
Section 3 -- (K-12, under 800, rated games)
Restricted to players rated below 800; K through 8th grade.
Rounds: 2:00PM, 3:15PM, 4:30PM, 5:45PM
All players with 2.5 or more points will receive a trophy.  Trophies are also awarded to the top three finishers.
Section 4 -- (K-12, under 1200, rated games)
Restricted to players rated below 1200; K through 8th grade.
Rounds: 2:00PM, 3:15PM, 4:30PM, 5:45PM
All players with 2.5 or more points will receive a trophy.  Trophies are also awarded to the top three finishers.

Glen Rock , NJ 07452

United States

Chess Zone

Sunday, February 22, 2026

Event Overview

Four Rounds, Swiss System, USCF rated
SECTIONS:
1300+: Open to scholastic players rated 1300 and up.
U1300: Open to scholastic players rated between 600 and 1299.
U600: Open to scholastic players under 600 and unrated.
PRIZES: Trophies to 1st-3rd place in each section. Medals to all finish with 50% or greater that don't win a trophy.
Time Control: G/25; d5; USCF dual rated (regular and quick).
Entry Fee:
Members: $38 if pre-registered by 2/18; $43 by 2/22; $48 on-site.
Non-Members: $45 if pre-registered by 2/18; $50 by 2/22; $55 on-site.
The field is limited to the first 40 registrants.
Schedule: All players, including pre-registrants, please check in by 9:45 am.
Rounds: 10:00 am, 11:30 am, 12:45 pm, 2:00 pm
1/2-Pt. Byes: Available, limit two. Must request 1/2-point byes before round 1 begins. 0-point byes available at any time for any round.
Unrated players must obtain a USCF membership (from https://uschess.org). Please arrive early (by 9:30 AM) if you need assistance on-site. US Chess Live rating will be used sections, pairings and prizes. Players may play up if rating within 100 points of the section requirement. Sections may be merged at TD discretion. Children may be dropped off at Chess Zone; please return by 2:15 PM to pick-up

Casselberry February Quick

Casselberry Recreation Center

Sunday, February 22, 2026

Event Overview

Casselberry February Quick
Time Control: G/15;d3 • 5 Rd Swiss • USCF Quick Rated
Date: Sunday, February 22nd
Location: Casselberry Recreation Center
200 N. Triplet Lake Dr.
Casselberry, FL 32707
Doors Open: 12:45p
Registration Closes: 1:15p
Round 1: 1:30p, Round 2: 2:15p, Round 3: 3:00p, Round 4: 4:00p, Round 5: 4:45p, with awards to follow. Anticipated completion: 5:30p
Register Online at ChessRoster.com
Sections:
• Open Rated - Open to all Adults and to Scholastic players 1000 rated or higher
• Scholastic U1200 Rated: Grades K-12 and U1200 or unrated
• Scholastic U600 Rated: Grades K-12 and U600 or unrated in grades K-5
• Casual/Non-Rated - This section is not USCF rated and does not require USCF membership.
Entry Fees with online registration:
• Open Rated: $30
• Scholastic Rated: $20
• Scholastic U600 Rated: $20
• Casual/Non-Rated: $15
- The entry fees will be $10 more for in person registration for Rated sections and $5 more for Non-Rated.
- NOTE: Scholastic sections will be combined if there are fewer than 6 players in either section. Sections may be split into additional sections by rating at the tournament director’s discretion if needed based on attendance and range of participant ratings.

Prizes:
• Open Rated section: A minimum of 60% of Open Rated section entry fees will be returned as cash prizes to top performers including a Best U1600 prize if a separate U1600 section is not split out.
• Scholastic: Trophies and/or Medals will be awarded to top performers in scholastic sections.
• Casual/Non-Rated: Trophies and/or Medals will be awarded to top performers in the Casual/Non-Rated section.
• These tie break systems will be used for non-monetary prize determination if needed: Modified Median, Solkoff, Cumulative, Cumulative opponent's score, Coin Flip. Read more about these tie break systems on wikipedia .

Additional Information: (Please Read)
• Attendance will be limited to 60 total players so please register early to guarantee a spot.
• One ½ point bye is allowed. It must be requested prior to round 2 being paired and cannot be changed.
• All players in rated sections must have a valid, active USCF membership to play. You can obtain or renew USCF membership with registration online, at the door, or directly from the USCF at uschess.org.
• Scholastic section entrants must be in grades K - 12 and rated under 1200 USCF or be unrated yet. Over 1200 rated students should register for the Open Rated section. Students rated between 1000 and 1200 may choose either Scholastic or Open. Unrated students in grades K-5 may enter the Scholastic U600 section.
• The current Month’s USCF Rating Supplement will be used for pairings and prizes. The highest of blitz, quick, or regular rating may be used for pairing and prizes at the tournament director's discretion.
• Refunds will be charged a $5 processing fee. No-shows without notification may forfeit their entry fee.
• Chess sets and clocks will be provided.

Register Online at ChessRoster.com
Call, text, or email with questions:
Orlando Regional Chess Alliance, Inc.
(407) 904-4477

https://www.orcachess.com

2026 New Jersey Elementary and Junior High School Championships

Brookdale Community College - Student Life Center

Sunday, February 22, 2026

Event Overview

2026 New Jersey Elementary and Junior High School Championships
A scholastic championship event open to all players from grades K-9 for players both from and beyond New Jersey.
Capacity : This tournament is limited to approximately 500 players.  We’ve reached it in two out of the last three years, and expect to do so again in 2026.  Registration will close when it fills.
Date : Sunday, February 22, 2026
Arrival : Suggested arrival time is  9:15 AM
Rounds : 10 AM, Noon, 1:30 PM, 3:00 PM, and 4:30 PM.  Awards ceremony to follow after the final round.
Format : 5 round Swiss, G/25;d5
Location : Brookdale Community College, Student Life Center near parking lots 6 and 7.  Approximately one mile from Parkway exit 109A.  By Train: North Jersey Coast Line to Red Bank station, 4 miles away.
Sections : K-2, 3-5, and 6-9.  Players wishing a challenge may select a higher section during registration; this cannot be changed on the day of the event.
Equipment :  Only boards and sets are provided; players should bring their own clocks.
Individual Prizes : The top 15 players in each section will receive a trophy.
Team Prizes : The top 5 teams in each section will receive a trophy.
Medals : Every player at the tournament will receive a commemorative medal.
Teams : A team consists of any number of students who attend the same elementary, middle, or high school. (Other organizations, such as chess academies, do not count for this purpose.) In the K-2 section, the sum of the three best scores on a team will be the team’s score. In the 3-5 and 6-9 sections, the sum of the four best scores on a team will be the team’s score.
Byes : One half-point bye may be requested for rounds 1-4. It must be requested in writing at least one hour before scheduled round start.
Entry fee : $45 by January 9.  $50 between January 10 and February 10.  $60 after.
Registration : Online:  https://pci.jotform.com/form/252719080633154
Registration closes at 8pm February 21, or when we reach capacity.  No on-site registration.
Chief Tournament Director : Stephen Lorimor or Alessandro de March-Blumstein

TCA Region V Scholastic 2026 (K1/Primary)

The Houston Chess Studio

Sunday, February 22, 2026

Event Overview

TCA Region V Scholastic 2026 (K1/Primary)
Date & Location
Date:  February 22, 2026
Location:  The Houston Chess Studio 250 Patton St. Suite I Houston, TX 77079

Contact Info
Organizer:  Edgar Acosta
Email:   [email protected]
Phone:  (281) 844 4139

Pricing

- Early Registration: $32, ends on January 31, 2026

- Regular Registration: $37, between February 1 - 15, 2026

- Late Registration: $40, between February 16 - 20, 2026

- Active USCF membership is required by February 15, 2026.
- Visit  new.uschess.org/join-us-chess  starting at $24 to join USCF or renew your membership!

- Visit  chess.jliptrap.us/hgroup.htm  for $13 discount Scholastic memberships and renewals!

- TCA Tournament membership is included in the tournament entry fee.
- Visit  texaschess.org/memberships  to join TCA or renew your membership!

Pricing is included in the registration form automatically.

Eligibility
Participants must live or attend school in one of these counties:

- Austin, Brazoria, Brazos, Chambers, Fort Bend, Galveston, Grimes

- Hardin, Harris, Houston, Jasper, Leon, Liberty, Madison

- Matagorda, Montgomery, Newton, Orange, Polk, Robertson

- San Jacinto, Trinity, Tyler, Walker, Waller, Wharton

The max number of registrations for this tournament is 74. Text Edgar Acosta to join a waiting list

Sections

- Primary Open: Any K-3 student may enter this section.

- Kinder-1st Open: Only Kindergarten and 1st Graders may enter this section, regardless of rating.

- Note:  Sections may be combined in case of low registrations.

Definitions:

- High School  - Grades 9-12; in some districts 10-12, if Junior High is 7-9.

- Middle School  - Grades 6 to 8 or 9 depending on how the school district divides them.

- Elementary  - K-6 if 6th grade is in the Elementary building, K-5 if 6 is in Middle School.
- A 5th-6th campus has been ruled Elementary, a 6th-only campus as Middle School.

- Primary  - K-3. Note that a first grader could enter K-1 or K-3 or K-5.

- K-8 and K-12 schools and Home School Associations are divided K-5, 6-8, and 9-12.

- Students not assigned a grade in school will be assigned a grade at the tournament based on their age as of September 1 of that school year as follows: six years old is assigned first grade, seven years old is assigned second grade, and so on through grade twelve.

Note:  Sections are based on USCF January 2026 ratings. "Current" ratings may be used to pair unrated players but will  not  determine section placement. Accelerate Pairings will be used at the discretion of the TD the day of the tournament.

Tournament Format

- Rounds:  Swiss 5 Rounds, Game in 25 with a 5-second delay (G/25 d/5).

- Membership:  USCF and TCA memberships required.

- Rules:  USCF rules apply.

- Open sections  require notation  and clocks (if available).
- Players who opt to not take notation will have their time start at 20 minutes instead of 25.

- Reserved sections are strongly encouraged to use notation and clocks.

- Touch-move / Touch-take:  Applies to all sections. Younger players, especially in Kinder-1st Open, will be encouraged to keep these rules with gentle reminders as needed.

- Equipment:  Plan on bringing your own chess set and clock if you have one, money for lunch, and a good attitude!
- Every player needs to bring their clocks!

- Please make sure your clocks are labeled with the player's name and USCF ID.

- Chess sets for the whole tournament  will  be provided!

Schedule

- No At-Site Registration. All registrations must be submitted online at  before 11:59pm on February 20, 2026.

- Please arrive between 8:15 and 8:45 to check in and get ready to play.

- Round 1:  Starts at 9:00 AM SHARP; subsequent rounds will start ASAP. No elimination.

- Players may request a single 1/2 point Bye missed, 0 point Bye for any subsequent Byes. Any Byes need to be requested by Friday February 20th, 2026 at 7pm.

- Lunch break after Round 3, estimating 12pm-1pm.

Teams
Teams consist of two or more (2+) players in the same section from the same school/association.

- Team members must attend the  same school campus  full-time or belong to the  same Home School Association .

- Sections are  not combined  for teams.

- Team scores will be calculated by summing the top four (4) individual scores from each team.

Awards

- Trophies:  Top 5 individuals in each section and Top 4 teams in each section.

- 1st Place Finishers qualify for a spot in the State Regional Invitational April 18-19th .

- Alternate awards (likely medals) to players who score 3 or more points but do not win a trophy.

- Tie Breaks:  Solkoff (sum of opponents' scores), Modified Median (dropping the lowest opponent's score), Cumulative of Opposition, then Cumulative (USCF Standard)

We look forward to seeing you at The Houston Chess Studio  on  February 22, 2026  for a day of competitive and fun scholastic chess!

MSJE 2026 Jingzhe Monday Night Marathon

MSJE MUR

Monday, February 23, 2026
- Monday, March 23, 2026

Event Overview

MSJE 2026 Jingzhe Monday Night Marathon is a USCF-rated tournament for all members of MSJE Chess community.
Jingzhe 惊蛰, also known as Awakening of Insects, is the 3rd of the 24 solar terms in the Chinese lunar calendar.

Date:  Monday, Feb 23, 2026  - Monday, Mar 23, 2026
Rating:  USCF Dual-Rated
Eligibility : The tournament is open to MSJE students, parents, and alumni. Players must have current US Chess Federation membership. Expiration date of their US Chess membership must be later than the last day of the tournament.
Capacity : 50
Tournament Format : Swiss System
Total Rounds : 4
Time Control : G/25;+5 (game in 25 minutes with a 5-second increment with each move. This means you get 25 minutes, your opponent gets 25 minutes, and with each move players get 5 seconds added to their clock.)
Round Times:   2/23 6:40pm, 3/2 6:40pm, 3/9 6:40pm,  3/23 6:40pm
Sections:  400+, Under 400
US Chess rating will be used for section determination and pairings.  Pairings are based on the  February 2026 regular supplemental regular US Chess rating.

MSJE Chess Team reserves the right to update any details of this event (including but not limited to sections, time control, round times, etc.) as we get closer to the event date to ensure an excellent tournament experience for players.

Parental Guidelines:

- Non-playing parents are kindly asked to drop off and pick up their children. Only players and tournament staffs are allowed to remain inside MUR while games are in progress. Thank you for your understanding.

Tournament Rules:

- All US Chess tournament rules apply.

- The tournament director's decisions are final.

- Notation is required, per MSJE Chess Head Coach's policy.

Bye Request:

- Maximum two half-point byes are available upon request. Please submit the request of half-point bye by 7pm Sunday before the Monday round.

Equipment:

- Chess sets will be provided.

- Please bring own notation sheets and pencils.

Go Mustangs!

Speedy Quads 64

J. Gilligan's Bar and Grill

Monday, February 23, 2026

Event Overview

Speedy - because the time control is G/5;d0 (each player gets 5 minutes to make all their moves.)
Quads - because we divide the players in groups of four based on ratings or skill level.
Players play two games against each of the three other players in their quad.
We hold a Speedy Quads tournament every fourth Monday each month. Speedy Quads has a FREE entry (but we do accept donations to cover the rating fees). There are no prizes. The games are blitz-rated and do not affect regular or quick ratings.
Time Control is G/5;d0; and we play double-round quads.
Register on site only - please arrive before 7:30pm. US Chess members will play rated quads. Non-members will play in an unrated small Swiss blitz tournament.

Academy Chess Challenge 2026-02

St.Giles Educational Center

Tuesday, February 24, 2026

Event Overview

Academy of Intellectual
Games
www.AoIGs.com
Kings & Queens Chess Club
AoIG 2026 Chess Challenge
USCF  dual  rated,   OPEN  to  players  of ALL ages and chess skills !
AoIG reserve the right to separate players into 3 sections : 12+ years old; 8 to 11,  7 and younger
3 hours of educational and entertainment experience:  all-in-one

Tuesday,   February 24th ,  2026 : from 5:30 to 8:30 p.m.
3025 Walters Ave , Northbrook, IL 60062
5:15 p.m. -  Doors will open
5:30 p.m. -  Chess Q&A: ask Chess Master a question
6:00 p.m. -  1st round will start, sharp!
4 rounds Swiss - time control G15 + d15

USCF membership will be required : membership available on site.
Field is limited  (Check the registration list https://www.aoigs.com/chess-tournaments/ before leaving home, if your intention is to register on site)

TEAMS:  Any 2 or 3 players can form a team at the time of REGISTRATION via email. Teammates will NOT be paired to play each other, but combined USCF rating for BEST 2 players on a team could not be greater than 2000 to win trophies.
On a 3-player team, 2 best scores are counted. Bring in your relative, friend, or neighbor and increase your chances to win a trophy!
Prizes, CHESS merchandise and TROPHIES  for everybody in a WINNING CIRCLE:      2.5+ points out of 4. Extra Trophies for top three TEAMs . Prizes will be given for the contribution to the Q&A session, and the best 1st board performance.
EXTRA Money Prizes: $100(50-30-20) to top three  – in the event of 30+ players;
TOTAL projected tournament’s Prize Pool is over $500
Electronically $35.02 before Feb 14th  , after  $40.02 ($45 at the door) - 100% refund                 if canceled by phone before 9:00 a.m. on a tournament day.
Registration: e-mail player’s First and Last name, phone number, USCF ID (if a member) and a B-day for a players NOT playing in OPEN session to  Click here to show mail address    (you can e-mail your chess question for a discussion, as well; if selected, player will win an indoor prize) and then send money via Zelle®  to
Academy of IG ; E-mail:  Click here to show mail address
(set Academy of IG as your friend, so, if necessary, we can instantly refund your money without any fees,)

For any inquiries please call AoIG educational director  Serge  847-778-5259   or your coaches:
Tamara  847-867-0116                        Mila  847-207-2819                         Leonid   847-845-4525.

2026 NC K-12 Championship

State Championship Event

Hilton Charlotte University Place

Friday, February 27, 2026
- Sunday, March 1, 2026

Event Overview

https://www.charlottechesscenter.org/events/nck12
OVERVIEW
The 2026 NC K-12 Championship is the official North Carolina state scholastic championship, and is the qualifier for several US Chess National Invitationals.  It will award over 150 trophies.

There is a registration cap of 500 players - registration will close once capacity is reached.

WHEN
February 27 - March 1, 2026

Friday, February 27 : Blitz tournament and suggested arrival
Saturday, February 28 : K-1 Section and Bughouse
Saturday, February 28 – Sunday, March 1 : K-12, K-8, K-5, K-3 Sections

WHERE
Hilton Charlotte University Place
8629 JM Keynes Drive
Charlotte, NC 28262
Free Internet, Free Parking
​

​ HOTEL BOOKING
$129/Night - Free Internet, Parking
Booking Link Coming Soon

REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS

- Only scholastic players (K-12) who live or attend school in North Carolina are permitted to play.

- No unrated players in K-3 or higher sections.
- Except for the K-1 section, all players must have a US Chess Over-the-Board Regular Rating based on at least 4 rated games. No exceptions.

- Quick, blitz, and online ratings are not accepted. Players must have OTB regular USCF ratings from at least 4 rated games.

- Unrated players in K-3 or above may register early, but must complete the 4 game requirement before the tournament, or they will be removed without a refund.

- US Chess membership is required for all players.  Membership renewal is not handled by the organizers and must be done before the tournament.

- Registration is online only – coming soon.  No mailed or on-site entries.

- Registration cap – 500 players.
- Registration will close when we are full.

- If we are not full, registration will close at 6:30pm on Friday, February 27.

- Organizers reserve the right to accept limited entries past 500 depending on specific space constraints.

- Side event registration:
- Blitz – online or on-site by 6:30pm Friday.

- Bughouse – on-site only by 6:30pm Saturday.

- Use this link  to change sections or other information for a player you have already registered.

- We have a strict no parent/spectator policy during play. See the full policy below. By registering for this event, you acknowledge that parents and coaches will not be able to see their children while they are playing until they are finished with their game.

SECTIONS AND TIME CONTROLS
All sections are 2 days (Sat/Sun) except for K-1 (Saturday only)

K-12 Championship : 5 rounds. Rounds 1-3: G/60, inc/5. Rounds 4-5: G/75, inc/5.

K-12 Under 1500 : 5 rounds. Rounds 1-3: G/60, inc/5. Rounds 4-5: G/75, inc/5.

K-8 Championship : 5 rounds. Rounds 1-3: G/60, inc/5. Rounds 4-5: G/75, inc/5.

K-8 Under 1200 : 5 rounds. Rounds 1-3: G/60, inc/5. Rounds 4-5: G/75, inc/5.

K-5 Championship : 6 rounds. G/45, inc/5.

K-5 Under 900 : 6 rounds, G/45, inc/5.

K-3 Championship : 6 rounds, G/45, inc/5.

K-3 Under 600 : 6 rounds, G/45, inc/5.

K-1 : Saturday only, 6 rounds. G/25, inc/5.

Blitz : Friday night. K-12 and K-5 Sections – 4 double rounds (8 games). G/5, inc/0.

Bughouse : Saturday night. K-12 and K-5 Sections - 5 double rounds (10 games). G/3, inc/0.

SCHEDULE

K-12 Champ, K-12 U1500, K-8 Champ, K-8 U1200

- Saturday Round Start Times: 10:00am, 1:00pm, 4:00pm

- Sunday Round Start Times: 9:30am, 1:00pm

- Awards Ceremony: Sunday 4:00pm

K-5 Champ, K-5 U900, K-3 Champ, K-3 U600

- Saturday Round Start Times: 9:30am, 12:00pm, 2:30pm

- Sunday Round Start Times: 9:00am, 11:30am, 2:00pm

- Awards Ceremony: Sunday 4:00pm

K-1 (Saturday only)

- Saturday Round Start Times: 10:30am, 11:30am, 1:00pm, 2:00pm, 3:00pm, 4:00pm

- K-1 Awards Ceremony: Saturday 5:00pm

Blitz: Friday 7:00-8:30pm, blitz awards 8:45pm.

Bughouse: Saturday 7:00-8:30pm, bughouse awards 8:45pm.
​

AWARDS

K-12 Championship
Trophies to top 10 players
Trophies to top 3 teams
1st Place qualifies to Denker High School National Invitational (see regulations below)

K-12 Under 1500
Trophies to top 10 players
Trophies to top 3 teams
​
K-8 Championship
Trophies to top 10 players
Trophies to top 3 teams
1st Place qualifies to Barber Middle School National Invitational (see regulations below)

K-8 Under 1200
Trophies to top 10 players
Trophies to top 3 teams

K-5 Championship
Trophies to top 15 players
Trophies to top 3 teams
1st Place qualifies to Rockefeller K-5 National Invitational (see regulations below)

K-5 Under 900
Trophies to top 15 players
Trophies to top 3 teams

K-3 Championship
Trophies to top 10 players
Trophies to top 3 teams
1st Place qualifies to Ashley K-3 National Invitational (see regulations below)

K-3 Under 600
Trophies to top 10 players
Trophies to top 3 teams

K-1
Trophies to top 10 players
Medals to all players
Trophies to top 3 teams

Blitz
Trophies to top 5 players in each section (K-12, K-5)
Trophies to top 2 teams in each section

Bughouse
Trophies to top 5 teams (2 trophies per team) in both sections (K-12, K-5)

​All trophies must be claimed on-site. No mailed awards.

ENTRY FEES

NC K-12 Main Event

- $70 online by January 10

- $89 online by February 20

- $110 online after February 20

- $30 K-1 to K-3 re-entry: on-site only by Saturday 7:30pm.

Side Events

- Blitz: $30 online by February 20, $40 online after February 20, $50 on-site. All blitz registration closes Friday 6:30pm.

- Bughouse : $40 per team, on-site registration only.  Bughouse registration closes Saturday 6:30pm.

MSJE Chess Championship 2026

MSJE multi-use room

Friday, February 27, 2026
- Friday, March 6, 2026

Event Overview

Our annual MSJE Chess Championship is a USCF-rated event for all members of MSJE Chess Program.
Tournament Format : Swiss System
Total Rounds : 4
Time Control : G/25;d5 (This means you get 25 minutes, your opponent gets 25 minutes, and with 5-second delay before clock starts counting down on each move)
Eligibility : Players must have current US Chess Federation membership. Expiration date of their US Chess membership must be later than the last day of the tournament.
Capacity : 80
Round Times:

- 1st round at 3pm on Friday 02/27/2026, and 2nd round begins after 1st round finishes.

- 3rd round at 3pm on Friday 03/06/2026, and 4th round begins after 3rd round finishes.

Sections:  Open, U600, U300, Unrated
We may update event details, like sections and round times, as the tournament date approaches to ensure the best possible experience for all players.
Parental Guidelines:
Parents are kindly asked to drop off and pick up their children. Only players and tournament staff are allowed to remain inside MUR while games are in progress. Thank you for your understanding.
Tournament Rules:

- All US Chess tournament rules apply.

- The tournament director's decisions are final.

- Notation is required for players in Open section and U600 section, per MSJE Chess Head Coach's policy.

Bye Request:

- maximum two half-point byes are available upon request.

- Please request half-point byes for 1st round and 2nd round by 10PM Thursday 02/26/2026.

- Please request half-point byes for 3rd round and 4th round by 10PM Thursday 03/05/2026.

Entry Fee:  none
Equipment:

- Chess sets will be provided.

- Please bring your own notation sheets and pencils.

- Please bring your own clock if you can.

Go Mustangs!  We look forward to seeing you at the tournament!

Fremont , CA 94539

10th annual George Washington Open

Grand Prix, Enhanced Grand Prix, Junior Grand Prix

Washington Dulles Marriott Hotel

Friday, February 27, 2026
- Sunday, March 1, 2026

Event Overview

US Chess Junior Grand Prix
FEB 27 – MAR 1 OR FEB 28 – MAR 1, 2026  VIRGINIA
US CHESS GRAND PRIX POINTS: 120 (enhanced)
10th annual George Washington Open
5-SS, 40/80, SD/30; d30 (2-day option, rounds 1-2 G/60 d10). Washington Dulles Marriott Hotel, 45020 Aviation Dr, Dulles, VA 20166.  Free parking, free shuttle to airport and Metro subway. $17,000 guaranteed prizes. In 5 sections. Major: Open to 1900/above (see peakrating.us). $2000-1000-600-400, clear/tiebreak win $100 bonus, top USCF Under 2300 $600-300. FIDE. Under 2100: $1300-700-400-200, top U1900 (no unr) $600-300. FIDE. Under 1800:  $1200-600-300-200, top U1600 (no unr) $500-250. Under 1500:  $1000-500-300-150, top U1300 (no unr) $400-200. Under 1200: $700-400-300-200, top U1000 (no unr) $200-100. Mixed Doubles Bonus Prizes: Best male+female 2-player combined team score among all sections: $500-300-200. Team must average under 2200; may play different sections and schedules; register (no extra fee) by 2 pm Sat. Biggest Upset Bonus Prize :  Free entry to 2026 World Open in DC to biggest individual upset among all rounds and sections (upset prize does not include any additional entry fee surcharges, based on players’ ratings, for players who elect to play up in World Open, Open Section but who are eligible for a lower section). Unrated prize limits: U1200 $100, U1500 $200, U1800 $400. Cannot play below USCF Online Regular rating minus 100 points. Top 4 sections EF:  $123 at chessaction.com by 2/24, $140 later online or at site (no checks, credit cards OK) until 1 hour before round 1. GMs, IMs & WGMs in Major: $100 from prize. Under 1200 Section EF:  all $20 less than top 4 sections. Re-entry $60, no Major to Major. March official ratings  used; unofficial USCF   ratings or USCF Online Regular Ratings usually used if otherwise unrated. Special 1-year USCF dues with magazine if paid online with entry: see chessevents.us.   3-Day Schedule: Reg. to Fri 6 pm. Rounds: Fri 7, Sat 11 & 5, Sun 10 & 3:30. 2-Day Schedule: Reg. to Sat 10 am. Rounds Sat 11, 2 & 5, Sun 10 & 3:30. Half point byes available all rounds, limit 2 byes, must commit before round 2. Prizes  not claimed at site usually paid through PayPal, may take a couple of weeks. HR: $133-133, use link at chessevents.us (or call 703-471-9500, mention Chess Rate); reserve by 2/5/26 or rate may increase. Enter online: chessaction.com. No mail entries. Refunds,  $15 service charge. Questions : chesstour.com, [email protected] . Entries posted at chessaction.com (click “entry list” after entering).  Blitz tournament  Sat. 9:30 pm, enter at site Sat. by 9:10 pm.

Dulles , VA 20166

United States

State Championship Event

Jackson Prep

Saturday, February 28, 2026

Event Overview

A United States Chess National Qualifying Event for the 2026 Ruth Haring National Girls Tournament of Champions
Check In:  No later than 8:30 AM
Mississippi Residents Only – The Mississippi Girls State Chess Championship is an officially rated US Chess tournament.  US Chess membership is required and student membership is available at uschess.org.
Schedule:  4 Rounds no elimination.  All rounds will be played 45 minutes for each player with 15 seconds added to the player’s clock for each move completed.
Saturday:  9:00 AM, 11:15 AM, 2:00 PM, 4:00 PM
The Swiss System tournament will consist of three sections, Open, Under 800, and Under 400. All players are eligible to play in the Open section. Players with US Chess Federation ratings below 800 and 400 can play in the other sections. The winner of the Open section will qualify for the Haring tournament.  If the first place finisher is not able to play in these tournament(s), the second place finisher (alternate) will be eligible for the tournament(s).
Entry Fee: $25 before midnight February 22, $35 after
Payment accepted on site (Cash or Check) before Check In.
Awards Ceremony to follow last round or tiebreaks.  Plaques or trophies will be given for the top 3 finishers.
One half-point bye only is available and must be requested before the start of the tournament.

ECE #120 – PA State Scholastic Warm-Up

Tri – Bridges Chess Club

Saturday, February 28, 2026

Event Overview

$100 Open Prize – 4 Round G40, d5
G40, d5 is the longest we can easily make and still complete in about 5 to 6 hours.
We are doing a longer time control to help people get ready for the State Championships in Harrkbur the following weekend.
The 1st round will start at 12 and the other rounds – roughly 12, 1:30, 3, and 4:30 (will be paired as soon as possible.)
The sections are Open, Under 1100, Under 800, and Under 500 (sections are chosen to copy some of the sections at the state championship the following weekend.)  The Open has 3 trophy prizes and a $100 for first place.  The other sections will have at least three trophy prizes.  Hope to see everyone there!

6th Oskaloosa Open

Oskaloosa City Hall

Saturday, February 28, 2026

Event Overview

I hear question #1 already: "Wait. Timeout. Where IS this so-called Oskaloosa, anyway?"
I'm glad you asked!
It's right where you want it to be!!
20 minutes from Lawrence. 30 minutes from Topeka. 1 hour from St. Joseph, MO or Overland Park. It's even just 90 minutes from Manhattan!
So you all can totally play in this event without having to get up too early or drive home too late.  See you there!
--------------------
Details and registration:  https://www.kingregistration.com/event/Osk6
Format:   4-SS (no eliminations).  Accelerated Pairings used if appropriate.

Time Control:   G/45; +15.
Registration:   8:30 - 9:15.
Rounds: 9:30 - 12:00 - 2:15 - 4:30.
Players who register in advance do not need to arrive early.
One 1/2-point bye may be requested at any time up to the start of round two.
-------------------
All players will compete in the same section, however:

All players aged 14 and below have the option of registering as amateurs if they wish to do so.
All players without ratings have the option of registering as amateurs if they wish to do so.
Amateurs will not be eligible for cash prizes, but there will be a trophy presented to the top-scoring amateur.
All games will be rated by the United States Chess Federation. (Regular and Quick)
All players must be members of the United States Chess Federation.
Membership in the USCF may be purchased at the event.
-------------------
EARLY BIRD PRO SPECIAL: Open: $30 by 12:00A on 2/14/26
Pro Entry Fee: $35 in advance after Early Bird cut-off Date or $40 at the door.
Amateur Entry Fee: $10 in advance or $15 at the door.

$500 Prize Fund (b/25 Pro entries, 50% guaranteed):
Overall:     $200 - 100.
U1600:      $100 - 50
U1200:       $50
--------------------
Please bring sets, boards, and chess clocks if you have them. Very few will be available as loaners.
and again:
Please bring sets, boards, and chess clocks if you have them. Very few will be available as loaners.
--------------------
THINGS TO KNOW:

Food:  There is pizza next door and a truly excellent 5-star coffee shop which I will totally vouch for about a 5 minute walk away.
There's also a Mexican Restaurant, a chicken place, and a Casey's within a short drive.
No chain restaurants in the area, though:  shop local or pack a lunch--we have a refrigerator to keep food and drinks in, and a microwave to cook it.

Free Parking: Ample, both in lot and on street.
--------------------
Director will be available to play an optional rated game against the player who receives a bye during any round where there is an odd number of players.
Director will not paired normally, and will not be eligible for any cash prizes.
Contact [email protected] or (570)762-5093 with any questions

Address: 212 W. Washington Street

Oskaloosa , KS 66066

United States

Grand Prix Points:
Prize Fund: 500

Handicap Accessible: No
Residency Restriction: No
Online Event: No

2026 Michigan High School & Junior High Team Championships

State Championship Event

Oakland Center

Saturday, February 28, 2026

Event Overview

Oakland Center
312 Meadow Brook Rd
Rochester, MI, 48309, United States
Directions:
https://www.oakland.edu/oc/

Directions to the Oakland Center
The Oakland Center is located in the heart of Oakland University’s main campus.
Oakland University is located in southeastern Michigan between Flint and Detroit. The 1,441-acre campus actually extends into two cities — Auburn Hills and Rochester Hills, between Adams Road and Squirrel Road, just south of Walton Boulevard. Take I-75 to exit 79 and go east on University Drive to the main entrance of campus. Or, take M-59 to the Squirrel Road exit and go north to the main entrance of campus at the corner of University Drive.

From OU’s Main Entrance
To get to the Oakland Center from the main entrance of campus, drive around the circle drive past the first entrance to Meadow Brook Road until you get to the second entrance to Meadow Brook Road and turn right. The Oakland Center is located on the right side of the road between North and South Foundation Halls. The best place to park is in Parking Lot 1 or 2.
Format:
Printable Flyer: Printable Flyer: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RMMuXsTyjjbycyCSt_cZ0n-fR5R9hysW/view?usp=sharing

High School: 4-SS, 2 Sections - High School Championship: HS Teams (Gr 9-12), High School Reserve: HS Teams (Gr 9-12) U1000 Avg Team Rating
Junior High (No HS 9th Grade Teams per MCA Rules): 5-SS, 2 Sections - Junior High Championship: K-9, Junior High Reserve: K-9 U600 Avg Team Rating
Average Team Rating Calculator: https://www.michess.org/team-rating-calculator

Michigan Chess Association and USCF Memberships Required for ALL Players

Event Policies:
MCA Scholastic Code of Conduct & Building Policies will be provided via a separate flyer online and via hard copy during the event. By registering for this event, players, parents, and coaches agree to abide by these policies. Any violations of these policies can lead to withdrawal of all teams from the school and ejection from the facility.

Teams:
- Each team is composed of 3-5 players. A standard team consists of 4 players. A team may compete with 3 players, possibly forfeiting on board 4. Teams of 5 players are also permitted where any 4 of the 5 players can play each round while keeping consistent board order.
- The players on a team must be part of the same educational system (“school’) as defined by USCF Scholastic Regulations Sections 5.2, 5.3, or 5.4. https://new.uschess.org/sites/default/files/media/documents/uschess-scholasticregulations_2024-2025.2024.08.05a.pdf
- Multiple teams from the same school may be submitted to any section or event.
- There is no requirement that the teams be sponsored by the school. A group of friends that meet the team eligibility requirements can register and compete.
- Individual players should not register for the event. Contact MCA for assistance forming a team.
- For teams that cannot participate due to last minute withdrawals, the remaining players may still participate in the extra rated games.

Section Eligibility:
MCA Standing Rule 82-01: Ninth grade students playing in an MCA scholastic team tournament must play in the event for the type of school they attend. Examples: (Adopted 01/13/82)
1. If a high school includes grades 9 12, then those ninth graders would play in the High School Tournament.
2. If a junior high school has grades 7 9, then those ninth graders would play in the Junior High School Tournament.

Board Order:
MCA Standing Rule 84-03: Regarding board order in team tournaments: Rated players should generally be placed in rating order; unrated players may be placed anywhere. This should be done with fairness in mind: The strongest player on each team should play on first board, no matter whether he has a relatively high or low rating or is unrated. The tournament director may, at his discretion, change submitted player placements, after considering evidence from various sources (non-USCF ratings, other coaches, etc.). (Adopted 06/21/84).

Average Team Rating:
Use our online tool to determine eligibility for Reserve sections: https://www.michess.org/team-rating-calculator

Match Games:
Individual games are between the players only without the assistance of parents, coaches, and teammates. All questions or concerns, including current match score, should be directed to the TD.

Extra Rated Games:
Each round, Fourth boards without an opponent and alternates are paired randomly so they can play rated games. These games are optional, and players are not guaranteed a game. Points scored in these matches DO NOT count for individual medals.

Equipment:
Boards and Pieces are provided for tournament games. Bring your own set for skittles between rounds.

Bring Clocks:
Games may start without clocks, but games running long will have a clock placed on them with very little time.

Notation:
Please bring writing utensils. All players must record the moves of their game until one player has less than 5 minutes remaining on the clock.

Cell Phones:
No Players may have a cell phone in their possession during their game.

Spectators:
Parents and Coaches may be separated from the playing area once games begin.
Time Control:
JH: G/40;d5
HS: G/55;d5
Rounds:
JH: 9am – 11am – 1pm – 3pm – 5pm
HS: 9:30am – 12:30pm – 3pm – 5:30pm
Entry Fee:
$25 per Player in Advance by 2/21/2026 (Sat week before) at Midnight
$33 per Player in Advance by 2/23/2026 (Mon prior) at Midnight
$55 per Player in Advance by 2/26/2026 (Thur prior) at 8pm
All mailed entries must be postmarked by 2/20/2026
ABSOLUTELY NO ENTRIES AFTER THURSDAY AT 8PM FOR ALL SECTIONS.
Online registration: http://www.onlineregistration.cc (Preferred Method)
If an invoice is needed for school payment, please contact the TD by 2/16/2026 to allow time for processing.
Registration:
The Online Registration ( https://onlineregistration.cc/index.php) system will be the main mechanism to register for the tournament, but not the only method. Those registering through other ways will not be listed at the Online Registration Entry List. MCA will provide a separate website link closer to the tournament date to view full entries along pairings and results during the tournament.

Online registration Links:
- JH: https://onlineregistration.cc/MCA/2026_MCA_JHTeam
- HS: https://onlineregistration.cc/MCA/2026_MCA_HSTeam

Mailed registration: Michigan Chess Association, P.O. Box 40, Flint, MI 48501

DO NOT register unless you are part of a known school team. Individual players without a team are not allowed to participate.

Check-In
Teams must be paid in advance and will be paired for round 1. Parents should check-in with their Coaches. Coaches with any changes must inform MCA staff in writing before 8:15am. No refunds will be given to any players or teams who are paired for the first round and do not arrive. Policy materials will be available onsite.
Prizes:
High School Sections: Individual Medals: Gold 4.0 pts, Silver 3.5 pts, Bronze 3.0 pts
High School Championship Team Awards: Top 10
High School Reserve Team Awards: Top 6

Junior High Sections: Individual Medals: Gold 5.0 pts, Silver 4.0-4.5 pts, Bronze 3.5 pts
Junior High Championship Team Awards: Top 10 teams + all at 3.5
Junior High Reserve Team Awards: Top 7 teams + all at 3.5
Contact:
Jeff Aldrich
810-955-7271
Click here to show mail address
https://www.michess.org/
Notes:
No outside food/drink or delivery services.
- Oakland Center Food Vendors will be open to purchase food

Building Policies: TBD

Video of Question & Answer Session from 2023 Elementary Team: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UuriHMkMHaAEn1GcsquCiKCBWj19pZth/view?usp=sharing

Address: 312 Meadow Brook Rd

Rochester , MI 48309

United States

2026 NJ HIGH SCHOOL CHESS CHAMPIONSHIP

State Championship Event

UNION COUNTY VOCATIONAL TECHNICAL SCHOOL

Saturday, February 28, 2026
- Sunday, March 1, 2026

Event Overview

FEB 28 & MAR 1, 2026. NEW JERSEY HIGH SCHOOL CHAMPIONSHIP 5SS, G/60 d5. Union County Vocational Technical School, 1776 Raritan Rd., Scotch Plains, NJ 07076. ** UCVTS is located near the Police Academy on the far side of the campus **

FORMAT: INDIVIDUAL/TEAM: students will play as individuals in three sections.
1) VARSITY BRACKET (must be in Grades 9-12) - the 5 Highest Rated players from the same school will constitute a team. A second VARSITY team* may be entered consisting of the 6th through 10th highest rated players from the same school. Schools with fewer than 5 players and/or individuals may also enter this section. A minimum of 2 players per school is needed to be considered a team. TROPHIES to: top 5 Schools; top 10 individuals.
2) JUNIOR VARSITY BRACKET (must be in Grades 9-12) - the 4 Highest Rated players from the same school will constitute a team.  A second JUNIOR VARSITY team* may be entered consisting of the 5th through 8th highest rated players from the same school. Schools with less than 4 players and/or individuals may also enter this section. A minimum of 2 players per school is needed to be considered a team. TROPHIES to: top 5 Schools; top 10 individuals.
* NOTE: If a school has more than 1 team in the VARSITY and/or JV bracket, players from the different teams could end up playing each other.  Players from the same team will not play each other.
3) BOOSTER (grades K-12) Open to all grades, all ages. There will be 2 sub-sections in the Booster Section: Booster A for players with USCF rating of 1000 or higher; Booster B for players under with USCF rating below 1000.  Trophies to top 10 individuals in each sub-section.
ALL SECTIONS: USCF membership required. Entry Fee: before 9 pm 2/26/26, TEAMS: 5 players = $200; 4 players = $160; smaller TEAMS and Individuals = $40 per player.
Online registration at njscf.org or mail registration Purchase Orders/Payments to: John Bartlett - P. O. Box 773 - Lincroft, NJ 07738.
Online registration closes at 9 pm on 2/26/26. After 2/26/26, registration on-site only (Check or Cash only - $50 per player and automatic ½ pt bye for round 1 only).
**ON-SITE REG** : (Sat only) 8:30-10:00  [On-Site Reg = 1/2 point bye for round 1 only].
BYES: Byes may be requested for any round.  Byes will be zero-point byes except for round 1 (1/2 point bye)
REGISTRATION must include: Full name; USCF ID # and expiration date; School; Grade; Coaches and/or Parents phone number; Make checks payable to: NJSCF
ROUNDS: SAT - 10:30, 2:00, 4:45; SUN – 10:30, 2:00
QUESTIONS - Email John Bartlett: [email protected]
PLEASE BRING CLOCKS AND SETS.

Address: 1776 Raritan Road

Scotch Plains , NJ 07076

United States

FEB 28, 2026, VIRGINIA
George Washington Saturday 11 AM Satellite Octos
3-SS, G/60; d10. 8 player sections, (the bottom section may have 8 to 15 players). Washington Dulles Marriott Hotel, 45020 Aviation Dr, Dulles, VA 20166.  Free parking, free shuttle to airport and Metro subway (also see TLA for George Washington Open, Feb. 27-Mar. 1). 1st prize: Free entry to the 2026 World Open to 1st in each 8-player section (ties for 1st broken by tiebreak, announced at site, if necessary; prize does not include any additional entry fee surcharges, based on players’ ratings, for players who elect to play up in World Open, Open Section but who are eligible for a lower section). EF:  $50 online by 2/27, $60 after or at site.  March Official Ratings used; unofficial or Online Regular USCF ratings usually used if otherwise unrated. Ruston February Swiss

Argent Financial Group

Saturday, February 28, 2026

Event Overview

Sections
Players will be split into two sections based on rating. Unrated players may choose to play in either section. Players may be allowed to play up at the tournament director's discretion. This must be requested beforehand.

Registration
You may register early or onsite. Onsite registration from 8:50 a.m. to 9:15 a.m. on the day of the tournament. Early registration ends at 11:59 p.m. Thursday, February 26. You can early register by emailing [email protected] , please include your name and USCF ID number when registering. Those who early register will pay on the day of the tournament.

Entry Fee
Early registration is $20. Onsite registration is $30. Cash only.

Rounds
All sections will play four rounds at a time control of G/45+5. Round times are 9:40 a.m., 11:25 a.m., 1:45 p.m., and 3:30 p.m. There will be a break for lunch between rounds two and three. Rounds will be accelerated when possible.

Details

- Please park and enter in the front of the building. If the front parking lot is full, you may park in the rear, the rear entrance will be the door on the far right.

- Byes - one 1/2 point bye is allowed if requested before the start of round 2. After the start of round 2, any byes requested become irrevocable.

- Equipment - please brings chess clocks if you have them.

- Membership - current US Chess Federation membership is required and may be purchased on site. However, we encourage you to register beforehand on their website .

- Prizes - 70% of entries returned.

- Late Arrival - Players who are running late should contact the tournament director. They may request to have a half point bye or to be paired for round 1. If a late arriving player does not contact the tournament director before 9:15 a.m. they may be given a zero point bye in round 1. If the player does not communicate with the tournament director and does not arrive before the end of round 1, they will be withdrawn from the tournament. Any players arriving after 9:15 a.m. may be given a 1/2 point bye, be given a zero point bye, or paired outside of standard pairing rules at the discretion of the tournament director.

- Tournament director will also be playing in the tournament.

- All children in grades 8 and below must have a supervising adult on site at all times.

- Space at the tournament venue is limited, please pre-register to ensure we have a spot for you.

Ruston , LA 71270

United States

4th Austin Chess Tour: Open Qualifier #2
In-Person USCF Rated Tournament
February 28, 2026
12466 Los Indios Trail, Ste.100
Austin, TX 78729
* USCF Membership Required *
Free Parking Provided
Capacity: 112 players
SECTIONS:
All players will be divided into 4 sections:
SECTION A: 1800+  Open USCF rated
SECTION B: 1400 - 1799 Open USCF rated
SECTION C: 1000 - 1399 Open USCF rated
SECTION D: U1000 Open USCF rated
**Players are not allowed to play up or down**
ENTRY FEES:
Early Bird: $50 before 11:59PM February 8, 2026
Standard Fee: $60 before 11:59 February 22, 2026
Late Fee: $75 after February 23, 2026
PRIZES:
Section A: $400, $200, $100
Section B: $200, $100, $50
Section C: $100, $75, $50
Section D: Chess books
Medals will be awarded to top 3 finishers in all sections
NOTE: Players who win prizes must provide us with their Paypal information or wait until the section is completed to receive cash prizes.
Open Qualifier Points:
Top 10 places in Section A will earn points according to the following table:
1st Place: 25 OQ Points
2nd Place: 18 OQ Points
3rd Place: 15 OQ Points
4th Place: 12 OQ Points
5th Place: 10 OQ Points
6th Place: 8 OQ Points

8th Place: 4 OQ Points
9th Place: 2 OQ Points
10th Place: 1 OQ Points

https://austin-chess.com/tournaments/

Section A: G/60, d5 (60 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section B: G/60, d5 (60 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section C: G/45, d5 (45 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section D: G/45, d5 (45 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)

4th round: 5:45 PM

1st round: 10:00 AM

Lunch Break: 1:30 PM

4th round: 4:15 PM

Binghamton Chess - February 28th Classical

University Union, Room 202

Saturday, February 28, 2026

Event Overview

The tournament is open to all, including students, faculty, and town residents. Open to beginners and experienced players. Includes a scholastic section for kids with Medals!
Any questions should be sent to the organizer at [email protected] or 646-685-4278 (email preferred).
Event Details
4 round Swiss, G/30;d5, Regular rated.
Rounds start promptly at 1pm and continue ASAP. Will run until approximately 6:00pm. Please arrive by 12:30 so as to not be late for your first round.
1/2 point byes available, please specify on the registration page or through email before the day of the tournament if needed.
Prize fund is 100$ based on 20 entrants. Prize scales with entries, with a minimum of $50 in prize per section. Prize is given to the top placing finisher(s) in each section.
The Scholastic-Novice section will be for players under 18 only, and will have medals for all participants instead of a prize fund. Players under 18 and under a rating of 1000 can choose to play in the scholastic section.
Adult sections are determined by rating, there are usually either 2 or 3, with an equal number of players in each.
Email is preferred for questions and registration, phone number is preferred if it is the day of or an emergency.
Please bring a clock if you have one, I will provide extras for those who need.
Registration
PLEASE REGISTER ONLINE THROUGH THIS LINK!!!!!!!!!!! If you have problems registering, contact the tournament director at [email protected] and she will register you. You may also register on the day of, in the tournament venue. YOU MUST ARRIVE BY 12:30 TO REGISTER IN PERSON!!!
https://www.reg4chess.com/register.asp?tid=9838
EF:25$ if you pay online through the registration page, through Paypal. Any credit card will work for this.
EF:30$ if you pay at the door through cash, Venmo, Cashapp, Zelle, or Paypal. Arrive by 12:30 to do this.
Discounts are available for all students and faculty of Binghamton University, all students and faculty of Syracuse, and for anyone who wants one. Simply email the Director for the discount code.
If you don't have an USCF ID, please buy one through the link below before registering, or buy one at the door of the tournament (arrive by 12:30 to do so.)  https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess
If the player is playing in the scholastic section, please include the information in the Under 18 part of the form, otherwise, that section is not needed.

Binghamton , NY 13902

Kreutz Creek Quads - February 2026

Kreutz Creek Library

Saturday, February 28, 2026

Event Overview

The Kreutz Creek Quads will be held the fourth Saturday of each month at the Kreutz Creek Library, 66 Walnut Springs Rd., Hellam Township, PA. Each tournament is limited to 40 players, so sign up now to reserve your spot!
Time: 10:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m.
Registration:

- Register online at  https://www.tickettailor.com/events/yorkchessclub/

- Online registration will end at 9 a.m. on tournament day.

- 10 – 10:30 a.m. on tournament day for last-minute entries

- Limited to 40 players due to space restrictions, so sign up early!

Sections:

- Open

- Scholastic

Format:

- Quads (Group of 4 players - each player plays each other player - 3 games total)

- Time control: G/40; d5 (Players get 40 minutes each, with a 5 second delay for each move)

- Rounds: Round 1 at 10:45; Round 2 at 12:30; Round 3 at 2:15. Rounds 2 and 3 may start sooner if all games in previous round are finished and all players agree.

Entry Fee:

- Open: $30

- Scholastic: $10

Prizes:

- Open: $100 to winner (Ties split evenly)

- Scholastic: 1st place trophy, 2nd place medal, ribbons for all players

If players are not in multiples of four, the tournament directors may use house players and/or modify tournament and prize structure dependent on the number of players in section.
No food is available for purchase at the event location, so we suggest packing a lunch. If players use all their clock time, it doesn't leave much time between rounds to drive for a meal. Visit  yorkchess.org  for more information about chess in York County, PA.

Address: 66 Walnut Springs Road

Hellam , PA 17406

United States

2/28 - - ST. PETERSBURG EXTRA QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT G60; d5

Saint Petersburg Chess Club

Saturday, February 28, 2026

Event Overview

There will be no “Byes” or withdrawals allowed. Please complete all your Quad games.

WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT?   After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest.  Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list.  The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each.  If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. A Quad Tournament consists of the top four ranked players (#s 1-4) on the Chess Ladder playing each other, then the second top four ranked players (#s 5-8) playing each other, then the third top four ranked players (#s 9-12) playing each other, and so forth. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad.
ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!!
LOCATION : Saint Petersburg Chess Club 540 4th Avenue North Saint Petersburg, FL 33701 (it is located in between Mirror Lake and the Coliseum, next to the Sunshine Center.)
REGISTRATION : 10:00-10:45 a.m. If you want to make sure you can play, you need to Pay ahead of time here -  https://home.chessregister.com/
ENTRY FEE: $25.00 if you pay in advance (to the day before the tournament)
$30 if you pay Saturday
USCF membership is required. Please check your USCF ID and renew it if it has expired. If you need me to do it on site add $5 to your bill.
ROUNDS: Three Rounds, First starts at approx. 11:00 a.m.
TIME CONTROL: G60; d5
PRIZES : $65 for first place at each Quad or very big trophies for 1st place (if two players tied for 1st place $33 each, or chess trophies for 1st place for both of them)
Trophies for 1st to 3rd place for the last section!
IMPORTANT NOTICE : Due to space limitation to secure your spot Pay online ahead of time!  BRING YOUR CHESS CLOCK!!!
Visit our website-  https://saintpetersburgchessclub.com/ for more information about chess at Saint Petersburg.
Join our Facebook groups Saint Petersburg Chess Tournaments -        https://www.facebook.com/groups/385692191510406/

58th annual New York State High School Championship

Heritage Event, Junior Grand Prix, State Championship Event

Saratoga Hilton Hotel

Saturday, February 28, 2026
- Sunday, March 1, 2026

Event Overview

A Heritage Event!
US Chess Junior Grand Prix!
A State Championship Event!
FEB. 28 – MAR. 1, 2026   NEW YORK
58th annual New York State High School Championship, Out Of State Welcome, but with prize restrictions– intended mostly for Grades 9-12  (grades 6-8 also can also play but with some prize restrictions in Championship Section), Saratoga Hilton Hotel, 534 Broadway, I-87 Exit 13-N, 4 miles north on US 9, Saratoga Springs, NY 12866 (s ee separate TLA, March 7-8, for NY State Scholastic Championship, Grades K-8).  6-SS, G/60, d10. Chess parking rate: $6 daytime, $12 overnight. May be limited to 400 players. In 4 sections. High School Championship (open to all in grades 6-12, top NY State player and team are NY State High School Champions; top NYS grade 9-12 born after 9/1/06 qualifies for Denker Tournament of HS Champions in Grand Rapids, MI), High School Under 1900/Unr, High School Under 1500/Unr., High School Under 1000/Unr. Team prizes based on top 4 scores from same school; teams of 2 or 3 allowed, but are at a disadvantage. Unrateds allowed any section. Online entry fee at chessaction.com,  all sections (space permitting) :  $120 per player by 2/7/26, $140 by 2/23. Registration may closer prior to these dates due to space limitations  and entries may be subject to wait list. If registration is still open, entry fee after 2/23 until registration closes is $200 (On-site entries may not be available this year). Special 1-year USCF dues with magazine if paid online with entry: see chessaction.com. Trophies, plaques or medals to top 10 players & top 5 teams each section, top 2 each U2000, U1800 (HS Championship), U1700, U1600 (in HS U1900), U1300, U1100 (in HS U1500), U800, U600, top 2 unrated (in HS U1000). $2,250 Bonus Prizes in top 2 sections for top-scoring players residing in NY or attending NY schools  (out-of-staters attending NY schools must confirm eligibility with TD by Round 3). Championship:  $1,000-500-250 (limited to NY players or players attending NY schools in grades 9-12); High School Under 1900/Unr.:  $250-150-100, $100 limit to Unr.; Free/reduced entry fee prizes to all CCA OTB tournaments (only for players residing in NY or attending NY schools) : Championship section (only NY players in grades 9-12 eligible for free/reduced EF prizes in Championship Section): 8 months 1st, 6 months 2nd, 4 months 3rd & 4th. Other sections: 6 months 1st, 4 months 2nd, 3 months 3rd & 4th  (all NY players grades 6-12 eligible in Under 1900 Section & below). 2 months bonus free entry to NY players with 6-0 scores. Some CCA events also have minimum rating requirements and/or additional surcharges, based on rating, to play in the top sections; the free/reduced entry fee prizes do not cover any such additional surcharges for playing in the top sections . $300 Mixed Doubles Bonus Prizes: $200-100,  to Best male+female 2-player team among all 4 sections combined, team rating must average U2200, may play in different sections and can be from same or different schools in grades 6-12 in any state; register at site (no extra fee) by 5 pm Sat. Overall School Team Bonus Prizes:  Awards (trophies, plaques or medals) to top 5 school teams among all 4 sections combined! First Place Overall Team (Boards 1-4) also wins 4 additional months of CCA Free/Reduced Entries, 2nd Place Overall Team (Boards 1-4) wins 2 months additional entries (all players grades 6-12 in any state eligible for Overall Team Bonus Prizes). Schedule: Rounds begin Sat 11, 2, 5; Sun 9, 12, 3. Awards: about 5:30 pm. Schedule: Reg. ends Sat 10 am, rounds Sat 11, 2, 5; Sun 9, 12, 3. Awards about 5:30 pm Sun. Half point byes OK all, limit 2, must commit before round 3. Cash prizes split if tied, ties for non-cash prizes broken by tiebreaks (or by speed playoff if 6-0 tie).  HR: see chessevents.us for rates, minimum stay and other details (hotel reservations links at chessevents.us should be open by mid-November or sooner). Hotels may sell out very quickly but could have availability much later due to late cancellations. For backup hotels see chessevents.us. Special car rentals:  Avis, 800-331-1600, use AWD #D657633. $15 per player service charge for refunds. Section switches subject to $20 extra charge after 2/23 (all substitutions from advance list subject to space limitations and charged late fee), no section switching or substitutions after 6 pm 2/26. Questions: chesstour.com, [email protected] . Bring digital clock if possible- none supplied. March official ratings used  (except unofficial USCF web ratings or USCF Online Regular ratings usually used if otherwise unrated). Players with USCF Online Regular ratings over 100 points over their OTB ratings may be assigned higher tournament rating and may be required to play in higher section (TD may use USCF Scholastic Regulations for eligibility guidance). TD reserves right to assign estimated rating to players with non-USCF ratings. Electronic devices rules:  Electronic scorekeeping devices not allowed. See also www.devicerules.com; players may not possess cellphones during play but may store them in bag under table. Unclaimed cash prizes usually paid by PayPal (may take a couple of weeks), but recipients are responsible for arranging delivery and/or replacement of other awards not claimed at site. Enter online:  www.chessaction.com .  No mailed entries.  NY State High School Blitz Championship:  8:00 pm Sat., register at site Sat. by 7:40 pm.
