Arizona Golden Cup 🏆

Phoenix Chess Academy

Saturday, February 28, 2026

Event Overview

Arizona's Premier Year - Long USCF Chess Series.
Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆
A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required.
4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points.
Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section.
Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over.
Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that.
Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event.
At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed.
Golden Points System:
Finish                 Points
1st Place              20
2nd Place            16
3rd Place             13
4th Place             10
5–6                           8
7–10                        5
Participation       3
Bonus Points:
+3 points — Perfect score (4/4).
+2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months.
Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions.
Tie-Breaks (Year-End):
1. Most 1st-place finishes.
2. Head-to-head results.
3. Most tournaments played.
4. Best December result.
TD decisions are final.

Crusader Library Series Chess Tournament

Judge Marquez Public Library

Saturday, February 28, 2026

Event Overview

Crusader Chess Proudly presents the continuation of our Crusader Chess Tournament Library Series

First Round Start time 10am
Player check in 9am to 9:30am
Onsite from 930am to 10am ONLY if space still available ( look at our facebook page for details)
See QR Code on  Facebooke event page Register NOW
Format :  SWISS/ no elimination play all rounds
Sections :  Two Sections
US CHESS MEMBER OPEN
Non Members Novice
Game Control and number of rounds : US CHESS MEMBER SECTION OPEN- G/ 45 Rounds Chess notation required
Non Member Novice Section G/30
4 Rounds each section
Awards:
US CHESS MEMBERS trophy to top three Players
Medals to top three Novice Players
Pre- registration preferred . Space limited. No lunch break play through. No food provided. Free Entry. No Elimination. Play all rounds.
Register by email/QR code: [email protected] or text/call 9152567783 or if space is available only  onsite from 900am to 9:30am
Contact Affiliate :  https://www.facebook.com/crusaderchessclubelp        Official Texas Chess Association Club Affiliate
Event Sponsored by : Crusader Chess Club of El Paso     Awards Sponsored by C&M Trophy and Plaque  Venue Sponored by El Paso Public Libraries
Part of the Cruader Chess Club Tournament Library Series
Chief TD : Michelle Hickman
Event Organizer/ President of Affiliate : Renate Garcia
US CHESS MEMBERSHIPS : May be obtained through Crusader Chess  prior to event and onsite  at 9am to 10:30am or by the following link  https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess prior to the event.   If you have a large amount of players you wish to register please send us a spreadsheet with pertinant info including us chess member ID and expiration date to our email indicated.
Know before you go :
All players must check in to chess control. If you are in the novice section and have not checked in before 9:30am you will be dropped from the tournament.  We do not sort by age. Event is open for all players and abilities.  You may be playing against a child or young adult as an Adult or Senior.  Age doesnt matter only skill and dont let appearances fool you we have some pretty strong players of all ages!  If you require special accomodations please contact organizer so we can assist you.
If you are playing in the US Chess section we will be following US Chess rules as always. ( as well as novice section mostly with a few variations for novice players)  Crusader Chess Club will offer a carbon copy of your notation sheet if you like but the white copy is property of Crusader Chess and must be submitted after every game. Therefore, all players will be required to notate their games and use a clock in OPEN section. We have limited clocks to lend players so please bring your clocks. We have a couple of clocks for sale. Novice section is not required to notate but strongly encouraged to practice and try to fill out as much as possible. We can help you and guide you through that process if you need assistance. We are here to help!
If you plan on registering we advise you to register now by texting or email [email protected] 915.256.7783 or QR CODE.
There will be no elimination. You will play all rounds regardless of win or loss. There will not be lunch provided and we will not be stopping for lunch. We suggest you bring a packed lunch or some snacks. We will be playing straight through. There are numerous locations of restaurants and fast food choices close by if you have someone to pick it up for you. We do allow uber deliveries but please refer them to front desk not play hall.
Onsite Check in for players is at 9am to 930am only if space is still available. Player check in is at 9am. All players must check into Chess Control.
1st round starts promptly at 10am.
Equipment:
We follow US Chess Guidelines for what players are responsible for. However, we realize we have many novice players learning the ropes. For this reason we will provide a complete chess set for you to play on, You may bring a set if you wish to play in the skittles area. We have a limited number of clocks to lend to players. Clocks are responsibility of players and we have some for sale if you like onsite.  Notation sheets are provided but we have some scholastic book notations sheets for sale as well.  We recommend the US CHESS sales website if you would like to purchase different items www.uscfsales.com
Offical Rules of Chess:
All  US CHESS players must be aware of the US Chess Rules which maybe found :
www.uscfsales.com/us-chess-federation-s-official-rules-of-chess-seventh-edition-2024
Skittles:
We always offer a seperate location for the players in between rounds  to get some extra game play time or go over their moves with coaches or parents. This location is inside the Library as the Tournament hall is closed to specators and only certified Tournament Directors or Crusader Chess Staff will be allowed in the Tournament playing hall during games. Please enjoy the ambiance of the library events and take advantage of their chess books we have been growing for your reading  pleasure. Please be advised,  bad behavior and distruptions in the libary may result in the removal of your player from the tournament. Please be respectful to the staff and the location and respect other patrons who are visiting the library. No running or loud noises will be tolerated.  Players are considered spectators when their games finish and must exit the play hall.  There may arrise a specific ocasion that a TD may allow spectators but we will announce this should we have the need and is up to TD discretion.

Grand Prix, Enhanced Grand Prix, State Championship Event

Saratoga Hilton Hotel

Saturday, February 28, 2026
- Sunday, March 1, 2026

Event Overview

US CHESS GRAND PRIX POINTS: 40 (ENHANCED)
A State Championship Event!
February 28 – March 1, 2026.  NEW YORK
New York State Senior Championship (With Young Adult/Middle Age Section), out of state welcome!   5-SS, G/90, d10, Saratoga Hilton Hotel, 534 Broadway (I-87 Exit 13-N, 4 miles north on US 9), Saratoga Springs, NY 12866. Chess parking rate: $6 daytime, $12 overnight. $4,200 Guaranteed Prizes!  2 sections. Seniors Section,  open to all born before 3/2/76. $$800-400-200, top U2300 $250, U1910 $150, U1610/Unr. $100. Top NYS resident qualifies to represent NY at 2026 Irwin National Tournament of State Senior Champions in Grand Rapids, MI. NY State title & $100 bonus to top NYS resident (both decided on tiebreak if tied).  Young Adult/Middle Age Section,  open to all born before 3/2/08 and after 3/1/76. $$800-400-200, top U2200 $250, U1900 $150, U1600/Unr. $100. EF: $98 online at chessaction.com by 2/24, $110 later or at site, GMs $80 from prize. Mixed Doubles Bonus Prizes:  Best male+female 2-player team combined score among both sections: $200-100, team must average under 2200; may play in different sections; register (no extra fee) onsite before 2 pm Sat. Special USCF dues  with magazine with online entry: see chessevents.us. Reg. ends 9 am Sat, rounds Sat 10, 2 & 6; Sun 10 & 2. All:  Online entry $7 less to NYSCA members (NYSCA dues $12/yr with 2 issues Empire Chess or $20/yr with 4 issues; may join with entry). Online March Madness

Chess.com

Sunday, March 1, 2026

Event Overview

ONLINE MARCH MADNESS
​ Bloodhound Chess Club
Chess.com Please Provide your Chess.com Username. Registration  link Below
https://www.kingregistration.com/register/OnlineMarch

​Date: Sunday, March 1st, 2026 10:00AM (CST)
​Sections: * Section 1: Open (USCF Rated & Experienced Players)
​Section 2: Unrated (New & Casual Players)
​Entry Fee: $0 (Free)
​Registration Deadline: Saturday, February 28, 2026, at 9:00 PM CST.
​Tournament Format
​Time Control: 5 minutes + 3-second increment (5+3 Blitz)
​Structure: 5-Round Swiss System
​Schedule: * Round 1: 10:00 AM CST
​Rounds Will begin ASAP immediately following the completion of the previous round.
​Byes: No byes are available. Players must be present for all rounds to remain eligible for prizes.
​ Prizes & The "Overtime Championship"
​Each section (Open and Unrated) features a $100 Grand Prize paid via CashApp.
​💰 The Tiebreaker Payout
​THE OVERTIME CHAMPIONSHIP: In the event of a tie for 1st place after 5 rounds, we’re going to Overtime. Traditional computer-generated tiebreak points will not be used to determine our champions.
​The top seeds in the tie will face off in a Winner-Take-All Final Match.
​The victor of this head-to-head showdown claims the undisputed title and the full $100 prize.
​This rule applies to both the Open and Unrated sections.
​🎖️ The Champion’s Perk
​In addition to the cash prize, the 1st place winners of the Overtime Championship in both sections will earn the exclusive right to organize and host their very own tournament through the Bloodhound Chess Club network.
​4. Fair Play & Conduct
​Integrity: All games will be reviewed by Chess.com’s Fair Play team and Bloodhound Chess Club officials.
​Disqualification: Any use of engines, opening books, or outside assistance will result in immediate disqualification, a permanent ban from the club, and forfeiture of all prizes.
​Sportsmanship: Respectful behavior is required in the chat. Excessive stalling or "trash talking" may result in removal from the event.
​5. Payout Instructions
​Winners must provide their CashApp Tag to the tournament director immediately following the conclusion of their section’s final match. Payouts will be processed once fair play is verified.

SCHOLASTIC SUNDAY by Indy Chess

St. Monica Catholic School Gym (Door 15)

Sunday, March 1, 2026

Event Overview

REGISTER FOR THIS TOURNAMENT HERE: https://www.indychess.org/events
Kids who have learned how the pieces move and some basic strategy are welcome to enter the world of rated chess tournaments!  All school-aged kids from kindergarten to 12th grade are welcome.  Walk-ins are discouraged, as we would appreciate all registering online in advance.  The chess playing room is a silent atmosphere to enable maximum concentration.
For the "rated" tournament, all players MUST be members of the US Chess Federation ($24/year).  Before registering for the rated event, become a member of USCF here (you will need to write down your child's USCF ID#).  However, being a member of Indy Chess--our local club--at $50/year/student or $75/year/family is optional.  If interested, you can do that here to get a $5 discount on this event and every other one you attend this year with us, including Weekly Tuesdays, and support the growth of chess in Indy!
[If a beginner and wanting to play in the "casual" tournament (unrated, does not require USCF membership), that is explained far below.]
Here are the details:

- Check-in on site: 1:45-2:00pm, entering the door up a few exterior stairs/ramp (not the street-level door).  Games start right after a player meeting at 2:15pm.

- 4ss: Four rounds in a "Swiss" system.  A Swiss tournament--the most common chess form--means every player plays every round, with future rounds pairing those who won and those who lost.  Up to two 1/2-point byes can be requested by emailing [email protected] or telling the tournament director at the event which rounds you would like byes.  Note: Premiere section is 3 rounds.

- G/25+5: Games are 25 minutes on each players clock, plus 5 seconds added to a player's time when they hit the clock every move.

- USCF-rated: All players must be members of the US Chess Federation and provide a member ID# in online registration.  This will give each child a "rating" in chess that will follow them with each tournament they play.  Ratings are in blitz, quick, and regular play, and the 25+5 time control affects their regular and their quick rating.

- Entry fee is $20/kid, or $15 for members of Indy Chess.

- Kids rated under 1000 are divided into three  sections so kids play only those in their age group (e.g., 3rd Grade & Under, 6th Grade & Under, and 12th Grade & Under).  Want your child to "play up?"  Just email Mike at [email protected] .  Notation is optional but encouraged in these sections.

- There is one "Premiere" section for kids rated 1000 or above (published rating from the 1st of the month).  Notation is required in the premiere sections.  The Premiere section is three rounds, and may be split by rating at TD discretion to achieve less than eight players per section.

Casual Tournament:
Alongside the rated tournament, kids can instead register for a casual tournament (i.e., unrated) which will begin at the same time.  The games will be optionally clocked, notation is not required, and the tournament director will determine section splits based on turnout.  It will be a Swiss tournament (i.e., all players play all rounds, unless someone gets a bye due to an odd number).  There will be four rounds.  There are trophies for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place winners!
Other details:

- Children under 12 years old must have an adult present and responsible for them, unless the parent/guardian has the permission of the tournament director.

- Concessions are typically available for sale by St. Monica, including hot food (less likely in summer months).

- An outside playground is available.

- Parents may watch chess silently from the bleachers in the gym, or sit at tables in the cafeteria.  There is a guest WiFi network with password August27.

- The site is wheelchair accessible.

- Parking is free in the school lot (Door 15 is located near the southeast side of the building), but is sometimes full right at 1:45p due to a church function.  Parking on a nearby street for overflow is available.

- Chess sets, clocks, and notation sheets are provided for up to 60 kids.  If the child has played in a tournament or two prior, it is helpful if they bring a regulation set and/or clock to ensure there are enough.

- Trophies are provided to the top five finishers in each of the three lower sections.  In the premiere section, a $50 Amazon gift card goes to the winner (decided by 5+0 blitz playoff if need be, Black/White randomly chosen).  Biggest upset earns a medal (unrated does not qualify).

- Players who notate at least one game get to pick a prize from the bin at the end of the tournament!  Learn how to notate chess moves here (YouTube link).

Questions?  Email Mike at [email protected] .  We hope to see you there!
REGISTER FOR THIS TOURNAMENT HERE: https://www.indychess.org/events

Glen Oak March Madness Scholastic (K-8)

Glen Oak Elementary School

Sunday, March 1, 2026

Event Overview

Glen Oak March Madness Scholastic (K-8)
Sunday, March 1, 2026
Glen Oak Elementary School
7300 Blue Holly Dr.
Lewis Center, Ohio 43035
Proudly Sponsored by the Glen Oak PTO
Tournament organizer:  Jim Bickley, (740) 657-5518 or  Click here to show mail address .
Sections and time controls:  There will be five rounds in each of the lower sections. The open section will consist of four rounds.  This is a Swiss System tournament.  All players play in all rounds.  No one is eliminated.
Unrated K-4 (G/30)
Unrated 5-8 (G/30)
K-8 Rated Under 500  (G/30; d5)
K-8 Rated Under 1000  (G/30; d5)
K-8 Rated Open (G/45; d5)
All sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided.  Notation is highly encouraged, but not mandatory.
Entry fee:  We strive to run efficient and affordable tournaments.  The early entry fee will be $25.00 by Monday, February 23.  After this date, the entry fee will be $40.00.  Please register early.  No additional registrations will be accepted after 4:00 p.m. on Friday, February 27.
Schedule:  Doors open at 8:00.  Announcements will be at 8:45.  No section changes after this time.  Round 1 will begin immediately after announcements.
Concessions:  We will offer coffee and doughnuts for breakfast.  We’ll also serve snacks and the Glen Oak Meal (slice of pizza, chips, cookie and drink for $5.00).
Awards:  Trophies will be awarded to those scoring 3.5 or more points (in the open section, 2.5 or higher is the trophy threshold).  Team trophies will be awarded to the top three teams in each of the rated sections.  A team consists of two or more players from the same school.  The top four scorers from that school will count toward the team award.
Registration:   https://pci.jotform.com/form/260204409278152
To check the status of registered players, please visit  www.glenoakchess.org under Glen Oak March Madness.

Lewis Center , OH 43035

George Washington Sunday 10 AM Satellite Octos

Washington Dulles Marriott Hotel

Sunday, March 1, 2026

Event Overview

MAR 1, 2026, VIRGINIA
George Washington Sunday 10 AM Satellite Octos
3-SS, G/60; d10. 8 player sections, (the bottom section may have 8 to 15 players). Washington Dulles Marriott Hotel, 45020 Aviation Dr, Dulles, VA 20166.  Free parking, free shuttle to airport and Metro subway (also see TLA for George Washington Open, Feb. 27-Mar. 1). 1st prize: Free entry to the 2026 World Open to 1st in each 8-player section (ties for 1st broken by tiebreak, announced at site, if necessary; prize does not include any additional entry fee surcharges, based on players’ ratings, for players who elect to play up in World Open, Open Section but who are eligible for a lower section). EF:  $50 online by 2/28, $60 after or at site.  March Official Ratings used; unofficial or Online Regular USCF ratings usually used if otherwise unrated. Cannot play below USCF Online Regular rating minus 100 points. Reg. ends 9 am Sun, rounds 10-1-4 pm.  Half point bye OK  in any round, must commit before round 2.  Special USCF dues:  see chessevents.us.  $15 service charge  for refunds.  Entries posted  at  chessaction.com (click "entry list" after entering).  Bring set, board & clock  if possible - none supplied.

TCA Region V Scholastic 2026 (Elementary)

The Houston Chess Studio

Sunday, March 1, 2026

Event Overview

TCA Region V Scholastic 2026 (Elementary)
Date & Location
Date:  March 1, 2026
Location:  The Houston Chess Studio 250 Patton St. Suite I Houston, TX 77079

Contact Info
Organizer:  Edgar Acosta
Email:   [email protected]
Phone:  (281) 844 4139

Pricing

- Early Registration: $32, ends on January 31, 2026

- Regular Registration: $37, between February 1 - 15, 2026

- Late Registration: $40, between February 16 - 27, 2026

- Active USCF membership is required by February 16, 2026.
- Visit  new.uschess.org/join-us-chess  starting at $24 to join USCF or renew your membership!

- Visit  chess.jliptrap.us/hgroup.htm  for $13 discount Scholastic memberships and renewals!

- TCA Tournament membership is included in the tournament entry fee.
- Visit  texaschess.org/memberships  to join TCA or renew your membership!

Pricing is included in the registration form automatically.

Eligibility
Participants must live or attend school in one of these counties:

- Austin, Brazoria, Brazos, Chambers, Fort Bend, Galveston, Grimes

- Hardin, Harris, Houston, Jasper, Leon, Liberty, Madison

- Matagorda, Montgomery, Newton, Orange, Polk, Robertson

- San Jacinto, Trinity, Tyler, Walker, Waller, Wharton

The max number of registrations for this tournament is 74. Text Edgar Acosta to join a waiting list

Sections

- Elementary Open : Any Elementary student may enter this section.

- Elementary U700 : Only Elementary students rated 700 or below may enter this section.

- Note:  Sections may be combined in case of low registrations.

Definitions:

- High School  - Grades 9-12; in some districts 10-12, if Junior High is 7-9.

- Middle School  - Grades 6 to 8 or 9 depending on how the school district divides them.

- Elementary  - K-6 if 6th grade is in the Elementary building, K-5 if 6 is in Middle School.
- A 5th-6th campus has been ruled Elementary, a 6th-only campus as Middle School.

- Primary  - K-3. Note that a first grader could enter K-1 or K-3 or K-5.

- K-8 and K-12 schools and Home School Associations are divided K-5, 6-8, and 9-12.

- Students not assigned a grade in school will be assigned a grade at the tournament based on their age as of September 1 of that school year as follows: six years old is assigned first grade, seven years old is assigned second grade, and so on through grade twelve.

Note:  Sections are based on USCF January 2026 ratings. "Current" ratings may be used to pair unrated players but will  not  determine section placement. Accelerate Pairings will be used at the discretion of the TD the day of the tournament.

Tournament Format

- Rounds:  Swiss 5 Rounds, Game in 25 with a 5-second delay (G/25 d/5).

- Membership:  USCF and TCA memberships required.

- Rules:  USCF rules apply.

- Open sections  require notation  and clocks (if available).
- Players who opt to not take notation will have their time start at 20 minutes instead of 25.

- Reserved sections are strongly encouraged to use notation and clocks.

- Touch-move / Touch-take:  Applies to all sections. Younger players, especially in Kinder-1st Open, will be encouraged to keep these rules with gentle reminders as needed.

- Equipment:  Plan on bringing your own chess set and clock if you have one, money for lunch, and a good attitude!
- Every player needs to bring their clocks!

- Please make sure your clocks are labeled with the player's name and USCF ID.

- Chess sets for the whole tournament  will  be provided!

Schedule

- No At-Site Registration. All registrations must be submitted online at  before 11:59pm on February 27, 2026.

- Please arrive between 8:15 and 8:45 to check in and get ready to play.

- Round 1:  Starts at 9:00 AM SHARP; subsequent rounds will start ASAP. No elimination.

- Players may request a single 1/2 point Bye missed, 0 point Bye for any subsequent Byes. Any Byes need to be requested by Friday February 27th, 2026 at 7pm.

- Lunch break after Round 3, estimating 12pm-1pm.

Teams
Teams consist of two or more (2+) players in the same section from the same school/association.

- Team members must attend the  same school campus  full-time or belong to the  same Home School Association .

- Sections are  not combined  for teams.

- Team scores will be calculated by summing the top four (4) individual scores from each team.

Awards

- Trophies:  Top 5 individuals in each section and Top 4 teams in each section.

- 1st Place Finishers qualify for a spot in the State Regional Invitational April 18-19th .

- Alternate awards (likely medals) to players who score 3 or more points but do not win a trophy.

- Tie Breaks:  Solkoff (sum of opponents' scores), Modified Median (dropping the lowest opponent's score), Cumulative of Opposition, then Cumulative (USCF Standard)

We look forward to seeing you at The Houston Chess Studio  on  February 27, 2026  for a day of competitive and fun scholastic chess!

Mar. Wilson Chess Scholastic
Sunday, Mar. 1st, 2026
New Location - DoubleTree by Hilton Lisle Naperville
3003 Corporate W Dr, Lisle, IL 60532
This tournament is open to all chess players (K-12).
US Chess membership required for all rated sections.

Round Times:

- Round 1 - 10 am

- Round 2 - 11:10 am

- Lunch

- Round 3 - 12:30 pm

- Round 4 - 1:40 pm

- Round 5 - 2:50 pm

- Awards - 4 pm or as soon as Round 5 is complete.

Sections:

- U1200 – Must be rated 600 to play up

- U800 - Intermediate level

- U400 – Beginner level

- Not-Rated (max rating of 300) -  This section is not rated.  US Chess membership not require

Awards:
Each section has individual 1st - 5th place.
Medals to all that tie for 5th place (that do not receive a trophy)
Top 2 school teams across all sections. Teammates are allowed to play in different sections!!
Teams are based on top 4 scores per team with a 2-player minimum.

Register:
Register Online - Here or onsite before 9:30am.
Space is limited; it is strongly recommended to register online.

Entry Fee:

- Online by 2/21 - $35

- Online by 2/28 - $40

- Day-of or Onsite - $50 – Onsite entries after 9:30am receive ½-point bye for round 1.

- *Note : $2 surcharge for all online entries.

Special Discount: US Chess Membership
Anyone who becomes a new member of US Chess or renews their membership through Wilson Chess will receive a $2 discount.
Contact: Wilson Chess: Email – Click here to show mail address Attn. Mar. Scholastic
Boards and sets provided
Clocks provided for U1200 section and is optional for U800
Notation is required for U1200 section and is optional for U800 and U400.

Refunds are subject to $5 processing fee.

San Marino Masonic Lodge

weekly on Monday, starting from Monday, March 2, 2026, until Monday, March 30, 2026

Event Overview

This is a five round event in three sections.  Players must play in their own rating section (no exceptions).  Either the latest Supplement or a players most recent "live" regular rating will be used at the TD's discretion. It starts March 2  and ends March 30.  One half-point is  available and any additional byes will be 0 point byes.   There is one round each Monday night and games start at 6:45 pm (games end by 10 pm). The Club opens at 6:00 pm.  Time control is Game/90 minutes with a five second delay.   The entry fee is $45 and should be paid online. Total prize fund to be determined based on entries. All players must be SGVCC members and have current USCF memberships. You can join our renew your SGVCC dues online at our website or in person.  You can join after the first round has started but you must contact the TD per below.  You can renew or join the USCF at our registration link.  We meet at the San Marino Masonic Lodge, located at 3130 Huntington Drive, San Marino, CA 91108.   For more information contact TD John Wright at  626/864-5744  or at [email protected]

Madison Area Chess Club - March on the Open Files

Growth Chess Center

Wednesday, March 4, 2026
- Wednesday, March 25, 2026

Event Overview

1. Dates & Location

- Four Wednesdays March 4th, 11th, 18th, 25th

- Location: Growth Chess Center 4506 Regent St Madison, WI

2. Tournament Format:

- Tournament Format: Individual Swiss

- Two Sections: Open & Reserve (U1500), if there are less than 6 players in either sections will be combined. Prizes will still be separate.

- Total Rounds: 4 (1 round each Wednesday night)

- Round Times: Wednesdays at 6:30PM

- Time Control Open: G/60+30  (Game in 60 minutes with 30 second increment on each move)

3. Byes

- Byes are available for players in any rounds in case they can't participate that evening, but would like to stay in the tournament.

- A maximum of one half-point byes can be requested in this tournament.

- Round 1-3 byes must be requested prior to the pairing of the round. Pairings usually are posted shortly after noon on Tuesday, the day before the round.

- Round 4 byes must be requested before start of Round 3. Round 4 bye is irrevocable to prevent possible prize-fund manipulations.

- Late registrations will receive a half-point bye for any missed round, up to a total one round.

4. Prizes -- $600 based on 20 paid entries. Prizes will increase proportionally after 40 entries. Single Game Entries are not counted towards the based on prizes.

- 1st place $160

- 2nd place $120

- 3rd place $80

- Reserve 1st Place $100

- Reserve 2nd Place $80

- Reserve 3rd Place $60

- Unrated players may enter any section for which they are otherwise eligible.
Unrated players are not eligible for Under-section (class) cash prizes unless explicitly stated.
When sections are combined for pairing purposes, prize eligibility remains based on the player’s entered section .

5. Prize Fund --  $600 based on 20 paid entries

- Please allow a week for processing prize checks.

- Per IRS rules anyone with a cumulative $600+ prizes in any calendar year will need to fill out a W9 and Growth Chess will be providing a 1099 form.

- Max Capacity: 60

6. Registration for Both Sections -- Including Single Game Option!

- $40 by 3/4/26

- Entry Prorated after each round

- Single Round Option available for any round $15

- Free Entry for NMs & Higher, email  Click here to show mail address  to register.

- $5 admin fee for all cancellations & refunds.

2026 Virginia Scholastic & College Chess Championships

Heritage Event, State Championship Event

Thomas Jefferson High School for S&T

Friday, March 6, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

PRE-TOURNAMENT ANNOUNCEMENT
2026 Virginia Scholastic & College
Chess Championships
hosted by
Thomas Jefferson High School
for Science and Technology
Saturday-Sunday, March 7-8, 2026
6560 Braddock Rd., Alexandria VA
WHAT : The Virginia Chess Federation (VCF) is partnering with Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology for the 2026 Virginia Scholastic & College Chess Championships.
WHEN : Saturday and Sunday, March 7-8, 2026, with a Blitz Tournament on Friday night, March 6th.
REGISTRATION : We will open Registration at  www.vachess.org by December 1st, 2025. Specific entry fees have not yet been determined; they are pending final logistical arrangements with the venue. Please do not contact TJ High School , they are relying on the VA Chess Federation to answer all questions about the tournament and event logistics.
HOTEL ARRANGEMENTS : TBD. We will seek agreements with hotels close to the High School. Details will be posted on the VCF website,  www.vachess.org .
EVENT FORMAT : The tournament has nine (9) sections:

- College: One section, with all games on Saturday.

- K-12 Championship and K-12 Under 1400

- K-8 Championship and K-8 Under 1200

- K-5 Championship and K-5 Under 1000

- K-3 Championship and K-3 Under 600

TOURNAMENT SCHEDULE :

- Friday, March 6th: On-site Registration for the Main Event and Blitz. Round 1 of BLITZ is at 6:30 PM.

- Saturday, March 7th: Rounds 1-3 at 9 am, 12:30 pm, and 4:30 pm. College Section games are at 9, noon, 3 pm, and 6 pm. Parents & Friends tournament starts at 12:45.

- Sunday, March 8th: Rounds 4-5 at 9:30 am and 1:30 pm. Awards Ceremonies held by section as soon as possible after the last game finishes in a section.

TEAMS : Teams must be comprised of players who attend the same school. A school is not required to have a “chess club” or “official school team” to form a team for this tournament. Two or more players who go to the same school and play in the same section of the tournament are automatically considered a team for the purposes of this tournament. More details will be available when we open registration.
PLAYER ELIGIBILITY :

- All players in the Scholastic sections (K-12, K-8, K-5, K-3) must be Virginia residents .

- In the College section, players must be attending college in VA or be a VA resident attending college out of state. All college players must be high school graduates.

- U.S. Chess Federation membership is required for all players. Players can join US Chess or renew their membership through the VCF at  www.vachess.org and select the “Join US Chess” tab on the left side of the webpage. We offer all Virginians a small discount on US Chess Federation membership. If you prefer, you also can join/renew your US Chess membership directly with US Chess, go to  www.uschess.org .

IMPORTANT : The VCF uses the results of this tournament to identify and nominate representatives to attend the US national tournaments of State Champions. These tournaments (see list below) will be held in early August in conjunction with the U.S. Open in Grand Rapids, Michigan. The VCF provides stipends to assist the Viriginia players selected to represent The Commonwealth at these tournaments.

- Denker Tournament of High School State Champions (Grades 9-12)

- Barber Tournament of Middle School State Champions (Grades 6-8)

- Rockefeller Tournament of Elementary School State Champions (Grades 4-5)

- NEW for 2026 : Maurice Ashley Tournament of Primary School State Champions (Grades K-3)

- Haring Tournament of Girls State Champions

FUN SIDE EVENTS :

- BLITZ on Friday evening March 6th (Round 1 at 6:30 pm). 4 double-rounds (2 games per round for 8 total games).

- 4-round “Parents & Friends” tournament open to adults. Scholastic or college players are NOT eligible to play in this event.

- “Challenge the Master” Simultaneous Exhibition.

TEAM ROOMS : We are working with the TJ High School administration to obtain a number of classrooms that can be used by teams with 10 or more players as well as by parents who wish to form a group in order to get a team room. Please do not contact the school for any information about this, the school relies on the VA Chess Federation to collect and consolidate all Team Room requests.
PRE-EVENT ZOOM INFO MEETINGS : The VCF will organize several options for players and parents to attend a pre-event Zoom Meeting in mid-to-late February 2026.

Alexandria , VA 22312

United States

Prize Fund: Trophies

Handicap Accessible: Yes
Residency Restriction: Yes
Online Event: No

Northern Nevada Senior Championship 2026

State Championship Event

Reno Chess Club / Mathewson Bridge Center

Friday, March 6, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

Silver State Chess Association
presents
2026 Northern Nevada State Seniors Championship
March 6-8 2026
Mathewson Bridge Center
125 West Plumb Lane
Reno, NV 89509
Swiss 5 Rounds Game/90+30
Note:  Players must be age 50+ prior to Aug 3, 2026.

Players must reside in Nevada in one of the following counties and have their eligible address on file with USCF: Washoe, Humbolt, Elko, Pershing, Storey, Churchill, Lander, Eureka, White Pine, Lyon, Douglas, Mineral and the independent city of Carson City.

Southern Nevada residents should register for the Southern Nevada State Seniors Championship in a separate tournament.
Schedule :  (all rounds G/90+30)
Round 1: Friday March 6 @ 6:00 pm
Round 2: Saturday March 7 @ 12:00 pm
Round 3: Saturday March 7 @ 5:00 pm
Round 4: Sunday March 8 @ 12:00 pm
Round 5: Sunday March 8 @ 5:00 pm
Top three winners advance to the State Championship to compete against top three winners from Southern NV in a proctored online tournament to be held at the Mathewson Bridge Center on April 24-26.
Please bring boards, sets, and clocks as none are provided.
Prizes
$1000.00 with 20 paid players:
Top Prize:  $500 + Trophy
Second:    $350 + Trophy
Third: $150 + Trophy
Top U1900: Trophy
Top U1600: Trophy

Above cash prizes adjusted proportionally for more or fewer players.
Note: Cash prizes will be awarded following the completion of the Nevada State Seniors Championship on April 26. To receive a cash prize in the Northern NV Championship, players must play in the Nevada State Seniors Championship. If a player is unable or unwilling to play in the online Nevada State Seniors Championship, entry and cash prize will be offered to the next highest scoring player.

The winner of the Nevada State Seniors Championship will represent Nevada in the John T. Irwin Tournament of Senior State Champions on August 3-6 (TBD) in Grand Rapids, MI. Silver State Chess will provide a travel stipend of $650 upon completion of the Irwin with no forfeited games.
Maximum number of entries: 40. Registration not confirmed until payment received.
Waitlist will start if/when max entries received.
Entry fee : $99 by March 5, $115 later.
Refunds : may be requested prior to start of Round 1. $15 withheld for processing fees
Entrants may register in person and pay with cash or check at the Reno Chess Club on Thursday evenings 6-9pm before March 6 @ 8:00pm.
Maximum two half-point byes available and must be requested before Round 3 and are irrevocable

US Chess Membership is required.
Please join or renew the player’s membership at  www.uschess.org  before registering for the tournament.
Registration:  https://www.kingregistration.com/event/NNV2026Seniors
Contact  Click here to show mail address

Parents & Friends Tournament at the 2026 VA Scholastic Championships

Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology

Friday, March 6, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

Parents & Friends Tournament
at the 2026 VA Scholastic Championships
Saturday and Sunday, March 7-8, 2026 – with Blitz on Friday March 6th
At the Thomas Jefferson High School for Science & Technology in Alexandria, VA What : Parents & Friends (P&F) Tournament at the VA Scholastic Championships. There’s also a Blitz Tournament on Friday night for Parents & Friends.

- New for 2026 : This year in the P&F BLITZ tournament there will be awards for the “Top Parent-Child” Team! A Parent-Child team is defined as a parent playing in the P&F tournament who has at least one child playing in the K-6, 7-12, or College Blitz Tournaments. The award recognizes the top 3 Parent-Child Teams by adding the parent’s blitz score to the blitz score of their highest-finishing child in the scholastic or the college sections.

When : Saturday and Sunday, March 7-8, 2026, with Round 1 on Saturday at 12:45 PM (this is 15 minutes after the start of Round 2 in the Scholastic sections). Blitz is on Friday evening at 6:30 PM.
Where : Thomas Jefferson HS for Science & Tech, 6560 Braddock Rd., Alexandria, VA. Please DO NOT call the school for information about the chess tournament .
Hotels : The Virginia Chess Federation is developing lodging options with several hotels near the school. The properties represent a range of selections and costs. See www.vachess.org for the options available. All hotel deals will have a “cut off”; reservations made after the cut-off date may no longer be eligible to get the “Chess Rate” for lodging.
Event Format : 4 Rounds using the Swiss System. This is NOT an elimination tournament! The Blitz Tournament will have 3 or 4 rounds of play (2 games per round), depending on the number of entries in the Blitz event.
Entry Fees and Registration : Select the “Register Now” button below to register for Parents & Friends!

- P&F Main Event Entry Fees: $30 through February 28th ; increases to $35 on March 1st and onsite. Entry onsite permitted on Friday March 7th and Saturday March 8th until 12 noon. Players who register after 12 noon on Saturday might not be paired until Round 2.

- P&F Blitz Entry Fees: $20 through February 28th ; increases to $30 on March 1st and onsite.

- Registration: On-line at this link or www.vachess.org .

- One half-point Bye is available in any of the 4 rounds of the main P&F tournament. No Byes allowed in Blitz.

Sections of Play : All players compete in one section in both the main and blitz P&F tournaments.
Event Schedule for the P&F Events :

- Registration Onsite:  4-9 pm on Friday and 9 am to noon on Saturday. Blitz players must be registered by 6 PM to play in Round 1 at 6:30.

- Main P&F Tournament Round Times:
- Saturday : Rounds 1 and 2 at 12:45 pm and 4:45 pm.

- Sunday : Rounds 3 and 4 at 9:45 am and 1:45 pm.

- Blitz Tournament Round Times : Round 1 at 6:30 PM

Time Controls : All players’ clocks will be set each round using the time controls listed here.

- Main P&F Tournament:
- Round 1: Game-45 + 5 seconds of time increment. This means each player has a total of 45 minutes to complete all moves in each game, plus each player gets an additional 5 seconds after completing each move.

- Rounds 2-4: Game-60 + 5 seconds of time increment.

- Blitz P&F Tournament: All games use a time control of Game-5, delay 0. You play two games each round. We will play 3 or 4 rounds, depending on the number of entries.

Ratings Used : Players will be paired using the higher of their US Chess over-the-board and online regular ratings found in the US Chess Rating Supplement for March 2026 (to be published by the US Chess Federation on or after Feb 21, 2025). Established ratings have priority over provisional ratings. Ratings from other systems such as FIDE or from another country will be considered, especially when a player has no US Chess rating. Ratings from platforms such as Chess.com, Chesskid.com, Lichess.com, and ICC are not used. The Chief TD makes the final decisions about all players’ ratings used in the tournament.
Awards : All awards are gift certificates to the onsite Chess Book & Equipment Store. There are no cash awards. Gift certificates must be redeemed onsite and cannot be exchanged for cash. Trophies/Plaques to Top 3 Parent-Child Teams.
Player Eligibility :

- The Parents & Friends event is not open to players eligible to compete in the College or Scholastic sections of the main tournament. You do not need to have a child playing in the main tournament to participate in our P&F events!

- A current US Chess Federation membership is required for all participants. Renew your US Chess membership or become a new US Chess member through the VA Chess Federation at www.vachess.org and select the “Join/Renew US Chess” tab on the left side of the screen. Joining the US Chess Federation through the VA Chess Federation saves you a little money.

The Houston Chess Studio

Friday, March 6, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

$2,500 MARCH CHAMPIONSHIP 2026
Open to Poison Pawn members AND non-members*
US CHESS RATED - MUST BE A US CHESS MEMBER TO PARTICIPATE
WHEN:  MARCH 6-8 or MARCH 7-8  Three-day or two-day schedule, take your pick.
WHERE: Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton St. Suite H, Houston TX 77009
FORMAT: 5 round Swiss, G/90, +30.  (round 1 of 2 day schedule is G/60,d5)
3 day schedule :  Round 1 at 6:30pm  Friday night . Round 2 at 1pm Saturday and Round 3 at 6pm.  Round 4 at 9:30 am Sunday and Round 5 at 2:00 pm.
2 day schedule :  Round 1 is at 9:30am  Saturday morning and is  G/60, d5.   Then merges with the 3 day schedule for rounds 2-5.
ENTRY FEE:  Non-members $105 thru Friday FEB 20TH; then $125 thru Wednesday MAR 4TH; $135 thereafter.  Poison Pawns club members $80 anytime!    For membership info contact Edgar at :  Click here to show mail address   GMs and IMs may enter free, their entry fee will be deducted from winnings.
2 SECTIONS:   Championship  (1900 and up);  Challengers  (U1900).
PLAYING UP:  If you are rated U1900 but are at least 1700 you may play up into the  Championship  section for $35.
PRIZE FUND $2,500 -   1st place in each section is guaranteed .  2nd place and 3rd place 25% OF ENTRY FEES   B/50. 15% BONUS FOR CLUB MEMBERS  in all sections combined.  Championship  1st $800 ; Challengers  1st $550 .  Un-rated may play in any section but are limited to winning $150 except in the top section where they are eligible for all prizes.  DRAWS PRIOR TO 30 MOVES AND BOTH PLAYERS ARE INELIGIBLE FOR ANY PRIZE MONEY!
ONLY MEMBERS OF POISON PAWNS CHESS CLUB ARE ONLY ELIGIBLE FOR 100% OF THE CASH PRIZES !  (So isn't it time you joined!)
CLICK HERE TO BECOME A MEMBER
CANCELLATION:  You may cancel up to 72 hours before the beginning of Round 1 and get a refund of what you paid minus $25, or you may apply the entire amount towards a future entry fee IF USED WITHIN 30-DAYS OF ORIGINAL EVENT .
BYES: One ½ point bye available, must be declared before the beginning of round 2.  No last round byes except for zero point byes.
RE-ENTRY:  If you are in the 3-day schedule, after round 1, you may re-enter immediately for $35 and be given a choice of a ½ point bye for round 1 OR you may choose to play in round 1 of the 2-day schedule.  If you are in the 2-day schedule you may re-enter immediately after round 1 and take a ½ point bye for round 1.
HOTEL INFO:    Holiday Inn Express , 3401 N. Main St., is less than a mile from The Studio. Phone 832-834-6197 and ask for The Houston Chess Studio discount, or if booking online use code ALDR9.  Also within a mile is the Heights House Hotel, an America’s Best Value, and a Luxury Inn .  Google them for info.
THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO:  is dedicated to providing a quality, high tech, chess playing experience for players of all levels.  Centrally and conveniently located at 250 Patton St., Suite H, Houston TX 77009.  Just inside North Loop 610 and just 2 blocks off North I-45.  There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway , and Patron Pizza .  Several others are within walking distance.  Plenty of FREE parking.
SCANNING  All players are subject to being scanned (“wanded”) in order to help prevent cheating. Any excessive visits to the bathroom will trigger a compulsory wand. Any player found with a phone or electronic device during a tournament game will be disqualified.

- Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

2026 Illinois K-8 State Championship
March 6 - 8, 2026
7SS, Hyatt Regency Schaumburg, 1800 E. Golf Rd., Schaumburg, IL 60173, (847) 605-1234
Rooms: $124 (single-quad), Free Wi-Fi at hotel, free parking, Near Woodfield Mall.
Reserve early here to get the rate  or call (847) 605-1234 and use code G-ILCH
Four Sections  – K-1 (G/25 d5), Grades 2-3 (G/40 d5), Grades 4-5 (G/55 d5), Grades 6-8 (G/55 d5).
Entry Fee:   Enter online here: https://www.kingregistration.com/event/2026ilk8
$50 on-line or postmarked USPS by 2/22/26; $60 on-line or postmarked by 3/1/26; $70 after that until 3/6/26 7 pm, $75 on-site (entries after 7:00pm 3/6/26 cannot be guaranteed pairing for round 1, instead they may receive 1/2 point bye round 1). Checks payable only to Chess Weekend.
Must be current USCF member by 8:30 am, 3/07 to be paired.
Note: Club teams are not allowed for this tournament. Only schools may be selected in the team field.
Awards:
Individual:  1st –25th Place in each section (K-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-8) INDIVIDUAL SECTION WINNER WILL ALSO RECEIVE A Custom Chess Clock. Grade Awards: 1st-2nd each grade.  Class Awards:  1st-2nd Place with several classes per section. Commemorative medal or ribbon to all players.  Teams:  1st-10th Place in each section. Special Sportsmanship trophy!
Schedule:  Opening Ceremony Sat., 3/07/26 at 9:30 am. K-1: Sat. 10-12:30-2-3:30, Sun. 9-10:30-12:30; Grades 2-3: Sat. 10-12:30-2:30-4:30 Sun. 9-11-1; Grades 4-5 & Grades 6-8: Sat. 10-12:45-3:15-5:45 Sun. 9-11:30-2.
Awards Ceremony:  Sun, 3/8/26, K-1: 2 pm in the K-1 playing room. 2-3, 4-5, 6-8 5:00 pm or ASAP in the main playing room.
Byes:  Maximum of 2 half-point byes are available. Zero-point bye only in the last round. Half-point byes must be requested by the end of the second round.
Side Events:  Click here to register for the side events .

- Bughouse Tournament  – Fri, 3/6/26, 6:15 – 7:45 pm. 5 round Swiss. Enter on-site only. $20 per team ($10 for individuals and we help you create a team) FREE INDIVIDUAL BUGHOUSE ENTRY WITH RECEIPT FOR BOTH BLITZ & PUZZLE SOLVING! Registration closes at 6 pm, Fri, 3/6/26. One section only, K-8. Bughouse Awards: 1st-3rd Place.

- Blitz Tournament  – 5 SS Fri, 3/6/26, 8-9:30 pm. 5 round Swiss.  $15  online  until 3/5/26. $20 after that or onsite. Registration onsite closes at 7:30 pm, 3/6/26. Blitz Awards: Individual: 1st-5th plus class awards.

- Puzzle Solving  – Saturday 3/7/26, 8:00 pm, $15 on-line by 3/6/26. $20 after that or onsite. Puzzle Solving Prizes: 1st-5th overall; 1st-5th U1000.

- Awards Ceremony for Blitz/Bughouse/Puzzle Solving:  Sun, 9 am.

Mailed entries:  Checks payable only to Chess Weekend (no checks to USCF): Mail registrations with name-contact info-grade-birthday-team/school-USCF ID & exp.-address-city-zip-e-mail address-coach name & contact info to: Glenn Panner, 21694 Doud Ct., Frankfort, IL 60423.
Entries:  $10 service charge for on-site changes, and all refunds. Book Vending by Rochester Chess.
Information:   Click here to show mail address ,  www.chessweekend.com
Pairings and Results will be available online during the tournament.
All special rules, details, and tournament conditions subject to change without notice; changes will be posted ASAP at the tournament site, at chessweekend.com, at il-chess.org, and at kingregistration.com.

2026 Virginia Scholastic and College Championships

Heritage Event, State Championship Event

Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology

Friday, March 6, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

2026 Virginia Scholastic & College
Chess Championships
hosted by Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology
Saturday-Sunday, March 7-8, 2026 -- 6560 Braddock Rd., Alexandria VA
WHAT : The Virginia Chess Federation (VCF) is partnering with Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology for the 2026 Virginia Scholastic & College Chess Championships.
WHEN : Saturday and Sunday, March 7-8, 2026, with a Blitz Tournament on Friday night, March 6th.
REGISTRATION : ONLINE at  www.vachess.org . Please do not contact TJ High School , they are relying on the VA Chess Federation to answer all questions about the tournament and event logistics. Registration Fees for the Blitz and Main tournament are as follows:

- Friday Night Blitz : An optional, but very fun event!!
- Scholastic Sections (Grades K-5 and 6-12): $35 through Feb 28th, $45 thereafter

- Parents & Friends Blitz: $20 through Feb 28th, $45 thereafter

- Main Tournament :
- All Scholastic & College Sections: $70 through Feb 28th, $90 from March 1-4, $110 thereafter.

- Parents & Friends Side Tournament: $30 through Feb 28th, $35 thereafter

HOTEL ARRANGEMENTS : TBD. We will seek agreements with hotels close to the High School. Details will be posted on the VCF website,  www.vachess.org .
MAIN EVENT FORMAT : These activities are on Sat and Sun, March 7th and 8th.

- 8 Scholastic Sections and 1 College Section : Round 1 is at 9 AM in all sections.
- College: Plays all games on Saturday, March 7th.

- K-12 Championship and K-12 Under 1400

- K-8 Championship and K-8 Under 1200

- K-5 Championship and K-5 Under 1000

- K-3 Championship and K-3 Under 600

- Side Events :
- Parents & Friends Tournament (starts 15 minutes after Round 2 in the Scholastic Sections ... e.g., 12:45 PM on Saturday)

- “Play the Master” simultaneous Exhibition on Saturday afternoon beginning about 2 PM.

TOURNAMENT SCHEDULE :

- Friday, March 6th : On-site Registration for the Main Event and Blitz. Round 1 of BLITZ is at 6:30 PM . Blitz is an optional event. Blitz is usually finished about 8:30 or 8:45 PM.

- Saturday, March 7th : Round 1 at 9 AM . Rounds 2-3 at 12:30 pm and 4:30 pm. College Section games are at 9, noon, 3 pm, and 6 pm. Parents & Friends tournament starts at 12:45.

- Sunday, March 8th : Rounds 4-5 at 9:30 am and 1:30 pm. Awards Ceremonies held section-by-section as soon as possible after the last game finishes in a section.
- NOTE: We remind everyone that Daylight Savings Time begins Sunday, March 8th .

TEAMS : Scholastic and College Teams must be comprised of players who attend the same school. A school is not required to have a “chess club” or an “official school team” to play as a team for this tournament. Two or more players who go to the same school and play in the same section of the tournament are automatically considered a team for this tournament. You can find detailed team eligibility information on the VA Chess website at  this helpful link .
PLAYER ELIGIBILITY :

- Scholastic Sections : All players in the Scholastic sections (K-12, K-8, K-5, K-3) must be attending school in Virginia or be a VA resident attending school out-of-state. Players attending an out-of-state school cannot compete as a team-- all teams must be Virginia-based schools . Players from neighboring states who attend school in VA are eligible to compete. Please check with us if you have questions!

- College Section : Players must be attending college in VA or be a VA resident attending college out of state. All college players must be high school graduates. High school students who are attending college cannot compete on a College team.

- U.S. Chess Federation membership is required for all players. Players can join US Chess or renew their membership through the VCF at  www.vachess.org and select the “Join/Renew US Chess” tab on the left side of our webpage. We offer a small discount on US Chess Federation membership. If you prefer, you also can join/renew your US Chess membership directly with US Chess, go to  www.uschess.org and hover your cursor over the “Join” option near the top of your screen.

AWARDS : Tons of trophies! See  www.vachess.org
IMPORTANT : The VCF uses the results of this tournament to select representatives to attend the US national tournaments of State Champions. These tournaments (see list below) will be held in early August as part of the U.S. Open in Grand Rapids, Michigan. The VCF provides healthy stipends to assist the 5 Virginia players who earn the right to represent The Commonwealth at these tournaments.

- Denker Tournament of High School State Champions (Top Player in Grades 9-12 from the K-12 Section)

- Barber Tournament of Middle School State Champions (Top Player in Grades 6-8, from the K-8 Section)

- Rockefeller Tournament of Elementary School State Champions (Top Player in Grades 4-5, from K-5)

- NEW for 2026 : Maurice Ashley Tournament of Primary School State Champions (Top Player in K-3)

- Haring Tournament of Girls State Champions (Top finishing Girl from Virginia’s K-12 Section)

FUN SIDE EVENTS :

- BLITZ on Friday evening March 6th (Round 1 at 6:30 pm). 4 double-rounds (2 games per round for 8 total games). Includes a Parents & Friends section.

- 4-round “Parents & Friends” tournament open to adults. Scholastic or college players are NOT eligible to play in this event.

- “Challenge the Master” Simultaneous Exhibition.

TEAM ROOMS : See  www.vachess.org . We are working with the TJ High School administration to obtain about 15 classrooms that can be used by teams with 10 or more players as well as by parents who wish to form a group in order to get a team room. Please do not contact the school for any information about this, the school relies on the VA Chess Federation to collect and consolidate all Team Room requests. The cost for a Team Room is $100 per room of which $25 is returned to you after the tournament and $75 is used to purchase a Gift Card for the teachers whose rooms we use.
PRE-EVENT ZOOM INFO MEETINGS : The VCF will organize several options for players and parents to attend a pre-event Zoom Meeting in mid-to-late February 2026. These events will be announced on our website and emails sent to all registered players.
QUESTIONS : Contact Mike Hoffpauir, VA Chess Federation,  Click here to show mail address or text to 757-846-4805.
The Virginia Chess Federation (VCF) is the US Chess Federation’s State Affiliate for Virginia
The VCF is a 501c(3) non-profit organization

Alexandria , VA 22312

33rd annual Western Class Championships

Heritage Event, Grand Prix, Enhanced Grand Prix, Junior Grand Prix

Hilton Orange County Airport Hotel

Friday, March 6, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

A Heritage Event!
US Chess Junior Grand Prix
MAR 6-8 OR 7-8,  2026  CALIFORNIA SOUTHERN
US CHESS GRAND PRIX POINTS: 120 (ENHANCED)
33rd annual Western Class Championships. 5-SS, 40/80, SD/30; d30 (2-day option, rounds. 1-2 G/60, d10), Hilton Orange County Airport, 18800 Macarthur Blvd, Irvine, CA 92612. Chess Rate Parking: $20. Free wireless, pool, airport shuttle, fitness center. $20,000 guaranteed prizes!   In 7 sections. Master (2100/up): $2000-1000-500-300, clear or tiebreak winner $100 bonus, top USCF U2300 $800-400. FIDE. Expert  (1900-2199): $1500-700-400-200. FIDE. Class A  (1700-1999): $1500-700-400-200. FIDE. Class B (1500-1799/Unr): $1500-700-400-200. Class C  (1300-1599/Unr): $1200-600-300-200. Class D  (1100-1399/Unr): $1000-500-300-200. Class E  (Under 1200/Unr): $600-300-200-100. These overlapping class rating boundaries  already include players rated in the top half of the section below.  Unrated may not win over $100 in E, $200 D, $300 C, $400 B. Mixed Doubles Bonus Prizes:  best male+female 2-player combined team score among all sections: $500-300-200. Team must average under 2200; may play different sections and schedules, register at site (no extra fee) by 2 pm Sat, Prize limits do not apply to Mixed Doubles prizes, limit one Mixed Doubles team per player. March Official Ratings used; unofficial uschess.org ratings  or USCF Online Regular Ratings usually used if otherwise unrated (see also peakrating.us). Cannot play below USCF Online Regular rating minus 100 points. Top 6 sections EF: $138 online at chessaction.com by 3/3, $160 later online or at site until 1 hour before round 1. Class E EF: all $40 less than top 6 sections. Online advance EF $5 less to SCCF members; join/renew at scchess.com. GMs: $120 from prize. No checks ; credit cards OK. All:   Special 1-year USCF dues with magazine paid online at chessaction.com with entry: Adult $54, Senior (age 65+) $48, Young Adult $33, Youth $24. Re-entry (no Master to Master) $60.  3-day schedule:  Reg. Fri to 6 pm, rounds Fri 7, Sat 11 & 5, Sun 10 & 3:30. 2-day schedule:  Reg. Sat to 10 am, rounds Sat 11, 2 & 5, Sun 10 & 3:30. Byes: OK all rounds, limit 2; must commit before round 2. HR: $172-172-172-172 Fri-Sun, higher other days, use link at  chessevents.us (or call 949-833-9999, mention Chess rate); reserve by 2/14 or rate may increase. Car rental:  Avis, 800-331-1600, use AWD #D657633. Questions: chesstour.com, [email protected] . Enter online:  chessaction.com. No mail entries. Prizes not claimed at site usually paid by PayPal (may take a couple of weeks). Refunds,  $15 service charge. Entries posted at chessaction.com (click “entry list” after entering). Bring set, clock, board if possible— no equipment supplied.  Blitz tournament Sat. 9:30 pm, enter onsite Sat. by 9:10 pm.

Irvine , CA 92612

United States

Monthly Saturday Swiss

Phoenix Chess Academy

Saturday, March 7, 2026

Event Overview

4 round Swiss. Game in 25 minutes with 5 sec delay. Boards, sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided.
Registration: Go to www.phoenixchessacademy.com.  USCF membership is required. New or renewing USCF members are welcome. Highest rating will be used for Swiss pairings and prize purposes.
Entry Fee: $25.00 by Wednesday; $30 by Friday; $35 same day.
Prizes: Trophies for top three in each section.
Sections: Open, Under 1700 & Under 1200 (No playing up allowed). Sections will be combined in case a section has less than 4 players registered.
Schedule: Round 1- 2:30 PM, Round 2- 3:35 PM, Round 3- 4:40 PM, Round 4- 5:45 PM. Awards Ceremony will start right after last game is over. Half point Byes are available in all 4 rounds and (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. Requesting a zero-point bye late in the tournament is considered the same as withdrawing.
Refund Policy: Full refund will be issued to players who withdraw at least an hour before the first round. In cases where a registered player does not show up for the tournament without prior notice, they will not be eligible for a refund.
A player will automatically forfeit the game if going in the bathroom with a cellphone.

Denny's Restaurant

Saturday, March 7, 2026

Event Overview

Saturday March 7, 2026
Denny’s Restaurant
1615 N. Main St.
Normal, IL 61761
3 Rounds, Round Robin, G55 + 10
Players will be placed in sections of 4 players in rating order (in the case of the total number of players being not divisible by 4, a small swiss section may be created).
Check your rating here:  https://ratings.uschess.org/
USCF Quick, Blitz, or any FIDE/foreign ratings may be used for section eligibility purposes for players without a regular rating.
US Chess Membership is Required. All US Chess Rules will be followed.
Eligibility: Players must be in high school or older (players younger than high school may participate if they have a US Chess rating over 1200; these players must be accompanied at the tournament site by a parent/guardian at all times and supervised when not playing).
Entry Fee: $15, Cash only
Pre register at by emailing  Click here to show mail address with name and US Chess ID#.
Prizes: 1st Place in Each Section - $50
Schedule:  Onsite Registration and Check-In 9:00am-9:45am | 1st Round 10:00am; subsequent rounds ASAP; break for lunch after 2nd round.
Due to the nature of round robin pairings, registrations after 9:45am cannot be accommodated
If you discover on the tournament date that you cannot play, please contact the organizer.
Please contact the tournament organizer if you have any questions.

Mar. '26 Palmetto Scholastic Chess League

Columbia Chess Club

Saturday, March 7, 2026

Event Overview

WWW.COLUMBIACHESS.ORG
A Premier Monthly Scholastic Tournament Series
The Columbia Chess Club organizes the Palmetto Scholastic Chess League (PSCL) as a regular monthly tournament series to encourage the organization of scholastic chess clubs and to promote scholastic chess throughout the state! Separate sections for High School, Middle School, and Elementary School provides balanced competition and encourages players to form teams representing their school to win awards. See past winners of the PSCL .

Conveniently Scheduled, Easy to Enter
PSCL events occur once a month on a Saturday. Games start at 10:00 a.m. and finish before lunch . The games are officially rated by US Chess , meaning that all players will be nationally ranked after playing ( for example, see scholastic player Charlie Jordan's US Chess profile ). If you are already a US Chess member, it's only $20 to enter.
First Timers Get a US Chess Membership!
For those playing their first US Chess tournament, registration is $25, which includes a US Chess membership that the Columbia Chess Club will create for you! (A youth membership itself costs $24 from US Chess as of January 1, 2025).

Register Online Now

First-Class Facilities
The Columbia Chess Club is located at 6169 St Andrews Road, Columbia, SC and is the vision of passionate chess players who wanted to create the perfect atmosphere to play chess. Wood pieces, specially-designed chess tables, a well-appointed spectator lounge with concessions, and state-of-the-art technology displaying real-time results and video of the top boards make the Columbia Chess Club the place to play chess.

Tournament Details:
Online Registration
Online registration only. Standard Registration is $20 for players with US Chess memberships. First-time tournament players $25, which includes a US Chess membership that the club will create for you using the email you provide at registration. Registration limited to first 74 players.  If you need to renew your existing US Chess membership, please visit  https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess.

Register Online Now

Format
4-Round Swiss.
Time Control: G/10;+5.
Sections: High School, Middle School, and Elementary School.
4-Round Swiss means that players play all 4 rounds and are not eliminated. Each player will play with a 10 minute starting time and will get an additional 5 seconds with each move. (G/10;+5). This will affect the player's US Chess "Quick" rating. All equipment provided. Tournament has three sections: High School (9-12), Middle School (6-8), Elementary School (K-5). Players must register with the section corresponding to their grade. We reserve the right  to combine sections during play, but prizes will be awarded separately for each section.
Rules Modification: For this tournament, USCF Rule 14K(2) is modified such that a Tournament Director may declare a game drawn after 50 moves without a capture or pawn move, rather than 75. We reserve the right to use a player's live rating for pairing purposes.  For blitz tiebreaks, Blitz Rule 7(d) is modified such that a player's first illegal move results in a 1-minute penalty, standard Blitz Rule 7(d) applying on any subsequent illegal move by that player (i.e. a second illegal move is a loss if opponent has sufficient mating material).

Schedule
Round 1: 10:00 a.m.
Round 2: 10:35 a.m.
Round 3: 11:10 a.m.
Round 4: 11:45 a.m.
Awards: 12:15 p.m.
Can't make every round? We can give you one 1/2 point bye for any round if you let us know in the registration comments or before the tournament starts.
Awards:
Team Trophies
Trophies to first and second place teams in each of High School, Middle School, and Elementary School sections . The top three players from each school have their points combined to form a team score. The school with the highest team score wins.  Results will be reported to school administration. Homeschooling students may register with the school for which they are zoned.

Individual Trophies
The top five players from each of the High School, Middle School, and Elementary School sections receive individual trophies. In the event of a tie for first, a blitz playoff is played between the players tied to determine first place. US Chess tiebreaks are used otherwise.

Superlative Awards
Special Awards to:

- Biggest Upset

- Top Female Performance

- Youngest Participant

- Best First Tournament

Please reach us at Click here to show mail address if you cannot find an answer to your question.

2026 Texas Scholastic “Super State” Championship

State Championship Event

DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Austin

Saturday, March 7, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

2026 Texas Scholastic “Super State” Championship
March 7, 2026 to March 8, 2026
DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Austin
6505 N Interstate 35, Austin, TX, 78752
Registration is limited to the first 800 players.

Sections
K-1 Championship
Primary K-3 JV (U700)
Primary K-3 Championship
Elementary School K-5/6 JV* (U800)
Elementary School K-5/6 Championship*
Middle School 6-8 JV (U900)
Middle School 6-8 Championship
High School 9-12 JV (U1000)
High School 9-12 Championship

Eligibility
The event is open only to Texas residents with a valid US Chess (valid through March 2026) and TCA membership. All sections are US Chess rated, and the March 2026 US Chess rating supplement will be used for pairings and prizes.
Winners of the Championship sections will earn official Texas State Champion titles. The top finishers in key sections will also qualify for the  2026 Texas Junior Invitational , and team results determine qualification for the  2026 Lone Star Cup .

Entry Fees
$65 by February 7, $75 by February 21, $85 by March 6 by 9pm, Onsite $95 with 1st round bye.

Hotel Information
DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Austin
6505 N Interstate 35, Austin, TX, 78752

Prizes
Individuals
Top 20 per section
Team:
Top 50% teams per section of 4 players registered by February 21, 2026

Tiebreaks
Modified Median, Solkoff, Cumulative, Cumulative of Opposition

Forfeit Rule
Players who fail to appear within 30 minutes of round start forfeit the game unless the Chief TD otherwise provides for good cause.

SCHEDULE
Primary/Elementary/Middle School/High School
Saturday, March 7 (G/60,d5)
Round 1 – 9:00am
Round 2 – 12:00pm
Round 3 – 3:00pm
Round 4 – 6:00pm
Sunday, March 8 (G/75,d5)
Round 5 – 9:00am
Round 6 – 12:30pm
Round 7 – 3:30pm
Awards  – 6:30pm
K-1 (G/45)
Saturday, March 7 (G/45,d5)
Round 1 – 10:00am
Round 2 – 12:30pm
Round 3 – 2:30pm
Round 4 – 4:30pm
Sunday, March 8 (G/45,d5)
Round 5 – 10:00am
Round 6 – 12:30pm
Round 7 – 2:30pm
Awards – 5:00pm

Pairings will be posted online 40 minutes before round start.
All changes must be submitted through the  Change Request Form 60 minutes prior to each round starting.

Side Events
Texas Scholastic Blitz Championship: March 6th 7:00pm. The entry fee is $20. Rated.
Texas Scholastic Bughouse Championship: March 7th 8:00pm. $40 per team.
Texas Scholastic Puzzles Championship: TBD. The entry fee is $20.
TCA Junior Chess Meeting: This is a business meeting where members will hear reports from officers and vote on important business affecting the Association. All TCA members who are Texas residents and at least 16 years of age are voting members. Everyone is welcome to attend. An agenda will be posted on the TCA website at least two weeks in advance.

Other Rules and Information
Chess sets provided; bring your own clock
Notation required except for K-1 and Primary JV. Time deduction will be ⅓ of your time for no notation. Must use tournament provided notation.
Food and drinks are not allowed in the playing hall. Water is the only exception.
Players may request up to two half-point byes before the end of Round 3. All bye requests after will be 0 points.
No electronic devices (except necessary medical equipment and clocks).
Players may use electronic notation devices endorsed by US Chess.
Only players whose game is in progress, tournament directors and staff, TCA officers, and press are allowed in the hall during rounds.
Refunds available until March 4th, subject to a $20 fee.
Only Texas residents are eligible for state champion titles.
Players requiring accommodations due to disability or religious reasons should contact the organizer as soon as possible, preferably at least two weeks before the tournament.

I invite you to participate in the  2025–2026 Gold Country Chess Kids Spring Chess Tournament.  Only three students are needed to form a school team , making participation accessible for schools of all sizes.

Students will compete for both team and individual awards, promoting critical thinking, teamwork, and school pride while connecting schools through friendly competition.

1st, 2nd, and 3rd team & individual trophies for each section.

9-12 High School Championship

Please bring a tournament chess set and a chess clock if you have one.  Please be familiar with your clock.
Format: Five Round Swiss System (maybe four, depending on turn-out)
Time Control: 35 minutes per side, sudden death (Dual Rated)
Match Type: Dual Clock timing; players are responsible for their own clocks.

Please arrive 30 minutes early to sign in and attend orientation.

Round 2: 10:15 AM-11:25 AM

Saturday, March 7, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

Scholastic State Championship Event
Any student enrolled in an Ohio school or home schooled in Ohio in grades K-12 is eligible to participate; 12 sections for players of all skill levels!

Elementary/Primary Sections: SATURDAY ONLY

- Elementary Championship (K-5) 5 Rounds: G/45; d5 The winner qualifies for the Rockefeller and receives a $300 stipend.

- Primary Championship (K-3) 5 Rounds: G/30; d5 The winner qualifies for the Ashley and receives a $300 stipend.

- U1000 (K-5), U700 (K-5), U400 (3-5), U400 (K-2): 5 Rounds: G/30; d5

High School/Middle School Sections: SATURDAY AND SUNDAY

- High School Championship (9-12) 6 Rounds. Rounds 1-4: G/60; d5. Rds. 5-6: G/90; d5 The winner qualifies for the Denker and receives a $300 stipend.

- Middle School Championship (6-8) 6 Rounds. Rounds 1-4: G/60; d5. Rds. 5-6: G/90; d5 The winner qualifies for the Barber and receives a $300 stipend.

- U1400 (6-12), U1000 (9-12), U1000 (6-8), U600 (6-12). 6 Rounds: G/60; d5

Free year-long USCF membership included for players with new or expired memberships! Progress With Chess will provide clocks for all Championship sections and 6-12 U1400, sets and boards provided for all sections. Up to two half-point byes available (no last round); must request before round two pairings are posted. USCF March Supplement ratings will determine section eligibility. Provisional or online ratings may be used for unrated players.
Free Ohio Blitz Championship Saturday 8:15 PM to determine Ohio High School, Middle School and Elementary Blitz Champions!! Individual trophies for the Winners. Under 1000 and Under 600 Sections as well!

Online Registration at  progresswithchess.org/ohstate
Entry fee:  $45 received by 3/4/26, $50 after.   No onsite entries!
Online registration will close at 6 PM on Friday, 3/6/26.
Discounted entry for students for students in financial need, contact Mike at (216) 321-7000.

Schedule
Doors open at 8:00 AM. No section changes after 9:00 AM. Announcements at 9:50 AM.
Elementary K-5 Championship Section (SATURDAY) Round 1: 10 AM

Round 2: 12 PM

Round 3: 1:45 PM

Round 4: 3:30 PM

Round 5: 5:15 PM

Primary K-3 Championship, U1000 (K-5), U700 (K-5), U400 (3-5), U400 (K-2) Sections (SATURDAY) Round 1: 10 AM

Round 2: 11:30 AM

Time Trouble March RAPID

Columbia Chess Club

Saturday, March 7, 2026

Event Overview

Time Trouble March Rapid
Time Trouble is a recurring tournament on scheduled Saturday afternoons from 2 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. Time Trouble is formatted on an alternating schedule as either a Rapid G/10+5, 5-Round Swiss or a Blitz G/3+2, 6-Round Double Swiss, depending on the scheduled Saturday. $400 Prize Pool b/30.

REGISTRATION
Standard registration is $20. Paid club members are $15. "Paid Club Member" rates are for players with Columbia Chess Club Memberships only. See our website if you are interested in becoming a member of the Columbia Chess Club .
Entry for titled players (National Master and above) is free, standard entry fee deducted from prizes. If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout.

Register Online Now

K-12 Player? Consider playing in our Palmetto Scholastic Chess League during the morning before Time Trouble.   More Details >>

SCHEDULE
RAPID SATURDAY SCHEDULE (G/10;+5, 5-Round Swiss):

- Round 1: 2:00 p.m.

- Round 2: 2:45 p.m.

- Round 3: 3:30 p.m.

- Round 4: 4:15 p.m.

- Round 5: 5:00 p.m.

- Estimated Completion 5:30 p.m.

FORMAT
Rapid Tournament : 5-Round Swiss. Time control is G/10+5 (10 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment), which will be USCF Quick rated.
All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit  https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess.
Rules Note: Per USCF Rule 28T, the pairing system will avoid pairing players registered under the same team during the first-half of the event.

PRIZES
$400 b/30*
1st: $100 ; 2nd: $80 ; 3rd: $60 ; 4th: $40
Top Under 1800: $40
Top Under 1300: $40
Top Under 800: $40
Players that are unrated in the applicable USCF rating category (Blitz or Quick) are not eligible for rating-based prizes.
*Based on 30 players, meaning that 50% of all prizes are guaranteed and scale with participation to the amount shown.

BYES
A single half-point bye is available any round (1-point bye in double Swiss format), including the final round. The bye may be requested as a part of the advance entry or on site before the tournament starts. Thereafter the only bye available is a zero-point bye. The chief tournament director shall have the ability to grant a half-point bye for any round on unusual circumstances.

LIVE STREAMING
Time Trouble tournaments will be live-streamed to the club's Twitch channel , and thereafter archived at the club's YouTube channel .
