Mississippi Scholastic Chess Association – 2025 Team Tournament Regulations

- INTRODUCTION
- To foster consistency between state and national-level scholastic events, the US Chess Federation encourages state scholastic organizations to adopt the National Scholastic Chess Tournament Regulations for all state scholastic championships.  However, the national tournament regulations deal with a great many details and situations that are not likely to be relevant at any of our state team tournaments, so what follows is a summary of the national regulations that will be applied.

- The Mississippi Scholastic Chess Association (MSCA) Team Tournament Regulations are intended to fulfill the needs and expectations of players, coaches and parents at our scholastic team chess events.

- ELIGIBILITY
- Age and Grade Eligibility.  The following ages are as of September 1 of the school year in which the competition takes place. These age requirements are considered upper bounds for each grade . Our events are grade-based and require all players to play in a section that allows for their current grade.

- Kindergarten: 6 years old

- 1st Grade: 7 years old

- 7th Grade: 13 years old

- 2nd Grade: 8 years old

- 8th Grade: 14 years old

- 3rd Grade: 9 years old

- 9th Grade: 15 years old

- 4th Grade: 10 years old

- 10th Grade: 16 years old

- 5th Grade: 11 years old

- 11th Grade: 17 years old

- 6th Grade: 12 years old

- 12th Grade 18 years old

- There shall only be one year of eligibility per grade level unless one of the following situations applies:
- Pre-schoolers may play as Kindergarteners in any event section. Kindergartners and Pre-schoolers may continue to play as Kindergartners in subsequent years until they start the first grade.

- Players who repeat a grade in school may have a second year of eligibility in that grade as long as they are age-eligible for that grade.

- TEAM REQUIREMENTS

- MSCA team tournaments are individual tournaments with team scoring. A student who does not qualify to represent a team can compete only as an individual.

- A team is comprised of students who attend the same school.  ( Students may “play up” for a school team in the same feeder pattern.  i.e.  an elementary student can play on a middle school team if that middle school is the school they will be attending in the future according to the feeder pattern )
- A school is defined as an institution which has one name, is located in one building or connected adjacent buildings, and is under one on-site administrator and which provides core curricular instruction in English, math, science, and social studies.

- A student will be considered to attend a school if and only if he or she physically attends classes at that school building and receives more than 50% of his or her core curricular instruction during those classes.

- Each school may enter only one team per section .

- Teams may also be comprised of home schooled or virtual school students.
- A home schooled student is defined as a student who receives at least 50% of his or her core curricular instruction at home.  Virtual school students are students who receive more than 50% of their core curricular instruction on-line, but not in a school building.

- A home schooled or virtual school student has the following two options for participating on a scholastic chess team:

- The student may join with other home schooled or virtual school students who reside within the boundary of the same local public school as defined in 3.2.

- The student may join with other home schooled students who physically attend the same instructional program.

- There may be more than one home school or virtual school team per recognized public school district.

- A scholastic team must contain a minimum of two players to be eligible for team prizes.

- There is no maximum number of players who may compete on a team, but only the top four(4) scores in any section count for team score.

- The coach, an adult team representative, or the ‘Team Captain’ is responsible for assuring that all of the team’s players are properly registered and eligible to participate as members of the team.

- TOURNAMENT FORMAT
- Mississippi scholastic team tournaments are individual tournaments with team scoring . Accordingly, they are paired as individual Swiss System tournaments , with individual scores added to create team scores.  Whenever a rated section has more than 2N players, where “N” is the number of rounds, the TD will consider using accelerated pairings.

- The combined total of the top four scoring players from the same school determines that team’s score.

- Players from the same team will not be paired together unless no other reasonable natural pairing can be made.

- When conflicts occur between individual pairings and team considerations – and where the top awards are at stake – individual pairings shall have higher priority.

- Points from unrated games shall compile toward team score as such:  1 win = 1 point, 1 draw = 0.5 point

- Points from RATED games shall compile toward team score as such:  1 win = 2 points, 1 draw = 1 point

Therefore, RATED play will count MORE toward your team score!

- RATING SUPPLEMENT

- For events starting before the 10th of the month , the previous month’s Rating Supplement will be used.
- For events starting on or after the 10th of the month , the current month’s Rating Supplement will be used.

- CHESS NOTATION
- The use of approved electronic notation devices is permitted.

- Chess notation is not currently required in any unrated sections but it is required for the rated sections (until one player has under 5 minutes, then notation for both can stop)

- TIE-BREAKS
- Computer programs are used to determine pairings, standings and tie-breaks for all sections.

- All players tied for first place are considered co-winners, but trophies will be awarded based on tie-breaks.

- Tie-breaks are used only to award trophies. Players or teams with like scores are equal and may change the plate on their trophy to reflect this (at their own cost).

- When individual or team scores are equal, the following order of tie-break systems will be used to designate awards:

- Modified Median

- Solkoff

- Cumulative Score

- Opposition Cumulative Score

- Head-to-Head

- Coin Flip

Directions: If you wish to drive to the Colvard Student Union for drop-off or pick-up, it is recommended that the building be approached from the South via Tracy Dr. and Lee Blvd.  Parking in the immediate area is limited, so please allow enough time to walk from another parking lot if necessary.

58th annual New York State Scholastic Championships, OPEN TO GRADES K-8 ONLY

Heritage Event, American Classic, Junior Grand Prix, State Championship Event

Saratoga Hilton Hotel and 3 other nearby locations

Saturday, March 7, 2026
- Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

An American Classic!
A Heritage Event!
US Chess Junior Grand Prix!
A State Championship Event!
MAR 7-8, 2026.  NEW YORK.
58th annual New York State Scholastic Championships  (out of state players allowed but with prize restrictions)-- OPEN TO GRADES K-8 ONLY. See separate TLA, 2/28-3/1, for NY State High School Championship , for grades 9-12 (grades 6-8 also permitted on 2/28-3/1, but with some prize restrictions). 6-SS, G/60, d10, top NYS player and team in each Championship section are NY State Champions. In 12 separate sections:  1). Middle School (K-8) Championship  (top NYS grade 6-8 born after 9/1/10 qualifies for Barber National Tournament of State K-8 Champions), 2). K-8 Under 1700 Section, 3). K-8 Under 1300, 4). K-8 Under 900; 5). Elementary (K-5) Championship  (top NYS player born after 9/1/13 qualifies for Rockefeller National Tournament of State K-5 Champions), 6). K-5 Under 1400, 7). K-5 Under 1000 , 8). K-5 Under 600; 9). Primary (K-3) Championship (top NYS grade K-3 born after 9/1/15 qualifies for Ashley National Tournament of State K-3 Champions), 10). K-3 Under 800; 11). K-1 Championship, 12). K-1 Under 400 Section.  In four separate playing locations: Saratoga Hilton Hotel (K-3 Under 800, K-1 Championship, K-1 Under 400 sections), 534 Broadway, I-87 Exit 13-N, 4 miles north on US 9 (Hilton Chess parking rate: $6 daytime, $12 overnight); Saratoga Springs City Center (K-8 Under 900, K-5 Under 1400, K-5 Under 1000, K-5 Under 600, K-3 Championship), adjacent to Saratoga Hilton Hotel (connected by indoor walkway), 522 Broadway; Saratoga Music Hall (K-5 Championship Section), 2½ blocks south of Convention Center at 474 Broadway; Courtyard By Marriott Hotel (K-8 Championship, K-8 Under 1700, K-8 Under 1300), 11 Excelsior Ave., 2/5 mile north of Saratoga Hilton; Saratoga Springs, NY 12866. Some K-5 Under 1400 Section games might also be played at Saratoga Music Hall.  Sections at Hilton/City Center may be limited to a total of 1200 players, sections at Marriott may be limited 340 players, section(s) at Music Hall may be limited to 220 players. Team prizes based on top 4 scores from same school, teams of 2 or 3 allowed, but are at a disadvantage. Players are subject to the specific rating and grade requirements for each section (Championship sections open to all players meeting grade requirements); the four Middle School (K-8) sections are open to players in grades 8 and below; the four Elementary (K-5) sections are open to players in grades 5 and below; the two Primary (K-3) sections are open to players in grades 3 and below; the two K-1 sections are open to players grades 1/below; unrated players meeting grade requirements allowed in any section. Online entry fee at chessaction.com,  all sections (space permitting) :  $120 per player by 2/7/26, $160 by 2/23. REGISTRATION MAY CLOSE PRIOR TO THESE DATES DUE TO SPACE LIMITATIONS. Entries may be subject to wait list. If  registration is still open,  entry fee after 2/23 until advance registration closes is $200. On-site entries: $250 and may not be available this year.    USCF Membership Required. Special 1-year USCF dues if paid online with entry: see chessaction.com. Trophies, plaques or medals to top 10 players & top 5 teams each section, top 2 unrated in U900, U800, U600 & U400, top 2 each U1800, U1600, U1400 (K-8 Championship), U1500, (K-8 U1700), U1100 (K-8 U1300), U700, U500, U300 (K-8 U900), U1700, U1500 (K-5 Championship), U1200, U1000 (K-5 U1400), U800, U700 (K-5 U1000), U500, U400, U300 (K-5 U600), U1400, U1200, U1000 (K-3 Championship), U600, U500, U400, U300 (K-3 U800), U800, U600, U400 (K-1), U300, U200 (K-1 U400). Speed playoff if 6-0 tie. Free/reduced entry fee prizes to all CCA OTB tournaments (only for players residing in NY and/or attending NY schools) : Championship sections: 8 months 1st, 6 months 2nd, 4 months 3rd & 4th. Other sections: 6 months 1st, 4 months 2nd, 3 months 3rd & 4th. 2 months bonus entries to NY players with 6-0 scores. Some CCA events also have minimum rating requirements and/or additional surcharges, based on rating, to play in the top sections; the free/reduced entry fee prizes do not cover any such additional surcharges for playing in the top sections. Schedule: Rounds begin Sat 11, 2, 5; Sun 9, 12, 3. Awards: about 5:30 pm Sun. Recipients responsible for arranging delivery and/or replacement of awards not claimed at site. Half point byes OK all, limit 2, must commit before round 2. HR:see chessevents.us for rates, minimum stay and other details (hotel reservations links at chessevents.us should be open by mid-November or sooner). Hotels may sell out very quickly but could have availability much later due to late cancellations. For backup hotels see chessevents.us. Special car rentals:  Avis, 800-331-1600, use AWD #D657633. $15 per player service charge for refunds. Section switches subject to $20 extra charge after 2/23 (all substitutions from advance list subject to space limitations and charged late fee), no section switching or substitutions after 5 pm 3/5. Questions: chesstour.com, [email protected] . Bring digital clock if possible- none supplied. March official ratings used  (except unofficial USCF ratings or USCF Online Regular ratings usually used if otherwise unrated). Players with USCF Online Regular ratings over 100 points over their OTB ratings may be assigned higher tournament rating and may be required to play in higher section (TD may use USCF Scholastic Regulations for eligibility guidance). TD reserves right to assign estimated rating to players with non-USCF ratings. Electronic devices rules:  Electronic scorekeeping devices not allowed. See also www.devicerules.com; players may not possess cellphones during play but may store them in bag under table. Entry:  www.chessaction.com . No mail entries. Blitz tournament: 8 pm Sat, enter at site Sat by 7:40 pm.

Southern Nevada Scholastic Chess Championships

State Championship Event

Del Sol Academy of the Performing Arts

Saturday, March 7, 2026

Event Overview

Silver State Chess Association LLC
Presents
SOUTHERN NEVADA STATE SCHOLASTIC
INDIVIDUAL AND TEAM CHAMPIONSHIPS
and QUALIFIER to NEVADA STATE SCHOLASTIC CHESS CHAMPIONSHIPS
Date: Saturday, March 7th, 2026 @ 8:45am
IMPORTANT: Both the Southern portion of the state (defined below) and the Northern portion of the state will hold separate Over-The-Board tournaments to determine individuals and teams from each region who will then compete in the Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship to be held on dates to be determined.
Individuals who reside in, or go to school in, the following Nevada counties will be eligible to participate in the Southern Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship: Clark, Nye, Lincoln and Esmerelda.
This announcement is for the Southern Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship. The Northern Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship will be held on a different day and will be detailed in a separate announcement.

Location:
Del Sol Academy of the Performing Arts
3100 E Patrick Ln
Las Vegas, NV 89120

To register please visit www.kingregistration.com/event/2026SNVSCh

A US Chess Rated Tournament in 6 Sections open to Southern Nevada residents or Southern Nevada students in the counties listed above.
K-3 Championship (Open to all players in grades K – 3)
K-5 Championship  ( Open to all players in grades K – 5)
6 rounds
Time Control Game/25 minutes +5 seconds
Middle School Championship (Open to all players in grades 6 – 8)
High School Championship (Open to all players in grades 9 – 12)
5 rounds
Time Control Game/30 minutes +10 seconds

K-5 Challengers (Open to all players in grades K – 5 rated Under 400 or unrated)
K-12 Challengers  ( Open to all players in grades K – 12 rated Under 800 or unrated)
6 rounds
Time Control Game/25 minutes +5 seconds
Individual and Team Trophies will be Awarded!
All players will receive a participation medal. Trophies will also be awarded.
Qualifiers
The top three individual scorers in each of the six Sections in the Southern Nevada Scholastic Chess Championship will meet on a date to be determined to compete in the Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship (individuals), an online tournament that includes the Southern Nevada individual qualifiers and the Northern Nevada individual qualifiers. We will provide digital tablets for that tournament. The winners of the four sections: High School, Middle School, K-5 Championship, and K-3 Championship from that tournament will represent the State of Nevada at national tournaments to be held on August 3-6 in Grand Rapids, Michigan.  Nevada State representatives will each receive a travel stipend from Silver State Chess after completing all games in the national tournament without a forfeit loss.
The top two scoring teams in each Section in the Southern Nevada Scholastic Chess Championship will meet on a date to be determined to compete in the Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship (teams), an online tournament that includes the Southern Nevada team qualifiers and the Northern Nevada team qualifiers. We will provide digital tablets for that tournament. The winning teams will not qualify for any national tournament because there is no national team tournament for which to qualify.
Additional Prizes
The top scoring player in each section will receive free entry to the  International Youth Championship in Las Vegas  June 13-14. Restricted to players born after June 14, 2011 and rated under 1800.
The second-place finishers in all six sections will receive an entry to a future one-day tournament of their choice at Southern Nevada Chess Club in Las Vegas.  The high school second place finisher may choose the Thursday night series instead of a one-day tournament.  The free entry offer expires 12/31/26.  Visit https://snvchess.com for more information about tournaments at the Southern Nevada Chess Club.

Entry Fees:
$50 before Feb. 8
$65 by Feb. 22
$75 before March 6
$100 before 6 AM on March 7
$125 on-site on March 7 may receive a half point bye in round 1
Refunds:
Refunds must be requested via email to [email protected] prior to 11:59pm on March 6 and will have a processing fee of $12 withheld.
Byes
Maximum two half-point byes are available upon request. All half-point byes must be requested before 8:30am on March 7. Half-point byes for Rounds 4 or later are irrevocable after 12:30pm on March 7. If any player is unable to play any round for any reason, including withdrawals, please notify a tournament director or score keeper.
Teams
Two or more players from the same school in the same section automatically form a team.

US Chess Membership required:  you may join or renew at https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess
Lunch:
We are seeking a sponsor to donate a pizza lunch for all participants and staff. A 60-90 minute lunch break will be provided following the completion of Round 2.  If we do not get a sponsor for a pizza lunch, we will invite one or more food trucks to provide food service in the parking lot.

Schedule:  Welcome and announcements will begin at approximately 8:45am. All players should be seated for Round 1 start at 9:00am. Subsequent rounds start about 15 minutes after the previous round ends. There will be a lunch break for players to eat lunch. Players registering on site may not be paired for round 1.
Players should bring a Chess clock capable of using Increments and they should be familiar with how to set the clock.

Las Vegas , NV 89120

Holy Cross Lutheran Church

Event Overview

G/45;d5 - Quad Format - No Prizes - All ratings welcome. $10 entry - cash only - Adults and Kids Welcome No Late Entries - No Byes - No Withdrawals ONSITE REGISTRATION ONLY US Chess Membership Required, will affect quick and regular rating.

- 9:15 AM - Registration Begins

- 9:45 AM - Registration Ends (NO LATE ENTRIES)

- 10:00 AM - Round One

- 12:30 PM - Round Two

- 2:15 PM - Round Three

What is Quad Format? Players are grouped in order of rating. The top four are grouped, then the next four are grouped, and so on. The groups (quads) of four play each other in a three-round round-robin. No late entries, no withdrawals . Quads are round robins. Please do not play if you can't stay for all three games. Leaving in the middle of a quad is rude and provides an extreme inconvenience to the other three players in your quad.

2025-26 Hartmayer Memorial, Tolland County & UCONN Championships; $1,000 Guaranteed!

State Championship Event

University of Connecticut, School of Engineering

Saturday, March 7, 2026

Event Overview

A Connecticut County Championship Event!
CSCA Grand Prix 20 Level 2 Enhanced Points!
$1,000 guaranteed and Trophies!
Live DGT Broadcast! Classic Collegiate Venue! Onsite Dining!
Sponsored by the Connecticut State Chess Associations

Saturday, March 7, 2026
Round 1 at 11:00 AM, then ASAP.
University of Connecticut, School of Engineering
Online registration link at  ChessCT.org ; Registration open through March 7 at 11:30 AM.

Sec/Rds/TC/Byes: Open (see Note [1]), U2000, U1300, U800, NER; 4 Rounds Swiss, Open & U2000: G/45+10, Others: G/30+10; NE and USCF-rated, NER NE-rated; One ½ pt bye in Rds 1-3; Discretionary bye/pairing for entries after 9 AM. Grand Prix: 20 Enhanced  CSCA Grand Prix Points. Prizes:  Open : $250-150, $100 to Top U2200. U2000 : $200-100, $100 to Top U1600.  U1300/U800/NER : Trophies to Top 3, Top U1000 in U1300, U500 and U300 in U800. LTD Thomas Hartmayer Memorial Prize : $100 & Plaque to Top Upset overall. Trophies to Open/U2000 winners and Top UCONN player. Trophies to 3-point or better results and medals to non-placing players. Cash prizes via PayPal. Tie break: Tie break on 4-0-0 ties: a) G/10+3 game; if drawn, b) G/3+2 game; if drawn, c) G/5/4+2 game. Seeding, color by USCF tiebreaks. Does not affect money prizes.  Entry Fee:  Register online ; $45 by 2/25, $55 by 3/3, $65 by 3/5, $80 thereafter. GM/IM FREE by 2/25, then from prizes. Titled and U1300/U800/NER: $10 less. Member/sibling/senior/veteran/hardship discounts, email us for discount code. Notes :  [1]  Open Section.  Players rated under 2000 are not permitted in the Open unless they are older than 18 years and rated over 1800. The organizer in its sole discretion may waive this requirement. [2] Prizes & tax requirements. All prizes are paid via PayPal. Players winning $600 or more in a calendar year must submit a W-9 to  Click here to show mail address . [3] Refunds/Cancellation Policy:  To withdraw and request a refund, players MUST email their request to  Click here to show mail address no later than Mar 4 at 11:59 PM. Refund requests not emailed or received after deadline, will not be honored. Refunds are subject to $20 administrative fee. For complete event notes and terms   please visit  ChessCT.org .

United States

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids

Chess Kings & Queens Academy

Saturday, March 7, 2026

Event Overview

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30.  Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00.  The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play.  Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections.  The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment.  Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $25.  Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information:  Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).
Information / registration link:  https://chesskq.com/tournament

Clara Roberts Memorial Chess Tournament '26

Max's Taphouse

Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

March 8th, 2026

Max's Taphouse (737 S Broadway, Baltimore, MD 21231)
USCF Rated
5 Round- Swiss G15+5
2 Sections: Open, U1600

Schedule:  10-minute break after each round, 40-minute break between rounds 3 and 4.
Check-in: 11:30am
Round 1: 12:15pm
Award Ceremony: 5:30 pm

PLEASE BRING A SET AND CLOCK!

Entry Fee: $45 with pre-registration complete by 11:30 PM (03/07), $50 registration at the door.
65 Player cap between both sections!

All Prizes Guaranteed
(Highest OTB USCF rating used for pairing and class prizes)

1st- $350
2nd- $200
3rd- $100

Pdk NINE Quads Tournament in Mt Laurel

Pdk NINE Board Game Café

Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

Register Now!
Date:  Sunday, March 8th.
Time:  Doors open at 8:30. | Please arrive by 8:45 AM for check-in. | First round starts promptly at 9:00 AM.
Location:  PDK NINE Board Game Cafe
Entry Fee:  $25 (Pre-registered only)
Registration closes at midnight on Saturday, March 7th. No walk-ins will be accepted. Please call the store for assistance in registering if necessary: 856-206-9615.
Prizes:

- 1st Place in Each Section:  $50

- 2nd Place in Each Section:  Free Game Block (Store Game Library Pass)

Tournament Format:

- Quads:  Players will be grouped into 4-person sections based on rating.

- Rounds:  3 total rounds per player.

- Time Control:  Game in 25 minutes with a 5-second delay (G/25; d5).

- Sections and games will be US Chess-rated.

Important Notes:

- The first round starts promptly at 9:00 AM.

- The store will be closed to the public during the event, but coffee and pastries will still be available for players and spectators to purchase.

- Please arrive by 8:45 AM to check in and be ready for pairings.

- Pre-registration is required – no walk-ins will be accepted on the day of the event.

New to Chess Tournaments? No Problem!
This event is perfect for both experienced players and newcomers looking to try out a fun, structured chess tournament in a relaxed setting.

- This is a US Chess-rated event, meaning your games will count toward an official chess rating and a paid membership is required.

- If you’re not a US Chess member yet, signing up is quick and easy! Just visit  www.uschess.org  before the event.

- A US Chess membership allows you to participate in rated tournaments nationwide.

Affordable options are available for adults, juniors, and first-time players. If you're unsure about the process, just ask—we’re happy to help!
All players must provide a US Chess ID number at check-in.
What to Bring?

- Bringing your own chess set and clock is strongly encouraged.

- A few chess sets and clocks will be made available by the store participants do not own their own.

Enjoy coffee and pastries before and between rounds!
Come test your skills, meet other chess enthusiasts, and enjoy a great day of games! Whether you're a tournament veteran or playing in your first rated event, we’d love to have you at the board.

Address: 127 Ark Rd #4

Mr Laurel , NJ 08054

United States

Dragon Knight Chess Start of Daylight Savings Grand Prix

Grand Prix, Enhanced Grand Prix

Dragon Knight Chess Center

Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

Dragon Knight Chess Center
2000 Bearcat Way
Suite 104, Morrisville, NC  27560
(919) 422-2535
Enhanced Grand Prix
3 round Swiss System
5 sections: Open Section; Under 2000 Section; Under 1750 Section; Under 1500 Section; and Under 1250 Section
Prize Fund:  Open Section: $150-100-50 Guaranteed ($300 Total Guaranteed)
Under 2000 Section: $232 total b/8 entries in Under 2000 Section
Under 1750 Section: $232 total b/8 entries in Under 1750 Section
Under 1500 Section: $232 total b/8 entries in Under 1500 Section
Under 1250 Section: $232 total b/8 entries in Under 1250 Section
Registration and Entry Fee:
Register by Feb 15 pay $30;
Register Feb 16-22 pay $35;
Register Feb 23-March 1 pay $40;
Register March 2-6 (6pm) pay $45;
After March 6 pay $50.
Onsite registration 9:00-9:30 morning of tournament; mandatory 1st round half point bye likely.
Masters play for free; $30 deducted from prize.
USCF membership required.
Time Control:  All sections G/65; delay 5 .  Each player receives 65 minutes plus a 5 second delay to complete each game.
3 round Swiss System; Round Schedule:
1st Round 10am;
2nd Round 1pm;
3rd Round 3:30pm
One single optional half point bye allowed for any round declared before Round 2.

Super Sunday USCF Tournament

Chess Kings & Queens Academy

Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

Note: There is also a FIDE-USCF hybrid section for those 1700+ USCF rating (1600+ FIDE).  See other listing for details.

Structure
- 3 rounds Swiss-Style.  G75 +15.  Accelerated pairings at the director's discretion.
- One half-point bye is available for any round, but must be requested before tournament start. All other requested byes are zero points.
- Clocks, boards, and weighed plastic pieces are provided. Players may use their own equipment with the agreement of their opponent.
Schedule
- Round times: 10:00 am / 1:30pm / 5:00 pm.
- Players should arrive no later than 9:45 am.
Registration
- Registration fee: $45
- Online registration only.  Registration closes at 9:00 a.m. the day of the event.  On-site registrations are discouraged but may be accepted at the TD's discretion.
- Registration link:  https://chesskq.com/tournament
- All sections in this tournament have a minimum rating to participate.
Under 1400 = 1000 USCF rating minimum
Under 1800 = 1300 USCF rating minimum
- This event has no age restrictions.
- All ratings are assessed based on the published USCF rating supplement for the month the tournament takes place. "Live" or "up-to-date" ratings may be accepted at the director's discretion.
- Players signing up for a section they are not eligible to join will be automatically shifted to the appropriate section.
- Players who sign up but are ineligible to participate, or players who withdraw from the tournament prior to 9:00 am on tournament day, will be provided a credit for a signup for a future tournament or class.
Prizes
$640 guaranteed in prizes
Prizes are paid out via Venmo, Zelle, or PayPal. Check-by-mail available for anyone without these options.
U1800 section
- 1st place: $160
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1600: $60
U1400 section
- 1st place: $160
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1200: $60
@45 players  (across all three sections) - we serve doughnuts and coffee.  Everyone wins!
@50 players - we add a Top Junior (under age 12) award to each section
@55 players - we add a Top Senior (age 55+) award to each section
@60 players - we increase 2nd place and "top under __  rating" prizes for all sections by $15
@65 players - we increase 1st place prizes for all sections by $20.
Additional information
- The tournament director for this event is Stephen Lorimor. Bye requests and other issues may be e-mailed to [email protected] , or by voice/text to 908-286-0720. Note that he may not notice or respond to e-mails, texts, or calls after 9:00 am the day of the event.
- The venue is located within walking distance of multiple restaurants and fast food businesses.  No food is allowed at the playing tables, but a waiting room with tables is available.

Address: 1030 Stelton Road

Suite 201 (use side entrance)

Piscataway , NJ 08854

United States

Super Sunday FIDE Tournament

Chess Kings & Queens Academy

Sunday, March 8, 2026

Event Overview

Note: This is a dual USCF - FIDE section of a larger USCF tournament (Super Sunday).  Please read the information carefully.  For the other sections and more events, please check our other listing.

Structure
- 3 rounds Swiss-Style.  G75 +15.  Accelerated pairings at the director's discretion.
- One half-point bye is available for any round, but must be requested before tournament start. All other requested byes are zero points.
- Clocks, boards, and weighed plastic pieces are provided. Players may use their own equipment with the agreement of their opponent.
- FIDE notice: Rules for late arrival will match standard USCF 60 minute rule.
Schedule
- Round times: 10:00 am / 1:30pm / 5:00 pm

USCF
- A current USCF membership is required to play.
- Players MUST have at least 1) 1700 USCF rating (live or current published), or 2) 1600 FIDE rating

FIDE
- A valid FIDE ID is required to play.  Most players with a valid USCF membership may request a USA-flagged FIDE ID at this URL.  Note that it may take several days to process.  https://tinyurl.com/3zcjwmex
- There is no minimum FIDE rating for this event.  There is a maximum rating of 2399.
- FIDE norms are not available at this event.

Registration
- Registration fee: $45
- Online registration only.  Registration closes at 9:00 a.m. on the day of the event.  On-site registrations are discouraged but may be accepted at the TD's discretion.
- Registration link: https://chesskq.com/tournament
- Free entry for all players rated 2200 or higher. ($45 will be deducted from the player's prize winnings.) E-mail name, USCF ID, and FIDE ID to Stephen Lorimor at [email protected] to sign up.
- This event has no age restrictions.
- Players signing up for a section they are not eligible to join will be automatically shifted to the appropriate section.
- Players ineligible to participate in any section of this event, or withdrawing before 9:00 AM on the day of the tournament, will receive a credit for a future class or tournament.

Prizes
Prizes are paid out via Zelle or PayPal. Check-by-mail available for anyone without these options.
- 1st place: $200
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1800 (FIDE): $60
@45 players  (across all three sections) - we serve doughnuts and coffee.  Everyone wins!
@50 players - we add a Top Junior (under age 12) award to each section
@55 players - we add a Top Senior (age 55+) award to each section
@60 players - we increase 2nd place and "top under __  rating" prizes for all sections by $15
@65 players - we increase 1st place prizes for all sections by $20.

Additional information
- The tournament director for this event is Stephen Lorimor. Bye requests and other issues may be e-mailed to [email protected] , or by voice/text to 908-286-0720. Note that he may not notice or respond to e-mails, texts, or calls after 9:00 am the day of the event.
- The venue is located within walking distance of multiple restaurants and fast food businesses.  No food is allowed at the playing tables, but a waiting room with tables is available.

Address: 1030 Stelton Road

Suite 201 (use side entrance)

Piscataway , NJ 08854

United States

Texas Grand Circuit ed.1 in Dallas

Champions Social Club Dallas

Thursday, March 12, 2026
- Monday, March 16, 2026

Event Overview

Texas Grand Circuit — Dallas (Edition 1) | March 12–16
If you’re chasing norms, crave world-class playing conditions, and want an event that treats players like VIPs without compromising integrity —this is the one.
Why this event is different

- Norm conditions by design : a curated, norm-eligible field built for real title chances—not a “maybe the pairings work out” situation.

- Player-first experience : punctual rounds, clear communication, professional staffing, and logistics that run like a machine.

- Elite venue & comfort : a premium tournament hall that belongs in the conversation with the best venues in the U.S.

- Treated like kings : hospitality touches that make you feel like a featured guest, not an entry fee.

- Strict anti-cheating & game integrity : serious measures, consistent enforcement, and an environment where results matter.

Event Schedule & Sections
International Section (Norm Eligible)
March 12–16
9-round Swiss | Norm eligible
$10,000 prize fund (based on 48 players)
A focused, premium section built for norm attempts and high-quality pairings round after round.
Open Section (FIDE/USCF Rated)
March 13–16
7-round Swiss | FIDE/USCF rated
3-day / 4-day schedules available
$3,000 prize fund (based on 64 players)
A strong open with top-tier organization and conditions you can feel from round one.
Important details

- Entry fee details : linked on the registration page

- Total event cap : 112 players (both sections combined)

This venue is hands-down one of the best tournament halls in the United States—an experience you need to see in person. If you’ve ever wanted “St. Louis-level” conditions with a player-first feel, Dallas in March is your move.

Dallas , TX 75287

United States

Event Overview

Cornerstone Chess Events Spring Classic
March 13-15

Domain Hotel, 1085 E El Camino Real, Sunnyvale, CA 94087
5-round Swiss, 90+30, USCF & FIDE Rated (top 3 sections FIDE Rated)
$10,000 prizes, 100% guaranteed
Conditions for the first 10 GM/IMs who commit by 2/13, reach out to Click here to show mail address to inquire*

M (2200+, FIDE Rated):  $2,000-$1,250-$750
X (2000-2199, FIDE Rated):  $1,000-$600-$400
A (1800-1999, FIDE Rated):  $750-$400-$300
B (1600-1799):  $400-$250-$200
C (1400-1599):  $400-$250-$200
DEu (u1400):  $400-$250-$200
Sections based on March published USCF ratings

Entry Fees
FIDE Rated Sections (M,X,A) : $150
GM, IM, & WGM - Free, by 2/13
FM, WIM, & WFM - $50 off, by 2/13
Non-FIDE Rated Sections  (B,C,DEu) : $100
$50 play-up, live or published must be within 200 points of section minimum **
$15 late fee after 2/20, $30 after 2/27, $50 after 3/9 -  Registration closes 3/13 10 AM

Max Capacity of 240 players
90 Players in Peak Ballroom (2nd Floor) - M & X sections
150 Players in Quantum Ballroom (1st Floor) - A, B, C, & DEu sections

Schedule (for all sections):
Round 1: Friday, March 13th - 6 PM
Round 2:  Saturday, March 14th - 11 AM
Round 3:  Saturday, March 14th - 5 PM
Round 4:  Sunday, March 15th - 10 AM
Round 5:  Sunday, March 15th - 3:30 PM

*GMs and IMs must play all five rounds in order to receive the agreed upon conditions.
**Please register for the section allowed or contact organizer for manual section override. To ensure the most competitive playing experience possible, section will be rearranged based on March published or live ratings, whichever is higher. Refunds or charges may be given based on updated March ratings.

- 5% processing fee for all refunds or future entry fee credit

- Boards, clocks, scoresheets, and pens are provided by the organizer.

- Top 36 boards to be broadcasted via DGT boards

- Byes: Players may request up to two half-point byes before the start of the event.

- Closest airports are SJC (15 min drive), OAK (40 min drive), and SFO (45 min drive). Public transportation is not easily accessible so Uber/Lyft/taxi is recommended.

- Hotel Booking:  Domain Hotel Link will be updated shortly. Free breakfast included!

- Parking: There is free parking for chess tournament participants. Check in with the front desk for parking pass upon arrival.
- Front:  26 spaces (including 2 handicap)

- Garage:  81 spaces (including 4 handicap)

- Back:  22 spaces

2026 Indiana Chess Congress

Heritage Event, Grand Prix, State Championship Event

La Quinta Inn & Suites Indianapolis South

Friday, March 13, 2026
- Sunday, March 15, 2026

Event Overview

2026 Indiana Chess Congress
and 85th Indiana State Chess Championship
MARCH 13-15, 2026
$15,000 PRIZE FUND (B/O 150 PAID ENTRIES)
FIVE SECTIONS, 5-SS with 2- and 3-day options

La Quinta Inn & Suites Indianapolis South
Friday, March 13, 2026 - Sunday, March 15, 2026
FULL INFORMATION, REGISTRATION, & HOTEL RESERVATIONS

REGISTRATION:
Follow link above to register online.
Onsite registration for main sections before Friday @ 6:30 PM (3-day) & Saturday @ 9:30 AM (2-day) to ensure a first round pairing.

ENTRY FEES:
On or before February 1:  $100 Early Special. Open to ISCA members only. Anyone, including out-of-state players, may join ISCA  before registering.
February 2 to March 11: $155. ($15 discount off this entry fee for ISCA members. ISCA membership costs $15, so it is always worth joining.)
On or after March 12: $170 for all registrants
Re-Entry Fee:  $50 before Saturday @ 9:30 AM
Cancellation of registration before event subject to $5 fee withheld from refund.
$3 convenience fee if paying by credit card, not charged to ISCA members.
Save on all ISCA tournaments by becoming a member at https://www.indianachess.org
Titled players: Feel free to contact the ISCA president ( [email protected] ) regarding possible conditions available. They are limited, so act soon.

SCHEDULES and TIME CONTROLS:
All championship sections are 5-round Swisses:
3-day schedule:  Fri: 7:00 PM | Sat: 11:00 AM & 5:00 PM | Sun: 10:00 AM & 3:30 PM (all G/90 inc/30)
2-day schedule:  Sat: 10:00 AM & 1:30 PM (G/60 inc/30), then merge with 3-day at 5:00 PM (G/90 inc/30)
Half-point byes allowed in rounds 1-4, limit 2, must be committed before round 2.
ISCA annual membership meeting Sunday @ 2:10 PM, after round 4 concludes

SECTIONS and PRIZES:
85th Annual Indiana State Chess Championship (1900+)*
Top Prizes
$1200 | $900 | $500 | $300
U2300 Prizes
$600 | $300
Top Indiana Resident Bonus:
$250 + Trophy | $175 | $125
Top Indiana Resident Seniors (must verify age before round 4)
$125 for age 60+ | $125 for age 50-59
Top Indiana K-12 Player (must verify grade before round 4)
$100
*Any IN resident may enter into this section; out-of-state players must be rated 1900 or above.

Indiana State Major Open Championship (U2100)
Players rated below 1800 in this section must either have had a peak non-provisional rating of 1800+ or have earned a USCF 1st Category norm and must give proof of eligibility in the comments at registration.
Top Prizes
$800 | $500 | $300 | $200
U1900 Prizes
$400 | $200
Indiana State Reserve Championship (U1801)
Players rated below 1500 in this section must either have had a peak non-provisional rating of 1500+ or have earned a USCF 2nd Category norm and must give proof of eligibility in the comments at registration.
Top Prizes*
$800 | $500 | $300 | $200
U1600 Prizes (no unrated)
$400 | $200
Top Indiana Resident Bonus:
$200 + Trophy | $100
*Unrated players limited to $300
Indiana State Booster Championship (U1500)
Players rated below 1200 in this section must either have had a peak non-provisional rating of 1200+ or have earned a USCF 4th Category norm and must give proof of eligibility in the comments at registration.
Top Prizes*
$800 | $500 | $300 | $200
U1300 Prizes (no unrated)
$300 | $200 | $150
*Unrated players limited to $300
Indiana State Novice Championship (U1200)
Top Prizes (no unrated)
$700 | $400 | $300 | $200
U1000 Prizes (no unrated)
$300 | $200 | $150
Unrated Player Prizes (if at least 3 unrated players registered)
$200 | $100

LOCATION / HOTEL:
La Quinta Inn & Suites by Wyndham Indianapolis South
5120 Victory Drive
Indianapolis, IN 46203
+1 (317) 783-7751

Event room rates available
$114/night
Follow link above for hotel reservations.
Many guest rooms newly renovated since last Congress!

GENERAL INFORMATION:
All prizes paid electronically via PayPal or Venmo.
Bring board, set, and clock. Equipment is generally not provided.
Published March ratings will be used.
In the State Championship section, all players must turn in their original signed scoresheet in addition to reporting results.
In the State Championship section, players may be assigned to play on a broadcasted DGT board. They must play on that board if assigned to it. Games are broadcast on a time delay to deter cheating.
More Information available at https://www.indianachess.org .

Organizer: Indiana State Chess Association
ISCA President:  FM Lester VanMeter ( [email protected] )
Chief Tournament Director: Ron Carrell ( [email protected] )
Principal Assistant Director: Daro Mott ( [email protected] )
Registrar: John Herr ( [email protected] )

Provide player USCF ID with all correspondence.

Annual ISCA Meeting
Sunday, March 15, 2026 at 2:10 PM., after round 4
Annual meeting is for ISCA Members Only (join at indianachess.org)

If you cannot play a full Congress Championship schedule, there will be other chess events held concurrently at the site. These events will have faster time controls, last only a single day, and have separate TLA announcements. Please check for their details on the USCF TLA site or at indianachess.org. Their details will be announced at a later date.

2026 Southern Nevada Senior Championship

State Championship Event

University of Nevada - Las Vegas

Friday, March 13, 2026
- Sunday, March 15, 2026

Event Overview

Silver State Chess Association
presents
2026 Southern Nevada State Seniors Championship
March 13-15 2026
University of Nevada Las Vegas
4505 S Maryland Pkwy
Las Vegas, NV
Swiss 5 Rounds Game/90+30
Note:  Players must be age 50+ prior to Aug 3, 2026.

Players must reside in Nevada in one of the following counties and have their eligible address on file with USCF: Clark, Nye, Lincoln and Esmerelda.

Northern Nevada residents should register for the Northern Nevada State Seniors Championship in a separate tournament.
Schedule :  (all rounds G/90+30)
Round 1: Friday March 13 @ 6:00 pm
Round 2: Saturday March 14 @ 12:00 pm
Round 3: Saturday March 14 @ 5:00 pm
Round 4: Sunday March 15 @ 12:00 pm
Round 5: Sunday March 15 @ 5:00 pm
Top three winners advance to the State Championship to compete against top three winners from Northern NV in a proctored online tournament to be held at UNLV on April 24-26.
Boards and Sets will be provided.
Prizes
$1000.00 with 20 paid players:
Top Prize:  $500 + Trophy
Second:    $350 + Trophy
Third: $150 + Trophy
Top U1900: Trophy
Top U1600: Trophy

Above cash prizes adjusted proportionally for more or fewer players.
The winner of the Nevada State Seniors Championship will represent Nevada in the John T. Irwin Tournament of Senior State Champions on August 3-6 (TBD) in Grand Rapids, MI. Silver State Chess will provide a travel stipend of $650 upon completion of the Irwin with no forfeited games.
Maximum number of entries: 40. Registration not confirmed until payment received.
Waitlist will start if/when max entries received.
Entry fee : $99 by March 10, $115 later.
Refunds : may be requested prior to start of Round 1. $15 withheld for processing fees
Entrants may register in person and pay with cash or check at UNLV.
Maximum two half-point byes available and must be requested before Round 3 and are irrevocable

US Chess Membership is required.
Please join or renew the player’s membership at  www.uschess.org  before registering for the tournament.
Registration: 2026 Southern Nevada Senior Championship

Las Vegas , NV 89154

Cedar Rapids Leatherjackets

Friday, March 13, 2026
- Sunday, March 15, 2026

Event Overview

2026 CEDAR RAPIDS IOWA
LEATHER JACKETS
MARCH 13-15, 2024
THREE-DAY & TWO-DAY SCHEDULES
Both Open & Reserve (U1600) Sections
$2,000 in Cash Prizes (b/40 in each section)
Saturday Night Blitz
USCF Rated; FIDE Rated in Open & Blitz

TIME CONTROL
3-Day: 5 Round Swiss, Game 90 minutes + 30 second increment.
2-Day: Rounds 1 & 2 Game 60 min delay 5 sec, then merge round 3 with Game 90 +30.
Saturday Night Blitz: 5 round Swiss, two games per round, Game 3 minutes delay 2 seconds.
SCHEDULE
3-Day: Friday 7 pm; Saturday 10 am and 3:30 pm; Sunday, 9:30 am and 3:00 pm.
2-Day: Saturday 10 AM and 12:30 PM (not FIDE rated) then merge with the 3-day schedule.
Blitz: Saturday 8 pm.
ENTRY FEE
Open: $75 if received before 2/25/26, $85 afterward, and $95 on-site. Players>1400 may play up for an additional $20 fee.
Reserve: $60 if received before 2/25/26, $65 afterward, and $75 on-site.
Play-up Option: $20 extra to play up from Reserve (U1600) into the Open section (Rating must be > 1400).
On-Site Registration: Fri: 5 pm - 6:30 pm, Sat: 8:0 am - 9:30 am
Blitz: $20 prior or onsite.
PRIZES
Open ($1,170 b/29): 1st $500, 2nd $250 3rd $160. Class Prizes: U2000 and U1800, $130 each; Unrated players are not eligible for class prizes.
Reserve ($640 b/29): U1600: 1st-3rd $200-$160-$120. Class Prizes: U1400, U1200 $80 each.
Blitz: 75% of entry fees returned as prizes.
REGISTRATION INFORMATION
IASCA Membership: Required for Open Section in-state participants. This is a IASCA GP Qualifier!
No round 5 byes.
PLAYING LOCATION & HOTEL
We are back at the Cedar Rapids Radisson  on Highway 100!

23rd annual Southern Class Championships

Grand Prix, Enhanced Grand Prix, Junior Grand Prix

Delta Hotels By Marriott Orlando Celebration

Friday, March 13, 2026
- Sunday, March 15, 2026

Event Overview

March 13-15 or 14-15, 2026  Florida
US CHESS GRAND PRIX POINTS: 80 (ENHANCED)
23rd annual Southern Class Championships
5-SS, 40/80, SD/30; d30 (2-day option, rounds 1-2 G/60, d10). Delta Hotels By Marriott Orlando Celebration, 2900 Parkway Boulevard, Kissimmee, FL 34747, one mile from Disney World (20 acres with two pools, whirlpool, free hotel shuttle to Disney World and Universal Studios). Free parking. Prizes $17,000 guaranteed!   In 7 sections; see peakrating.us. Master (2100/up): $1600-800-400-300, clear/tiebreak win $100 bonus. FIDE. Expert (1900-2199): $1200-700-400-200.  FIDE. Class A  (1700-1999): $1200-700-400-200. FIDE. Class B (1500-1799): $1200-700-400-200. Class C  (1300-1599): $1000-500-300-200. Class D (Under 1400): $1000-500-300-200. Class E ( Under 1200): $600-400-200-100. These overlapping class rating boundaries  already include players rated in the top half of the section below.  Unrated may enter A through E, with prize limit $100 E, $200 D, $300 C, $400 B. Mixed Doubles:  Best male+female 2-player combined score among all sections: $500-300-200. Team rating must average under 2200, may play different sections and schedules; register (no extra fee) at site by 2 pm Sat.  Cannot play  below USCF Online Regular rating minus 100 points.  Top 6 sections EF: $118 online at chessaction.com by 3/10, $130 later online or at site until 1 hour before Round 1 (no checks, credit cards OK). GMs, IMs & WGMs; $100 from prize. Class E EF:  all $30 less than above. Unofficial uschess.org ratings or USCF Online Regular ratings usually used if otherwise unrated. Special 1- year USCF dues with magazine paid online with entry: see chessevents.us. Re-entry (no Master to Master) $60. 3-day schedule: Reg ends Fri 6 pm, rds. Fri 7 pm, Sat 11 & 5, Sun 10 & 3:30. 2-day schedule:  Reg ends Sat 10 am, rds. Sat 11, 2 & 5, Sun 10 & 3:30. All:  Half point byes OK all, limit 2, must commit before round 2. HR:  $145-145-145-145, reservations link to be posted at chessevents.us (or call 407-396-7000, request Chess rate); reserve by 2/27 or rate may increase. Car rental: Avis, 800-331-1600, AWD D657633, or reserve online at chesstour.com. Enter online: chessaction.com. No mail entries. $15 service charge for refunds. Questions: [email protected] ,  chesstour.com. Prizes not claimed at site are usually paid by PayPal (may take a couple of weeks). Entries posted at chessaction.com (click “entry list” after entering).  Blitz tournament Sat 9:30 pm, enter on site Sat. by 9:10 pm.

Address: 2900 Parkway Boulevard

Kissimmee , FL 34747

United States

Handicap Accessible: No
Residency Restriction: No
Online Event: No

Sections

Tunnelvision XLII

Columbia Chess Club

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

The Columbia Chess Club Presents Columbia Tunnelvision XLII
March 14, 2026
$1000 Guaranteed
10:30 a.m. 4-Round G/45;inc.5
Columbia Chess Club
6169 St. Andrews Rd.
Columbia, SC 29212
Register
Registration
Standard registration is $40 until the day before the tournament.  $50 late registration the day before/morning of.  Registration online only, registration limited to first 74 players.
Entry for titled players (National Master and above) is free, standard entry fee deducted from prizes.  If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout.
Considering Tunnelvision as your first chess tournament?  Great!  We've put together a guide to help first-time players .
Register Now
Pre-Registered Players
Format
4 Round Swiss. Time control is G45/inc.5 (45 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment ), which will be USCF dual-rated under both Quick and Classical. All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. Tournament has three sections: Championship (1600+), Under 1600, and Under 1000. Players may register for a higher section if they are within 100 USCF rating points of the cutoff.
If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit  https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess.
Live Standings/Pairings/Boards
The top board of each section will be live streamed to the DGT LiveCloud along with real-time updates to Lichess.org and Chess.com.  A live video stream of the top Championship board will also be available on the club's Twitch page.  See this site's "Live" menu for links.
Live standings (including current pre-registration information) and pairings are also available below.
Live Standings
Prizes
$1000 Prize Fund Guaranteed.
Championship (1600+)
$400 Fund. 1st: $200; 2nd: $130; 3rd: $70
Under 1600
$300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50
Under 1000
$300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50
Schedule

- Round 1: 10:30 a.m.

- Round 2: 12:50 p.m.

- Round 3: 2:40 p.m.

- Round 4: 4:30 p.m.

Byes
A single half-point bye is available any round, including the final round.  The half-point bye may be requested as a part of the advance entry or on site before the tournament starts.  Thereafter the only bye available is a zero-point bye.  The chief tournament director shall have the ability to grant a half-point bye for any round on unusual circumstances.
Location
Columbia Chess Club
6169 St. Andrews Rd., Ste A
Columbia, SC 29212
Questions?
Email  [email protected] or call/text James Brandmair at 803.569.0938.
Parking
The Columbia Chess Club is located in a shopping center with ample parking.
Food
The Columbia Chess Club offers on-site concessions, including drinks and snacks.  By the Fire Pizza and Zorba's Restaurant are located in the same shopping center and will be open during the tournament.  Many other restaurants are available close by!

6169 St. Andrews Road, Suite A

Columbia , SC 29212

United States

Phoenix Chess Academy

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

4 round Swiss. Time control: Game in 40 minutes with 5 sec delay. Boards, sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided.
Registration: Go to www.phoenixchessacademy.com. USCF membership is required. New or renewing USCF members are welcome. Highest rating will be used for Swiss pairings and prize purposes.
Sections: Open, Under 1700, Under 1200 & Under 700. No playing up allowed for Open and U1700. Players Under 700 can play in the U1200 Section. Sections will be combined in case a section has less than 4 players registered.
Schedule: Round 1- 9:00 AM, Round 2- 10:30 AM, Round 3- 12:00 PM, Round 4- 1:30 PM. Awards Ceremony will start right after last game is over. Half point Byes are available in all 4 rounds and (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. Requesting a zero-point Bye late in the tournament is considered the same as withdrawing.
Contact: Liulia Cardona at [email protected] or (602) 402-4985
Prizes: Trophies for top three in each section.
Entry Fee: $30.00 by Wednesday; $35 by Friday; $40 same day. Refund Policy: Full refund will be issued to players who withdraw at least an hour before the first round. In cases where a registered player does not show up for the tournament without prior notice, they will not be eligible for a refund.
A player will automatically forfeit the game if going in the bathroom with a cellphone.

25-26 Greater Cleveland Scholastic Chess League #4 - Rocky River

Rocky River High School

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

— Registration Closes 5PM Friday Before Each Event —
2025-2026 GREATER CLEVELAND SCHOLASTIC CHESS LEAGUE
4 Monthly Tournaments – 9 Sections for Players of All Skill Levels!
Friendly competition, great value, flexible options!
Schedule and Format:  4 Round Swiss.  Doors Open: 8:30am, 1st Game: 10am Sharp.
Estimated completion: K-2 Section: 1:30, Championship, U1600 and U1200: 3:30
Other Sections: 2:30. All competitors play 4 games, no elimination.
Recording of moves is not required in U400 and U800.

#1 Oct 25 SOLON – Solon Middle School, 6835 Som Center Rd, Solon, OH 44139
#2 Dec 6 WESTLAKE – Westlake High School, 27830 Hilliard Blvd, Westlake, OH 44145
#3 Jan 17 SOLON – Solon Middle School, 6835 Som Center Rd, Solon, OH 44139
#4 Mar 14 ROCKY RIVER – Rocky River High School, 20951 Detroit Road, Rocky River, OH 44116

Sections:
Championship – Open to all scholastic players!
Under 1600 – Players from all Grades with ratings below 1600
Under 1200 – Players from all Grades with ratings below 1200
HS Premier – Players from Grades 9-12 with ratings below 1000
MS Premier – Players from Grades 6-8 with ratings below 800
Elem Premier – Players from Grades K-5 with ratings below 800
MS Reserve – Players from Grades 6-8 with ratings below 400
Elem 3-5 Reserve – Grades 3-5 with ratings below 400
Primary K-2 Reserve – Grades K-2 with ratings below 400

Unsure where to play? Check if you or your child has a rating here:  USCF Rating Lookup
If the player in question does not have a rating, online ratings may be used to estimate USCF Rating.
Unrated players may choose any grade appropriate section.

Time limit:  Championship, Under 1600 and Under 1200: G/30; d5, All other sections: G/25; d5.
Individual Awards: Trophies to the top 5 players in each section at each event, and all players scoring 3 or more points.
Participation medals to all players at each event!
Team Awards:  Team trophies will be presented to the top 3 school teams in each section at the last event, based on the accumulated scores from the best three tournaments. Team scores at each event are determined in each section by adding the best 4 individual scores (in the same section) per school. A minimum of two players in the same section for each school are required to have a team score for that event.
Scholarship Prizes:  $1,500 in College Scholarship money awarded ; determined by adding the scores from each player’s best three events.  Championship 1st Place $1,000, Championship 2nd Place $500.
Fees:  $90 for all four league events, or $35   per tournament.
No on-site registration —  Registration will close at 5PM the night before each event!
Registration at progresswithchess.org/gcscl

or Michael Joelson, (216) 321-7000, Click here to show mail address

Daniel Naroditsky Memorial

Salinas Valley Community Church

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

Daniel Naroditsky  Memorial
open to all chessplayers, ages 5 to 105, novice to master!
$12 entry fee, waived for K-12 students and SVCC chess club members
Hosted and co-sponsored by Salinas Valley Community Church.  Organized and co-sponsored by Chess Monterey.
Your donations toward Chess Monterey community outreach are gratefully appreciated.
Saturday, March 14
Salinas Valley Community Church, 368 San Juan Grade Road, Salinas CA 93906
4 sections:  USCF-rated Championship , Challengers , Contenders ,
and non-rated Candidates
Entrants to rated sections must be current members of USCF -- join or renew at uschess.org
Championship section is limited to the eight top-rated entrants (incl. qualifier from February 7 Challengers).
Challengers section is limited to the next group of eight entrants based on USCF ratings.
Contenders section is for the remaining entrants, including unrated players wanting to earn a USCF rating.
Candidates section is a non-rated introductory section for novice and youth players.
Player registration and check-in:  9:15-10am
3 rounds: 10:30, 1:00, 3:30
Candidates section has 4 rounds: 10:45, 12:15, 2:00, 3:30
Swiss-system pairings.  No eliminations̶―everyone plays all rounds.
Half-point bye(s) may be arranged at registration or requested at least 20 minutes before scheduled round.
Games timed with 30 minutes per player, plus 30s increment added with each move. (G/30;+30)
Please bring your chess set, board, and clock. A limited number of sets and clocks are provided by the organizer.
Players must record all moves of their games on provided scoresheets or in their own scorebook.
Trophy to 1st place and 2nd place in Championship and Challengers sections.
Medal to 1st, 2nd and 3rd place in Contenders and Candidates sections.
USCF-rated blitz playoff match (G/5;+2) in the event of prize-winning ties in rated sections.
Medal to K thru 12 students who complete their scheduled rounds.
Winners of Challengers section are seeded into the April 18 Championship section.
Winners of Candidates section must play in USCF-rated sections in subsequent tournaments.

Joseph Rice, USCF Tournament Director,  Click here to show mail address   831 524-4488

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids

Chess Kings & Queens Academy

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30.  Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00.  The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play.  Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections.  The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment.  Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $25.  Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information:  Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).
Information / registration link:  https://chesskq.com/tournament

3/14 - Quad chess tournament G40; d5

Saint Petersburg Chess Club

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

There will be no “Byes” or withdrawals allowed. Please complete all your Quad games.
WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest. Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list.If two family members are in the same quad, I can move one of them quad up or down.The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each. If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad.
ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!!
LOCATION: Saint Petersburg Chess Club 540 4th Avenue North Saint Petersburg, FL 33701 (it is located in between Mirror Lake and the Coliseum, next to the Sunshine Center.)
REGISTRATION: 10:00-10:45 a.m. If you want to make sure you can play, you need to Pay ahead of time here -  https://www.chessregister.com/ .
ENTRY FEE:
$25 if paid by Wednesday (3 days before the tournament)
$30 afterward.
$35 if paid on Saturday.
USCF membership is required. Please check your USCF ID and renew it if it has expired. If you need me to do it on site add $5 to your bill.
ROUNDS: Three Rounds, First starts at approx. 11:00 a.m.
TIME CONTROL: G40; d5
PRIZES: $65 for first place at each Quad or 1st place very big trophy (if two players tied for 1st place $33 each or 1st place big trophy each)
Trophies for 1st to 3rd place for last section!
IMPORTANT NOTICE: Due to space limitation to secure your spot Pay online ahead of time! BRING YOUR CHESS CLOCK!!!
Visit our new website-  https://saintpetersburgchessclub.com for more information about the chess at Saint Petersburg.

2026 Southern Nevada Girls Scholastic Championship

State Championship Event

University of Nevada - Las Vegas

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

Silver State Chess Association LLC
Presents

2026 SOUTHERN NEVADA STATE GIRLS SCHOLASTIC TOURNAMENT
INDIVIDUAL and TEAM CHAMPIONSHIPS
and QUALIFIER to NEVADA STATE SCHOLASTIC GIRLS CHESS CHAMPIONSHIP

Date: Saturday March 14, 2026 @ 10:15am

IMPORTANT:  Both the Northern portion of the state and the Southern portion of the state (defined below) will hold separate Over-The-Board tournaments to determine individuals and the top team from each region who will then compete in the Nevada State Girls Scholastic Chess Championship to be held online on Sunday, April 26th and the Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship (teams & individual) to be held online on Saturday, April 25th, respectively.

Girls who reside in, or go to school in, the following Nevada counties will be eligible to participate in the Southern Nevada State Girls Scholastic Chess Championship: Clark, Nye, Lincoln and Esmerelda.

***This announcement is for the Southern Nevada State Girls Scholastic Chess Championship. The Northern Nevada State Girls Scholastic Chess Championship will be held on a different day and will be detailed in a separate announcement.
Location:
***NOTE: This event will be held alongside the 2026 Intermountain Collegiate Tournament and the 2026 Southern Nevada Seniors
University of Nevada - Las Vegas
4505 S Maryland Pkwy, Las Vegas, NV 89154

US Chess Membership is required
Please join or renew the player’s membership at  www.uschess.org  before registering for the tournament.
Girls must reside in Nevada or be a full-time student in grades K-12 at a Nevada school
and born after September 1, 2006.

K-12 Open Section (Open to all girls in grades K-12)
5 rounds
Time Control Game/25 minutes + 5 seconds
Round 1 begins at 10:15 AM

Prizes:
Individual Trophies and a Top Team Trophy will be awarded. All Players will receive a participation medal.

Qualifiers:
The top three individual scorers in the Southern Nevada Scholastic Girls Chess Championship will meet at the University of Nevada - Las Vegas on Sunday, April 26th to compete in the Nevada State Scholastic Girls Chess Championship (individuals), an online tournament that includes the Northern Nevada individual qualifiers and the Southern Nevada individual qualifiers. We will provide digital tablets for that tournament. The winner of that tournament will represent the State of Nevada at the 14th Annual WIM Ruth Haring National Tournament of Girls State Champions in Grand Rapids, MI from August 3-6th. The  Nevada State representative will receive a travel stipend from Silver State Chess after completing all games in the national tournament without a forfeit loss.
https://new.uschess.org/haring
The top team scorer in the Southern Nevada Scholastic Chess Championship will meet at University of Nevada - Las Vegas on Saturday, April 26th to compete in the Nevada State Scholastic Chess Championship (teams), an online tournament that includes the Northern Nevada team qualifier and the Southern Nevada team qualifier. We will provide digital tablets for that tournament. The winning teams will not qualify for any national tournament because there is no national team tournament for which to qualify.

Additional Prizes:
**Can be found at 2026 Southern Nevada Girls Scholastic Championship

Entry Fees
$50 before February 22nd
$65 before March 2nd
$75 before March 8th @ 11:59pm, PST
$100 after March 8th @ 11:59pm PST

US Chess Membership required:  you may join or renew at  https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess

Refunds:  Refunds must be requested via email to [email protected] prior to 11:59pm on March 22nd and will have a processing fee of $12 withheld.

Byes:  Maximum one (1) half point bye is available upon request. Half-point byes must be requested by 12:00pm on March 14th and will be irrevocable after that time. If any player is unable to play any round for any reason, including withdrawals, please notify a tournament director or score keeper.

Teams:  Two or more players from the same school in the same section automatically form a team.

Snacks:
No food will be provided. Competitors are encouraged to bring water bottles, which can be used in the playing area and snacks, which can be consumed outside of the playing area between rounds.

Schedule:  Welcome and announcements will begin at 10:00am. All players should be seated for Round 1 start at 10:15am. Subsequent rounds start about 15 minutes after the previous round ends. There will be a lunch break for players to eat player-brought lunches. Players registering after 10:00am may not be paired for round 1.

Address: 4505 S Maryland Pkwy

Las Vegas , NV 89154

United States

2026 Maryland State Girls Championship 3/14

State Championship Event

Bender JCC of Greater Washington

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

Register at  chessacademy.com/tournaments !

The official Maryland State Girls Championship and Haring Qualifier!
This is a US Chess rated Swiss style tournament. There are two different sections for this event, the K-12 U-800 and K-12 Championship . Participants play only against opponents in their own section.  The first round is at 9:00am for both sections.  The tournament concludes around 3:45pm with an awards ceremony where the top players receive trophies.
The Championship section is only open to girls who live in or attend school in MD, the under 800 section is open to girls from any state.

- All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all four rounds.

- We provide FREE US Chess Federation memberships for all participants, a $24 value!

- For players using chess clocks, the time control is G/45 with a 5-second time delay.

- Trophies to the top players in each section.

- Prices increase $10 at noon on Tuesday, 2/24 and $10 at noon on Tuesday, 3/10.

Questions?  Please let us know at  Click here to show mail address !

2026 Intermountain Collegiate Tournament

University of Nevada - Las Vegas

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

UNLV Chess Presents:
2026 Intermountain Intercollegiate Chess Tournament

Location: UNLV Institute of Gaming (Stan Fulton Building), Ballroom A

Proposed Date : Saturday, March 14th
Time: 1st round starts at 10:00 am. Please check in by 9:30 if possible or
text me at 801-560-0498.

Team Schedule (4 rounds, G/45;+5): Registration opens at 9:00am and closes at 9:45
Round 1: 10:00am
Lunch 12 noon or when Round 1 finishes
Round 2: 12:30pm
Round 3: 2:30pm
Round 4: 4:30pm

Individual Schedule (5 rounds, G/25+5)
Round 1: 10:00am
Round 2: 11:00am
Lunch: 12 noon or when Round 2 finishes
Round 3: 1:00pm
Round 4: 2:30pm
Round 5: 3:30pm

Lunch: Will be provided announced the week prior to the tournament

Registration/Entry List :
***can be found at: 2026 Intermountain Collegiate Chess
For teams:
Teams may comprise of students enrolled in the 2025-2026 semester or current University faculty. Each University may bring up to 2 teams (A and B). Send a list of those constituting your 3-man team to UNLV Chess ( Click here to show mail address ) or DM @unlvchessclub on Instagram. Please check the entry list on King Registration to confirm that each player is in the correct team. Entry Fee is $20 either on site or by Zelle ( Click here to show mail address )
For individuals:
Individuals may register either on King Registration or on site. Entry fee is $10 either on site or by Zelle ( Click here to show mail address )
****Registration opens at 9:00am and closes at 9:30am. Please make any adjustments to teams as soon as possible. (Adjustments to your list of participants, including who is on boards 1,2 and 3 may be made by 9:45am the day of the tournament (this includes substitutes who may join the team section). If there are an odd number of teams, an additional team may be made up of those from different schools, or the host school may add a B team, if required. Therefore, if you have less than three players from your school, we
can create a team from two or even three colleges.)

Eligibility: Consistent with previous years, all participants (with exception to faculty) to be currently enrolled students at least have taken classes in the 2024-2025 academic school year. Students may be required to show any of the following:

- A valid student ID

- Unofficial transcript from either current or previous semester

- Proof of payment

Trophies:
Team: 1st-3rd place
Individual 1st and 2nd place for boards 1, 2 and 3 (You could
come home with a trophy or plaque even if your team doesn’t.)
Individual: 1st-5th place in the individual open section and 1st woman

……………………………………………………………………………………….
Lodging: To be determined, though AirBnb or lodging off the Strip is likely the most affordable option

Address: 4505 S Maryland Pkwy

Las Vegas , NV 89154

United States

Sections: 2

Prize Fund:

Handicap Accessible: Yes
Residency Restriction: No
Online Event: No

Phone: 702-722-8530

Limited on-site registration, register online as space is limited

USCF ratings will be used for prize purposes in all sections
TD has discretion to appoint ratings
Hotel Rate available at Chase Park Plaza and AC Hotel (Ask for Chess Club Rate)

MFPL March Rapid Tournament for Kids & Teens

Mammen Family Public Library

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

Join us for a FREE Rated Rapid Chess Tournament for ages 5-18!
Tournament Details:

- Please register for free on the library event page .

- List of registered players can be found at this link .

- Swiss tournament, 5 rounds, G/15 inc/5 (15 minute clock for each player with a 5 second increment).

- Sign-in begins at 10:00 AM. Announcements and briefing will occur at 10:20.
- Round 1 start time: 10:30 AM

- Subsequent rounds will take place 10 minutes after the previous round ends.

- Lunch break will be from 1:00 to 1:30 (may be shifted slightly depending on the previous round's end time).

- NOTE: If you need a half-point bye round because of scheduling conflicts, please contact Click here to show mail address with the round you will need a bye (limit: 1 bye round). Must commit before round 1 begins.

- Players will be divided into 2-3 sections by USCF rating or age, depending on the number of registered rated players.

- Official USCF rules apply. Common rules to be aware of include:
- Touch moves (you must move the first piece you touch on your turn).

- Only one hand is allowed to touch the pieces and clock.

Bulverde , TX 78163

United States

When:
Saturday, March 14, 2026
Round 1 starts approximately at 9:00 AM. Remaining rounds will start as soon as possible after the previous round.
Time Controls:
G30; d5 (30 minutes with 5-second delay)
4-Round Swiss System (based on entries)
Sections:
MS/HS Championship (Grades 6–12)
Elementary Championship (Grades K–5)
Primary Championship (Grades K–3)
* Sections may be merged or split based on participation.
Entry Fee:

- $35 Early Bird (on or before February 21, 2026)

- $45 Regular Entry

- $55 Late Entry (after March 7, 2026)

Awards:

- Texas Region III Girls Championship Title for each section.

- Trophies will be awarded to the Top 3 individuals in each section.

- Tiebreaks will be used to determine final standings for trophy positions. If there is a tie for first place, a blitz playoff game (3 minutes with a 2-second delay) will be conducted among the tied players. If the blitz game also results in a tie, an Armageddon playoff will be used to determine the champion.

Byes:

- Up to one ½-point bye is allowed for any round except the last round. The bye must be requested before the end of Round 2.

- A zero-point bye/withdrawal must be requested before the section pairing is done.

Withdrawals/Refund:

- Any withdrawal before the tournament will incur a $10 processing and transaction fee. No refunds will be issued for withdrawals in the last two days before the tournament.

More Details:

- February/March US Chess ratings and rules will be used for pairings and awarding prizes.

- Chess boards and pieces will be provided. Bring your own chess clock.

- Unrated players will be placed at the Tournament Director’s discretion.

- No spectators are allowed in the tournament area.

- Players may not eat at the board. Only water or soft drinks are allowed.

- All non-essential electronic devices must be completely powered off and remain in the player’s bag or face up on the table during play. Violations may result in penalties up to loss of game or removal from the tournament.

- Only US Chess–approved electronic notation devices are allowed.

- Notation is required for the MS/High School Championship section.
