El Dorado Afternoon Crazy Quads

El Dorado Train Depot, East Room

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

Prologue:
I personally dislike waking up hours before I normally would to make the long drive to a chess tournament that starts early in the morning, playing for 6-8 hours, and drive back. And I sure as heck am not paying for pet boarding and a hotel on top of the entry fee. What an exhausting mess. If you can relate to that, then boy do I have the event for you!
Tournament:
Format: Quads. Up to four groups of four players in a round-robin. 3 rounds total.
Time Control: g/45; d5.
Registration: Register online before 11:59PM on 03/12. Venue opens at 11AM. Register at KingRegistration.com
Round timings: Round 1 pairings at 11:50AM     Rounds:  12:01 - 1:45 - 3:30.
Registered players must arrive early or give director notice of late arrival. Failure to arrive on time or give notice of tardiness will result in automatic withdrawal.
No byes may be requested. Please come prepared to play all three rounds. If you aren't sure you can make it, please withdraw early to give someone else the chance for a seat.
Registration And Fees:
There are only 16 seats available due to space constraints. Registrations are first-come, first-serve. You are  required to check in before first round pairings or you will lose your seat. There are only three rounds, so I'm not going to make someone sit at an empty board on the off-chance you do show up late.
All games will be rated by the United States Chess Federation. (Regular and Quick)
All players must be members of the United States Chess Federation.
KCA membership not required.
Entry Fee : $0. Donations welcome but not required.
Sections:
There will be 1 section available to register in, but players will be sorted into sections of four players the day of the event. Section 1 will have the top four rated players, then the second will have the next highest group of four, and so on.
If the registered players cannot form a multiple of four and the last section has 3 players available, the director will enter himself into the appropriate quad for his rating to ensure everyone gets a full quad.
If the registered players plus director cannot form a multiple of four, the bottom two quads will be merged and ran as a 3-round swiss. In that case, the director reserves rights to use accelerated pairings if deemed necessary for better pairings. Director may enter himself if necessary for better pairings.
Equipment:
Boards, pieces, and clocks will all be provided by the director. Do not bring your own.
Nearby Amenities:
Coffee: Great coffee shop (Dilly Deli) within a short walk
Food: Mexican restaurant within a short walk, Casey's, Taco Bell, Wendy's, and Arby's within a short drive. We have a refrigerator to keep food and drinks in, and a microwave to cook it.
Parking: Free, on-site.
Contact:
Feel free to reach out with any questions you might have.
Email: [email protected]
Phone (Text only): (316) 350-7354

Address: 430 N Main St

El Dorado , KS 67042

United States

4th Austin Chess Tour: Junior Qualifier #3

Saturday, March 14, 2026

Event Overview

4th Austin Chess Tour: Junior Qualifier #3
In-Person Scholastic USCF Rated Tournament
March 14, 2026
12466 Los Indios Trail, Ste. 100
Austin, TX 78729
* USCF Membership Required *
Free Parking Provided
Capacity: 100 players
Note that this is a scholastic event, only players who are 18 years of age or under can play in this tournament.
All players will be divided into five sections:
SECTION A: 1600+ USCF rated
SECTION B: 1200 - 1599 USCF rated
SECTION C: 800 - 1199 USCF rated
SECTION D: 400 - 799 USCF rated
SECTION E: Under 400 USCF rated or unrated
**Players are not allowed to play up or down**
ENTRY FEES:
Early Bird: $40 before 11:59pm, February 22, 2026
Standard Fee: $50   before 11:59 March 8, 2026
Late Fee: $65 after March 9, 2026
PRIZES:
Trophies for 1st Place, Medals for 2nd and 3rd
Junior Qualifier Points:
Top 10 places in Section A will earn points according to the following table:
1st Place: 25 JQ Points
2nd Place: 18 JQ Points
3rd Place: 15 JQ Points
4th Place: 12 JQ Points
5th Place: 10 JQ Points
6th Place: 8 JQ Points
7th Place: 6 JQ Points
8th Place: 4 JQ Points
9th Place: 2 JQ Points
10th Place: 1 JQ Points
For more information about the point system, visit
https://austin-chess.com/tournaments/
TIME CONTROL:
Section A: G/60, d5 (60 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section B: G/60, d5 (60 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section C: G/45, d5 (45 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section D: G/30, d5 (30 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section E: G/30, d5 (30 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
4-Round Swiss System Schedule
SECTIONS A and B:
1st round: 9:00 AM
2nd round: 11:15 PM
Lunch Break: 1:30-2:30 PM
3rd round: 2:30 PM
4th round: 4:45 PM
SECTION C:
1st round: 10:00 AM
2nd round: 11:45 AM
Lunch Break: 1:30-2:30 PM
3rd round: 2:30 PM
4th round: 4:15 PM
5-Round Swiss System Schedule
SECTIONS D and E:
1st round: 10:00 AM
2nd round: 11:15 AM
3rd round: 12:30 PM
Lunch Break: 1:30 PM
4th round: 2:30 PM
5th round: 3:45 PM
Closing ceremony: After the last game of the section finishes.
NOTE: Half-point byes are acceptable for all rounds, limit 1. Must commit before the 1st round.

PLAYERS MAY NOT POSSESS CELL PHONES DURING THE TOURNAMENT.  Please leave your phone at home, in your car, or turned off (vibrate/silent not acceptable) on top of your table.
Any violators may be subject to disqualification and forfeiture.
CANCELLATION POLICY: If you do not wish to participate in our tournament after paying the entry fee, please email us at  [email protected] no later than 24 hours in advance for an 80% refund. We reserve the right to charge a service fee for cancellations. NO refunds will be issued if we are notified of cancellation within 24 hours of the start of the event.
WITHDRAWAL POLICY: If you would like to withdraw from the tournament after it begins, please alert the tournament director. NO refunds will be issued after the tournament begins.
NO-SHOW POLICY: There are NO refunds or credit for players who do not show up for their scheduled tournament matches.
For additional questions, please contact us at [email protected]

Address: 12466 Los Indios Trail, Ste.100

Austin , TX 78729

United States

Residency Restriction: No

The DMV Spring Action Tournament (In Person)

Hampton Inn and Suites Dulles

Sunday, March 15, 2026

Event Overview

The DMV Spring Action Tournament
Hampton Inn and Suites Dulles
22700 Holiday Park Drive, Sterling, VA 20166
Sunday, March 15 at 4 pm
Register here: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8459

Tournament Information:

- 4 round Swiss tournament.

- USCF regular and quick rated. Time control: Game in 30 minutes with a 5-second delay.

- Sunday, March 15, 4 pm to approximately 9 pm. (First round starts at 4, subsequent rounds occur ASAP.)

- Entry fee: $30 on or before Wednesday the week of the tournament, $35 on or before Saturday, $40 on Sunday (on-site registration is allowed, registration for round one closes at 3:45 pm on Sunday). Free entry to players over 2200 ($30 entry deducted from prizes--please email to register).

- Two Sections: Open (minimum 1300 rating to play) and Under 1500.

- Note: In order to play in the open section, players must have a USCF rating of at least 1300. Players rated between 1300 and 1499 can play in either section. Players under 1300 should play in the Under 1500 section. A player can still join the open section if their unpublished (live) rating is over 1300, even if their monthly rating isn't 1300 yet. The tournament director may decide to have a lower rated player join the open section to maintain an even number of players in the section. The tournament director has the option to use a provisionally-rated player's live rating (regardless of whether it is higher or lower than the player's official rating) for pairings purposes and section eligibility.

- PRIZES: $100 for 1st in Open; $50 for 1st in U1500.

- Up to two half-point byes are allowed. Half-point byes can be requested for any round. The deadline to request a half-point bye is prior to the start of round 3.

- We will have enough chess sets for all players, but clocks will not be provided for everyone. If you have a clock, please bring one.

- This tournament is open to everyone (adults and children of any skill level).

- There is plenty of free parking at the playing venue.

- For questions, please email us at Click here to show mail address  or call us at 703-609-0499.

How to Register

2026 Ohio All-Girls State Championship

State Championship Event

Glen Oak Elementary School

Sunday, March 15, 2026

Event Overview

2026 Ohio All-Girls Championship
Sunday, March 15, 2026
Glen Oak Elementary School
7300 Blue Holly Dr.
Lewis Center, Ohio 43035
Proudly Sponsored by the Glen Oak PTO
Tournament organizer:  Jim Bickley, (740) 657-5518 or  Click here to show mail address .
Eligibility: Any girl enrolled in an Ohio school, or home schooled in Ohio, in grades K-12 is eligible to participate. All players need to have a current USCF membership. To purchase a membership, visit  https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess .  The March rating supplement will be used.
The top finisher of the Championship section will receive a $300 stipend from OSCA and qualify as Ohio's delegate for the 2026 Ruth Haring National Girls’ Tournament of Champions in Grand Rapids Michigan, August 3-6.
Accommodations:  The Ohioan Hotel and Event Center, 100 Green Meadows Dr.  Lewis Center, Ohio 43035.  (614) 880-4300.  Ask for the chess rate of $155.00.  The online code for this rate is GSCC.  This includes breakfast and is a five minute drive to Glen Oak.  This is a beautiful resort and has been recently updated.  https://www.nwhotelandconferencecenter.com/
Sections and time controls:
Championship (K-12)  5 rounds, G/45; d5.
U1000 Premier (K-12)  5 rounds, G/30; d5.
U600 Reserve (K-12)  5 rounds, G/30; d5.
Sets, clocks and scoresheets provided.  Notation is required in the championship section and strongly recommended in the premier and reserve sections.
Schedule:  Doors open at 8:00.  Announcements will be at 8:45.  No section changes after this time.  Round 1 will begin immediately after announcements.  We will take a 30 minute break for lunch between rounds at a suitable time.
Concessions:  We will offer coffee and doughnuts for breakfast.  We’ll also serve snacks and the Glen Oak Meal (slice of pizza, chips, cookie and drink for $5.00).
Entry fee:  $40.00 by March 7.  $45.00 after this date.  Registration ends on March 14 at 6:00 p.m.  On-site registrations will not be accepted.
Registration:     https://pci.jotform.com/form/260045844154151
Withdrawals and refunds.  Players will get a full refund if requested by Saturday, March 14.
Awards:  Trophies befitting of a state champion will be awarded in the championship section.  Players who score 3 or more points will earn a trophy.  Participation medals will be awarded to those not earning a trophy.  Trophies will be awarded to the top three teams in each section.  A team consists of a minimum of two players per school, per section.  A maximum of the top four players from each school, per section, will count toward team scores.
To check the status of registered players, please visit  www.glenoakchess.org under Ohio Girls Championship.

4th Annual East Coast Scholastic Championship (In Person)

Hampton Inn and Suites Dulles

Sunday, March 15, 2026

Event Overview

4th Annual East Coast Scholastic Championship
Hampton Inn and Suites Dulles (same venue as last year)
22700 Holiday Park Drive, Sterling, VA 20166
Sunday, March 15, 2026 at 10 am
Register here: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8458

Congratulations to last year's winners:
K-12 Section: Lance Pitrolo from West Virginia and Aman Shaik from Maryland
K-8 Section: Vladislav Inchin from Virginia
K-5 Section: Etamin Kent from Maryland
K-3 Section: Zoran Shaik from Maryland and Nikhil Matthew from Virginia
Tournament Information

- Last year's tournament drew about 100 participants! We hope to have an even greater turnout this year. Please help us by spreading the word about this tournament!

- Four rounds: first round at 10 am, subsequent rounds occur as soon as possible

- Four sections: K-12, K-8, K-5, and K-3

- Time control: Game in 25 minutes with a 5-second delay ( US Chess regular and quick rated)

- Entry fee: $35 by 2/28, $40 by 3/8, $45 by 3/14, $50 on 3/15 (on-site registration closes 30 minutes before round 1)

- Boards and pieces will be provided for all players, but we don’t have enough clocks for everyone (those who have clocks are welcome to bring them)

- This tournament is US Chess rated, so an active US Chess membership is required. Click here to join the US Chess Federation for the first time or to renew an inactive membership:  https://new.uschess.org/user/login?destination=/form/membership

- Don’t hesitate to reach out to us at Click here to show mail address  with any questions

PRIZES
Trophies for 1st through 5th in each section, plus special prizes for the 1st place winner in each section!

Venue Information/Logistics

- PARKING:  The hotel has plenty of free parking.

- Free water will be provided for attendees.

- There is no scheduled lunch break, but there is almost always time for players to have food between games. There aren't any scheduled round times--rounds will occur as soon as possible.

- See below for information about sleeping rooms if traveling from out of town.

Hotel Accommodations:
Visit this link to reserve rooms at the hotel where the tournament will be held (Hampton Inn and Suites Dulles):  https://www.hilton.com/en/hotels/wasduhx-hampton-suites-washington-dulles-international-airport/?flexibleDates=false&numRooms=1&numAdults=1&numChildren=0&room1ChildAges=&room1AdultAges=&sessionToken=dcb93e8c-54fe-4f76-890b-86457a9a56d1
Alternative Option Nearby: The Best Western Dulles Airport Inn on 45440 Holiday Drive offers a very affordable rate and is right next to the playing venue. This hotel is only about a twenty-second walk from the tournament. The Best Western also offers free breakfast.  http://www.bestwestern.com/en_US.html

How to Register
Register here: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8458

Side Event
At 4 pm we have another tournament which is open to both adults and scholastic players. The scholastic championship will be over by then, so it is possible to play both events. Here is the link to view information about the 4 pm tournament:  https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8459

MVP Chess K-12 Quads (FREE for US Chess Members)

Mount Vernon Rec Center

Sunday, March 15, 2026

Event Overview

Date: Sunday, March 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM
Venue: Mount Vernon Rec Center – Multi-Purpose Room 1. The center has recently been renovated and features state-of-the-art facilities including a gym, two skating rinks, an indoor pool, and a rock-climbing wall.
Organizer: MVP Chess is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Alexandria, Virginia. Our mission is to make chess accessible for everyone and develop growth-minded players. For questions, please email [email protected] .
Register Now: MVP Chess K-12 Quads | March 2026 - Organized by MVP Chess | Chess Nut
Entry & Donations
This tournament is FREE for all US Chess members in grades K–12.
An active US Chess membership is required — you can join or renew here .
The event is limited to 32 players, so please register in advance to secure your spot and help us plan pairings and sections.
We welcome voluntary donations to help cover the cost of room rental, awards, and other tournament-related expenses.
All contributions are tax-deductible and may be made online or onsite at the event.
Format

- 3-round quad (final section may be a small Swiss)

- Time control: G/25; d5 (25 minutes per player, 5-second delay)

- Rated by US Chess

Awards

- 🏆 Trophies for each quad winner

- 🎖️ Medals for all other participants

- 📺 Game Analysis Feature: Select games will be analyzed on the MVP Chess YouTube channel. To be considered, players should submit their scoresheets at the end of the event.

Schedule

- Check-in: 12:45 PM

- Round 1: 1:00 PM

- Rounds begin as soon as prior games finish

- Awards Ceremony: immediately after the last round

- Expected finish: no later than 4:00 PM

Rules & Expectations

- US Chess rules apply

- Notation optional

- Chess sets and clocks provided

- Parents/guardians should stay on-site during the event

- Please show respect for opponents, staff, and the venue

Media Policy
MVP Chess may take photos or short video clips for educational and promotional purposes.
Names will not be published without consent. If you prefer not to be photographed, simply let us or the photographer know.

Alexandria , VA 22307

Ridgefield March 15th Sunday Open

Saint Andrew's Lutheran Church

Sunday, March 15, 2026

Event Overview

*** Players who recently created or renewed a US Chess account may find that the membership expiration date is invalid and consequently, are unable to register successfully for the tournament.  If so email [email protected] with member ID and intended section, and the tournament director should be able to assist. ***
Times  (All sections may end earlier or later depending on gameplay)

- All sections - Round 1 starts promptly at 1:05PM, subsequent rounds ASAP.

- Award ceremony and group photo for U400 section expected to end at 5:00 PM, and by 6:30 PM for other sections.

Location : St. Andrew's Lutheran Church, 6 Ivy Hill Road, Ridgefield, CT, 06877

Sections* :

- U400 : 4SS, G/30.  Four rounds of US Chess rated chess in Swiss System format. Each player has 30 minutes to make their moves in a game with no delay per move. Players will be grouped by live regular rating, and notation is not required.

- U1300, U800 and U600 sections : 4SS, G/30;d/5.  Four rounds of US Chess rated chess in Swiss System format. Each player has 30 minutes to make their moves in a game with 5 second delay per move. Players will be grouped by live regular rating.  Players may choose not to notate, but will receive a 5 minute penalty to compensate opponent for their notation time (G/25 instead of G/30).  S ections may be combined if there are <7 players in a section.

- Players should already be familiar with how to move and capture pieces, castle, how to check/checkmate an opponent, and play to the end of each game without being distracted.  If unsure whether a player is ready, please email  tournament director .

- Beginner players in grades K-5 who do not yet have rated tournament experience are suggested to register for the U400 section, although parents are free to register players in the U800 section.  Beginner players in grades 6-adult should register in the U600 section, although stronger players are encouraged to register for the U1300 section.  All players grades K - adult may register for the U1300 section.

- All sections are rated, and a valid US Chess membership is required for all players.

- When siblings are playing in the same section, a pairing exception will be added if possible.

- If a section is full, seating will not be increased.  If a player registration is cancelled before the tournament date, that seat will be available.

Discounts
Entry fee increases on March 1st and March 12th, so register early to avoid the higher entry fees.

Byes:

- A half (1/2) point bye requests (1 maximum) is available for round 1.

- Zero (0) point bye requests are available for later rounds.

- Byes must be requested before pairing for each round is announced.

- Players may request a half point bye for their first round when registering, if anticipating that a player will arrive late.  Players not playing the first round should arrive by 2:45 PM latest for the U400 section, and 2:50 latest for the other sections.

Entry deadline : Saturday 10 pm (day before tournament). No on-site registration.

Prizes (All sections except U1300)

- Gold medals for player(s) in top half of pool for each section, (for example, 1 point for each game won, 0.5 points for each game drawn), with no computer calculated tie-breaks. Silver medals for all other players.

- Trophies are awarded to top player/players in each section.  (See note at bottom for tie break rules if there are 2+ players with a tie).

Prizes (U1300 section)

- $90 cash prize for section winner/winners, with $45 for the second place winner/winners.

Refunds/Cancellation/Inclement Weather Policy :

- If unable to participate, registered players may withdraw by contacting the tournament director.  If cancelling by Tuesday midnight before tournament, fee will be refunded but are subject to a $10 administrative fee.  If cancelling after Tuesday, refund is subject to a $15 administrative fee.

- If a player is feeling unwell (coughing, has fever, sore throat, etc) day of event, they should not compete in consideration of the health of other players.

- If there is heavy snow day of event and road conditions are unsafe locally in Ridgefield, tournament will be rescheduled and players will be given the option to have their entry fee refunded with a $2 fee to cover platform and credit card costs.

Additional Details :
*  This event takes place on Sunday afternoon, not Saturday afternoon.
* To register, go to link  https://www.events4chess.com/events/?event_ID=2543&cat=1
* An active US Chess membership is required prior to registering for this tournament for all sections. - available at  https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess . The fee for one child under 19 is $24/year, and the membership fee for adults (under 65) is $54/year.  Other membership options are available.
* Chess sets, clocks, pencils, erasers, and score sheets are provided, and players do not need to bring their own equipment.  Players are welcome to use their own score sheets/score books.
* Supervision: Tournament director and tournament assistant(s) will be coordinating this event.  Dropoff is possible, and parents can be contacted via cellphone as needed.  Parents with players who require supervision should plan to attend the event for duration.  For players without cellphone, parents may request at sign-in a text message to be sent to contact phone number at the start of round 4.
* Pizza will be delivered to venue  at 3 PM, with water bottles and chips also available for purchase.  Payment on-site via Venmo or Paypal.
* Safety: Masks are optional, and no food is allowed in the playing area.   A water bottle for players is suggested.
* Parking: There are plenty of parking spaces in the venue parking lot.
* Social media: Photos/videos will be taken at the event and may be posted to the club website or social media accounts for outreach and marketing purposes. Inform the tournament director before the day of the event to opt-out if desired.
* See  tournament handout  for event rules and tournament etiquette.  Taking notation is required for players in all sections except U400, although players may request an exemption with 5 minute penalty.  Notation is not required for players in the U400 sections.
* For families visiting Ridgefield,  Ridgefield's local library  is open until 5 PM, and there are coffee shops ( Queen B ,  Tazza Cafe , an ice cream and candy shop (Deborah Ann's), and the local bookstore ( Books on the Common ) in downtown Ridgefield.  Limited seating provided for parents and family members.  Parents are welcome and encouraged to stay for the beginning and end of the tournament for the orientation and award ceremony.
* Tournament results and link to event photos will be posted to  https://tournaments.wayoftheboard.org .
* Latest published ratings are used for tournament registration as opposed to official ratings.  A player's official published rating will not be given to a player until 25+ games have been played and is updated 12 times a year.  Tournament director may move a player to different section on day of event if rating has changed from time of registration (for example, if rating was initially 399 but on day of event is 401 player may be moved to the U800 section).
* An Events4Chess account is not necessary to register a player for a tournament, only the player's US Chess account ID.  It is only needed to auto-populate fields when registering, or to be notified when a new event is live.
* Payment: Paypal/credit card/debit card accepted for payment.  To use a payment method other than Paypal after checkout, select "Pay with Debit or Credit Card".
* Tie Break format for U400/U800 sections - If there are 2+ top players tied in a section, a playoff will determine the section winner and trophy recipient, and will immediately follow the last round. The playoff format will be G/5/4 d2 Armageddon game, blitz rules apply, with pawn hand determining player color (tournament director will have black and white pawns in hand, players choose hand to determine color).   All other ties broken by US Chess standard tie break rules.
* To confirm if a player was successfully registered after submitting the registration fee, check the Participants list.  If the player is listed, registration was successful.
* An orientation email will be sent out at 8 AM day of event with additional details for first-time parents and players, but parents/players can email tournament director with any questions.
* Printable flyer:  https://www.events4chess.com/dashboard/events/rds_generate_flyer.php?event_ID=2543

Farmers Branch Chess Club

1804 Mindehall Drive, Farmers Branch Texas 75234

IMPORTANT :

Participants MUST bring their own Tournament Clocks & Scoresheets.
Tournament will be initially limited to 30 players.

United States Chess Memberships Required for all sections - Can Be Purchased using this online registration form

Open to All the players

US Chess Rated.

Date : 3/15/2026

In the event of low turnout , sections MAY be merged.
Entry Fee :  $30

Format:
4 Round Swiss, non-elimination
Time : 9 AM CST

Round 1 starts at 9:00 AM.
Lunch break for 30 minutes after Round 1. All others ASAP.
All rounds G/30; D5 Second Time Delay.

Awards : Trophy

Blitz :

Section : Open
Entry Fee :  $15

Format:
5 Round Swiss, non-elimination
Time : Immediately upon Regular Rounds completion

All rounds G/5; 0 Second Time Delay.

Awards : Trophy

Registration:  On-line  - https://www.farmersbranchchessclub.com/
Mandatory to Submit this form online AFTER making the Zelle Transfer - Registration ends at 11:00pm the day before the event.

Payment  : Zelle Transfer to [email protected] .(Include  Participant   Full name in the Memo Field during Zelle Transfer)

Inquiries  : [email protected]
Lunch\Drinks  : Not available at Location - Participants may bring sack lunches. Please plan accordingly

Tournament Policy :

Refunds: A player can receive Tournament credits if notified in an email by 11:00pm the day before the event. Players that no-show do not receive a refund. No exceptions.
Photography: Photos will be taken of the tournament

Note :

Parents/Guardians of Minors

We welcome children to play in our tournament, but please be aware of the following:
Your child will play against adults, will be treated like an adult, and will be expected to interact like an adult. Your child will not be supervised by us. If a child is under 16 years old, a parent/guardian must remain in the building.

Rule Variations in Effect at the Tournament

1H1. Director as witness only.  In an event in which most games are not watched by directors, a director may refrain from correcting all illegal moves he or she may notice but simply serve as a witness should one of the players point out the illegal move before any moves have been made.
15A. Paper scoresheet variation.  The player using a paper scoresheet may first make the move, and then write it on the scoresheet, or vice versa.

TCA Region V Scholastic 2026 (Middle School)

The Houston Chess Studio

Sunday, March 15, 2026

Event Overview

TCA Region V Scholastic 2026
(Middle School)
Date & Location
Date:  March 15, 2026
Location:  The Houston Chess Studio 250 Patton St. Suite I Houston, TX 77079

Contact Info
Organizer:  Edgar Acosta
Email:   [email protected]
Phone:  (281) 844 4139

Pricing

- Early Registration: $32, ends on March 1, 2026

- Regular Registration: $37, between March 2-8, 2026

- Late Registration: $40, between March 9-13, 2026

- Active USCF membership is required by March 1, 2026.
- Visit  new.uschess.org/join-us-chess  starting at $24 to join USCF or renew your membership!

- Visit  chess.jliptrap.us/hgroup.htm  for $13 discount Scholastic memberships and renewals!

- TCA Tournament membership is included in the tournament entry fee.
- Visit  texaschess.org/memberships  to join TCA or renew your membership!

Pricing is included in the registration form automatically.

Eligibility
Participants must live or attend school in one of these counties:

- Austin, Brazoria, Brazos, Chambers, Fort Bend, Galveston, Grimes

- Hardin, Harris, Houston, Jasper, Leon, Liberty, Madison

- Matagorda, Montgomery, Newton, Orange, Polk, Robertson

- San Jacinto, Trinity, Tyler, Walker, Waller, Wharton

The max number of registrations for this tournament is 74. Text Edgar Acosta to join a waiting list

Sections

- Middle School Open: Any Middle Schooler (Junior High Student) may enter this section.

- Middle School U800: Only Middle Schoolers rated 800 or below may enter this section.

- Note:  Sections may be combined in case of low registrations.

Definitions:

- High School  - Grades 9-12; in some districts 10-12, if Junior High is 7-9.

- Middle School  - Grades 6 to 8 or 9 depending on how the school district divides them.

- Elementary  - K-6 if 6th grade is in the Elementary building, K-5 if 6 is in Middle School.
- A 5th-6th campus has been ruled Elementary, a 6th-only campus as Middle School.

- Primary  - K-3. Note that a first grader could enter K-1 or K-3 or K-5.

- K-8 and K-12 schools and Home School Associations are divided K-5, 6-8, and 9-12.

- Students not assigned a grade in school will be assigned a grade at the tournament based on their age as of September 1 of that school year as follows: six years old is assigned first grade, seven years old is assigned second grade, and so on through grade twelve.

Note:  Sections are based on USCF January 2026 ratings. "Current" ratings may be used to pair unrated players but will  not  determine section placement. Accelerate Pairings will be used at the discretion of the TD the day of the tournament.

Tournament Format

- Rounds:  Swiss 5 Rounds, Game in 25 with a 5-second delay (G/25 d/5).

- Membership:  USCF and TCA memberships required.

- Rules:  USCF rules apply.

- Open sections  require notation  and clocks (if available).
- Players who opt to not take notation will have their time start at 20 minutes instead of 25.

- Reserved sections are strongly encouraged to use notation and clocks.

- Touch-move / Touch-take:  Applies to all sections. Younger players, especially in Kinder-1st Open, will be encouraged to keep these rules with gentle reminders as needed.

- Equipment:  Plan on bringing your own chess set and clock if you have one, money for lunch, and a good attitude!
- Every player needs to bring their clocks!

- Please make sure your clocks are labeled with the player's name and USCF ID.

- Chess sets for the whole tournament  will  be provided!

Schedule

- No At-Site Registration. All registrations must be submitted online at/or before 11:59pm on March 13, 2026.

- Please arrive between 8:15 and 8:45 to check in and get ready to play.

- Round 1:  Starts at 9:00 AM SHARP; subsequent rounds will start ASAP. No elimination.

- Players may request a single 1/2 point Bye missed, 0 point Bye for any subsequent Byes. Any Byes need to be requested by Friday February 13th, 2026 at 7pm.

- Lunch break after Round 3, estimating 12pm-1pm.

Teams
Teams consist of two or more (2+) players in the same section from the same school/association.

- Team members must attend the  same school campus  full-time or belong to the  same Home School Association .

- Sections are  not combined  for teams.

- Team scores will be calculated by summing the top four (4) individual scores from each team.

Awards

- Trophies:  Top 5 individuals in each section and Top 4 teams in each section.

- 1st Place Finishers qualify for a spot in the State Regional Invitational April 18-19th .

- Alternate awards (likely medals) to players who score 3 or more points but do not win a trophy.

- Tie Breaks:  Solkoff (sum of opponents' scores), Modified Median (dropping the lowest opponent's score), Cumulative of Opposition, then Cumulative (USCF Standard)

We look forward to seeing you at The Houston Chess Studio  on March 15, 2026  for a day of competitive and fun scholastic chess!

2026 St Patrick’s Quad/Mini Swiss (FIDE rated)

Charles W Hatherill

Tuesday, March 17, 2026

Event Overview

LOCATION: Panera Bread, 2001 Indian River Blvd, Vero Beach, FL 32960
Date : Tuesday, March 17, 2026
ROUNDS: Three Rounds:  First round starts at approximately  6:30 PM .
TIME CONTROL : G15; d5
Limited to the first 32 players based on space and upper Quads will be FIDE rated.
PRIZES : $50 for first place at each Quad (if two players tied for 1st place $25 each) A donation of $5 will be made per Quad to Military Chess ( https://new.uschess.org/form/donate ).
ENTRY FEE : $20.00 if you pay by Tuesday March 16 by 11:59 pm. $25 after that and at the door. USCF membership is required. A donation of $5 will be made per Quad/Mini Swiss to Military Chess.
Register online:  Click here .
Please check your USCF ID and renew it if it has expired.
IMPORTANT NOTICE : Due to space limitation to secure your spot and pay ahead of time! BRING YOUR CHESS CLOCK and Chess Board and Pieces!!!
WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT? After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest.  Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list.  The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each.  If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. A Quad Tournament consists of the top four ranked players (#s 1-4) on the Chess Ladder playing each other, then the second top four ranked players (#s 5-8) playing each other, then the third top four ranked players (#s 9-12) playing each other, and so forth. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.
ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS : The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience can compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players can win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have the opportunity for your rating to go up faster!!!

Grand Prix

Hilton Garden Inn - Southpark

Friday, March 20, 2026
- Sunday, March 22, 2026

https://www.charlottechesscenter.org/events/springfide

OVERVIEW
The 2026 Spring Southeastern FIDE takes place March 20-22, 2026 in SouthPark Charlotte. There are three FIDE and US Chess rated sections with a minimum rating of 1500 to participate. There is a $5,500 guaranteed prize fund - $5,000 in the main event plus a free $500 Saturday evening blitz tournament.

There is a registration cap of 125 players. The Spring SE FIDE runs alongside the Spring GM/IM Norm Invitational .

5th Annual Old Line Open

Rockville Hilton

Friday, March 20, 2026
- Sunday, March 22, 2026

Event Overview

5th Annual Old Line Open
Rockville, Maryland
Individual Registration
Group Registration
Championship, U2100, U1900, U1700, U1500: 5SS, Game/90 inc/30 -- (2-day schedule: Rnds 1-2 Game/45 inc/30)
U1250 and U1000 : 5SS, Game/75 d/5 with Rnds 1-2 at Game/45 d/5;
U1250 3-day schedule : all rounds Game/75 d/5
Playing Site
Rockville Hilton, Rockville, MD
We aim to create a pleasant environment for playing chess. Below are the answers we received at a previous tournament to the question of what do we do better than other tournaments.
Advance Entries
Tournament Features

- We pair rounds as early as possible and start rounds on time → You have time to get ready and don't have to waste your time waiting for the round to start

- 30" increment time control in the top five sections → No more clock smashing scrambles at the end of the game.

- Score-based prizes → See the advantages below.

- Additional 1st place prizes to clear first when there is no 5-0 player in the section, added to your score prize → More prize money

- Minimum ratings to play in the top 5 sections → Less mismatch games.

- Sets, boards and clocks provided for everyone → No more carrying around pieces and a board, just bring a clock.

- Free Sunday morning Continental breakfast → Relax, have some coffee and a danish before you start your game.

- Texting or emailing of pairings to your cell phone available → No rush at the pairing chart before the round

- $149 hotel rate, Reserve a room → Relax and stay at the tournament hotel. $5 EF discount if staying at hotel.

- Hotel next to DC Metro stop → Take the Metro directly to the tournament.

- Shorter time controls in lower sections → Less waiting around between rounds.

Prizes
This tournament will pay prizes based solely on your final score. All the prizes are guaranteed. If the total pay out in the Open section is less than $1500, extra money will be added to the pay out of the top score group to bring the total to $1500.

Advantages over place-based scoring
Less Waiting
Your score determines your prize. Once you finish your last game, you can receive a check.
Less Uncertainty
Your prize does not get lowered if others tie with you. For example, if there are two 5-0 players, both receive the full amount for 5-0.
Less short draws
The total payout is always higher when games are decisive.

Under 1250 section: all entrance fees $45 less.

Free early entrance to GMs.  nothing will be subtracted from any prizes.

$5 discount if staying at hotel.
Individual Registration
Group Registration
Mail Registrations to:
Maryland Chess Assn.
1827 Thornton Ridge Road
Towson, MD 21204
Mailed registrations should include name, section, schedule(2-day or 3-day). The chief TD for the tournament will be Mike Regan. If you have any questions about the tournament email him at [email protected] .
Advance Registrations
Schedules
3-day schedule Champ - U1500: Reg ends Fri 6 pm, rds. Fri 7 pm, Saturday 11am and 5:30, Sunday 9:30 am and 2:45.
2-day schedule Champ - U1500: Reg ends Sat 10 am, rds. Saturday 11am, 2:15 and 5:30, Sunday 9:30 am and 2:45.
U1000 and U1250 2-day schedule: Reg ends Sat 10 am, rds. Saturday 11, 12:45 and 3:00, Sunday 9:30 am and 12:15 pm.
U1250 3-day schedule: Reg ends Fri 6 pm, rds Friday 7 pm, Saturday 11 and 3:00, Sunday 9:30 am and 12:15 pm.
Byes
Half point byes: all must commit before rd 3
Reentries:
all, $80 except U1000 and U1250 $40. You can reenter any schedule taking 1/2 point byes for unplayed games. If you reenter with a single 1/2 point bye, the cost is $70/$35. If you reenter with two 1/2 point byes, the cost is $60/$30.
Hotel Rates: $149 per night $5 EF discount if staying at hotel. Reserve a room
Parking : $6 for day guest and $10 overnight. Parking is free in Metro parking lot over the weekend.
Rooms are limited. So make your reservations early.
Rule Variations

- In sections that the organizer provides clocks, if both players are not present at the start of the round, the tournament director will start white's clock.

- Clocks that halt on end are preferred in all sections with increment time controls.

- Any player forfeiting a round must pay a $50 fine before being allowed to play in a future tournament organized by MCA or Baltimore Chess.

- The electronic score keeping devices, ChessNoteR and eNotate, cannot be used at this tournament.

- All players with provisional ratings will have 100 points added to their rating for determining section eligibility

- Players with byes who are eligible to play in a lower section that also has a bye player may get paired in that section as a house player. They will still have the bye for standings in their original section. The game in the lower section does count for standings and must be played.

- The TD will specify which direction the clocks must face.

- The provided clocks will be set to "halt on end".

- FIDE rated sections will use FIDE rules. A summary of the differences is here.

Phone Rules

- All phones should be off. Phones should not be on your person when you leave the room. In non-FIDE rated sections you can store you phone on the table or in a bag next to your chair. Phone lockers are available for all sections.

- Any with ringing phone or leaving (or returning to ) the playing hall with a phone will receive a time reduction of 30 minutes or half your remaining time which ever is less.

- Anyone using their phone to affect the game will be forfeited.

Texas Chess Center - Irving

Friday, March 20, 2026
- Sunday, March 22, 2026

Event Overview

Date: March 20th - March 22nd, 2026 (Friday through Sunday)
Location: TCC Irving Location - 4343 W Royal Lane #114, Irving, TX 75063
Sections: Championship & U1800 & U1400 (U1400 section, USCF rated )
Time Control: G/90;+30
3 Day Schedule: March 20th - March 22nd, 2026
Friday: Round 1 @ 7:00PM
Saturday: Round 2 @ 2:00PM, Round 3 @ 7:00PM
Sunday: Round 4 @ 10:00AM, Round 5 @ 3:00PM
2 Day Schedule: March 21st - March 22nd, 2026
Saturday: Round 1 @ 9:00 AM, Round 2 @ 2:00PM, Round 3 @ 7:00PM
Sunday: Round 4 @ 10:00AM, Round 5 @ 3:00PM
Championship Section Registration:
Early Bird: $108 before or on 02/06
Regular Fee: $123 before or on 03/10
Late fee: $138
U1800 Section Registration:
Early Bird Price: $88 before or on 02/06
Regular Price: $103 before or on 03/10
Late Price: $118
U1400 Section Registration (US Chess Rated Only):
Early Bird Price: $78 before or on 02/06
Regular Price: $93 before or on 03/10
Late Price: $108
Prizes (All Prizes Guaranteed):
Championship - 1st: $640, 2nd: $320, 3rd: $160
U1800 - 1st: $240, 2nd: $120, 3rd: $60
U1400 (USCF Rated) - 1st, 2nd, 3rd - Trophies
First three GM/IMs to enter get a minimum prize of $200(GM)/$100(IM), valid until late fee deadline; must play all rounds. FM+ are free before late fee deadline. Please email [email protected] for entry under these conditions.
How do I get a FIDE ID? Play in one of our FIDE tournaments and fill the registration form and we’ll take care of it for you. Alternatively, you can contact USCF and request an ID as well. However, to be officially FIDE rated, one must play five games against previously rated FIDE players, score at least a half point in those games, and have a performance rating of at least 1400.
USCF monthly ratings used for pairings. Default late forfeiture time is one hour. Re-entry is available for half the late fee price.

30th annual Mid-America Open

Heritage Event, Grand Prix, Enhanced Grand Prix, Junior Grand Prix

Clayton Plaza Hotel St. Louis-Clayton

Friday, March 20, 2026
- Sunday, March 22, 2026

Event Overview

A Heritage Event!
US Chess Junior Grand Prix
March 20-22 or 21-22, 2026                           MISSOURI
US CHESS GRAND PRIX POINTS: 120 (ENHANCED)

30th annual Mid-America Open. 5-SS, 40/80, SD/30; d30 (2-day option, rounds 1-2 G/60, d10). Clayton Plaza Hotel St. Louis-Clayton, 7750 Carondelet Ave., St. Louis, MO 63105 (I-64 W/US 40-W Exit 32B, 1.2 miles north on Hanley Rd). Free parking.  $$ 20,000 GUARANTEED PRIZES!   In 6 sections: Major: open to 1900/over (see peakrating.us). $2000-1000-600-400, clear win or tiebreak 1st $100 bonus, top USCF U2300 $800-400. FIDE. Under 2100: $1500-700-500-300. FIDE. Under 1900: $1500-700-500-300. Under 1700: $1400-700-500-300. Under 1500: $1200-600-400-300. Under 1200: $900-500-300-200. Unrated prize limits: $150 in U1200, $300 U1500, $500 U1700. Mixed Doubles:  best male+female 2-player team combined score among all sections: $800-400-200. Team must average under 2200, may play different sections and schedules; register (no extra fee) by 2 pm Sat. Top 5 sections EF: $123 at chessaction.com by 3/17, $140 later online or at site until 1 hour before round 1. GMs $100 from prize. U1200 Section EF:  all $20 less than above.  Online EF $3 less  to MCA members (join/renew at mochess.org). No checks,  credit cards OK.  March Official Ratings  used. Unofficial uschess.org ratings or USCF Online Regular ratings usually used if otherwise unrated. Cannot play below USCF Online Regular rating minus 100 points. Special 1-year USCF dues with magazine paid online with entry: Adult $54, Senior (age 65+) $48, Young Adult $33, Youth $24.  Re-entry (no Major to Major) $60. 3-day schedule: Reg. ends Fri 6 pm, rds Fri 7 pm, Sat 11 & 5, Sun 10 & 3:30. 2-day schedule: Reg. ends Sat 10 am, rounds Sat 11, 2 & 5, Sun 10 & 3:30. Byes: OK all, limit 2; must commit before round 2. HR: $124 King, $128 Plaza or Executive double queen, $134 (3 people), $139 (4 people), includes free full hot buffet breakfast. Reserve at chessevents.us (or 888-303-1746, 314-726-5400, request chess rate); reserve by 2/27 or rate may increase. Car rental: Avis, 800-331-1600, use AWD #D657633, or reserve car online through chesstour.com. Prizes not claimed at site are usually paid by PayPal (may take a couple of weeks). Enter online: Chessaction.com. Questions:  [email protected] , chesstour.com. $15 service charge for refunds. No mail entries. Blitz tournament Saturday 9:30 pm, enter on site Sat. by 9:10 pm.

2026 SuperStates Blitz Championship

State Championship Event

LAX Marriott

Friday, March 20, 2026

Event Overview

Registration Online: SuperStates.org
Venue
Los Angeles Airport Marriott, 5855 West Century Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90045, US
(Click the link above to book a hotel room: $155/night)

🗓 Date & Time
Friday, March 20
6:30–8:30 PM

📍 Location
Los Angeles Airport Marriott

💵 Entry Fee: $40 by Mar 1 (11:59 PM)
Late: $50 by Mar 20 (6 PM)

⛔ Deadline: No entries after 6 PM, Mar 20

One OPEN Section: All students, adults, families, and coaches are welcome. (If entries exceed 60, the section will be split into two.)

- 🏆 Trophies to the Top 25% of players (max 10 trophies if exceeding 40 players for one section)

- This is a US Chess Blitz-rated event. Current US Chess membership is required.

Format

- 2×4SS or 2×5SS (4 or 5 double-rounds with higher-rated partner playing White & Black against opposing higher-rated partner)

- Time Control: G/3 +2

- Touch-move (same as the main event)

Blitz Rules
The current edition of the Official Rules of Chess and the current online edition of “Rulebook Changes” shall be used to resolve any situation not covered by these Scholastic Blitz Rules.

- Bring a clock. Each player is responsible for coming to the game with a clock. If neither player has a clock, then both players will receive a forfeit loss for both games. (Organizers will have a few clocks on hand, but not guaranteed.)

- Know how to use your clock. All players are required to know how to operate their clock and how to make any changes that may be necessary during a game.

- Only a TD can replace a defective clock. Only a TD may determine if a clock is defective and change the clock once the game begins.

- Same hand rule. Each player must press the clock button with the same hand used to move the pieces. This also applies to castling and capturing.

- Clock direction & seating. The TD may state the direction clocks face. The player with Black chooses which side of the table to sit on.

- Pressing the clock.
a) Except for pressing the clock button or straightening the clock, neither player should touch the clock.
b) If a player knocks over the clock, the opponent gets one minute added to the opponent’s clock.
c) If a player’s clock does not start, the opponent may try to start it by pressing the player’s clock button; if unsuccessful, signal for a TD.
d) After moving, each player must always be allowed to press the player’s clock.
e) Neither player should keep a hand on (or hovering over) the clock.

- Knocking over a piece.
a) It is unsportsmanlike conduct to knock over a piece and then press the clock.
b) First offense: warning. Second: one minute added to opponent. Third: loss of the game.
c) A player will not lose a game on time if the opponent knocks over a piece and presses the clock without picking it up; the player receives an additional minute to continue.

- Disputes. Either player may stop the clock to summon a TD. The TD will consider testimony and reliable witnesses. Appeals must be made to the Chief TD.

- Conduct. Excessive banging of pieces or clock will not be tolerated. The offending player may be penalized with loss of time.

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids

Chess Kings & Queens Academy

Saturday, March 21, 2026

Event Overview

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30.  Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00.  The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play.  Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections.  The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment.  Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $30.  Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information:  Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).
Information / registration link:  https://chesskq.com/tournament

Levy Activity Center

Saturday, March 21, 2026

Event Overview

3SS G/60, delay 5. USCF Dual Rated
Open to players who are EITHER age 14 and older OR whose US Chess Current Published Regular Rating for the month of the tournament is 900 or higher.
US Chess Membership is required.
Three Sections
Section Gold:  1700 and over (1600 - 1699 may play up to Gold)
Section Silver:   1200-1699 (1100 - 1199 may play up to Silver)
Section Bronze:  U1200 and unrated
Sections may be combined at TD discretion.  IMPORTANT: We use the US Chess Current Published Regular rating for the month of the tournament to place players in sections. We don’t make exceptions.
Junior players:  Junior players (under fourteen years) rated 900+ are welcome. Must be accompanied by an adult throughout the event. We do not accept junior players rated under 900.
Three rounds. Digital clocks are required and will be set to G/60, delay 5 . You may take one half-point bye in round 1 or round 2.
Prizes:  Your prize is an excellent playing experience at a reasonable cost. We've been running these since 2007 and people like playing here.
Entry fee is $20.  Please pre-register and pay here  when registration opens. Online registration closes when the tournament is full; we don’t have a wait list; we reopen registration if spaces become available.
On-Site Entries:  Check evanstonchess.org the morning of the tournament. If space is available  on-site entries for $20  cash are taken on an as-available basis starting at 9:00 a.m.
Master and Expert Entries:  First two Masters or Experts who sign up get free entry. If your USCF or FIDE regular rating is 2000 or higher, email your name and USCF ID to  Click here to show mail address  by 5 p.m. the Tuesday before the tournament to pre-register.

Schedule:
Check-in and On-site Registration  from 9:00 to 9:30 AM.
Players must check in on the posted registration list by 9:30 am; players who don’t check in receive a half-point bye for the first round or will be paired with another late arrival.
First Round 9:50 am, last round over roughly 5:00 pm.
Bring your lunch!  We will have a brief lunch break with no time to go out for food. On-site we have vending machine snacks, coffee and soft drinks.
Other information:  Sets supplied. Bring digital delay clocks. Wheelchair accessible. No Smoking. Limit 50 players.

2026 Sioux Falls Open Chess Championship

HyVee Grocery Store

Saturday, March 21, 2026
- Sunday, March 22, 2026

Event Overview

2026 Sioux Falls Open City Chess Championship
Dates: March 21-22
Event Site: 3000 S. Minnesota Ave., Sioux Falls, SD (2nd Floor Conference Area of Hy-Vee Grocery Store)
Sections: Two sections, U1200 and Open.  Players with ratings U1200, along with Unrated players, may register for either the U1200 or Open section.
Requirements:  Current memberships in both the United States Chess Federation and the SDCA (USCF membership registrations available online or at the site.  SDCA membership at the site).
Registration and Entry Fees : Registration available either online ( https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8211 )  or starting at 7:30 AM, at the tournament site.  Fees--$40 if completed online on or before 3/1, $45 if completed online between 3/2 and 3/20, $50 if done at the tournament site on 3/21.
Tournament Director: Waylon Lowe
email: Click here to show mail address
Time Controls: game in 90 minutes/30 sec increments (G90+30)
Byes: A maximum of two byes (1/2 point each) will be granted if requested at least one day prior to the day(s) of the match(s).
Prizes: Prizes: 1st-$100, 2nd-$50, 3rd-$25, 1st Scholastic-$50, U2000-$50, U1800-$50, U1600-$50, U1400-$50, U1200-$50 and Unrated-$25 (Prize money assumes 42 tournament players).  Trophies will be given to the top three Open finishers, the top Scholastic player, as well as to both the top scoring Open and Scholastic individuals that are also Sioux Falls residents.  Along with trophies, those two top scoring Sioux Falls residents will also be respectively bestowed with the titles of “Sioux Falls City Champion” and “Sioux Falls Scholastic City Champion”.  Trophies will also be given to the highest scoring individual in each bracket.  In case of ties, the trophy winners will be determined by standard USCF tie-break methods, as calculated in CaissaChess software. The methods, in order of precedent, will be Modified Median, Solkoff, Cumulative, and Opposition’s Cumulative. Prize money will be divided equally among the tied winners.
Additional Rules and Notes: Cellular phones and electronic devices are prohibited from use during the chess match. Please turn off all cellular phones and place in the center of the table (face-down) during tournament play. Other USCF rules will be followed during the tournament.
Equipment: Please bring chess sets and clocks.
Rounds: 3/21—9:00 AM, 1:30 PM, 6:00 PM, 3/22—9:00 AM, 2:00 PM
Questions:   Tournament Director—Waylon Lowe (email: Click here to show mail address );
Organizer—Gary Schuster (cell 605 400 4116, email: Click here to show mail address )

Fairfax Chess Tournament 3/21/26

Pozez Jewish Community Center of Northern Virginia

Saturday, March 21, 2026

Event Overview

Register at  chessacademy.com/tournaments !
This tournament is for scholastic players in grades K-12 with and without prior tournament experience.  We recommend that players in their first tournament choose the Unrated option, where they will be grouped by age and play 3 or 4 games.
Players who've previously done well in an Unrated section or have previous rated tournament experience should choose the Rated option, where they'll be placed in a group of 4 players according to their age and rating.  Each participant then plays one game against each of the other three players in their group. At the end of the third game, the winner of each group receives a trophy.
This event should typically finish in 1-2 hours, but can potentially take as long as 3 hours for the most advanced players (although that is rare).
Everyone will use a clock!  We'll go over how to use clocks on-site, and you can watch this short video to see how they work. Unrated section players will play a game in 10 minutes with a 5 second delay, and Rated games are 25 minutes with a 5 second delay for each player.
Players can play in the morning at 10am, the afternoon at 1pm, or both!

- All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all rounds

- If you're playing in the Rated sections and have a US Chess ID# and membership, please include it.  If you don't have one, we will purchase it for you ($24 value!).  If you're not sure what your ID# is you can look it up  here

- Please arrive 15 minutes before games start.  Players who arrive after that may not be placed in quads.

- Prices increase by $10 at noon the Tuesday before the tournament.

Questions?  Please let us know at  Click here to show mail address !

Lansing Center

Saturday, March 21, 2026
- Sunday, March 22, 2026

Event Overview

Lansing Center
333 E Michigan Ave
Lansing, MI, 48933, United States
Directions:
Parking in Downtown Lansing: https://www.lansingmi.gov/167/Parking-Services

Hotel Option: Doubletree by Hilton Lansing, 111 N. Grand Avenue, Lansing, MI 48933
(Near the State Capitol in Downtown Lansing); $132 + tax by February 18, 2026.
Call 833-904-2206 & identify as part of MI Chess Association Mar2026 w/ Code 92T for discounted rate
Online Reservation Link: https://www.hilton.com/en/book/reservation/rooms/?ctyhocn=LANDTDT&arrivalDate=2026-03-20&departureDate=2026-03-22&groupCode=CDT92T&room1NumAdults=1&cid=OM*2CWW*2CHILTONLINK*2CEN*2CDirectLink__;JSUlJQ!!FOfmI8qiWcWBHqypJtzENF0!zp5oXTsL2T_V2OMUyw9rCgvGIK00ZPMt05oyprc9GiCLzL5muwDA4dQaf9XVzvnlbN8k6gBzIzZj-VPuDVgmAS1qVSO3KBk$
Format:
Printable Flyer: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sTpZyaTAg0ygaiPoA8D-SOoyHmUtVdOn/view?usp=sharing

5-SS, 10 Sections - All One Day Schedules are held on Saturday, March 21
Junior Championship (K-12): March 21-22
Junior Reserve (9-12 U1200): March 21 (Sat only)
Young Junior Championship (K-8): March 21 (Sat only)
Young Junior Reserve (6-8 U1000): March 21 (Sat only)
Young Junior Booster (6-8 U600): March 21 (Sat only)
Children's Championship (K-5): March 21 (Sat only)
Children's Reserve (4-5 U800): March 21 (Sat only)
Children's Booster (4-5 U400): March 21 (Sat only)
Young Children's Championship (K-3): March 21 (Sat only)
Young Children's Reserve (K-3 U300): March 21 (Sat only)

Event Policies: See below for MCA Scholastic Code of Conduct & Building Policies online links. By registering for this event, players, parents, and coaches agree to abide by these policies. Any violations of these policies can lead to withdrawal of all teams from the school and ejection from the facility.
MCA Scholastic Code of Conduct: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Je7_Q-SsTjU_0I9lEi4k0OU28Ce-AKpy/view?usp=sharing
Building Policies: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1mKoo1HUS-i4kyShc76nhrOrGpgoZPJee/view?usp=sharing

Tournament Information: This information is key rules that players should know during the tournament. This will include information to help the event run smoother.
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1j9EQ9jB4nIZ4kVHKG-1Qs6Sl3Oz4Ro6m/view?usp=sharing

Eligibility: All players that meet grade eligibility are welcome to participate including out of state players. Out of state players are not eligible for scholarships, state champion titles, nor being state representative.
Time Control:
Junior Championship (K-12): G/90+30
One Day Sections: G/40;d5
Rounds:
Junior Championship (K-12): Sat: 9:30am – 1:45pm – 6pm, Sun: 9:30am – 1:45pm
One Day Sections: 9am - 11am - 1pm - 3pm - 5pm
Entry Fee:
Junior Championship (K-12): $38 Advance by 3/16/2026
One Day Sections: $33 Advance by 3/16/2026
After 3/16/2026, Add $22 to Advanced Entry Fee; Online Registration Closes Friday (3/20/2026) at 10pm.
Onsite Entry Fee: Add $37 to Advanced Entry Fee with Half-Point Bye for Round 1
All mailed entries must be postmarked by 3/13/2026

The most recent USCF rating supplement (March 2026) will be used for determining ratings. Players under rating limits for under sections must play in an under section to register with the base entry fee. Playing up into the championship section allowed with $15 play up fee. Players who have demonstrated recent tournament achievements qualifying them for the championship section may request to be placed in that section without incurring the play-up fee.
Registration:
Both Championship and Reserve/Booster sections for the respective grade levels are listed under the respective links.
Junior (K-12): https://onlineregistration.cc/MCA/2026_MCA_K12
Young Junior (K-8): https://onlineregistration.cc/MCA/2026_MCA_K8
Children’s (K-5): https://onlineregistration.cc/MCA/2026_MCA_K5
Young Children’s (K-3): https://onlineregistration.cc/MCA/2026_MCA_K3

Mail: Jeff Aldrich P.O. Box 40, Flint, MI 48501
Prizes:
Junior Championship (K-12): Top 5, Top 3 Gr 9u, 10, 11, 12; Scholarships: 1st $500, 2nd $250 (Awarded upon enrollment in post HS education, ties will split prize)
Junior Reserve (9-12 U1200): Top 5 Overall + any with 4.0 points, Medals to all with 3.5 points
Young Junior Championship (K-8): Top 5, Top 3 Gr 6u, 7, 8
Young Junior Reserve (6-8 U1000): Top 5 Overall + any with 4.0 points, Medals to all with 3.5 points
Young Junior Booster (6-8 U600): Top 5 Overall + any with 4.0 points, Medals to all with 3.5 points
Children's Championship (K-5): Top 5, Top 3 Gr 4u, 5
Children's Reserve (4-5 U800): Top 5 Overall + any with 4.0 points, Medals to all with 3.5 points
Children's Booster (4-5 U400): Top 5 Overall + any with 4.0 points, Medals to all with 3.5 points
Young Children's Championship (K-3): Top 5, Top 3 Gr Ku, 1, 2, 3
Young Children's Reserve (K-3 U300): Top 5 Overall + any with 4.0 points, Medals to all with 3.5 points

Phoenix Chess Academy

Saturday, March 21, 2026

Event Overview

Scholastic Chess Tournament designed for beginners and players with a short experience.
ONLY FOR K-12 PLAYERS RATED UNDER 1000.
4 Rounds Swiss Game in 25/5d.
Entry Fee: $25 by Wednesday, $30 by Friday, $35 Same Day. Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that.
Sections: Open, K-12 Under 600, K-3 Under 500, and K-3 Under 200. Highest rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2.
Schedule: First round starts at 2:00 PM. Rounds 2, 3, and 4 will start as soon as the previous round is over. Ceremony will follow right after the 4th round is over.
Prizes: Trophy for every Kindergarten! Trophies for top 5 in each section, and Top 3 School Team.
USCF membership is required.
Register at www.phoenixchessacademy.com.

Individuals: Individuals may request to be a part of a team. $40 per player by March 11th, $50 after.  Registration cutoff is March 20th at 8 PM. No on-site registrations. Saturday, March 21, 2026
- Sunday, March 22, 2026

Event Overview

2026 WISCONSIN STATE SCHOLASTIC CHESS CHAMPIONSHIP
March 21-22
this page is for K-12 Varsity I and Varsity II team sections; for Individual sections please go to: Individual Sections Registration
Please note important changes compared to 2025:
1. registration deadline is March 4th
2. location: Madison
3. it is a 2-day event
4. there are five rounds
5. round 1 is at 10am on Saturday
6. round 4 is at 9:30am on Sunday
7. Reserve your hotel ASAP
Pairings and Standings: link will be added here at 9:30am on March 21st

Playing Site: Madison Marriott West, Middleton, WI 53562
1313 John Q Hammons Dr.
Chess Rate of $125 (includes free parking, free internet, and a discounted breakfast buffet) is available for Friday and Saturday if reserved by February 27th or until all rooms are sold out.  Reservation link:   WI State Scholastic Chess Championships
**UPDATE** : our large room block for Saturday night is fully booked and the hotel is sold out for that night. It is possible that a few rooms will open up due to cancelations, please check the above link.
We were able to secure courtesy blocks with a few nearby hotels. Please reserve ASAP as these room blocks will likely sell out quickly:

Comfort Suites Madison West - Middleton  (1253 John Q Hammons Dr., Madison, WI 53717; (608) 820-2370):  $125  (complimentary breakfast, parking, and Wi-Fi) Reservation link:  State Scholastic Suites

Fairfield by Marriott Inn & Suites Madison West/Middleton  (8212 Greenway Blvd, Middleton, WI 53562; (608) 831-1400; mention code WSCP if calling to reserve):  $99  (complimentary hot breakfast, parking, and Wi-Fi). This hotel is undergoing renovation, so some noise is possible between 8am and 6pm. Reservation link:  State Scholastic Fairfield

Hilton Garden Inn Madison West/Middleton  (1801 Deming Way, Middleton, WI 53562; (608) 831-2220; mention code CHE26 if calling to reserve) :  single  $109,  double  $119  (complimentary breakfast, parking, and Wi-Fi). Reservation link:  State Scholastic Hilton
Courtyard by Marriott Madison West/Middleton  (2266 Deming Way, Middleton, WI 53562; (608) 203-0100; mention code CCM if calling to reserve): $109 (complimentary breakfast, parking, and Wi-Fi) Reservation link:  State Scholastic Courtyard

Baymont by Wyndham Madison West/Middleton  (8102 Excelsior Dr., Madison, WI 53717; (608) 616-4527):  $105  (complimentary breakfast, parking, and Wi-Fi). Reservation link:  State Scholastic Baymont

K-12 TEAM VARSITY FORMAT :  5-Round team Swiss tournament with 4 players per team and one optional alternate. A match is won by the team scoring the most game points (2.5 points or more out of 4 games).
Varsity I   Division is Open to teams with any average rating. Varsity II Division is open to teams with an average team rating of less than 1100. Teams will be seeded based on a team rating derived from the rating average of the four players. Players must play in rating order except that the players within 50 rating points of each other may permanently switch positions prior to round one.
Unrated players can play on any board. In calculating the average team rating, an unrated on board four is assigned 50 points below the rating of board three. An unrated on board three is assigned the average of the board two and four ratings. An unrated on board two is assigned the average of the board one and three ratings. An unrated on board one is assigned 50 points above the rating of board two.
Schools may enter multiple teams in either section. No club teams are allowed. Players of all abilities are encouraged to participate. This is not a US Chess rated event.
ELIGIBILITY and TEAM COMPOSITION:  Only Wisconsin students are eligible.  All K-12 Varsity teams must be composed entirely of 9th through 12th graders OR 8th graders and below. All players must be full-time students from the same school that holds classes during week days. If a high school does not have a 9th grade, then they may tap 9th graders from eligible feeder schools. Students in grades K-8 may play as a team in K-12 Team Varsity sections if from the same school.
A home school or virtual school student may play on either a public or private school team. To play on a public school team, the student must live within the attendance boundary (not district) from which that public school draws. Any private school seeking to have these students on their team must use the same public school attendance boundary in which their school building is located. Players from outside their boundaries are not allowed to play on that school’s team. Home-schooled students are considered to be in 9th grade when they are 14 as of September 1st of the school year. Players must be under the age of 19 as of September 1st of the school year.
RATINGS : March rating supplement will be used. Tournament Directors can choose the highest of the  US Chess ratings (regular, quick, live, online)  for pairing purposes only.  Ratings are not affected by this event.

SCHEDULE:
Round 1         Saturday at 10:00am
Round 2         Saturday at 1:00pm
Round 3         Saturday at 4:00pm
Round 4         Sunday at 9:30am
Round 5         Sunday at  12:30pm
Awards           Sunday at 3:30pm or earlier
The time control is Game in 60 minutes with a 5-second delay. Accelerated pairings may be used for the first two rounds. Boards, sets, and clocks are provided.

PRIZES :   Trophies/Plaques will be awarded to the top eight Division I teams and top eight Division II teams, first place team members, their coach, and each board champion. If a tie for 1st place in Division I exists, a blitz playoff will determine the State Champion.  Every participant is eligible for an additional award (medal, chocolate or fruit leather).

TIEBREAKS :   US Amateur Team tiebreaks will be used as a primary tiebreak for team standings (if needed, the order of additional tiebreaks is Solkoff, Cumulative Opposition, Cumulative, and Modified Median). For board prizes, every person involved in a tie will receive a prize.

ENTRY FEE :  $160 per team.  Varsity teams need to register by March 4th.  If you are unsure about the exact roster, please register your team(s) by emailing the organizers. All rosters must be finalized by 8:00am of March 21st. REGISTER ONLINE:   Register for 2026 WI State Scholastic (K-12 Team sections: Varsity I and Varsity II)
Registrations after March 4th will likely not be accepted.
Online registration is best, but if you prefer Zelle, Venmo or check payments, please email Chris Wainscott at  Click here to show mail address

BUGHOUSE:  Waupaca High School will sponsor the Wisconsin State Bughouse Championship. It will start at 7:30pm on Saturday. 2026 WI State Bughouse Championship

QUESTIONS:   please email Chris Wainscott  Click here to show mail address  or Alex Betaneli Click here to show mail address You may also reach Chris by texting 414-839-5232.
Refund Policy: If you register for the tournament and are unable to make it, please notify us at least two hours in advance of the start of round one. If this is done, then your entry will be refunded less the cost of online registration ($1) and payment processing ($0.30 + 2.9% of the entry fee.)

TIEBREAKS:  the order of tiebreaks for team and individual prizes is Solkoff, Cumulative Opposition, Cumulative, and Modified Median.

ENTRY FEE :  The early bird entry fee is  $40  per player if received  by March 6th . The regular entry fee is  $45  per player if received by  March 19th . The late entry fee is $60 per player and is accepted until 8:00am on March 21st . Online payments are preferred.
REGISTER ONLINE: Register for 2026 WI State Scholastic (Individual sections: K-12 Junior Varsity, K-8, K-5) .  If you need to make an alternative arrangement,  please email Chris Wainscott at  Click here to show mail address   Checks can be made payable to Chris Wainscott.

SIDE EVENT: Waupaca High School will sponsor the Wisconsin State Bughouse Championship. It will start at 7:30pm. 2026 WI State Bughouse Championship

QUESTIONS:   please email Chris Wainscott  Click here to show mail address  or Alex Betaneli Click here to show mail address  You may also reach Chris  by texting  414-839-5232.
Refund Policy: If you register for the tournament and are unable to make it, please notify us at least two hours in advance of the start of round one. If this is done, then the IAC will refund your entry fee less the cost of online registration ($1) and payment processing ($0.30 + 2.9% of the entry fee.)

Phoenix Chess Academy

Saturday, March 21, 2026

Event Overview

4 round Swiss. Time control: Game in 25 minutes with 5 sec delay. Boards, sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided.
Registration: Go to www.phoenixchessacademy.com. USCF membership is required. New or renewing USCF members are welcome. Highest rating will be used for Swiss pairings and prize purposes.
Sections: Open, Under 1700 & Under 1200 (No playing up allowed). Sections will be combined in case a section has less than 4 players registered.
Schedule: Round 1- 9:00 AM, Round 2- 10:05 AM, Round 3- 11:10 AM, Round 4- 12:15 PM. Awards Ceremony will start right after last game is over. Half point Byes are available in all 4 rounds and (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. Requesting a zero-point bye late in the tournament is considered the same as withdrawing.
Entry Fee: $25.00 by 03/18; $30 by 03/20; $35 same day. Full refund will be issued to players who withdraw at least an hour before the first round. In cases where a registered player does not show up for the tournament without prior notice, they will not be eligible for a refund.
Prizes: Trophies for top three in each section.
A player will automatically forfeit the game if going in the bathroom with a cellphone.

2026 TEXAS SENIOR STATE CHAMPIONSHIP

State Championship Event

THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO

Saturday, March 21, 2026
- Sunday, March 22, 2026

Event Overview

2026 Texas Senior Chess Championship
REGISTRATION:  https://www.kingregistration.com/event/2026SeniorChamp
$375 First Place plus Trophy, 2nd & 3rd place trophies.  PLUS the TCA will pay a $500 stipend for the winner to attend the 2026 Irwin tournament of Senior State Champions
A US Chess & Texas Chess Association sanctioned  State Championship  event
Organized by the  Poison Pawns Chess Club , played at  The Houston Chess Studio , 250 Patton St. Suite H, Houston TX 77009.
Always Plenty of  FREE  Parking at The Studio.
WHEN:  Saturday, March 21, 2026 - Sunday, March 22, 2026
WHO CAN ENTER? - Any player aged 50 and over as of the first day of the John T. Irwin National Tournament of Senior State Champions 2026.  The Texas resident winner of the Texas Senior Championship will be invited to play in the Irwin.

- Entry Fee: $65 if received by March 1st, 2026, otherwise $85.  GMs & IMs get free entry, entry fee deducted from any winnings.

- US Chess and TCA Memberships Required.

- Out of state players are not eligible for any prizes

- 5 Rounds of G/75,d5

- Rounds: Saturday 10:00 am, 2:00 pm, 6:00 pm; Sunday 9:00 am, 1:00 pm.

- Tie-breaks used are: 1) Modified Median, 2) Solkoff, 3) Cumulative, 4) Cumulative of Opposition.

- One 1/2 point bye (rounds 1-4 only) is allowed if requested before round one

- Prizes:  Trophies to top 3.  $375 for first place, plus the trophy, plus the TCA will pay a $500 stipend to play in the "John T. Irwin National Tournament of Senior State Champions."   2nd & 3rd place trophies to Texas residents.

The Texas resident with the highest score after round five will be named, " 2026 Texas Senior Chess Champion ". If two or more Texas residents are tied with the highest score after round five, they will all be named co-champions.  Out of state residents are not eligible for any prizes.  Trophies will be awarded to the top three Texas resident finishers using tie breaks.
The Texas Senior Champion will be invited to represent Texas in the 2026 Annual "John T. Irwin National Tournament of Senior State Champions" and,  after  competing in that tournament, will receive a  stipend  of $500 from the TCA to help cover expenses of attendance at that event. If there are co-champions, the champion with the highest tie breaks will be invited to represent Texas in the national tournament and receive the $500 stipend. If the first place winner does not play in the National Senior Tournament then the 2nd place finisher will be eligible for the $500 stipend.  If the second place winner does not play then the 3rd place finisher will be eligible.
HOTEL INFO:  Holiday Inn Express, 3401 N. Main St., is less than a mile from The Studio. Phone 832-834-6197 and ask for The Houston Chess Studio discount, or if booking online use code ALDR9.  Also within a mile is the  Heights House Hotel , an  America’s Best Value,  and a  Luxury Inn .  Google them for info.
RESTAURANT INFO:   There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway, and Patron Pizza.  Several others are within walking distance.
Sections: 1, with a 2-day schedule.
Prize Fund: $375 plus trophies, plus a TCA $500 stipend
FIDE Rated:  No
Handicap Accessible:  Yes
Residency Restriction:  Not to play, but must be a Texas resident to win any prize.
Online Event:  No

12th annual Mid-America Open Blitz Championship

Grand Prix, Enhanced Grand Prix

Clayton Plaza Hotel St. Louis-Clayton

Saturday, March 21, 2026

Event Overview

MAR. 21,  2026   MISSOURI
US Chess Grand Prix points 10 (enhanced)
12th annual Mid-America Open Blitz Championship
4-SS, G/3 d2, double round (8 games),  Clayton Plaza Hotel St. Louis-Clayton, 7750 Carondelet Ave., St. Louis, MO 63105 (I-64 W/US 40-W Exit 32B, 1.2 miles north on Hanley Rd). Free parking.  $500 guaranteed prizes:  $150-100, top Under 2300 $72, Under 2000 $70, Under 1700/Unr. $60, Under 1400 $48. Entry fee (Sat. night at site only): $20, no checks. GMs $20 from prize. Enter by 9:10 pm. Round 1 begins 9:30 pm, then ASAP, should end by 11:30 pm. One pair of half-point byes  allowed in any round, must commit before round 2. March ratings used. Blitz rated (will not affect regular ratings); higher of Regular or Blitz used for pairings and prizes. $10 service charge for refunds before Rd. 1 pairings (no refunds after Round 1 is paired). No equipment supplied.

Address: 7750 Carondelet Ave.

(I-64 W/US 40-W Exit 32B, 1.2 miles north on Hanley Rd)

St. Louis , MO 63105

United States

Sections: 1
Grand Prix Points: 10
Prize Fund: $500
FIDE Rated: No
Handicap Accessible: Yes
Residency Restriction: No
Online Event: No

Organizer Overview

Continental Chess

Phone: [email protected]
Website: https://www.chesstour.com
