8A Habilis U19 Play & Learn!

Signature Regus

Saturday, March 21, 2026

Event Overview

Tournament Training with Game Reviews!
Saturday, March 21st, 2026.
Signature 222 South Prospect, Park Ridge, IL 60068
Sections:  2 - Under 1200 and Under 700, open to all ages, play-up fee: $20
Rounds: 3
Style:  Swiss System
Eligibility:  Grade 12 or under
Time Control:  G30; d5
Schedule:  9:00 AM, 10:15 AM, 11:30 AM.
Features : Game analysis by FM Kevin Bachler available after each game.
Entry Fee:

- $25 until 3/15.

- $35 until 3/21.

- Caveman Chess Subscribers: $20 off.

- No entries onsite, online entries only.

Entry: Register at Caveman Chess Registration
Byes:  One half-point bye is available if requested with online registration.
US Chess Membership Required:  Please obtain one BEFORE THE EVENT.  Save approximately 50% at U.S. Chess Vouchers — Caveman Chess Free US Chess membership to Park Ridge K-12 students (ages 5-18).
Late Players: Players that arrive after 8:40 AM receive a round 1 half-point bye.
Prizes:

- Plaques for 1-3 in each section.

- Participation awards to all players.

Chess Equipment:  Boards, sets, and clocks provided by Caveman Chess, LLC.
Parking:  Free parking. Visitors' parking behind the building and the SW corner lot at Garden & S. Fairview Streets also street parking.
Questions:  Click here to show mail address .
Watch for additional information on upcoming events at
1.  https://www.cavemanchess.com/new-events
2.  Caveman Chess Registration  at  https://register.cavemanchess.com

Special note to players!
Habilis was the first form of human to make and use tools - representing a step up in the ability to think.
Make sure to carefully read the terms and conditions.

Park Ridge , IL 60068

United States

Farmers Branch Chess Club

Saturday, March 21, 2026

Event Overview

Tournament Location :
Farmers Branch Chess Club

1804 Mindehall Drive, Farmers Branch Texas 75234

IMPORTANT :

Participants MUST bring their own Tournament Clocks & Scoresheets.
Tournament will be initially limited to 30 players.

United States Chess Federation Memberships Required for all sections - Can Be Purchased using this online registration form

Open to All the players

US Chess Rated.

Date : 3/21/2026

Sections : U600, U1200, Championship.(Live US Chess rating might be considered)

In the event of low turnout , sections MAY be merged.
Entry Fee :  $55

Format:
4 Round Swiss, non-elimination
Time : 9 AM CST

Round 1 starts at 9:00 AM.
Lunch break for 30 minutes after Round 1. All others ASAP.
All rounds G/60; D10 Second Time Delay.

Awards : Trophy

Blitz :

Section : Open
Entry Fee :  $15

Format:
5 Round Swiss, non-elimination
Time : Immediately upon Regular Rounds completion

All rounds G/5; 0 Second Time Delay.

Awards : Trophy

Registration:  On-line  - https://www.farmersbranchchessclub.com/
Mandatory to Submit this form online AFTER making the Zelle Transfer - Registration ends at 11:00pm the day before the event.

Payment  : Zelle Transfer to [email protected] .(Include  Participant   Full name in the Memo Field during Zelle Transfer)

Inquiries  : [email protected]
Lunch\Drinks  : Not available at Location - Participants may bring sack lunches. Please plan accordingly

Tournament Policy :

Refunds: A player can receive Tournament credits if notified in an email by 11:00pm the day before the event. Players that no-show do not receive a refund. No exceptions.
Photography: Photos will be taken of the tournament

Note :

Parents/Guardians of Minors

We welcome children to play in our tournament, but please be aware of the following:
Your child will play against adults, will be treated like an adult, and will be expected to interact like an adult. Your child will not be supervised by us. If a child is under 16 years old, a parent/guardian must remain in the building.

Rule Variations in Effect at the Tournament

1H1. Director as witness only.  In an event in which most games are not watched by directors, a director may refrain from correcting all illegal moves he or she may notice but simply serve as a witness should one of the players point out the illegal move before any moves have been made.
15A. Paper scoresheet variation.  The player using a paper scoresheet may first make the move, and then write it on the scoresheet, or vice versa.

Battle on the BB-64

Nauticus / Battleship Wisconsin

Saturday, March 21, 2026

Event Overview

Hampton Roads Chess Association
and
Nauticus / Battleship Wisconsin
present
Battle on the BB-64
A chess tournament on the ship!
Norfolk, Virginia
March 21, 2026
REGISTER HERE:   Battle on the BB-64

Hampton Roads Chess Association and Nauticus / Battleship Wisconsin join forces to present the third annual chess tournament to be held on board the Battleship Wisconsin (BB-64) docked at Nauticus on the Norfolk Waterfront!  Games will be played in the Crew Mess, where sailors from WWII to Operation Desert Storm dined while underway!
There is a LOT of information to share for this event, and most questions can be answered below.   Please read thoroughly!
By registering and attending in this event (as participant or guest), you acknowledge and agree to abide by the  US Chess Federation's Safe Play Policy , and  HRCA's Code of Conduct and General Liability Waiver and Release.  More details below.
Registration for this event closes at 11:59pm EST on Thursday, March 19th!  No last-minute or on-site registration!
This is an HRCA Scholastic Cup Event!
HRCA membership is not required for the tournament but IS required to participate in the Scholastic Cup awards.
New Memberships must be purchased within one week of event conclusion for points to qualify.
For more information visit  https://hrchessclub.org/scholastic-cup/

SCHEDULE

- 9:15-10:00 AM -  Recommended time to arrive for parking and walking to the venue.  Check-in table to pick up pre-ordered wristbands on the deck outside the main entry to the Nauticus will be open by 9:30AM.

- 10:00 AM -  Doors open

- 11:00 AM  -- Round 1

- 12:15 PM -- Round 2

- 1:30 PM -- Round 3

- 2:45 PM -- Round 4

- 3:45 PM -- Awards in the Brock Theater

- 4:45 PM -- Photos on the fantail

- 5:00 PM -- Everyone must be off the ship / Nauticus closes

PARTICIPANTS
***NEW THIS YEAR -- THIS IS AN ALL-AGES EVENT!!!***
Players under age 14 require an adult to be onsite for the duration of the event -- All guests must have a Nauticus day pass (see below).  We have a special group rate through March 19th.  After that, you may purchase regular admission or utilize any discount programs directly with the front desk.
PLAYER REQUIREMENTS:
US Chess membership is required for Open, Amateur, and Novice -- these are rated sections.
US Chess membership is NOT required for Rookie sections.
HRCA membership is only required if you want your points counted for the HRCA Scholastic Cup.
FORMAT
A Swiss System (like a bracket system -- NOT  an elimination event! ) tournament of four rounds.  Time control is G/25; d3, meaning each side has 25 minutes to complete all their moves, and the clock will not start counting down for the first 3 seconds of each move. Select a bye during registration ONLY if you know you will be missing a round due to a conflict with another event.  One half-point bye allowed if requested prior to the start of Round 3.
Boards, sets, and clocks are provided.  Notation is NOT required in any section due to Quick time control, but notation sheets and pencils will be provided if desired.
Section choices are:

- K-3 Rookie:   Grades Pre-K through 3rd with little to no tournament experience.  No rated players allowed.  US Chess membership is not required.

- K-6 Rookie:   For youth in grades 4th-6th with little to no tournament experience.  No rated players allowed.  US Chess membership is not required.

- Senior Rookie :  For ADULTS and youth in grades 7th-12th with little to no tournament experience.  No rated players allowed.  US Chess membership is not required.

- Scholastic Novice (U300):   Youth in grades PK-12th who are US Chess members with a Regular over-the-board (OTB) rating Under 300.  The March supplement will be used.  Unrated players are allowed in the Novice section and are eligible for place prizes or Top Unrated prizes only.

- Amateur (U800):  All ages who are US Chess members with Regular over-the-board (OTB) rating Under 800.  The March supplement will be used.  Unrated players are allowed in the Amateur section and are eligible for place prizes only.

- Open:   All ages who are US Chess members -- unrated or of any rating -- but designed for players rated over 800.  Playing up is allowed.  Unrated players are allowed in the Open section and are eligible for place prizes only.  The March supplement will be used.

A note on Unrated players:  Per new US Chess Scholastic Regulations, HRCA will apply the current Regular OTB rating to Unrated players, if applicable, even if earned after the cut-off for the supplement used for the tournament.  In a dual-rated event, if there is no Regular OTB rating, a current Quick rating will be applied, if applicable, but only for prizes, not sectioning (e.g. someone with a 500 published Quick rating but Unrated Regular may still play in the U300 section but is ineligible for Unrated prizes).  Bottom line -- only actually Unrated players at the time of the event will be allowed in Rookie sections and eligible for Unrated class prizes in rated sections.
Check your US Chess membership here
AWARDS

- Individual:
- TROPHIES to the Top 5 finishers in each section.  Trophy to Top U1000 in Open.  Trophies to Top U500 in Amateur and Top Unrated in Novice.  Trophy to Top K-1 in K-3 Rookie.  Medals to additional players with at least 2 points.  Participation ribbons to all remaining players.

- Team:   A team is comprised of two or more players from the same school, with the top four scores counting toward the team score.  Team awards will be cross-section with trophies for Top 3 Elementary Schools and Top 2 Middle Schools.  Top High School trophy will be added only if more than one high school team enters by March 9th.

ENTRY FEE
$35 Early Entry Fee through 11:59 PM on Sunday, February 22nd.
$40 Standard Entry Fee through 11:59 PM Sunday, March 8th.
$45 Late Entry Fee through 11:59 PM Sunday, March 15th.
$50 Last Week Entry Fee through 11:59 PM Thursday, March 19th.
TOURNAMENT REGISTRATION WILL CLOSE AT 11:59 PM ON MARCH 19th.  NO EXCEPTIONS.  NO WALKUPS.
There are no scholarship or Title 1 entry fee waivers for this event.
REFUNDS
If you need to withdraw, please contact the Event Organizer.
Refunds will be given as a tournament credit ONLY.     Refunds create a lot of administrative work and loss of important operational revenue to HRCA.   Our default refund is to now give participants a CREDIT towards a future HRCA tournament.  The credited amount will be $30 and is valid for 1 year.  After February 8th, there is a 50% credit.  No refunds after February 19th.
** Please check the ENTRY LIST before registering to make sure you do not register multiple times.    Duplicate entries are subject to an administrative refund fee of $10.
Nauticus guest tickets must be purchased separately and are NOT refundable.
Tournament Orientation for New Players
There will be no New Player Orientation the day of the event -- Use this link and passcode for a recording of a complete orientation to tournament procedures and rules.
https://us02web.zoom.us/rec/share/k1QA3hzoj0hYP7z5uwD7DYE2Mn-atQYhQO6YHRxyvfL_FDVO5HqW1C_6MDyyTNmv.NxHuuWAIwUzGT4sB
Passcode: h.8mre41
A copy of the slides will be sent to all registered players the evening of March 19th.  For an earlier copy, contact the event organizer.

Special Notes for Event Day
PARKING :
Adjacent garages are approximately $13 a day; the MacArthur Center garage within walking distance is $1 a day on weekends!
MEALS :
No outside food or drink is allowed inside Nauticus or the Battleship.  For anyone bringing their own lunch and eating on the front porch, they have a lunch bin system. Guests can drop their lunches in the bin at check-in, and they’ll wheel it into storage. At lunchtime, you can bring it back out to the porch.
If you leave the museum, your wristband will give you re-entry.   Please make sure your player knows where to find you or designate another adult to supervise if you leave the premises without your player.  Be aware the tournament rounds are very close together, so do not depart the site with your player and risk missing a round.
The on-site cafe is under new management, and they are offering pre-orders of box lunches, which is strongly recommended to get your food on time for your player to eat between rounds -- Click here for a menu .
CLICK HERE TO PRE-ORDER LUNCH .
WAITING AREAS ("SKITTLES") :
Please enjoy the venue and pack light (you may go back to your vehicle if needed).   All players and accompanying family members / friends are strongly encouraged to explore Nauticus and the Battleship between rounds!  Camp chairs are not permitted at the venue.
The Brock Theater on the 3rd floor of Nauticus is the main waiting area for parents.   This will be open to all museum guests, so please be mindful of others enjoying the space and secure your belongings.   A short film will be shown at 11am and 2pm for all museum guests.
YOU MAY NOT USE THE NAUTICUS CAFE AS A WAITING AREA.    Volunteers will be enforcing this.
*Parents of younger children who may not be able to navigate from the ship's crew mess back to Nauticus will be allowed to wait in the galley (standing) next to the crew mess.
Please make sure your players know where to find you after each round!

BATHROOMS :
There is ample access to public bathrooms in Nauticus.  There is one bathroom available on the deck of the ship prior to descending the stairs to the crew mess.  We STRONGLY urge parents to ensure their kids use the bathroom BEFORE the start of a round.  Once the round has started, getting a child back and forth to a bathroom on the ship is challenging.

HANDICAPPED ACCESSIBILITY :
Access to the ship's galley requires the physical ability to climb up and down one short but steep ladder.  Players unable to make that climb can contact us in advance to make arrangements for an alternative assigned board in an accessible area of the ship or Nauticus.

Discounted Group Nauticus/Battleship Tickets :
Required for all guests.    Admission to Nauticus and the Battleship is included in the entry fee for players only.
IMPORTANT - After registering your player for the tournament, go to  2026 Battle on the BB-64 ADMISSION tickets to purchase your group rate admission tickets for family members or friends accompanying the player.  You will receive a wristband upon arrival for entry.  These tickets are non-refundable.  Your PLAYER'S admission is included in their entry fee - do NOT purchase a ticket for registered players.

- For accompanying parents / siblings / guests, the group admission rates (tax included) are:
- $15 for students (ages 3-17)

- $18 for adults (ages 18+)

- ages 0-2 free but must be listed on reservation

- NO PLAYER UNDER THE AGE OF 14 MAY BE DROPPED OFF / UNACCOMPANIED FOR THIS EVENT.   Carpooling is welcome.  All players under age 14 must have a designated adult onsite for the duration of the day.

Group sales end March 19th at 11:59PM -- No exceptions.  Regular admission fees may be paid at the door the day of event.  Please visit the Nauticus website for any other eligible discounts and ticket reservations if not purchasing group tickets through HRCA.     You will receive a confirmation with check-in instructions when you order tickets through HRCA.

VOLUNTEERS NEEDED !

Volunteers help ensure our events run smoothly and that players and families have an enjoyable experience.   Volunteer spots include set up, clean up, wristband distribution, player escorts (Safe Play certification required), scorekeepers, CERTIFIED Tournament Directors (TDs), and assistant/junior TDs (not certified).   Key (all-day) volunteers receive complimentary entry.
Sign up to volunteer for a part of the day here: Hampton Roads Chess Association: Battle on BB-64

CONTACT US

Please contact the Tournament Organizer:

For more information/questions, contact the Tournament Organizer, Tina, at [email protected] or 757-472-5909.
Email is the fastest way to reach us.
POLICIES AND RULES
It is our goal to provide a fun, safe, and supportive environment.  Community partnerships are vital to HRCA, and we want to ensure we remain good stewards to our partners and their facilities. There is a lot of downtime during tournaments --  parents are responsible for supervising their children when they are not playing a scheduled match.     Please note only designated areas of the facility are open to players and guests.   No one is allowed in undesignated areas (including classrooms) at any time.   No drop-offs for youth under age 14.
By registering and attending in this event (as participant or guest), you acknowledge and agree to abide by the  US Chess Federation's Safe Play Policy , and  HRCA's Code of Conduct and General Liability Waiver and Release.  For more information on Safe Play or HRCA's Code of Conduct and General Liability Waiver and Release, please click the BLUE links above.   Violations of these policies may result in warnings, or ultimately, disqualification or dismissal from the event without refund.
Photo Policy:   Please be advised that photos and/or videos may be taken at HRCA events for use in HRCA's marketing, grant reporting, educational, news, or other promotional materials, whether in print, electronic, or other forms of media, including on our website and social channels.  HRCA will not identify images using the full names of those photographed without express written permission.    By attending an HRCA event, you consent to have your image recorded for distribution and agree to release, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify HRCA from any and all claims, including compensation, involving using your picture or likeness. If you wish to opt-out, you can make your wishes known to the photographer, and/or the event organizers, and/or contact HRCA at  Click here to show mail address .

Heritage Event

Christ the King Lutheran Church

Saturday, March 21, 2026

Event Overview

2026 Iowa Senior Qualifier
When : March 21, 2026
4 round swiss g60 d5
Where: Christ the King Church,  325 Mormon Trek Blvd,  Iowa City, Iowa 52246
Entry Fee:  $25 online until March 15th $30 Thereafter.
Must be 50+ years of age to enter.  Must be member of Iowa Chess Association and resident of the state of Iowa.  Memberships available onsite.
Rounds : 4 Rounds.  If less than 8 players TD will reduce that section to 3 rounds.
Round Times: Saturday 9am - 11:30 pm – 2:00pm – 5:00 pm.
Prizes:
1st place $70 + trophy and the right to represent Iowa for the National Senior Invitational tournament, the Irwin to be held at the US Open along side the Barber/Denker/Rockefeller/Haring/Ashley, 2nd place $50 3rd Place $30 Winner will have the right to represent Iowa in the Irwin Senior tournament of champions held concurrently with the US Open in Grand Rapids, MI on  3-7 August 2026.    Players are encouraged to complete all games in tournament, and submit copies (scoresheets) of all their games played and submit one annotated game to Iowa En Passant .
All Sections One half point bye if requested before round1.
Additional Info:  if tournament ends in a tie. A playoff will be played, each player will play both colors,  G5 d2 until a winner is determined.

Super Sunday USCF Tournament

Chess Kings & Queens Academy

Sunday, March 22, 2026

Event Overview

Note: There is also a FIDE-USCF hybrid section for those 1700+ USCF rating (1600+ FIDE).  See other listing for details.

Structure
- 3 rounds Swiss-Style.  G75 +15.  Accelerated pairings at the director's discretion.
- One half-point bye is available for any round, but must be requested before tournament start. All other requested byes are zero points.
- Clocks, boards, and weighed plastic pieces are provided. Players may use their own equipment with the agreement of their opponent.
Schedule
- Round times: 10:00 am / 1:30pm / 5:00 pm.
- Players should arrive no later than 9:45 am.
Registration
- Registration fee: $45
- Online registration only.  Registration closes at 9:00 a.m. the day of the event.  On-site registrations are discouraged but may be accepted at the TD's discretion.
- Registration link:  https://chesskq.com/tournament
- All sections in this tournament have a minimum rating to participate.
Under 1400 = 1000 USCF rating minimum
Under 1800 = 1300 USCF rating minimum
- This event has no age restrictions.
- All ratings are assessed based on the published USCF rating supplement for the month the tournament takes place. "Live" or "up-to-date" ratings may be accepted at the director's discretion.
- Players signing up for a section they are not eligible to join will be automatically shifted to the appropriate section.
- Players who sign up but are ineligible to participate, or players who withdraw from the tournament prior to 9:00 am on tournament day, will be provided a credit for a signup for a future tournament or class.
Prizes
$640 guaranteed in prizes
Prizes are paid out via Venmo, Zelle, or PayPal. Check-by-mail available for anyone without these options.
U1800 section
- 1st place: $160
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1600: $60
U1400 section
- 1st place: $160
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1200: $60
@45 players  (across all three sections) - we serve doughnuts and coffee.  Everyone wins!
@50 players - we add a Top Junior (under age 12) award to each section
@55 players - we add a Top Senior (age 55+) award to each section
@60 players - we increase 2nd place and "top under __  rating" prizes for all sections by $15
@65 players - we increase 1st place prizes for all sections by $20.
Additional information
- The tournament director for this event is Stephen Lorimor. Bye requests and other issues may be e-mailed to [email protected] , or by voice/text to 908-286-0720. Note that he may not notice or respond to e-mails, texts, or calls after 9:00 am the day of the event.
- The venue is located within walking distance of multiple restaurants and fast food businesses.  No food is allowed at the playing tables, but a waiting room with tables is available.

Address: 1030 Stelton Road

Suite 201 (use side entrance)

Piscataway , NJ 08854

United States

Sections: 2
Grand Prix Points: 0
Prize Fund: 640
FIDE Rated: No
Handicap Accessible: No
Residency Restriction: No
Online Event: No

Stephen D Lorimor

Email: [email protected]
Phone: 9082860720
Website: https://chesskq.com/tournament

- 3 rounds Swiss-Style.  G75 +15.  Accelerated pairings at the director's discretion.
- One half-point bye is available for any round, but must be requested before tournament start. All other requested byes are zero points.
- Clocks, boards, and weighed plastic pieces are provided. Players may use their own equipment with the agreement of their opponent.
- FIDE notice: Rules for late arrival will match standard USCF 60 minute rule.
Schedule
- Round times: 10:00 am / 1:30pm / 5:00 pm

USCF
- A current USCF membership is required to play.
- Players MUST have at least 1) 1700 USCF rating (live or current published), or 2) 1600 FIDE rating

FIDE
- A valid FIDE ID is required to play.  Most players with a valid USCF membership may request a USA-flagged FIDE ID at this URL.  Note that it may take several days to process.  https://tinyurl.com/3zcjwmex
- There is no minimum FIDE rating for this event.  There is a maximum rating of 2399.
- FIDE norms are not available at this event.

Registration
- Registration fee: $45
- Online registration only.  Registration closes at 9:00 a.m. on the day of the event.  On-site registrations are discouraged but may be accepted at the TD's discretion.
- Registration link: https://chesskq.com/tournament
- Free entry for all players rated 2200 or higher. ($45 will be deducted from the player's prize winnings.) E-mail name, USCF ID, and FIDE ID to Stephen Lorimor at [email protected] to sign up.
- This event has no age restrictions.
- Players signing up for a section they are not eligible to join will be automatically shifted to the appropriate section.
- Players ineligible to participate in any section of this event, or withdrawing before 9:00 AM on the day of the tournament, will receive a credit for a future class or tournament.

Prizes
Prizes are paid out via Zelle or PayPal. Check-by-mail available for anyone without these options.
- 1st place: $200
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1800 (FIDE): $60
@45 players  (across all three sections) - we serve doughnuts and coffee.  Everyone wins!
@50 players - we add a Top Junior (under age 12) award to each section
@55 players - we add a Top Senior (age 55+) award to each section
@60 players - we increase 2nd place and "top under __  rating" prizes for all sections by $15
@65 players - we increase 1st place prizes for all sections by $20.

Additional information
- The tournament director for this event is Stephen Lorimor. Bye requests and other issues may be e-mailed to [email protected] , or by voice/text to 908-286-0720. Note that he may not notice or respond to e-mails, texts, or calls after 9:00 am the day of the event.
- The venue is located within walking distance of multiple restaurants and fast food businesses.  No food is allowed at the playing tables, but a waiting room with tables is available.

RiseNShine Monthly Quads - Mar 22nd

Holiday Inn Express & Suites Gilbert near Mesa Gateway Airport

Sunday, March 22, 2026

Event Overview

OVERVIEW

- Tournament Format: Round-Robin

- Total Rounds: 3

- Round Times: 2 pm and Rounds 2 & 3 on a rolling schedule

- Time Control: G/30;+5  (Game in 30 minutes with a 5-second increment at each move.)

- Games will be US Chess regular & quick-rated (so called dual-rated).

- Players will be split into groups of four (quads) based on their ratings, from the highest-rated to the lowest-rated.

- In case the last quad is not four players, they will play a mini-3 round Swiss tournament with 5-7 players or they may play double round robin.

- Monthly supplemental OTB regular rating will be used. The Chief TD has discretion to use a player's USCF online rating (ONL) or live rating for pairing purposes in extreme cases where fairness will be preserved by doing so

- Minor roster shifts to avoid family member pairings may be possible

- No byes are available

- Forfeit time is 30 minutes

WHEN
March 22nd , 2026 (Sunday) @ 2:00 PM
Please arrive at the venue at least 10 minutes before the start time.
WHERE
​Holiday Inn Express & Suites Gilbert near Mesa Gateway Airport
5530 S Power Road, Gilbert, AZ 85295, USA
Intersection:  Power Rd & E Ray Rd
APPROXIMATE HOURS
2:00pm – 5:30pm
Might end early based on the quad.
REGISTRATION
Registration Link   https://pci.jotform.com/form/260106735864156
Entry List
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1pLx0Snwqym2nb8_dbdGhhH_MWYSULrSN0El3L18iKQs/
Entry Fee:

- $25 on or before March 16th (Monday)

- $30 through March 21st (Saturday)

- $35 on March 22nd (Sunday) until 12:00 PM (noon)

Refunds are available only for cancellations made on or before Saturday, March 21st , and will incur a $5 administrative fee.
Registrations may also be transferred to a future tournament if requested on or before Saturday, March 21st .
No refunds for no-shows.
For cancellations, refunds or transfers, email [email protected] . Refunds will be processed after March 22nd .
PRIZES
For each quad,
- Trophy for 1st place.
- Trophy for 2nd place.
- Participation medals for all other players.
Special prizes:
- Trophy for best parent-kid pair (cumulative score and cumulative tiebreak score)
- Trophy for best siblings pair (cumulative score and cumulative tiebreak score)
REQUIREMENTS

- Players must have current US Chess Federation membership. Expiration date of their US Chess membership must be later than the last day of the tournament.

- Not sure if you have a membership? Need to check the expiration date of your membership? Visit:  https://ratings.uschess.org/

- Become a member or renew your membership:  https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess

ROUND TIMES
Round 1: 2:00 pm
Round 2: ASAP
Round 3: ASAP
End Time: Around 5:30 pm. Might end early based on the quad.
Check our prior rated events at https://ratings.uschess.org/affiliate/A9214088

Gilbert , AZ 85295

United States

Speedy Quads 65

J. Gilligan's Bar and Grill

Monday, March 23, 2026

Event Overview

Speedy - because the time control is G/5;d0 (each player gets 5 minutes to make all their moves.)
Quads - because we divide the players in groups of four based on ratings or skill level.
Players play two games against each of the three other players in their quad.
We hold a Speedy Quads tournament every fourth Monday each month. Speedy Quads has a FREE entry (but we do accept donations to cover the rating fees). There are no prizes. The games are blitz-rated and do not affect regular or quick ratings.
Time Control is G/5;d0; and we play double-round quads.
Register on site only - please arrive before 7:30pm. US Chess members will play rated quads. Non-members will play in an unrated small Swiss blitz tournament.

Arlington , TX 76010

MSJE Chess Puzzle-Solving Championship 2026

Mission San José Elementary

Thursday, March 26, 2026

Event Overview

Our annual MSJE Chess Puzzle-Solving Championship is a free event for all MSJE students in kindergarten through second grade.   The Puzzle-Solving Championship concludes our series of Thursday Night Tactics (TNT) in December through March.
Time:  Thursday March 26, 2026, 7pm - 7:45pm
Format: a total of 4 rounds

- Speed round: 18 chess puzzles, all puzzles on paper to solve in 10 minutes

- Mathematics round: 4 chess-themed combinatorics questions, courtesy of MSJE Math Club

- Blindfold round: 4 chess puzzles, 1 puzzle at a time is read out and also given out in text (but no pieces and board) and 2 minutes for contestant to write down a solution

- Target round: 4 chess puzzles, 1 puzzle at a time is shown on demonstration board and 2 minutes for contestant to write down a solution

We may update event details, like sections and number of rounds, as the competition date approaches to ensure the best possible experience for all players.
Sections: one single section (K-2)
Prize:  trophy to top solver in each grade
Go Mustangs! Please let's have fun solving chess puzzles together.

Fremont , CA 94539

United States

Winterville Cultural Center

Friday, March 27, 2026
- Saturday, March 28, 2026

Event Overview

MARCH 27-28 GEORGIA: 5th Annual Bolivar Morales Memorial Winterville Chess Club Championships
Winterville Cultural Center
Friday, March 27, 2026 - Saturday, March 28, 2026
Event Overview
MARCH 27-28 GEORGIA
5th Annual Bolivar Morales Memorial Winterville Chess Club Championships
Friday, March 27: BLITZ Championship &
Saturday, March 28: CLASSIC Championship
FRIDAY BLITZ Registration:  https://bit.ly/WCC_Bolivar_Blitz_2026
Registration: 6:00 - 7:00 pm     Start Time: 7:15 pm    Entry Fee: $25
7-SS, USCF-rated, G/5;+2; 70% of entry fees returned as cash prizes.
Prizes to 1st-Place (35%) and 2nd-Place (25%) Finishers and Top Upset (10%).
Championship Trophies awarded to 1st-Place Winner and Top Finisher under 1300 USCF.
(Trophy qualifier: Club Championship Trophies will be awarded to players who have played
three or more USCF-rated tournaments at the Winterville Chess Club.)
A separate $50 Prize will be awarded to the Top Senior (Age 50+).
Distribution of Prizes: No player can win more than one cash prize.
Special Note: registration is limited to the first 40 players.

SATURDAY CLASSIC Registration:    https://bit.ly/WCC_Bolivar_Classic_2026
Registration: 9:00 - 10:00 am    Start Time: 10:00 am    Entry Fee: $35
2-section, 4-round USCF-rated Swiss, G/45;+5; 80% of entry fees returned as cash prizes.
Rounds: 10:00 am; 12 noon; 2:00 pm; 4:00 pm or as soon as possible.
Players rated 2200+: Free Entry ($35 EF deducted from Prize).
Championship Section (1300+ USCF): Prizes to 1st-Place (35%) & 2nd-Place (15%) Finishers.
Reserve Section (U1300 USCF): Prizes to 1st-Place (20%) & 2nd-Place (10%) Finishers.
Championship Trophies awarded to winners of Championship and Reserve Sections.
(Trophy qualifier: Club Championship Trophies will be awarded to players who have played three or more USCF-rated tournaments at the Winterville Chess Club.)
A separate $50 Prize will be awarded to the Top Senior (Age 50+).
Distribution of Prizes: No player can win more than one cash prize.
Special Note: registration is limited to the first 40 players.
Note: Bring chess sets and clocks as the club has a limited number of chess sets. USCF membership is required.
For Information, contact:

JP Caillault (706-286-6762; [email protected] ).

St Catherine of Siena Catholic School

Saturday, March 28, 2026

Event Overview

Strategic Thoughts NOLA, Crescent City Chess, and Downriver Chess Present:
CLICK HERE TO REGISTER!
THE NEW ORLEANS YOUTH CHESS 2025-2026 SEASON
Venue:  St Catherine of Siena Catholic School, 400 Codifer Blvd, Metairie, LA
Format:  Four round swiss format, G/25;d5 tournament. Five sections: K-2; K-4; K-6; K-8, K-12
Prizes:  Individual and team trophies in each section
Registration:  8:45AM-9:15AM; Anyone not registered by 9:15AM will be given a first round bye
Check in:  Check in is not necessary if your name is on the "entry list" tab of the King Registration page and there are no problems listed
Round times:  10AM, 11:15AM, 12:30PM, and 1:45PM
Entry fee:  $30 if received by midnight one week before the event date (Saturday night). $35 if received by midnight two days before (Thursday night). $40 day before or same day (Friday-Saturday).
USCF requirement:  Current USCF membership required,  join here.  If your membership does not have an expiration date, it is not yet current.
Eligibility:  All K-12 students are welcome. You do not need to be part of a school or chess team to compete.
Discount codes:  Use code FAMILY for a $5 discount when registering multiple siblings of the same family. Use code LUNCH for a $10 discount if student or family receives free or reduced lunch benefits.
Contact:  email Click here to show mail address .
Byes:  Two half-point byes available upon request. All byes must be requested before round 3, with exceptions made for emergency situations. All bye requests final after beginning of round 1.
Teams:  Teams are comprised of the top four players per school per grade section. Minimum two players to qualify as a team. Team totals are calculated using cumulative score of each player.
Late arrivals:  Games are forfeited 30 minutes after the round start time if a player has not arrived.
Refunds:  Players who withdraw 30 minutes before round one are eligible for a refund of their entry fee, minus any applicable payment-processor fees (typically 5-7%).
Calendar: Full season calendar here .

Metairie , LA 70005

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids

Chess Kings & Queens Academy

Saturday, March 28, 2026

Event Overview

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30.  Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00.  The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play.  Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections.  The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment.  Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $30.  Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information:  Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).
Information / registration link:  https://chesskq.com/tournament

United States

Arizona Golden Cup 🏆

Phoenix Chess Academy

Saturday, March 28, 2026

Event Overview

Arizona's Premier Year - Long USCF Chess Series.
Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆
A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required.
4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points.
Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section.
Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over.
Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that.
Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event.
At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed.
Golden Points System:
Finish                 Points
1st Place              20
2nd Place            16
3rd Place             13
4th Place             10
5–6                           8
7–10                        5
Participation       3
Bonus Points:
+3 points — Perfect score (4/4).
+2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months.
Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions.
Tie-Breaks (Year-End):
1. Most 1st-place finishes.
2. Head-to-head results.
3. Most tournaments played.
4. Best December result.
TD decisions are final.

FREE Pizza and drinks for those playing in the Golden Cup tournament in the morning!
6 round Swiss. Time control: Game in 5 minutes. Boards, sets and clocks will be provided.

Half point Byes are available in all 6 rounds and (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. Requesting a zero-point Bye late in the tournament is considered the same as withdrawing.

Prizes: Over 1200: Cash for top three. 1st - 30%, 2nd - 14%, 3rd - 10%.
Under 1200: Trophy for top three. Trophy for the Best Under 700.

2025-26 CalChess Super States: K & K-5 Championship and K-12 Sections

Santa Clara Convention Center

Saturday, March 28, 2026
- Sunday, March 29, 2026

Event Overview

Join the 2025-26 CalChess Super States K & K-5 Championship and other K-12 sections for a high-level weekend of friendly chess competition! This is the greatest opportunity for scholastic players to earn state-level recognition in a supportive competitive environment, as well as to earn personal trophies.
Register here

- You must  log in or sign up  before you can register.

- Online registration closes at  12:00 a.m.  the day of the tournament.

- Onsite registration is subject to availability ($44 additional fee incurred).

- Late fees applied starting March 21 or when reaching capacity.

Sections

- Players will need to register based on their 2025-26 school grade and their March Supplement Rating (i.e., rating as of Feb. 19) into one of the following sections:
- K-12 Rookie (unr.)

- K-12 Beginner (100-399)

- K-5 Jr. Varsity (400-799)

- K-12 Intermediate (400-799)

- 6-12 Jr. Varsity (800+)

- KG Champ (400+)

- K-5 Champ (800+)

- 6-12 Advanced (800+)

Play-up rule

- A player may pay to play up one higher section, double play up is  NOT  allowed.

- Players must be within 300 points of the rating cutoff to play up.
(Note: The rating used to determine if a player may play up is their  March USChess Published Supplement Rating)

Schedule

- K-5 Jr. Varsity, K-12 Rookie, K-12 Beginner & K-12 Intermediate:
- Time Control: 5x G/25 d5

- Two schedules available: Saturday OR Sunday

- Round Times:
- Sat, Mar. 28 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.
OR

- Sun, Mar. 29 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.

- 6-12 Jr. Varsity:
- Time Control: 5x G/25 d5

- Round Times:
- Sat, Mar. 28 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.

- KG Champ:
- Time Control: 5x G/25 d5

- Round Times:
- Sun, Mar. 29 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.

- K-5 Champ & 6-12 Advanced:
- Time Control: 6x G/65 d5

- Round Times:
- Sat, Mar. 28 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m.

- Sun, Mar. 29 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m.

- ½-point bye is available for  ONE (1) round, except for the last round (Byes must be requested  at least 30 min  before that round's start).

- 0-point byes are available for any round.

- If you request more than one bye, we will give you a ½-point for the latest round possible except for the last round (0-point byes for all other rounds).

Awards

- Personal Trophies to all players with a winning record.
- One trophy per player.

- Trophy size vary based on standings.

- Medals to all other players.

- Team Trophies to all of the following with two or more players in all sections combined:
- Clubs

- Schools

- A player who withdraws during the tournament is not eligible for awards.

Fees

- Entry fee:
- K-5 Champ and 6-12 Advanced: $113

- All other sections: $79

- Play up fee: +$29

- Discount for BayAreaChess Membership Subscribers ( More info ).

- Late fees, starting:
- Mar. 22: +$11

- Mar. 24: +$22

- Mar. 26: +$33

- Onsite fee: +$44

- BayAreaChess Membership discounts are  NOT  redeemable for late and onsite fees.

Withdrawals

- Withdrawals are eligible for a partial refund, subject to the following deductions:
- until Mar. 21, 4% processing fee.

- from Mar. 22 to Mar. 23, $11 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee.

- from Mar. 24 to Mar. 25, $22 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee.

- from Mar.  26 onward,  NO REFUND  will be issued.

- Only withdrawals made  before or on Mar. 25 are eligible for refund.

Change requests

- After registration, changes can be requested at  bayareachess.com/changeform and are subject to the following fees:
- until Mar. 26, $7 change fee.

- on Mar. 27, $15 change fee.

- The following requests are exempt from the change fee:
- playing up to a higher section.

- requesting byes.

- updating club and/or school.

Other requirements

- USCF membership must be active.

More info available  here .

Cincinnati Tornado MARCH. Last Saturday of Month

Wyoming Baptist Church

Saturday, March 28, 2026

Event Overview

Cincinnati Tornado Monthly Tournament
Held on the Last Saturday of the Month
We provide all clocks & chess sets

Advance Entry Fee $45
Online Registration – By Friday 12 midnight deadline
Online Registration:   https://chessearth.com/tornado-registration/
Advance Registration ends on Friday 12 midnight.
NEW OPTION for returning players.   EMAIL or  TEXT MESSAGE  us to pre-register and enter the tournament:

- Email admin@chessearth:   1.) First & Last Name   2.) USCF ID  3.) Section you are playing in  and  4.)  Pay $45 at the Tournament Site

On-Site Entry Fee $50; On-Site Registration – By 9:30am Saturday morning deadline

- On-Site Registration – Ends at 9:30am Saturday morning

- Credit Cards, PayPal, Venmo, CashApp, Zelle, Apple Pay accepted on site

- Tournament  Address:    Wyoming Baptist Church, 170 Burns Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45215

4-Round Swiss Tournament
TTime Control: G/45 +5; Each player receives 45 minutes with a +5-second increment. A Tornado is a one-day tournament where you play four games. Cash Prizes and Awards are given at the end of the tournament based on your final score.
Round Start Times:
Round #1: 10:00am
Round #2: 12:30pm
Round #3: 2:30pm
Round #4: 4:30pm
Choose a Section To Play In:

- Open Section  -  Includes the Master Bounty Prize - $100

- Under 1600 Section

- Under 1000 Section

- Award Winning Chili.  Good Food; Hot Meals

- Chess Equipment and Merch available to purchase

- USCF Rated Tournament.  Join/Renew USCF on-site.

- Purchase a New Membership at Registration.

- 1/2 Point Bye is available if notified before Round 2.

- Prizes Fund based on 70 players.

- We provide all the Chess Clocks & Chess Sets

Open Section:     **NEW** Rating must be 1600 or above to play in the Open Section.
Or a player can pay $30 to “play up” into the Open Section.
1st – $200      2nd – $150
Top Under 2001   – $100
Top Under 1801   – $100
Includes the Master Bounty Prize - $100

- Master Bounty Prize:  Win your game against the #1 Master in the tournament and win $100. If you draw the Master, win $50.  If the Master wins all the games, then he/she wins the $100.

Under 1600 Section:   The heart of the tournament
1st – $200      2nd – $150
$100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter.
$100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter.
Under 1000 Section :  Rating must be lower than 1001. Great for beginners and 1st time tournament players.
1st – $200      2nd – $150
$100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter.
$100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter.
Chess Community Gathering

- Hang Out & Analyze;  Play Casual Chess Games in the Skittles room.

- TVs are in the Skittle rooms

- Enjoy Good Food

- Buy Chess Merch

- Watch the Tournament.

- Chess Social Life.

- We are looking for volunteers to help with the clean-up; putting chairs and tables away.  Please email us if you can help.  We appreciate it!!

2026 Upcoming Cincinnati Tornadoes
Always Last Saturday of the Month

- Saturday, Jan. 31, 2026 - Tornado

- Saturday, Feb. 28, 2026  – Tornado

- Saturday, March 28, 2026 – Tornado

- Saturday, April 25, 2026 – Tornado

- Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026 – a brief interruption in our normal schedule to host the Ohio Chess Congress

- Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026 – Tornado

- Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 – Tornado

- Saturday, Nov. 28, 2026 – Thanksgiving Tornado

- Saturday, Dec. 26, 2026 – Holiday Tornado

TCA Region V Scholastic 2026 (High School/ Young Ladies)

The Houston Chess Studio

Saturday, March 28, 2026

Event Overview

TCA Region V Scholastic 2026
(High School/ Young Ladies)
Date & Location
Date:  March 28, 2026
Location:  The Houston Chess Studio 250 Patton St. Suite I Houston, TX 77079

Contact Info
Organizer:  Edgar Acosta
Email:   [email protected]
Phone:  (281) 844 4139

Pricing

- Early Registration: $32, ends on March 1, 2026

- Regular Registration: $37, between March 16-22, 2026

- Late Registration: $40, between , March 23-26, 2026

- Active USCF membership is required by February 15, 2026.
- Visit  new.uschess.org/join-us-chess  starting at $24 to join USCF or renew your membership!

- Visit  chess.jliptrap.us/hgroup.htm  for $13 discount Scholastic memberships and renewals!

- TCA Tournament membership is included in the tournament entry fee.
- Visit  texaschess.org/memberships  to join TCA or renew your membership!

Pricing is included in the registration form automatically.

Eligibility
Participants must live or attend school in one of these counties:

- Austin, Brazoria, Brazos, Chambers, Fort Bend, Galveston, Grimes

- Hardin, Harris, Houston, Jasper, Leon, Liberty, Madison

- Matagorda, Montgomery, Newton, Orange, Polk, Robertson

- San Jacinto, Trinity, Tyler, Walker, Waller, Wharton

The max number of registrations for this tournament is 74. Text Edgar Acosta to join a waiting list

Sections

- High School Open: Any High Schooler may enter this section.

- High School U1000: Only High Schoolers rated 1000 or below may enter this section.

- Girls Open: Any Young Lady from Grade K-12

- Girls U1000: Any Young Lady Under 1000

- Note:  Sections may be combined in case of low registrations.

Definitions:

- High School  - Grades 9-12; in some districts 10-12, if Junior High is 7-9.

- Middle School  - Grades 6 to 8 or 9 depending on how the school district divides them.

- Elementary  - K-6 if 6th grade is in the Elementary building, K-5 if 6 is in Middle School.
- A 5th-6th campus has been ruled Elementary, a 6th-only campus as Middle School.

- Primary  - K-3. Note that a first grader could enter K-1 or K-3 or K-5.

- K-8 and K-12 schools and Home School Associations are divided K-5, 6-8, and 9-12.

- Students not assigned a grade in school will be assigned a grade at the tournament based on their age as of September 1 of that school year as follows: six years old is assigned first grade, seven years old is assigned second grade, and so on through grade twelve.

Note:  Sections are based on USCF January 2025 ratings. "Current" ratings may be used to pair unrated players but will  not  determine section placement. Accelerate Pairings will be used at the discretion of the TD the day of the tournament.

Tournament Format

- Rounds:  Swiss 5 Rounds, Game in 25 with a 5-second delay (G/25 d/5).

- Membership:  USCF and TCA memberships required.

- Rules:  USCF rules apply.

- Open sections  require notation  and clocks (if available).
- Players who opt to not take notation will have their time start at 20 minutes instead of 25.

- Reserved sections are strongly encouraged to use notation and clocks.

- Touch-move / Touch-take:  Applies to all sections. Younger players, especially in Kinder-1st Open, will be encouraged to keep these rules with gentle reminders as needed.

- Equipment:  Plan on bringing your own chess set and clock if you have one, money for lunch, and a good attitude!
- Every player needs to bring their clocks!

- Please make sure your clocks are labeled with the player's name and USCF ID.

- Chess sets for the whole tournament  will  be provided!

Schedule

- No At-Site Registration. All registrations must be submitted online at  before 11:59pm on March 26, 2026.

- Please arrive between 8:15 and 8:45 to check in and get ready to play.

- Round 1:  Starts at 9:00 AM SHARP; subsequent rounds will start ASAP. No elimination.

- Players may request a single 1/2 point Bye missed, 0 point Bye for any subsequent Byes. Any Byes need to be requested by Thursday March 26th, 2026 at 7pm.

- Lunch break after Round 3, estimating 12pm-1pm.

Teams
Teams consist of two or more (2+) players in the same section from the same school/association.

- Team members must attend the  same school campus  full-time or belong to the  same Home School Association .

- Sections are  not combined  for teams.

- Team scores will be calculated by summing the top four (4) individual scores from each team.

Awards

- Trophies:  Top 5 individuals in each section and Top 4 teams in each section.

- 1st Place Finishers qualify for a spot in the State Regional Invitational April 18-19th .

- Alternate awards (likely medals) to players who score 3 or more points but do not win a trophy.

- Tie Breaks:  Solkoff (sum of opponents' scores), Modified Median (dropping the lowest opponent's score), Cumulative of Opposition, then Cumulative (USCF Standard)

We look forward to seeing you at The Houston Chess Studio  on March 28, 2026  for a day of competitive and fun scholastic chess!

West Texas '26 March Open

Mad Hatter's House of Games

Saturday, March 28, 2026

Event Overview

PURPOSE: Our goal is to expand rated chess opportunities in our community to benefit and encourage both new and experienced players.

MONTHLY SPECIAL PROMOTIONS & ANNOUNCEMENTS:

- Always FREE registration for players with current USCF rating over 2000! Entry fee deducted from winnings.

- SPECIAL AWARD: Check registration form for details

2025-2026 SEASON SPECIAL PROJECTS, CONTESTS & SPECIAL RECOGNITIONS:

- 2025-2026 Brilliancy Award - Throughout the 2025-2026 season, players may submit notation to report their, or their opponent's, most brilliant moves! The notation must be legible, clearly labeled with player names, and the brilliant move must be marked. All submissions will be reviewed, and the player with the most brilliant move this season will receive an award at the May Open! SUBMISSIONS DUE BY APRIL 30.

- 2025-2026 Texas Chess Association Region I Recognition Program (Details are to be determined) -  Categories and nomination procedures will be announced in the spring. You'll be able to make nominations; self-nomination will not be allowed. Winners must be TCA members. Awards will be presented at the May Open!  SUBMISSIONS DUE BY APRIL 30.

DATE: Saturday, March 28, 2026
LOCATION:   Mad Hatter's House of Games; 1507 Texas Ave., Lubbock, TX 79401
START TIME: Round 1 begins at 11 AM (Players registered in advance online arrive to pay and check-in before 10:45; Players registering onsite arrive before 10:30am)
***NOTE: If you have not checked in by 10:45 you may receive a round 1 bye.
END TIME:  Most sections will finish at approximately 5:30 PM. The Novice Sections will finish at approximately 4:30 PM if players use full time allowed, but usually end earlier. Section awards will be presented shortly after all players in a section have completed their final round. Lower sections typically wrap up earlier than higher sections.
COST: FREE REGISTRATION for players with current USCF rating over 2000 (entry fee deducted from winnings);   $16/player for Early (Online at https://forms.gle/Uaj9FQctxt5TD73B7 ) or $21/player for Late (On-site) registration. Payment options include PayPal at the time of online registration or cash on-site at the door. ***There is a $1 cash payment discount, bringing cash payments down to $15 for early registration or $20 for onsite registration.***
REGISTRATION DEADLINES:  Early (Online at https://forms.gle/Uaj9FQctxt5TD73B7 ) pre-registrations are due by 6 PM Friday,  March 27, 2026. Late (On-site) registrations must be done between 10:00 and 10:30 AM on Saturday,  March 28, 2026.

TOURNAMENT DETAILS:
Tournament Director: Robert Moore, Region I Director – Texas Chess Association

USCF Rated Event: Current USCF membership required - PLEASE update your membership prior to tournament day. Contact us if you need help registering or renewing your USCF membership.

Schedule: This is a swiss style tournament; See below for number of rounds and time controls for each section. Pairings will be posted 5 minutes after the last game in the previous round ends, and the new round will begin 10 minutes after the previous round is complete. This effectively adds a 10-minute break for players who are the last to finish a round.  Round 1 begins promptly at 11 AM; if you are not checked in by 10:45, you may receive a round 1 bye.

Equipment: Chess sets and notation supplies will be provided. Some chess clocks will be available, but please bring your own clock if you have one .

Five sections as follows:

- Open Championship - Must be rated above 1300. If fewer than 8 players are above 1300, highest rated players below 1300 will be used to ensure at least 8 players in the section; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5

- Reserve A (U1300) - Rating between 950 and 1300 and unrated players; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5

- Reserve B (U1000) - Rating between 750 and 1000 and unrated players; 4 Rounds, G/40;d5

- Novice A (U800) - Rating between 350 and 800 and unrated scholastic players; 5 Rounds, G/25;d5

- Novice B (U400)  - Rating under 400 and unrated players 5th grade or below; 5 Rounds, G/25;d5

- EXCEPTIONS FOR PROVISIONALLY RATED PLAYERS :  Adult players with provisional ratings below 750 may choose to play up into a Reserve section, but they may also register for the novice section that matches their provisional rating. Scholastic players with provisional ratings may be placed in an appropriate section by the tournament director.

- NOTE ABOUT PLAYERS' SECTION PLACEMENT: At the TD's discretion, sections may be added, deleted, or combined.  A player near the rating cut-off may be moved to maintain an even number of players in as many sections as possible. Also, at the TD's discretion, section rating ranges may be revised onsite based on natural breaks in rating distributions, which could increase the number of players in the Open Championship section to more than 8.

- RATING DETERMINATION:   USCF ratings as of March 23 will be used to determine section eligibility for this event.

Prizes:

Cash prizes for Open Championship and Reserve Sections:  Cash prize guarantees are based on 50 registered players .

- The total guaranteed prize fund for 50 players is $350.

- The available cash prize fund will be increased or decreased based on registration variance from 50 players.  At 100 players, the prize fund will grow to $1000!

- If there are fewer than 50 players, prizes may be given for fewer than 3 places in each section.

- Ties will follow USCF rules for splitting cash prizes.

Trophies & medals for Novice sections:

- Trophies will be awarded to the top three finishers in each Novice section.

- Medals will be awarded to players who tie for third but do not receive a trophy.

- Standard tie breaks will be used.

PHOTOGRAPHY: Photos may be taken during the tournament and awards ceremony. These images may be shared with Texas Chess Association, news outlets, or other interested groups or individuals. Images may be used for promotion of subsequent chess events.

CONTACT: Completing the registration form linked below should generate an email to the address used to complete the form. Prior to the tournament, another email communication will be sent with a link to check tournament registration details.

If you have any questions please email us:

- Robert Moore - [email protected] ; 334-233-4373

- Amy Jones - [email protected] ; 806-787-3568

Lubbock , TX 79401

United States

EASTERN KENTUCKY OPEN

Morgan County Fiscal Court Building

Saturday, March 28, 2026

Event Overview

This is a qualifying event for the 2026 Kentucky Closed Championship. The top Kentucky player who has not already qualified will receive an invitation to this event.
US Chess Membership is REQUIRED. All US Chess rules will be followed.
Membership must be current through March 2026
Membership will NOT be available onsite, sign up at uschess.org
Please bring membership ID number to the tournament
Notation is required for all players. Players 8 years old or younger (or their parents) can ask
tournament director before Round 1 for an exemption.
Players younger than high school age (~14) must be accompanied by an adult.
FORMAT
Two Sections: both will be 4 Rounds - Swiss System
OPEN Section: open to all USCF players and any rating level
U1500 Section: open to USCF players with ratings below 1500 (unrated to 1499)
G30;d5 (clocks will be set to 30 minutes per player, 5 second delay)
Note: we reserve the right to have only one OPEN section if there is a low turnout the day of the tournament.
ENTRY FEE
$30 if pre-registered online by Friday, March 27th, 2026, otherwise $35 the day of the tournament.
CASH ONLY PAYMENT IS DUE BEFORE ROUND ONE BEGINS
SCHEDULE
Check-in and registration will take place from 9:15 AM to 9:45 AM on Saturday.
Round 1 will commence at 10:00 AM or soon thereafter, and the subsequent rounds will begin as soon as possible, approximately at 11:30 AM, 1:00 PM, and 2:30 PM.
Players who arrive late after round 1 is paired will receive a half-point bye in the first round and will be paired in subsequent rounds. One 1/2 point bye’s available for any round. Must  declare during registration.
PRIZES
The tournament offers a prize fund of $1200 based on 30 players, and cash prizes will be
distributed promptly after the conclusion of the fourth round.
The distribution of closed championship invitations will be determined by a KCA (Kentucky
Chess Association) representative at a later date.
Please note that for the top female player, the cash prize will be awarded, but the invitation is for an alternate only.
One cash prize per player. Standard USCF Tiebreakers will be used in all sections to determine
the winner. If there are ties, the prize money will be equally divided.
In the event of a perfect score tie (4.0/4.0) in the OPEN SECTION for qualifying for the closed event a tie break game will be played G10;d5.
Open Section
Top adult player (21 and over) $200
Top junior player (under 21 at time of this tournament) $200
Top female player (USCF record must list "F" under gender) $200
Top U1900 $100
Top U1700 $100
Under 1500 Section
Top U1500 $100
Top U1300 $100
Top U1100 $100
Top Unrated $100
OTHER
A limited number of chess boards, pieces, and clocks are available, please bring your own if you have them.
TOURNAMENT DIRECTORS AND ORGANIZERS
Please contact tournament organizers if you have any questions.
Chief TD: Landyn Frazier ( Click here to show mail address ) 606-207-5843
Assistant TD: Allen Maddix ( [email protected] ) 859-298-1561

The Indianapolis Public Library - Central Library

Saturday, March 28, 2026

Event Overview

Free to play G/25+5 chess tournaments. RATED and UNRATED tournaments. Rated tournament (requires USCF membership) with scholastic and open sections. Casual Play also available.
The Library's Day of Chess at Central Library, presented by Books & Rooks Chess Club with partners Cloud City Youth and Summit Chess Club.
First 50 players to sign in on day of tournament receive free Books & Rooks t-shirt.
Rated and Unrated Tournaments. G/25+5 sec increment time control. Free and open to all. Rated Tournament requires USCF membership. Casual Play available.
Unrated Tournament with prizes for finalists (number of finalists depending on number of registrants). G/25+5 time control. A great way to compete in your first tournament. No USCF membership required.
A FREE USCF rated tournament (players must have a USCF membership to play in the rated section) with sections based on rating and age. Registration required.
SECTIONS:
Scholastic Sections (K-12):
11 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. (EST) - Please check-in at 10:30 am
G/25 minute + 5 sec increment
4 USCF Rated Games
3U, 6U, 8U & 12U sections
USCF ID required
Trophies & Medals
TD may combine sections based on the number of participants
OPEN Sections (Adults & Kids):
11 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. (EST) - Please check-in at 10:30 am
G/25 minute + 5 sec increment
4 USCF Rated Games
PRO, RESERVE & NOVICE sections
USCF ID required
Apparel and Gear for prizes
TD may combine sections based on the number of participants
UNRATED/CASUAL Arena:
Open to all ages and skills
USCF ID not required
REGISTRATION LINK: Click HERE to Register
TOURNAMENT DETAILS:
This event is open to both Adults and Kids
Please renew or join USCF before March 25th @ https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess if you're playing in the rated sections
1st Round starts at 11 am EST; Next rounds ASAP;
One 1/2 point bye allowed and request prior Round 2
No cell phones / devices during play; All devices off, face down on table is okay
Only USCF approved notation devices allowed
No eating during game
TD may combine sections based on turnout
Chess sets/Clock/Notation sheets provided

DMV Spring Scholastic Tournament (In Person)

SpringHill Suites by Marriott Dulles Airport

Saturday, March 28, 2026

Event Overview

The DMV Spring Scholastic
SpringHill Suites by Marriott Dulles Airport
22595 Shaw Road, Sterling, VA 20166
Saturday, March 28, 2026 at 9 am
Register here: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8461

Note about special rules for pairings:
This tournament will feature Monrad pairings, which is a variation on Swiss pairings that reduces mismatches. The use of Monrad pairings eliminates the need for multiple sections as players are often paired against closely related opponents, especially in early rounds. To read more about Monrad Swiss pairings, visit Wikipedia:  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss-system_tournament#Monrad_system  Because we are using Monrad pairings, which are better at reducing mismatches, there are no separate K-3, K-5, K-8, and K-12 sections. Instead, there is just one section for everyone. To be eligible for grade-based prizes, please include the player's grade in the "grade" field when you register.
Advantages of Monrad Pairings:

- Fewer mismatches, more games against closely-rated opponents

- Eliminate need for multiple sections

- Anyone can win the tournament (lower-rated players are more likely to play each other, which means that anyone has a chance to win)

- Less playing down (higher-rated players are less likely to have to play down)

Tournament Information​

- Four rounds: first round at 9 am, subsequent rounds occur as soon as possible

- One section: Monrad pairings reduce mismatches, eliminating the need for separate K-3, K-5, K-8, and K-12 sections (see note above)

- Time control: Game in 25 minutes with a 5-second delay ( US Chess regular  and quick rated)

- Prizes: trophies for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd in each section

- Entry fee: $35 by 3/16, $40 by 3/23, $45 by 3/27, $50 by 3/28 (on-site registration closes 30 minutes before round 1)

- Boards and pieces will be provided for all players, but we don’t have enough clocks for everyone (those who have clocks are welcome to bring them)

- This tournament is US Chess rated, so an active US Chess membership is required. Click here to join the US Chess Federation for the first time or to renew an inactive membership:  https://new.uschess.org/user/login?destination=/form/membership

- Don’t hesitate to reach out to us at Click here to show mail address  with any questions

Venue Information/Logistics

- PARKING:  The hotel has free parking on the street. In the event that street parking is full, the hotel also has a garage. Chess players can park for a special rate of $5 in the garage.

- Free water will be provided for attendees.

- There is no scheduled lunch break, but there is almost always time for players to have food between games. There aren't any scheduled round times--rounds will occur as soon as possible.

How to Register
Register here: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8461

2nd DMV Adults-Only Classical Tournament (In Person)

SpringHill Suites by Marriott Dulles Airport

Saturday, March 28, 2026
- Sunday, March 29, 2026

Event Overview

2nd Annual DMV Adults-Only Classical Tournament
SpringHill Suites by Marriott Dulles Airport
22595 Shaw Road, Sterling, VA 20166
NOTE: This is a different hotel than the one we used last year.
Saturday and Sunday, March 28-29
Register here: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8462

Adults Only!
This tournament is only for adults. All players must be at least 18 years of age. If you are under 18, please do not register for this event. Thank you.

Tournament Information:

- 4 round Swiss tournament.

- USCF regular rated. Time control: Game in 95 minutes with a 10-second increment.

- Only open to adults (18+). No exceptions.

- Round times: Saturday at 2 pm, Saturday at 6:30 pm, Sunday at 9 am, Sunday at 1 pm
- Later start on Saturday and earlier finish on Sunday allows players to drive to this tournament who live several hours away.

- Entry fee: $58 by 3/15, $65 by 3/21, $70 by 3/27, $75 on the day of the tournament.
- National masters will current ratings over 2200 play for free ($58 entry deducted from prizes). Email [email protected] to register for free as a 2200+ rated player.

- Three Sections: Premier (also FIDE rated), Under 1800, and Under 1400.

- Note: Players may not play up more than 100 points.  A player may use either their live (unpublished) or published rating to qualify for a higher section. Players may also use their FIDE rating to qualify for a higher section. In the event that a player uses their live rating (or FIDE rating) to qualify for a higher section, this rating will also be used for pairings.

- Forfeit policy: A player who is more than thirty minutes late can be forfeited.

- PRIZES: $200 for 1st, $100 for 2nd in Premier; $100 for 1st in U1800, $100 for 1st in Under 1400; Top senior overall in the tournament (50+) prize of $100 (includes $50 donated to this prize from last year's winner). (Note that the top senior prize is accross all sections and is calculated completely separately from the other prizes. It is possible for a player to win the top senior prize in addition to another prize.)

- Up to two half-point byes are allowed. Half-point byes can be requested for any round. The deadline to request a half-point bye is prior to the start of round 3.

- We will have enough chess sets for all players, but clocks will not be provided for everyone. If you have a clock, please bring one.

- There is plenty of free parking at the playing venue.

- For questions, please email us at Click here to show mail address or call us at 703-609-0499.

How to Register

Western IL Chess Club March Madness Open 2026

Western Illinois University QC Campus

Saturday, March 28, 2026

Event Overview

Quad Cities March Madness Open Chess Tournament 2026
Brought to you by Western Illinois Chess Club
(follow us on facebook https://www.facebook.com/chess.moline1)
Open to all ages. USCF membership required in all sections. This tournament is an Iowa State Chess Association Grand Prix points Mini-Qualifier in the Open section.
When:  Saturday, March 28, 2026 9am - 9pm
Where:  Western Illinois University - Quad Cities Campus, Riverfront Building, rooms 103/104, 3300 River Drive Moline, Illinois, 61265
Registration & Fee:  Coffee, snacks, lunch included with registration fee.
Open: $35 online in advance or $40 cash-only in-person same day
Reserve: $25 online in advance or $30 cash-only in-person same day
Beginner/Youth: $20 online in advance or $25 cash-only in-person same day
Register online at https://www.kingregistration.com/event/QuadCityMarchMadness2026
Sections & Time Controls:

- Open: 4-Round Swiss, G/65, d5

- Reserve (under 1400): 4-Round Swiss, G/60, d5

- Beginner/Youth (under 800): 4-Round Swiss, G/20, d0

♟️♟️♟️
Open & Reserve Section Rounds:
1st round: 10:00am
Lunch Break - Pizza and Drinks included with registration fee
2nd round: 1:30pm
3rd round: 4:00pm
4th round: 6:30pm
*Rounds may start earlier if prior round has been completed and if all players are in agreement.
Beginner/Youth Section Rounds:
1st round: 10:00am and then Rounds 2-4 ASAP there after with Lunch break approximately between 3rd & 4th rounds
♟️♟️♟️
Prizes:

- Open Section: 1st Place: $150 ; 2nd Place: $100 ; 3rd Place: $75 ; 4th Place: $50

- Reserve Section (under 1400): 1st Place: $100 ; 2nd Place: $75 ; 3rd Place: $50

- Beginner/Youth Section (under 800): Trophies for 1st - 5th Place ; 6th - 20th Place will receive participation medals.

♟️♟️♟️
Additional info:

- US Chess Federation (USCF) membership required. On Site Registration Available. $3 off for adults, young adults and students if you register through our affiliation.

- Parents/Guardians of young chess players are responsible for their children. Parents/Guardians must be present at all times of the tournament and may enjoy some light snacks or coffee in waiting area while games are in progress.

- Boards and clocks will ONLY be provided for the Beginner/Youth section games. Open and Reserve section players must bring their own regulated clock and board (dimensions listed below).

- Notation of moves on scoresheet is mandatory for Open and Reserve sections games. Scoresheets will be provided. No electronic scoresheets allowed.

- By registering for this event, you also agree to have your photo taken to be used on our facebook page for promo purposes. Sometimes the local news stations show up as well.

♟️♟️♟️
For questions:  Contact Luis Peralta or Mariela Treviño at [email protected] or (309) 737-2890
♟️♟️♟️
Tournament Directors:  Gary Nordick & Mariela Treviño
♟️♟️♟️
Key Rules, Procedures, Cheating & Etiquette:
Scoresheets:  Notation of moves in Open and Reserve sections is required. Players must record moves in algebraic notation, typically writing the move after executing it on the board.
Contacting the TD:  Stop the clock and immediately call the Tournament Director for any rule violation, illegal move, or dispute.
Touch-Move Rule:  If you touch one of your pieces, you must move it if it has a legal move. If you touch an opponent's piece, you must capture it if possible.
One-Hand Rule:  Use only one hand to move a piece and press the clock.
Clock use:  Make your move then press the clock to stop your time until it is your turn again. Running out of time before checkmate means you lose the game automatically.
Illegal Moves:  If you make one, your opponent stops the clock, shows the TD the illegal move, and you get a time penalty (2 minutes extra time will be added to your opponent).
Castling:  Touch the King first, then the Rook, using one hand.
"J'adoube" (I adjust):  Say this before touching a piece to adjust it, not to move it.
Pawn Promotion:  The pawn is considered "touched" when it reaches the promotion square and must be promoted immediately to the piece you place on that square.
No Outside Help:  No computers, phones (strict penalties), books, or talking to others about the game during play.
Communication:  Only talk to your opponent or the TD. Be courteous. Be courteous of the players and their ongoing games around you. Whisper if talking must happen.
Cell Phones:  Keep them off and away; penalties are severe.
Disputes:  Handle calmly; argue with the TD, not your opponent.
USCF Board Regulations & Features:

- Square Size:  2.25 inches is standard, though 2 to 2.5 inches is permissible.

- Overall Size:  20" x 20" or 22" x 22" (approx. 50-55 cm).

- Material:  Usually flexible vinyl, often featuring algebraic notation on all sides.

- Proportion Requirement:  The King's base diameter should occupy roughly 75% to 80% of the square size.

Where to Find More rules:  The full rules are in the US Chess Federation's website under Official Rules of Chess section.
♟️♟️♟️
Western Illinois Chess Club Mission Statement:  To strengthen our community by bringing people together through providing opportunities for chess education, fostering respect, collaboration, and mutual growth.
Western Illinois Chess Club meets every Tuesday from 5:30pm to 8pm at WIU Riverfront Campus, 3300 River Drive, Moline, IL 61265 rooms 103/104. We are open to all chess players of all ages and all levels. Follow us on https://www.facebook.com/chess.moline1 for more chess club news and tournaments. You can also email us at [email protected] or call at (309) 737-2890.

2026 Spring Tournament

Houston Chess Studio

Sunday, March 29, 2026

Event Overview

Organizer
Azeri Chess Academy LLC ( USCF Affiliate ID A9567106 )
Tournament Director
International Grandmaster and Local TD Ulvi Bajarani ( USCF ID 17112757 )
Tournament Purpose
This tournament is part of the Azeri Chess Academy Houston Circuit 2026.
Date & Time
Round 1 starts on March 29, 2026, at 10:00 AM .
Venue
Houston Chess Studio, 250 Patton Street Suite H Houston, Texas 77009.
Time Control
G/30, d10 (Each player gets 30 minutes with a 10-second delay per move).
Format
6-round Swiss system.
Pairings will be generated using ChessRoster SwissSys 11.75 (subject to updates to more recent versions).
Ratings
This tournament is USCF-rated , and the official April 2026 USCF ratings will be used.
Byes

- Up to two (2) half-point byes is allowed and must be declared during registration.

- No additional byes are permitted except for 0-point byes .

- A 1-point bye is awarded to a player who is left without an opponent when the number of players is odd in a given round.

Entry Fee

- $60 – Until February 28, 2025, or for the first 10 players, whichever comes first.

- $80 – Until March 14, 2026, or for the next 20 players, whichever comes first.

- $100 – Until March 29, 2026 at 12:00 AM (midnight), or until all spots are filled.

Cancellation & Refund Policy

- A 50% refund will be granted if a player requests cancellation by March 25, 2025, at 12:00 AM (midnight) .

- No refunds will be issued after this deadline.

Withdrawal Policy

- Players must notify an arbiter before the start of a round if they intend to withdraw.

- Failure to notify an arbiter may affect eligibility for future tournaments organized by Azeri Chess Academy LLC.

Number of Entries
Maximum of 64 participants.
Eligibility

- Open to all players with active USCF membership .

- Players must ensure their USCF membership is active before the start of Round 1.

- Onsite check-ins may be available for players needing USCF membership renewal. They must pay the required renewal fee plus an additional $10 processing fee.

- Failure to renew an expired membership before the tournament will result in exclusion without a refund .

Tournament Schedule (Estimated Round Start Times)
1st Round – 10:00 AM
2nd Round – 11:25 AM
30-minute break
3rd Round – 1:20 PM
4th Round – 2:45 PM
5th Round – 4:05 PM
6th Round – 5:25 PM
Closing Ceremony – 6:45 PM
Prize Fund
Prize distribution is based on the final number of players in the tournament:
< 10 players
1st: $300 + plaque
Total prize fund: $300
10–15 players
1st: $400 + plaque
2nd: $100
Total prize fund: $500
16–20 players
1st: $500 + plaque
2nd: $250
Total prize fund: $750
21–25 players
1st: $500 + plaque
2nd: $250
3rd: $150
Total prize fund: $900
26–30 players
1st: $500 + plaque
2nd: $250
3rd: $150
Best U1600: $150
Best U1200: $150
Total prize fund: $1,200
31–35 players

2nd: $250
3rd: $150

Total prize fund: $1,350

2nd: $350
