SCHOLASTIC SUNDAY by Indy Chess

St. Monica Catholic School Gym (Door 15)

Sunday, April 12, 2026

Event Overview

REGISTER FOR THIS TOURNAMENT HERE: https://www.indychess.org/events
Kids who have learned how the pieces move and some basic strategy are welcome to enter the world of rated chess tournaments!  All school-aged kids from kindergarten to 12th grade are welcome.  Walk-ins are discouraged, as we would appreciate all registering online in advance.  The chess playing room is a silent atmosphere to enable maximum concentration.
For the "rated" tournament, all players MUST be members of the US Chess Federation ($24/year).  Before registering for the rated event, become a member of USCF here (you will need to write down your child's USCF ID#).  However, being a member of Indy Chess--our local club--at $50/year/student or $75/year/family is optional.  If interested, you can do that here to get a $5 discount on this event and every other one you attend this year with us, including Weekly Tuesdays, and support the growth of chess in Indy!
[If a beginner and wanting to play in the "casual" tournament (unrated, does not require USCF membership), that is explained far below.]
Here are the details:

- Check-in on site: 1:45-2:00pm, entering the door up a few exterior stairs/ramp (not the street-level door).  Games start right after a player meeting at 2:15pm.

- 4ss: Four rounds in a "Swiss" system.  A Swiss tournament--the most common chess form--means every player plays every round, with future rounds pairing those who won and those who lost.  Up to two 1/2-point byes can be requested by emailing [email protected] or telling the tournament director at the event which rounds you would like byes.  Note: Premiere section is 3 rounds.

- G/25+5: Games are 25 minutes on each players clock, plus 5 seconds added to a player's time when they hit the clock every move.

- USCF-rated: All players must be members of the US Chess Federation and provide a member ID# in online registration.  This will give each child a "rating" in chess that will follow them with each tournament they play.  Ratings are in blitz, quick, and regular play, and the 25+5 time control affects their regular and their quick rating.

- Entry fee is $20/kid, or $15 for members of Indy Chess.

- Kids rated under 1000 are divided into three  sections so kids play only those in their age group (e.g., 3rd Grade & Under, 6th Grade & Under, and 12th Grade & Under).  Want your child to "play up?"  Just email Mike at [email protected] .  Notation is optional but encouraged in these sections.

- There is one "Premiere" section for kids rated 1000 or above (published rating from the 1st of the month).  Notation is required in the premiere sections.  The Premiere section is three rounds, and may be split by rating at TD discretion to achieve less than eight players per section.

Casual Tournament:
Alongside the rated tournament, kids can instead register for a casual tournament (i.e., unrated) which will begin at the same time.  The games will be optionally clocked, notation is not required, and the tournament director will determine section splits based on turnout.  It will be a Swiss tournament (i.e., all players play all rounds, unless someone gets a bye due to an odd number).  There will be four rounds.  There are trophies for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place winners!
Other details:

- Children under 12 years old must have an adult present and responsible for them, unless the parent/guardian has the permission of the tournament director.

- Concessions are typically available for sale by St. Monica, including hot food (less likely in summer months).

- An outside playground is available.

- Parents may watch chess silently from the bleachers in the gym, or sit at tables in the cafeteria.  There is a guest WiFi network with password August27.

- The site is wheelchair accessible.

- Parking is free in the school lot (Door 15 is located near the southeast side of the building), but is sometimes full right at 1:45p due to a church function.  Parking on a nearby street for overflow is available.

- Chess sets, clocks, and notation sheets are provided for up to 60 kids.  If the child has played in a tournament or two prior, it is helpful if they bring a regulation set and/or clock to ensure there are enough.

- Trophies are provided to the top five finishers in each of the three lower sections.  In the premiere section, a $50 Amazon gift card goes to the winner (decided by 5+0 blitz playoff if need be, Black/White randomly chosen).  Biggest upset earns a medal (unrated does not qualify).

- Players who notate at least one game get to pick a prize from the bin at the end of the tournament!  Learn how to notate chess moves here (YouTube link).

Questions?  Email Mike at [email protected] .  We hope to see you there!

3:30 PM Scholastic Quads (In Person)

Hampton Inn and Suites Dulles

Sunday, April 12, 2026

Event Overview

Scholastic Quads (Groups of 4 based on rating)
Hampton Inn and Suites Dulles
22700 Holiday Park Drive
April 12 at 3:30 pm

***This is a side event for the Dulles International Scholastic Championship. To register or find out more information about the quads, visit the main Dulles International registration page: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8465

Additional info
At 3:30 pm on April 12, in addition to the Dulles International Scholastic happening earlier, we also have a scholastic quads tournament. Players may choose to play in just the championship at 10 am, play only the quads at 3:30 pm, or play both events. Players who play in both events will receive a discounted entry into the quads. If playing both events, the quads will only be $20, regardless of registration date. Otherwise the entry fee for the quads is $30 by 3/26, $35 by 4/3, $40 by 4/11, $45 on 4/12.
A quad is a four-person round robin section in which all participants play each other once (three rounds). Our quads are open to all scholastic players in grades K-12, and each quad will be divided based on rating rather than grade.  The advantage of quads is that players get the chance to compete against opponents with close USCF ratings.  The tournament director has discretion when determining quad seeding (for example, the TD may use a player's unpublished rating). Depending on the exact number of registrations, the bottom section may have five, six, or seven players, in which case that section will be paired as a Swiss tournament.
To register or find out more information about the quads, visit the main Dulles International registration page: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8465

How to Register
To register for the Dulles International Scholastic (or the quads side event), visit this link: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8465

Scholastic Quads Event
At 3:30 pm we also have a scholastic quads tournament. Players may choose to play in just the championship at 10 am, play only the quads at 3:30 pm, or play both events. Players who play in both events will receive a discounted entry into the quads. If playing both events, the quads will only be $20, regardless of registration date. Otherwise the entry fee for the quads is $30 by 3/26, $35 by 4/3, $40 by 4/11, $45 on 4/12.
A quad is a four-person round robin section in which all participants play each other once (three rounds). Our quads are open to all scholastic players in grades K-12, and each quad will be divided based on rating rather than grade.  The advantage of quads is that players get the chance to compete against opponents with close USCF ratings.  The tournament director has discretion when determining quad seeding (for example, the TD may use a player's unpublished rating). Depending on the exact number of registrations, the bottom section may have five, six, or seven players, in which case that section will be paired as a Swiss tournament.

The DMV Action Tournament (In Person)

Hampton Inn and Suites Dulles

Sunday, April 12, 2026

Event Overview

The DMV Action Tournament
Hampton Inn and Suites Dulles
22700 Holiday Park Drive, Sterling, VA 20166
Sunday, April 12 at 4 pm
Register here: https://caissachess.net/online-registration/index/8466

Tournament Information:

- 4 round Swiss tournament.

- USCF regular and quick rated. Time control: Game in 30 minutes with a 5-second delay.

- Sunday, April 12, 4 pm to approximately 9 pm. (First round starts at 4, subsequent rounds occur ASAP.)

- Entry fee: $30 on or before Wednesday the week of the tournament, $35 on or before Saturday, $40 on Sunday (on-site registration is allowed, registration for round one closes at 3:45 pm on Sunday). Free entry to players over 2200 ($30 entry deducted from prizes--please email to register).

- Two Sections: Open (minimum 1300 rating to play) and Under 1500.

- Note: In order to play in the open section, players must have a USCF rating of at least 1300. Players rated between 1300 and 1499 can play in either section. Players under 1300 should play in the Under 1500 section. A player can still join the open section if their unpublished (live) rating is over 1300, even if their monthly rating isn't 1300 yet. The tournament director may decide to have a lower rated player join the open section to maintain an even number of players in the section. The tournament director has the option to use a provisionally-rated player's live rating (regardless of whether it is higher or lower than the player's official rating) for pairings purposes and section eligibility.

- PRIZES: $100 for 1st in Open; $50 for 1st in U1500.

- Up to two half-point byes are allowed. Half-point byes can be requested for any round. The deadline to request a half-point bye is prior to the start of round 3.

- We will have enough chess sets for all players, but clocks will not be provided for everyone. If you have a clock, please bring one.

- This tournament is open to everyone (adults and children of any skill level).

- There is plenty of free parking at the playing venue.

- For questions, please email us at Click here to show mail address  or call us at 703-609-0499.

Tunnelvision XLIII

Columbia Chess Club

Saturday, April 18, 2026

Event Overview

The Columbia Chess Club Presents Columbia Tunnelvision XLIII
April 18, 2026
$1000 Guaranteed
10:30 a.m. 4-Round G/45;inc.5
Columbia Chess Club
6169 St. Andrews Rd.
Columbia, SC 29212
Register
Registration
Standard registration is $40 until the day before the tournament.  $50 late registration the day before/morning of.  Registration online only, registration limited to first 74 players.
Entry for titled players (National Master and above) is free, standard entry fee deducted from prizes.  If you are a titled player, simply use the "Titled Player" option at checkout.
Considering Tunnelvision as your first chess tournament?  Great!  We've put together a guide to help first-time players .
Register Now
Pre-Registered Players
Format
4 Round Swiss. Time control is G45/inc.5 (45 minutes starting time with a 5-second increment ), which will be USCF dual-rated under both Quick and Classical. All equipment provided. USCF Rules Apply, active USCF Membership required. Tournament has three sections: Championship (1600+), Under 1600, and Under 1000. Players may register for a higher section if they are within 100 USCF rating points of the cutoff.
If you need to renew or obtain a USCF membership, please visit  https://new.uschess.org/join-us-chess.
Live Standings/Pairings/Boards
The top board of each section will be live streamed to the DGT LiveCloud along with real-time updates to Lichess.org and Chess.com.  A live video stream of the top Championship board will also be available on the club's Twitch page.  See this site's "Live" menu for links.
Live standings (including current pre-registration information) and pairings are also available below.
Live Standings
Prizes
$1000 Prize Fund Guaranteed.
Championship (1600+)
$400 Fund. 1st: $200; 2nd: $130; 3rd: $70
Under 1600
$300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50
Under 1000
$300 Fund: 1st: $150; 2nd: $100; 3rd: $50
Schedule

- Round 1: 10:30 a.m.

- Round 2: 12:50 p.m.

- Round 3: 2:40 p.m.

- Round 4: 4:30 p.m.

Byes
A single half-point bye is available any round, including the final round.  The half-point bye may be requested as a part of the advance entry or on site before the tournament starts.  Thereafter the only bye available is a zero-point bye.  The chief tournament director shall have the ability to grant a half-point bye for any round on unusual circumstances.
Location
Columbia Chess Club
6169 St. Andrews Rd., Ste A
Columbia, SC 29212
Questions?
Email  [email protected] or call/text James Brandmair at 803.569.0938.
Parking
The Columbia Chess Club is located in a shopping center with ample parking.
Food
The Columbia Chess Club offers on-site concessions, including drinks and snacks.  By the Fire Pizza and Zorba's Restaurant are located in the same shopping center and will be open during the tournament.  Many other restaurants are available close by!

6169 St. Andrews Road, Suite A

Columbia , SC 29212

Grand Prix, State Championship Event

Spanish River Library

Saturday, April 18, 2026
- Sunday, April 19, 2026

Event Overview

FLORIDA STATE WOMEN’S CHESS CHAMPIONSHIP
DATE & TIME: April 18-19, 2026, 9:30 am-6:00 pm
SECTION (FIDE Rated):  Open (includes girls in K-12)
TOURNAMENT LOCATION: Spanish River Library, 1501 Spanish River Blvd, Boca Raton, FL 33431
ROUNDS: 5 rounds, game 60; d30 (60 minutes per player with a 30-second delay)
Saturday: Round 1 at 9:30,  then round 2 and round 3 ASAP (Lunch/snack provided) Sunday: Round 4 at 10:00, then half-hour lunch break before round 5

PRIZES (BASED ON 30): Open: $300, $200, $100 U1600: $60 & U1200: $40
Trophy and titles to the female champion, top female senior and top girl K-12 scholastic player from Florida.
Note: The top finishing K-12 participant will be the Florida State High School Girls Champion and will also represent Florida in the Haring National Tournament of Girls State Champions at the US Open in Grand Rapids, Michigan in 2026.
ENTRY FEE:  $40 if received by April 15; $50 if received later. Online entry closes 8:30 AM April 18. No onsite entry.
Register: https://www.chessregister.com/register?event_key=zywfr9hvD6psP6SNxCyONs1V04Ucuw73-2nkGVypuPY%3D
6 Grand Prix Points
Chess sets will be provided for the games. Bring a chess clock if you have one.
USCF MEMBERSHIP IS REQUIRED.  If the USCF website does not show you as a current member, you will not be paired.
QUESTIONS: Chief Tournament Director – Charles Hatherill, NTD/FIDE IA -- Email: [email protected]

2026 Maryland State Scholastic Championships

State Championship Event

Hammond High School

Saturday, April 18, 2026
- Sunday, April 19, 2026

Event Overview

Register at  chessacademy.com/tournaments !
The  official Maryland State Scholastic Championship tournament and Denker, Barber, Rockefeller, and Ashley Qualifiers!
With special guest IM Danny Rensch, who will be doing a lecture and book signing of his memoir Dark Squares at 11am on Saturday
This is a US Chess rated Swiss style tournament. There are ten different sections for players depending on their age and skill.  Sections include  K-1 U-400, PS U-600, ES U-800, MS U-1000, HS U-1200, K-1 Champ, PS Champ (550+), ES Champ (750+), MS Champ (950+), and HS Champ (1150+).  Participants play only against opponents in their own section. Under sections for elementary school, K-1 Champ, and PS Champ will play all their games on Saturday. Under sections for middle and high school will play all their games on Sunday. ES Champ, MS Champ, and HS Champ will play their games on Saturday and Sunday.
Championship sections are only open to students who live in or attend school in MD, under sections are open to participants from any state.

- All sections are non-elimination, and all players participate in all five rounds.

- We provide FREE US Chess Federation memberships for all participants, a $24 value!

- For players using chess clocks, the time control is G/25 with a 5-second time delay. For ES, MS, and HS championship sections, the time control is G/75 d5.

- Trophies to the top players and teams in each section.

- Prices increase $10 at noon on Tuesday, 3/31 and $10 at noon on Tuesday, 4/14.

Questions?  Please let us know at  Click here to show mail address !

- Players must have an active (paid) US Chess Federation membership to compete in the rated sections.

- Check membership status

Rapid Tournaments

- Round 1: 9:00am

- Round 2: 9:30am

- Round 3: 10:00am

- Round 4: 10:30am

- End Time: ~11:15am

- Byes: Limit one 1/2-point bye if requested prior to the first round. No last round byes.

- Time Control: G/15

- Rating: Games will be USCF quick-rated.

- Notation: Notation not required.

Grand Prix

Community Church of Glen Rock Education Building

Saturday, April 18, 2026
- Sunday, April 19, 2026

Event Overview

This is a two-day dual FIDE and USCF-rated tournament.
Registration Fee: $120.  Early bird!  Register by April 11, 11:59 pm for just $100.
Free entry to GMs, IMs, and 2400+ FIDE rated players. Email  Click here to show mail address for a coupon for free entry.
For full refund, canceled registrations must be requested by e-mail by 11:59 pm the night before the tournament.
Format: 4 round Swiss-System (two rounds per day).  G110 d10.  Pairings based on FIDE ratings.
Minimum rating:  A monthly published rating of 1600 USCF or 1500 FIDE
All players must have a valid FIDE ID.  Players may request a USA-flagged FIDE ID at this URL:  https://tinyurl.com/nebafd36 .  Players wishing a non-USA flagged FIDE ID must contact the relevant country’s chess federation.
Schedule:  Saturday 11:00 am, 3:30 pm.  Sunday 1:00 pm, 5:30 pm.
Prizes:   Prize distribution will follow standard USCF rules.
1st - $500
2nd - $360
3rd - $240
Under 2200 (FIDE) - $180
Under 2000 (FIDE) - $180
Under 1800 (FIDE) - $180
Under age 13 - $180
Over age 55 - $180
Byes:  Two half-point byes available for any round.  Half-point byes must be requested before the start of round two. Byes must be requested 15 minutes before the start of each round.
Online registration:  Closes at 10:00 am on the first day of the tournament
Online registration link: https://ica.jumbula.com/ICATournaments2026/ICAFIDEChampionshipApril18April19
On-site registration is open from 10:00 am to 10:30 on the day of the tournament.
Equipment:  All participants must bring clocks.
Norms:  FIDE norms are not available at this event.
Late arrivals:  Late arrivals will be handled as per USCF rules
Parents and caregivers:  There is waiting space for parents and caregivers where they can keep an eye on young players.
Parking:  Please enter via parking lot entrance on Hamilton Avenue.  After parking, please enter through the door that has an “International Chess Academy” sign then proceed to the second floor.
By train:  Glen Rock has two NJ Transit stations within easy walking distance of ICA: Glen Rock - Main Line and Glen Rock - Boro Hall.
By bus:  Take 164, 164B, 164E, or 175B to Rock Road at Central Avenue.  All stop directly in front of ICA.

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids

Chess Kings & Queens Academy

Saturday, April 18, 2026

Event Overview

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30.  Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00.  The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play.  Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections.  The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment.  Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $30.  Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information:  Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).
Information / registration link:  https://chesskq.com/tournament

4/18 - ST. PETERSBURG EXTRA QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT G60; d5.

Saint Petersburg Chess Club

Saturday, April 18, 2026

Event Overview

There will be no “Byes” or withdrawals allowed. Please complete all your Quad games.

WHAT IS THE QUAD CHESS TOURNAMENT?   After all the players have entered, they’re ordered from highest rating to lowest.  Unrated players are placed at the low end. The top four players are placed into their own section (a “quad”), then the next four highest in another section, and so on down the list.  The players in each quad play a round robin, one game against each of the players in their section, for a total of three games each.  If there is not an even multiple of four players, the lowest section (usually) will have the few extra players and play a three round Swiss tournament rather than a round robin. The quad format is popular in one day events, and results in players of the most similar playing strengths being paired together for all three rounds. A Quad Tournament consists of the top four ranked players (#s 1-4) on the Chess Ladder playing each other, then the second top four ranked players (#s 5-8) playing each other, then the third top four ranked players (#s 9-12) playing each other, and so forth. Each group of four chess players is called a Quad.If two family members are at the same Quad,I can move one of them to another Quad.
ADVANTAGES OF QUAD TOURNAMENTS: The advantage of Quad Tournaments, and why players enjoy them so much, is that players of the same strength and experience are able to compete against each other. In addition, the less experienced players are able to win the same "First Place" prizes as their more experienced, stronger counterparts in Quad I and II. You have opportunity your rating to go up faster!!!
LOCATION : Saint Petersburg Chess Club 540 4th Avenue North Saint Petersburg, FL 33701 (it is located in between Mirror Lake and the Coliseum, next to the Sunshine Center.)
REGISTRATION : 10:00-10:45 a.m. If you want to make sure you can play, you need to Pay ahead of time here -  https://home.chessregister.com/
ENTRY FEE:
$25 if paid by Wednesday (3 days before the tournament)
$30 afterward
$35 if paid on Saturday
USCF membership is required. Please check your USCF ID and renew it if it has expired. If you need me to do it on site add $5 to your bill.
ROUNDS: Three Rounds, First starts at approx. 11:00 a.m.
TIME CONTROL: G60; d5
PRIZES : $65 for first place at each Quad or very big trophies for 1st place (if two players tied for 1st place $33 each, or chess trophies for 1st place for both of them)
Trophies for 1st to 3rd place for the last section!
IMPORTANT NOTICE : Due to space limitation to secure your spot Pay online ahead of time!  BRING YOUR CHESS CLOCK!!!
Visit our website-  https://saintpetersburgchessclub.com/ for more information about chess at Saint Petersbug.
Join our Facebook groups Saint Petersburg Chess Tournaments -        https://www.facebook.com/groups/385692191510406/
For more information you can call (727) 776-5583, or send me email to  Click here to show mail address

The Emory Tate Chess Classic

Roots-101 Museum, 124 North 1st Street

Saturday, April 18, 2026

Event Overview

This tournament is sponsored by the Tate Siblings. It is the only one sponsored by his daughter and sons.
Registration starts 1030 am to 11 am, first round at 1115 am and all rounds as soon as possible. Blitz, G/5, open, EF seven dollars; Speed Chess, G/10, K/12, EF seven dollars; based on the entry fees received there will be a 70% pay out. Bughouse starts at 1 pm. The entry fee is fourteen dollars. Based on total entry fees received, the pay out is 70% to the top four teams. Open bughouse, K/12 bughouse. The two teams in reach receive a cash prize. The other participants earn Chess Dollars.
Affordable concessions table. Bring small bills. Concessions help fund chess education programs for seniors citizens.

Phoenix Saturday Action

Phoenix Chess Academy

Saturday, April 18, 2026

Event Overview

4 round Swiss. Time control: Game in 25 minutes with 5 sec delay. Boards, sets, clocks and scoresheets will be provided.
Registration: Go to www.phoenixchessacademy.com. USCF membership is required. New or renewing USCF members are welcome. Highest rating will be used for Swiss pairings and prize purposes.
Sections: Open, Under 1700 & Under 1200 (No playing up allowed). Sections will be combined in case a section has less than 4 players registered.
Schedule: Round 1- 9:00 AM, Round 2- 10:05 AM, Round 3- 11:10 AM, Round 4- 12:15 PM. Awards Ceremony will start right after last game is over. Half point Byes are available in all 4 rounds and (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. Requesting a zero-point bye late in the tournament is considered the same as withdrawing.
Entry Fee: $25.00 by 04/15; $30 by 04/17; $35 same day. Full refund will be issued to players who withdraw at least an hour before the first round. In cases where a registered player does not show up for the tournament without prior notice, they will not be eligible for a refund.
Prizes: Trophies for top three in each section.
A player will automatically forfeit the game if going in the bathroom with a cellphone.

2025-26 CalChess Super States: K-3 & K-8 Championship and K-12 Sections

Sonesta Silicon Valley Event Center

Saturday, April 18, 2026
- Sunday, April 19, 2026

Event Overview

Compete in the 2025-26 CalChess Super States K-3 & K-8 Championship and other K-12 sections, where scholastic players enjoy exciting games at a state-level championship! It's the perfect opportunity to gain experience and earn trophies.
Register here

- You must  log in or sign up  before you can register.

- Online registration closes at  12:00 a.m.  the day of the tournament.

- Onsite registration is subject to availability ($44 additional fee incurred).

- Late fees applied starting April 12 or when reaching capacity.

Sections

- Players will need to register based on their 2025-26 school grade and their April Supplement Rating (i.e., rating as of Mar. 19) into one of the following sections:
- K-12 Rookie (unr.)

- K-12 Beginner (100-399)

- K-3 Jr. Varsity (400-799)

- 4-12 Intermediate (400-799)

- K-12 Intermediate (400-799)

- 4-12 Advanced (800-1199)

- K-12 Advanced (800-1199)

- K-8 Jr. Varsity (800-1199)

- K-3 Champ (800+)

- K-8 Champ (1200+)

- 9-12 Advanced (1200+)

Play-up rule

- A player may pay to play up one higher section, double play up is  NOT  allowed.

- Players must be within 300 points of the rating cutoff to play up.
(Note: The rating used to determine if a player may play up is their  April USChess Published Supplement Rating)

Schedule

- K-12 Rookie & K-12 Beginner :
- Time Control: 5x G/25 d5

- Two schedules available: Saturday OR Sunday

- Round Times:
- Sat, Apr. 18 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.
OR

- Sun, Apr. 19 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.

- K-3 Jr. Varsity , 4-12 Intermediate & K-12 Advanced :
- Time Control: 5x G/25 d5

- Round Times:
- Sat, Apr. 18 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.

- K-3 Champ , K-12 Intermediate & 4-12 Advanced :
- Time Control: 5x G/25 d5

- Round Times:
- Sun, Apr. 19 - 9:00 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 12:20 p.m., 2:00 p.m., 3:40 p.m.

- K-8 Jr. Varsity , K-8 Champ & 9-12 Advanced :
- Time Control: 6x G/65 d5

- Round Times:
- Sat, Apr. 18 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m.

- Sun, Apr. 19 - 9:00 a.m., 12:00 p.m., 2:50 p.m.

- ½-point bye is available for  ONE (1) round, except for the last round (Byes must be requested  at least 30 min  before that round's start).

- 0-point byes are available for any round.

- If you request more than one bye, we will give you a ½-point for the latest round possible except for the last round (0-point byes for all other rounds).

Awards

- Personal Trophies to all players with a winning record.
- One trophy per player.

- Trophy size vary based on standings.

- Medals to all other players.

- Team Trophies to all of the following with two or more players in all sections combined:
- Clubs

- Schools

- A player who withdraws during the tournament is not eligible for awards.

Fees

- Entry fee:
- K-8 Jr. Varsity, K-8 Champ and 9-12 Advanced: $113

- All other sections: $79

- Play up fee: +$29

- Discount for BayAreaChess Membership Subscribers ( More info ).

- Late fees, starting:
- Apr. 12: +$11

- Apr. 14: +$22

- Apr. 16: +$33

- Onsite fee: +$44

- BayAreaChess Membership discounts are  NOT  redeemable for late and onsite fees.

Withdrawals

- Withdrawals are eligible for a partial refund, subject to the following deductions:
- until Apr. 11, 4% processing fee.

- from Apr. 12 to Mar. 13, $11 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee.

- from Apr. 14 to Mar. 15, $22 withdrawal fee + 4% processing fee.

- from Apr.  16 onward,  NO REFUND  will be issued.

- Only withdrawals made  before or on Apr. 15 are eligible for refund.

Change requests

- After registration, changes can be requested at  bayareachess.com/changeform and are subject to the following fees:
- until Apr. 16, $7 change fee.

- on Apr. 17, $15 change fee.

- The following requests are exempt from the change fee:
- playing up to a higher section.

- requesting byes.

- updating club and/or school.

Other requirements

- USCF membership must be active.

More info available  here .

4th Austin Chess Tour: Open Qualifier #4

Saturday, April 18, 2026

Event Overview

4th Austin Chess Tour: Open Qualifier #4
In-Person USCF Rated Tournament
April 18, 2026
12466 Los Indios Trail, Ste.100
Austin, TX 78729
* USCF Membership Required *
Free Parking Provided
Capacity: 112 players
SECTIONS:
All players will be divided into 4 sections:
SECTION A: 1800+  Open USCF rated
SECTION B: 1400 - 1799 Open USCF rated
SECTION C: 1000 - 1399 Open USCF rated
SECTION D: U1000 Open USCF rated
**Players are not allowed to play up or down**
ENTRY FEES:
Early Bird: $50 before 11:59PM March 29, 2026
Standard Fee: $60 before 11:59 April 12, 2026
Late Fee: $75 after April 13, 2026
PRIZES:
Section A: $400, $200, $100
Section B: $200, $100, $50
Section C: $100, $75, $50
Section D: Chess books
Medals will be awarded to top 3 finishers in all sections
NOTE: Players who win prizes must provide us with their Paypal information or wait until the section is completed to receive cash prizes.
Open Qualifier Points:
Top 10 places in Section A will earn points according to the following table:
1st Place: 25 OQ Points
2nd Place: 18 OQ Points
3rd Place: 15 OQ Points
4th Place: 12 OQ Points
5th Place: 10 OQ Points
6th Place: 8 OQ Points
7th Place: 6 OQ Points
8th Place: 4 OQ Points
9th Place: 2 OQ Points
10th Place: 1 OQ Points
For more information about the point system, visit
https://austin-chess.com/tournaments/
TIME CONTROL:
Section A: G/60, d5 (60 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section B: G/60, d5 (60 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section C: G/45, d5 (45 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
Section D: G/45, d5 (45 minutes per player with a 5-second delay)
4-Round Swiss System Schedule
SECTIONS A and B:
1st round: 10:00 AM
2nd round: 12:15 PM
Lunch Break: 2:30 PM
3rd round: 3:30 PM
4th round: 5:45 PM
SECTIONS C and D:
1st round: 10:00 AM
2nd round: 11:45 AM
Lunch Break: 1:30 PM
3rd round: 2:30 PM
4th round: 4:15 PM
Closing ceremony for each section will take place after the final round of that section.
NOTE: Half-point byes are acceptable for all rounds, limit 1. Must commit before the 1st round.

PLAYERS MAY NOT POSSESS CELL PHONES DURING THE TOURNAMENT.  Please leave your phone at home, in your car, or turned off (vibrate/silent not acceptable) on top of your table.
Any violators may be subject to disqualification and forfeiture.
CANCELLATION POLICY: If you do not wish to participate in our tournament after paying the entry fee, please email us at  [email protected] no later than 24 hours in advance. We reserve the right to charge a $15 service fee for cancellations. NO refunds will be issued if we are notified of cancellation within 24 hours of the start of the event.
WITHDRAWAL POLICY: If you would like to withdraw from the tournament after it begins, please alert the tournament director. NO refunds will be issued after the tournament begins.
NO-SHOW POLICY: There are NO refunds or credit for players who do not show up for their scheduled tournament matches.
For additional questions, please contact us at [email protected]

PA Senior Championship - Irwin Qualifier

State Championship Event

Tri-Bridges Chess Club

Saturday, April 18, 2026
- Sunday, April 19, 2026

Event Overview

This event is the official Pennsylvania Senior Open. You must be 50 or older to play as of 8/3/25 (when the Irwin tournament starts all participants must be 50 or over.)  You may be from any state. However, to represent Pennsylvania in the Irwin Championship at the U. S. Open, you must be a citizen of Pennsylvania.

One section – G/90 d5. Round Times: Saturday – 10 – 1:30 – 5; Sunday 9:30 – 1
Prizes: Irwin representative for top Pennsylvanian; 1st Overall – $200, 2nd Overall – $100; Top Under 2000 – $90; Top Under 1800 – $80; Top Under 1600 – $70; Top Under 1400 – $60; Top Under 1200 – $50; Top Under 1000 – $50;
Entry Fee: $30
Please note that there are stairs to both playing areas. If this is a problem, I can arrange to use a room on the main floor (there are still two steps to get into the building), but it would be helpful to know beforehand. Coffee/tea/water is available. Fast food/sit-down restaurants/convenience stores are within a few minutes’ commute. Two or three hotels are about 5 minutes away, and many are within about 20 minutes. There will also be a small selection of chess literature for sale.
One half-point bye allowed; must declare by the start of round 2.
When signing up, click blue registration button, fill out form, don’t worry if there is no grade, etc. (we do many kid events, but you can just ignore those blanks), click submit, and then reload page to see if you want to double check that you have signed up.
Please note that we have moved into April as the first weekend in March is the State Scholastic and the Ira Lee Riddle State Championship.
You may register on site between 8:30 and 9:30.  The entry fee for registering on site is $50.

Missouri All Girls Tournament

Rockbridge High School

Saturday, April 18, 2026

Event Overview

The Tournament is open to all female players, grade K-12.  Hosted by the Missouri Chess Association.
Qualification : Girls currently in Kindergarten through 12th grade, are welcome to play.  USCF membership is required.
Rounds:   G/60 d;5 .   Round Times:  10, 12:30, 2:45, 5.  Later rounds will start early if possible
Entry Fee :  $10
Prizes:
-State Champion Trophies to top 3 Overall.
-Trophies to Top scorer in K-8, and Top scorer in K-5.
-The overall winner will be the 2025 Missouri All Girls Champion, and will be offered Missouri’s spot in the annual Ruth Haring National Girls Invitational Tournament, held in August 2025.   The Haring tournament is an invitational only tournament run by the USCF, with each state selecting one representative.
Registration : Preregistration by email appreciated.  Payments will be made on site.  Include Name, grade, and USCF ID# to [email protected]
Check-in Saturday 9 – 9:45am.
Tournament is run concurrently with the High School Denker tournament and the Columbia Open.  Events have a shared location and round times for those traveling together.

- Round 1 begins at  10:00 AM

- Subsequent rounds occur  as soon as possible  after each round finishes

- Sections:  Five sections
- K–12

- K–8

- K–5

- K–3

- Unrated -Anyone between age 4-12 with no USCF rating can play.

- 🏆 School Team Champion Trophy (New!)
Each section will award a School Team 1st Place Trophy .
To qualify, a school must have at least two players competing in the same section .
The trophy is awarded to the top-scoring school team in that section .

- Time Control:   Game in 30 minutes with a 5-second delay
- US Chess Regular and Quick rated

- Entry Fees (K–12, K–8, K–5, K–3 sections):
- $50  by  04/04

- $55  by  04/09

- $60  by  04/14

- $65  by  04/18

- On-site registration closes one (1) hour before Round 1

- Equipment:
- Boards and pieces will be provided for all players

- We don’t have enough clocks for everyone

- Players who have clocks are welcome to bring them

- US Chess Membership:
- This tournament is  US Chess rated , so an  active US Chess membership is required

- If you don’t have one or are not sure what your ID# is, you can look it up here:  US Chess

- Electronics Policy:
- No electronic scoring devices are allowed

- Parent Supervision:
- Parents should look after their kids  before and after  the games

- Questions:
- Please email:  [email protected]

PRIZES
Cups and trophies  for  1st through 3rd place  in each section.
All participants will receive participation medals.
Additional Prize:

- 1st place in the other sections  will each receive  one-month free entry  into a GMChessPrep.*
- Admission into some weekday course cannot be guaranteed due to limited seat availability.

Tiebreaks / Ties:

- For cups, trophies, and prizes, ties will be broken using  standard US Chess tiebreaks

- In the event of a tie, the  free course prize  will be determined by tiebreaks

- If multiple players get a perfect score,  each of them will receive a free course entry

MORE TOURNAMENT INFO

- More Tournament Info is here:  Caissa Chess Software

- The tournament is  limited to 60 total players

- No refunds after registration unless tournament is cancelled by organizer.

VENUE INFORMATION / LOGISTICS

- Parking:  The school has free parking. There are spots in front of the school.

- Food / Breaks:
- There is  no scheduled lunch break

- There is almost always time for players to have food between games

- There aren’t any scheduled round times — rounds will occur as soon as possible

National Championship Event

Embassy Suites by Hilton Milwaukee Brookfield

Friday, April 24, 2026
- Sunday, April 26, 2026

Event Overview

2026 U.S. Amateur North Championship
April 24-26 (or 25-26 for 2-day schedule)
STANDINGS AND PAIRINGS (expect about 30 minute before round time):
This event is limited to 140 participants. Please register as soon as possible.
if you are looking to register for the Great Lakes Festival, use this link: Great Lakes Festival
Embassy Suites by Hilton Milwaukee Brookfield
1200 S Moorland Rd, Brookfield, WI 53005 (262) 782-2900
Chess Rate is $119 (King bed or two Queen beds; please reserve by April 12th): Book your room here . If the link doesn't work, please contact the organizers and we will make sure you get the chess rate! Free Breakfast and Free Cocktail reception ($40 daily value!). Free Internet. Free parking. **Please see below for food concessions and outside food/drink policy**
EQUIPMENT:  uniform equipment (boards, sets, clocks) is provided and should be used
QUESTIONS : Alex Betaneli  Click here to show mail address
PRIZES

- National Champion Title

- 30 valuable trophies

SECTIONS
PRIZES

u2200
Trophies to top ten places; National Title to the overall winner

u1701
Trophies to top ten places

u1301
Trophies to top ten places

TIEBREAKS:  the order of tiebreaks for team and individual prizes is Solkoff, Cumulative Opposition, Cumulative, Modified Median.

First time players are welcome. Good preparation can consist of games, tutorials and tactics on lichess.org

This is a National Event limited to players who are rated below 2200. If you would like to face stronger opponents, the Great Lakes Festival  is held simultaneously: it offers cash prizes and is FIDE rated.
Notation is mandatory for the entire game (except for Round 1 of the 2-day schedule).

Accelerated pairings might be used.
Organizers reserve the right to choose the highest of the published ratings (Regular, Rapid, Online Regular, Online Rapid, FIDE) for the purpose of section selection, pairings, and prizes. Only regular ratings are affected by this event.

ENTRY FEES
TIME CONTROLS AND PLAYING SCHEDULE

- $69 online by April 6th

- $79 online by April 20th

- $99 after that or onsite

- 3-day entries after 6:30pm Friday receive ½-point bye for round 1

- 2-day entries after 8:30am Saturday receive ½-point bye for round 1

- 1/2 point byes OK all rounds, must commit before round 1 (maximum 2); please email organizers

- Register Online: Register for 2026 U.S. Amateur North Individual Championship

3-day
G/90+30 second increment

- Friday 7:00pm

- Saturday 11:00am, 4:00pm

- Sunday 10:00am, 3:00pm

2-day

This event is limited to 50 participants. Please register as soon as possible.

April 24-26 (or 25-26 for 2-day schedule)
if you are looking to register for the U.S. Amateur North Championship, use this link: U.S. Amateur
Embassy Suites by Hilton Milwaukee Brookfield
1200 S Moorland Rd, Brookfield, WI 53005 (262) 782-2900
Chess Rate is $119 (King bed or two Queen beds; please reserve by April 12th): Book your room here . If the link doesn't work, please contact the organizers and we will make sure you get the chess rate! Free Breakfast and Free Cocktail reception ($40 daily value!). Free Internet. Free parking.  Hotel has no outside food/drink policy in the meeting rooms and public spaces (personal water bottles are ok).

31st Space Coast Open Chess Festival

Heritage Event, Grand Prix, Enhanced Grand Prix, Junior Grand Prix

Hilton Melbourne at Rialto Place

Friday, April 24, 2026
- Sunday, April 26, 2026

Event Overview

Event Overview
April 24-26 OR 25-26, FLORIDA
US Chess Grand Prix Points: 120 (Enhanced)

Space Coast Open,   5SS , Top 2 sections FIDE rated , (USCF ratings used for pairings & prizes). All sections but Under 1200 G/90+30 sec. incr., Under 1200 section G/90 d5 (2-day schedule rounds 1-2, all sections, G/60;d5).
Hilton Melbourne at Rialto Place,
200 Rialto Place, Melbourne, FL 32901.
Free parking. No resort fee. 5 minutes from Melbourne International Airport.

Prizes:   $20,000 Guaranteed . 5 Sections:
Master/Expert: (Min. USCF or FIDE rating of 2000 required) $2000+trophy-1000-500-250, U2400 $1400+trophy-750, U2200 $1300+trophy-700, Top Senior $200.
Under 2000:  $1300+trophy-700-400, U1850 $500+trophy-300, Top Senior $200.
Under 1800: $1000+trophy-550-300, U1650 $500+trophy-300, Top Senior $200.
Under 1500: $1000+trophy-550-250, U1350 $500+trophy-300, Top Senior $200.
Under 1200: $800+trophy-400-250, U1000 $400+trophy-300, U800 $300+trophy-200, Top Senior $200, trophies to top scholastics players in K-3, K-5, K-8, K-12.
All: Unrated may enter any section except Master/Expert and may not win over $300 or trophy. Unrated not eligible for U1000 or U800 prizes. Must be 60+ on April 24 to win Senior prize (prize is in addition to any other prize). Prizes for 1st-3rd brilliancy & biggest upset rds. 1-4.

EF: $124 early-bird by 3/22, $144 by 4/17, $154 later, $160 on-site; $20 less if Unrated or under age 18. Re-entry $70. GM/IM free entry available by request to TD until 3/31, else $144 from prize. Special EF for Brevard County K-12 students in any section: $29 by 3/22, $49 by 4/17, $59 later, $65 on-site. $10 service charge for refunds.

Reg.:  On-site registration ends 1/2 hr before 1st rd. Online registration ends 5pm Friday. No phone, US Mail, or email entries.

Rds.:
All Sections but Under 1200:   3-Day:  Fri. 7:00 pm; Sat. 10:30 am, 4:30 pm; Sun. 10:30 am, 3:30 pm;
2-Day:  (merges with 3-day after round 2) Sat. 10:30 am, 1:30 pm, 4:30 pm; Sun. 10:30 am, 3:30 pm.
Under 1200 Section Only:   3-Day:  Fri. 7:00 pm; Sat. 10:30 am, 2:45 pm; Sun. 10:30 am, 2:45 pm;
2-Day:  (merges with 3-day after round 3) Sat. 10:30 am, 1:30 pm, 4:30 pm; Sun. 10:30 am, 2:45 pm.

Players may pause clocks during pre-round announcements for later-starting sections.

Other info: ½-pt Bye available any round if requested in advance and before Rd 2 (limit 2).  Players in Master and Under 2000 sections required to turn in completed scoresheets. Bring clocks, sets, and boards – none supplied, but vendor will be on-site. No cell phones. See website for additional information and policies.

Space Coast Open Blitz Tournament: 6SS. Saturday at 9:15 pm, G/3 d2, Cash prizes based on entries. Online EF $20, $30 if not playing in main tournament. Blitz online entry is available until noon Saturday, otherwise $5 more.
Free Master & GM lectures: 9:15am Saturday and Sunday.
HR:  See website for hotel rooms and rates information:  http://www.spacecoastchessfoundation.org/spacecoastopen .

2026 Tulane Classic

Tulane University

Friday, April 24, 2026
- Sunday, April 26, 2026

Event Overview

The Tulane Chess Club and Downriver Chess invite you to a two-day classical event with $2,100 in prizes!
Venue:  The Qatar Ballroom, on the second floor of the Lavin-Bernick Center at Tulane University. 29 McAlister Drive, New Orleans, LA.
Tournament details: Five round, two-section, swiss system, G/60;i30, USCF rated tournament. Top section FIDE-rated.
Sections: Two, open and U1500.
Prize fund: $2,100 in prizes. Total prize fund b/60 with 50% guaranteed.
Class prizes: Class prizes to be determined by official April USCF rating. Unrated players are eligible for class and section prizes in the open section.
Prize Structure:

- Open section: 1st $600, 2nd $300

- U2000 class: 1st $300, 2nd $150

- U1500 section: 1st $300, 2nd $150

- U1200 class: 1st $200, 2nd $100

Date:  April 24-26, 2026. Estimated round schedule,

- Friday 7:00 PM Blitz side event

- Saturday 10:00 AM, 2:00 PM, 5:30 PM

- Sunday 10:00 AM, 2:00 PM

Blitz side event:  $25 entry, 60% returned as prize money. 7 PM Friday evening. USCF-rated. Six rounds of G/5;d2. Register by clicking here . Walk in registration allowed.
Eligibility: $60 early entry fee if purchased one week prior. $70 standard entry fee if purchased two days prior. $80 late and same-day entry fee. Capacity limited to the first 120 players, please pre-register to guarantee your spot. Current USCF membership required. Free FIDE membership available to all players in top section with valid USCF membership.
Ratings: If a player does not have a regular rating, the highest of their quick and blitz will be used. 100 elo added to provisional ratings. Unrated players should report to the tournament directors so they may attempt to assign a rating for pairing and prize purposes. Unrated players may play in the open section or the U1500 section, but will only be eligible for the open section place prizes unless the tournament directors have been able to assign a rating.  For unrated USCF players with established foreign ratings, the most current USCF conversion will be used (with preference toward their FIDE rating, if available). Games including FIDE rated players 2400 or above are not FIDE rated due to time control and format.
Byes: Two half point byes are available upon request. No bye requests shall be made after round three other than for emergency situations.
Parking:  Parking permits are not required in most parking zones on Tulane University campus during the weekend. For ease, we recommend using the Diboll Garage. Diboll Garage is a short walk from the Lavin-Bernick Center and has plenty of space available for our attendees. Consult the  annotated parking map here .
Hotel info:  We recommend the St Charles Inn - Superior Hotel. We do not have a group rate, however.
Late players: Any player arriving at the chessboard more than 30 minutes late from the actual starting time of the round will lose their game (xref USCF 13D and FIDE 6.7.1). If both players arrive late elapsed time will be split between the players (xref USCF 16K and FIDE 6.7.2).
Prize payouts:  Players have 10 days after the conclusion of the tournament to claim their prize. We will email you twice. Please check your email if you believe you are prize eligible.
Contact:  Email Click here to show mail address with all questions.
Refunds:  Players who withdraw 60 minutes before round one are eligible for a refund of their entry fee, minus any applicable payment-processor fees (typically 5-7%).
Tulane students:  Please contact the Tulane Chess Club for discounted entry.
Visit:  www.downriverchess.com for all other upcoming tournaments!

New Orleans , LA 70118

United States

Event Overview

A Connecticut State Championship Event!

ALL STATES AND COUNTRIES WELCOME!

$5,000 GUARANTEED and Trophies!

USCF and NEW ENGLAND Rated!

50 USCF Enhanced Grand Prix Points!

60 CSCA Enhanced Grand Prix Points!

Amazing New Collegiate Venue! DGT Broadcast! GM/IM FREE!

Sponsored by the Connecticut State Chess Association

Fri-Sat, April 24-25 (2-Day) or Sat, April 25 (1-Day)
Schedules : 2-Day: 4/24: 7p, 4/25: 9a, 1:30p, 6p; 1-Day: 4/25: 9a, 11a, 1:30p, 6p; U700 and NER : 1-Day, 4/25 (Sat only) 9a, 11a, 1:30p, 3:30p

Connecticut College, Crozier-Williams, 270 Mohegan Ave, New London, CT
Hotel information provided on our website  at ChessCT.org .

Register online or onsite thru 10 AM on 4/25; Onsite ends 6 PM 4/24, 10 AM 4/25. Online registration link at  ChessCT.org .

Sec/Rds/ TC/Byes:  4 Rounds SS; Open (note[1]), U2100, U1700, U1200: 2-Day : G/90+10; 1-Day : 2 Rds G/45+5, 2 Rds G/90+10; U700/NER: G/45+5 all; USCF-, NE-rated. One ½ bye in Rds 1-3; Discretionary bye for registration 1 hour ahead of day start. Grand Prix: 50 Enhanced USCF Grand Prix Points; 60 Enhanced CSCA Grand Prix Points. Prizes:  Open : $1,000-600-400, $250 to Top U2300. U2100 : $700-400-300, $200 to Top U1800. U1700 : $500-300-200, $150 to Top U1400. U1200 : Trophies to Top 3, Top U900. U700 : Trophies to Top 3, Top U400. NER : Trophies to Top 3. Trophies to Upper Section winners. Medals to others. Cash prizes via PayPal. Tie break: Tie break on 1st place ties: a) G/10+3 game; if drawn, b) G/3+2 game; if drawn, c) G/5/4+2 game. Seeding, color by USCF tiebreaks. Does not affect money prizes.  Entry Fee:  Register online ; $98 by 4/15, $108 by 4/21, $128 by 4/23; $160 thereafter. U1200: $40 less. U700/NER: $50 less. GM/IM FREE by 4/13, then from prizes.  Reentry: Before Round 2, $60 cash, not Open to Open. Member/sibling/senior/veteran/hardship discounts. Email us for discount code. Notes : [1]  Open Section.  Players rated under 2000 are not permitted in the Open unless they are older than 18 years and rated over 1800. The organizer in its sole discretion may waive this requirement. [2]  Unrated.  Unrated limited to $300 in U2100 and $200 in U1700.  [3] Prizes & tax requirements. All prizes are paid via PayPal. 2026 TEXAS QUICK CHESS STATE CHAMPIONSHIP

State Championship Event

THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO

Saturday, April 25, 2026

Event Overview

2026 TEXAS QUICK CHESS  STATE CHAMPIONSHIP
A TCA GRAND PRIX EVENT!
Registration:   https://www.kingregistration.com/event/2026QuickChessChamp
9 rounds of G/15 (no delay no increment) on Saturday April 25th.  One section.  USCF rated for Quick Chess only.    This tournament will not affect your regular rating. Keeping score (notation) is  not  required in Quick Chess!
QUALIFICATIONS :  All chess players, regardless of residence, are welcome as long as they meet the membership requirements.  You must have an unexpired USCF  and  Texas Chess Association membership in good standing on the day of the tournament . Please note, however, that while residents of other states may participate, and win cash prizes,  state champion titles are for Texas residents only .
BYES :  Every player is entitled to a single half-point bye if requested before the beginning of round 1. After that time, all requested byes will be for zero points.  All last round byes are zero point byes.
SECTIONS:   Just one open section.  The  April  Rating Supplement will be used for pairings and for determination of the Class State Championship certificates.
SCHEDULE :  Round 1 at 10am, others ASAP, one hour lunch break from  about  noon to 1. Last round should end about 4 or 4:30.
CAPACITY:   Limited to 72, so register early, it might sell out.  It is a  State Championship  event after all.
ENTRY FEES :  $45 by April 4th, $55 by April 22nd, $65 thereafter.   Poison Pawn members use your $10 off coupon.  GM's & IMs enter free, entry fee deducted from any prize won.
CANCELLATION :  You may cancel up to 24 hours before the beginning of round 1 and get a refund of what you paid minus $15, or you may apply  the entire amount  towards a future entry fee.
PRIZES : Overall 1st place - the title of "2026 Texas Quick Chess State Champion", a trophy, and  $250 guaranteed .  Overall 2nd place $175, and overall 3rd place $100. 2nd & 3rd place based on 25 paid entries.  All 3 cash prizes increased proportionally with more than 25 entries. (last year's prize fund was $380/$270/$160 with 49 entries). All cash prizes paid via PayPal.  In case of a tie for first place the trophy will be awarded using standard USCF tiebreakers:   Modified Median, Solkoff, Cumulative, Cumulative Opponent's score. HOWEVER, the others who tie for first will get certificates designating them "2025 Texas Quick Chess State Co-Champion".
ALSO,  CLASS  STATE CHAMPIONSHIP CERTIFICATES AWARDED TO TOP SCORE IN CLASS A (1999-1800), CLASS B (1799-1600), C (1599-1400), D (1399-1200), & E (1199 & lower).  No tie breaks , if 2 or more tie for top score in a class they will  each  get a certificate declaring them the "2026 Texas  Quick Chess  State Co-Champion" of that Class!
CLOCKS, SETS & BOARDS:   Please bring your own if you can, there might be enough equipment at The Studio but depending on the turnout there might not be, and Poison Pawns club members get first dibs on those.  Know how to set your clock to G/15!!
HOTEL INFO :  Holiday Inn Express , 3401 N. Main St., is less than a mile from The Studio. Phone 832-834-6197 and ask for The Houston Chess Studio discount, or if booking online use code ALDR9.  Also within a mile is the  Heights House Hotel , an  America’s Best Value , and a  Luxury Inn .  Google them for info.
WHERE:   THE HOUSTON CHESS STUDIO ,   is dedicated to providing a quality, high tech, chess playing experience for players of all levels,  and their parents.   Centrally and conveniently located at 250 Patton St., Suite H, Houston TX 77009.  Just inside North Loop 610 and just 2 blocks off North I-45.  There are 3 restaurants in the same strip center as The Studio: The Red Hot Noodle (Asian), Subway, and Patron Pizza.  Several others are within walking distance.  Plenty of FREE parking.
SCANNING:  All players are subject to being scanned (“wanded”) in order to help prevent cheating.
UPCOMING EVENTS:  https://www.kingregistration.com/affiliate/poisonpawns
QUESTIONS?   Ask Edgar at 281-844-4139  or  Click here to show mail address

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids

Chess Kings & Queens Academy

Saturday, April 25, 2026

Event Overview

CKQ Saturday Piscataway Rapids
Start time: Players should arrive no later than 4:15 p.m. The first game begins promptly at 4:30.  Latecomers risk their clock running when they arrive.
End time: The Under 600 section typically ends by 8:30 p.m., the Under 1200 section more like 9:00.  The tournament could go a bit longer if players use all their time.
Players: Most players at this event will be children (ages 6-16), but adults are welcome to play.  Beginners are welcome, but at a minimum players should know how to legally move chess pieces, recognize when they’re in check, and how to perform basic checkmates (ex; king and queen vs. king).
Structure / time controls: 4-SS, G30 +5. (Each player will play four games. Each player receives 30 minutes per game, plus another five seconds per move.)
Sections: Under 600 and Under 1200 rating sections.  The Under 1200 section requires at least 500 rating to enter. Lower-rated and unrated players may enter with the tournament director's permission.
Requirements: A USCF membership is required to play in the tournament. Contact the tournament director if you need assistance creating or renewing a membership.
Equipment: Players do not need to bring any equipment.  Players are recommended to eat before arriving, or at least bring a snack.
Registration: The registration fee is $30.  Online registration closes at 5pm on the day of the event.
Byes: If you can’t attend the entire tournament, a half-point bye (limit one) is available for any round. Byes must be requested before the tournaments starts. If you are going to take first-round bye please contact the tournament director at least one hour before the tournament starts.
Prizes: Top three winners in each section receive a trophy or a medal.
For more information:  Contact tournament director Stephen Lorimor ( [email protected] , phone/text: 908-286-0720).
Information / registration link:  https://chesskq.com/tournament

Arizona Golden Cup 🏆

Phoenix Chess Academy

Saturday, April 25, 2026

Event Overview

Arizona's Premier Year - Long USCF Chess Series.
Earn Points. Win Gold. Become a Champion. 🏆
A year-long USCF-rated chess series. Players earn Golden Points at each monthly event. Final standings after December determine the Arizona Golden Cup Champion, 2nd and 3rd Place in each section. Players may enter the series at any time during the year. Tournament is open to everyone. USCF membership is required.
4 Round Swiss G/30; d5 USCF-rated tournament series with cumulative points.
Sections: Open (1800 +). Under 1800. Under 1200. No playing up allowed. Official rating will be used for sections and prizes. Half point Byes available in all 4 rounds (Max 2) and must be requested before round 2. If a player moves to a higher section during the year, points earned in the previous section do not transfer. The player begins earning Golden Cup points in the new section.
Schedule: Round 1: 9:00 AM. Round 2: 10:15 AM. Round 3: 11:30 AM. Round 4: 12:45 PM. Ceremony will follow right after last game is over.
Entry Fee: $35.00 by Wednesday, $40.00 by Friday, $45.00 Same Day. Refund Policy: Full refund if canceling up to 1 hour before the event. No refund after that.
Awards: Top 3 Trophy in each section, Best U1400 and Best U800 in each monthly event.
At the end of the series-After December event: Champion Trophy (in each section) + 7 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 2nd Place Trophy (in each section) + 5 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. 3rd Place Trophy (in each section) + 3 Months of Free entry for 2027 series. Players are eligible to win only one Arizona Golden Cup prize, awarded in the highest scoring section in which they competed.
Golden Points System:
Finish                 Points
1st Place              20
2nd Place            16
3rd Place             13
4th Place             10
5–6                           8
7–10                        5
Participation       3
Bonus Points:
+3 points — Perfect score (4/4).
+2 points (only in December) — Played Most consecutive months.
Monthly Event Tie-Handling (Point Splitting): When two or more players are tied for placement in a monthly Arizona Golden Cup event, Golden points are split evenly among the tied positions.
Tie-Breaks (Year-End):
1. Most 1st-place finishes.
2. Head-to-head results.
3. Most tournaments played.
4. Best December result.
TD decisions are final.

Phoenix , AZ 85022

FREE Pizza and drinks for those playing in the Golden Cup tournament in the morning!

Entry Fee: $30.00 by 1/28; $35.00 by 1/30; $40.00 same day. Refund Policy: Full refund will be issued to players who withdraw at least an hour before the first round. In cases where a registered player does not show up for the tournament without prior notice, they will not be eligible for a refund.
Prizes: Over 1200: Cash for top three. 1st - 30%, 2nd - 14%, 3rd - 10%.
Under 1200: Trophy for top three. Trophy for the Best Under 700.

Cincinnati Tornado APRIL. Last Saturday of Month

Wyoming Baptist Church

Saturday, April 25, 2026

Event Overview

Cincinnati Tornado Monthly Tournament
Held on the Last Saturday of the Month
We provide all clocks & chess sets

Advance Entry Fee $45
Online Registration – By Friday 12 midnight deadline
Online Registration:   https://chessearth.com/tornado-registration/
Advance Registration ends on Friday 12 midnight.
NEW OPTION for returning players.   EMAIL or  TEXT MESSAGE  us to pre-register and enter the tournament:

- Email admin@chessearth:   1.) First & Last Name   2.) USCF ID  3.) Section you are playing in  and  4.)  Pay $45 at the Tournament Site

On-Site Entry Fee $50; On-Site Registration – By 9:30am Saturday morning deadline
-  10am First Round.

- On-Site Registration – Ends at 9:30am Saturday morning.     10am First Round.

- Credit Cards, PayPal, Venmo, CashApp, Zelle, Apple Pay accepted on site

- Tournament  Address:    Wyoming Baptist Church, 170 Burns Ave, Cincinnati, OH 45215

4-Round Swiss Tournament
Time Control: G/45 +5; Each player receives 45 minutes with a +5-second increment. A Tornado is a one-day tournament where you play four games. Cash Prizes and Awards are given at the end of the tournament based on your final score.
Round Start Times:
Round #1: 10:00am
Round #2: 12:30pm
Round #3: 2:30pm
Round #4: 4:30pm
Choose a Section To Play In:

- Open Section  -  Includes the Master Bounty Prize - $100

- Under 1600 Section

- Under 1000 Section

- Award Winning Chili.  Good Food; Hot Meals

- Chess Equipment and Merch available to purchase

- USCF Rated Tournament.  Join/Renew USCF on-site.

- Purchase a New Membership at Registration.

- 1/2 Point Bye is available if notified before Round 2.

- Prizes Fund based on 70 players.

- We provide all the Chess Clocks & Chess Sets

Open Section:     **NEW** Rating must be 1600 or above to play in the Open Section.
Or a player can pay $30 to “play up” into the Open Section.
1st – $200      2nd – $150
Top Under 2001   – $100
Top Under 1801   – $100
Includes the Master Bounty Prize - $100

- Master Bounty Prize:  Win your game against the #1 Master in the tournament and win $100. If you draw the Master, win $50.  If the Master wins all the games, then he/she wins the $100.

Under 1600 Section:   The heart of the tournament
1st – $200      2nd – $150
$100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter.
$100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter.
Under 1000 Section :  Rating must be lower than 1001. Great for beginners and 1st time tournament players.
1st – $200      2nd – $150
$100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter.
$100 – Class Prize. We figure out the class prize after seeing the number of players who enter.
Chess Community Gathering

- Hang Out & Analyze;  Play Casual Chess Games in the Skittles room.

- TVs are in the Skittle rooms

- Enjoy Good Food

- Buy Chess Merch

- Watch the Tournament.

- Chess Social Life.

- We are looking for volunteers to help with the clean-up; putting chairs and tables away.  Please email us if you can help.  We appreciate it!!

Always Last Saturday of the Month

Eureka College Open

Cerf Center - Eureka College

Saturday, April 25, 2026

Event Overview

Event Overview
Saturday April 25, 2026
Cerf Center
S Burgess St.
Eureka, IL 61530
US Chess Membership is Required for Open and U1401 sections. All US Chess Rules will be followed. Notation is required in all rated sections. Players 8 years old or younger (or their parents) can ask the tournament director before Round 1 for an exemption, if they are still learning to write in general.
Players and spectators younger than high school age (~14) must be accompanied by an adult. The accompanying adult must be present at the tournament site. Disruptive and/or destructive behavior will result in dismissal from the tournament and site. Players are responsible for the behavior of anyone accompanying them to the tournament.

Three Sections:

- Open - Open to all players. Active US Chess membership required.

- U1401 - Players must have a published USCF Regular Rating below 1401. Unrated players may play in this section, however they are only eligible for place prizes. Active US Chess membership required.

- Non-rated - Geared towards players who would like to try out tournament chess before committing to a US Chess membership. Notation not required for this section. US Chess membership not required.

Check your rating here:  https://ratings.uschess.org/
USCF Quick, Blitz, or any FIDE/foreign ratings may be used for section eligibility purposes for players without a regular rating.

Format:
Open and U1401 Sections
4 Rounds SS; G/40+10 (Clocks will be set with 40 minutes per player, and a 10 second increment that adds back after each move)
Non-rated Section
4 Rounds SS; G/20+5 (Clocks will be set with 20 minutes per player, and a 5 second increment that adds back after each move)

Entry Fees:
Entry Fees will be paid onsite with cash only.
General Entry Fee for Open and U1401 Sections: $30
Players with a US Chess Regular Rating 1800 or higher (using published or most recent live rating): $15
Players with a US Chess Regular Rating 2200 or higher (using published or most recent live rating): Free
General Entry Fee for Non-rated Section: $10
*Eureka College Students, Staff, and Faculty will receive free entry to any section.
**If a live rating is used for a discounted entry fee, that rating will be used for prize and pairing purposes.
Pre-registration link:  https://forms.gle/EcjG5QydNEm448so6

Prizes
Prizes for Open and U1401 sections are based on 30 paid entries in rated sections.
Open
1st - $150
2nd - $90
Top U2001/Unrated - $60
Top U1701/Unrated - $50
U1401
1st - $100
2nd - $60
Top U1201 - $40
Top U900 - $35
USCF Quick, Blitz, or any FIDE/foreign ratings may be used for prize eligibility purposes for players without a regular rating. Unrated players playing in the U1401 section are only eligible for place prizes (i.e. 1st-2nd). Unrated players are eligible for all prizes in the Open section.
Non-rated
1st - $40
2nd - $20
3rd - $10

Schedule:
Onsite Registration and Check-In: 9:00am-9:45am
Open and U1401 Sections
Round 1: 10:00am
Round 2: 11:45am
Lunch Break
Round 3: 2:00pm
Round 4: 3:45pm
Estimated end: 5:30pm
Non-Rated Section
*Rounds will start ASAP, generally 15 minutes after the conclusion of the previous round
Round 1: 10:00am
Round 2: 15 minutes after the end of Round 1
Round 3: 15 minutes after the end of Round 2
Round 4: 15 minutes after the end of Round 3
Estimated end: 1:30pm

Players arriving after registration will receive one half-point bye and will be paired in subsequent rounds. Half-point byes may be requested for any round during registration only.
Boards and pieces will be provided. Please bring clocks (clocks will be provided for the Non-rated section).
Board 1 in the Open Section may be streamed via Facebook Live or Youtube.
Please contact tournament organizer if you have any questions.
David Sye, Click here to show mail address

Eureka , IL 61530

United States

Saturday, April 25, 2026

Event Overview

Dublin Jerome High School
8300 Hyland-Croy Rd, Dublin, OH 43016 ( map )

Chess sets and clocks provided.
Registration https://cclchess.com/dublin-jerome-spring/

Sections, Format and Time Controls:

K12 Open, K12 U1500 & K12 U1200  4 Round Swiss, G45;d5
K-12 U900, K-12 U600, K-6 U300  5 Round Swiss, G30;d5
K-3 Nonrated, 4-8 Nonrated 9-12 Nonrated 5 Round Swiss, G30;d5

ONE half-point bye is allowed if declared before round 1.
Current US Chess membership is required to players in the rated section. Nonrated sections do not require US Chess membership.
Round 1 starts at 9:30 am for ALL sections. Check out specific section's schedule on site.

Individual and Team Awards:

K12 Open, K12 U1500 & K12 U1200  Individual trophies for anyone scoring 2.5 out of 4. Div I team trophies for top 2 overall best schools across the sections.
K-12 U900, K-12 U600, K-6 U300  Individual trophies for anyone scoring 3.5 out of 5. Div II team trophies for top 2 overall best schools across the sections.
K-3 Nonrated, 4-8 Nonrated, 9-12 Nonrated  Individual trophies for anyone scoring 3.5 out of 5. Div III team trophies for top 2 overall best schools across the sections.

Special Award: top girl player in each section

Participation medals for all.

Special Entry Fee to Dublin Schools District Student: $30 before April 11, then $40 until April 24, $50 on site.
Discounted Entry Fee to active student: $35 before April 11, then $45 until April 24, $50 on site.
General Entry Fee to the others:  $40 before April 11, then $45 until April 24, $50 on site.

Acceptable Payments: major credit cards, or Zelle to [email protected] or Venmo to @Jeff-Shen-23  with a note of player's name. Refund is promised if withdrawal before April 24.

Concessions  will be available on-site for purchase (cash only).
Free Parking lot is   off Brand RD

Super Sunday USCF Tournament

Chess Kings & Queens Academy

Sunday, April 26, 2026

Event Overview

Note: There is also a FIDE-USCF hybrid section for those 1700+ USCF rating (1600+ FIDE).  See other listing for details.

Structure
- 3 rounds Swiss-Style.  G75 +15.  Accelerated pairings at the director's discretion.
- One half-point bye is available for any round, but must be requested before tournament start. All other requested byes are zero points.
- Clocks, boards, and weighed plastic pieces are provided. Players may use their own equipment with the agreement of their opponent.
Schedule
- Round times: 10:00 am / 1:30pm / 5:00 pm.
- Players should arrive no later than 9:45 am.
Registration
- Registration fee: $45
- Online registration only.  Registration closes at 9:00 a.m. the day of the event.  On-site registrations are discouraged but may be accepted at the TD's discretion.
- Registration link:  https://chesskq.com/tournament
- All sections in this tournament have a minimum rating to participate.
Under 1400 = 1000 USCF rating minimum
Under 1800 = 1300 USCF rating minimum
- This event has no age restrictions.
- All ratings are assessed based on the published USCF rating supplement for the month the tournament takes place. "Live" or "up-to-date" ratings may be accepted at the director's discretion.
- Players signing up for a section they are not eligible to join will be automatically shifted to the appropriate section.
- Players who sign up but are ineligible to participate, or players who withdraw from the tournament prior to 9:00 am on tournament day, will be provided a credit for a signup for a future tournament or class.
Prizes
$640 guaranteed in prizes
Prizes are paid out via Venmo, Zelle, or PayPal. Check-by-mail available for anyone without these options.
U1800 section
- 1st place: $160
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1600: $60
U1400 section
- 1st place: $160
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1200: $60
@45 players  (across all three sections) - we serve doughnuts and coffee.  Everyone wins!
@50 players - we add a Top Junior (under age 12) award to each section
@55 players - we add a Top Senior (age 55+) award to each section
@60 players - we increase 2nd place and "top under __  rating" prizes for all sections by $15
@65 players - we increase 1st place prizes for all sections by $20.
Additional information
- The tournament director for this event is Stephen Lorimor. Bye requests and other issues may be e-mailed to [email protected] , or by voice/text to 908-286-0720. Note that he may not notice or respond to e-mails, texts, or calls after 9:00 am the day of the event.
- The venue is located within walking distance of multiple restaurants and fast food businesses.  No food is allowed at the playing tables, but a waiting room with tables is available.

Address: 1030 Stelton Road

Suite 201 (use side entrance)

Piscataway , NJ 08854

United States

Sections: 2
Grand Prix Points: 0
Prize Fund: 640
FIDE Rated: No
Handicap Accessible: No
Residency Restriction: No
Online Event: No

Organizer Overview

Stephen D Lorimor

Email: [email protected]
Phone: 9082860720
Website: https://chesskq.com/tournament

Super Sunday FIDE Tournament

Chess Kings & Queens Academy

Sunday, April 26, 2026

Event Overview

Note: This is a dual USCF - FIDE section of a larger USCF tournament (Super Sunday).  Please read the information carefully.  For the other sections and more events, please check our other listing.

Structure
- 3 rounds Swiss-Style.  G75 +15.  Accelerated pairings at the director's discretion.
- One half-point bye is available for any round, but must be requested before tournament start. All other requested byes are zero points.
- Clocks, boards, and weighed plastic pieces are provided. Players may use their own equipment with the agreement of their opponent.
- FIDE notice: Rules for late arrival will match standard USCF 60 minute rule.
Schedule
- Round times: 10:00 am / 1:30pm / 5:00 pm

USCF
- A current USCF membership is required to play.
- Players MUST have at least 1) 1700 USCF rating (live or current published), or 2) 1600 FIDE rating

FIDE
- A valid FIDE ID is required to play.  Most players with a valid USCF membership may request a USA-flagged FIDE ID at this URL.  Note that it may take several days to process.  https://tinyurl.com/3zcjwmex
- There is no minimum FIDE rating for this event.  There is a maximum rating of 2399.
- FIDE norms are not available at this event.

Registration
- Registration fee: $45
- Online registration only.  Registration closes at 9:00 a.m. on the day of the event.  On-site registrations are discouraged but may be accepted at the TD's discretion.
- Registration link: https://chesskq.com/tournament
- Free entry for all players rated 2200 or higher. ($45 will be deducted from the player's prize winnings.) E-mail name, USCF ID, and FIDE ID to Stephen Lorimor at [email protected] to sign up.
- This event has no age restrictions.
- Players signing up for a section they are not eligible to join will be automatically shifted to the appropriate section.
- Players ineligible to participate in any section of this event, or withdrawing before 9:00 AM on the day of the tournament, will receive a credit for a future class or tournament.

Prizes
Prizes are paid out via Zelle or PayPal. Check-by-mail available for anyone without these options.
- 1st place: $200
- 2nd place: $100
- Top U1800 (FIDE): $60
@45 players  (across all three sections) - we serve doughnuts and coffee.  Everyone wins!
@50 players - we add a Top Junior (under age 12) award to each section

2026 Fremont All-Girls Chess Championships

Warm Springs Community Center Multipurpose Room

Sunday, April 26, 2026

Event Overview

The event will be completely  FREE , made possible by generous sponsorship from US Chess Women grants .

Time:  10:00am - 3:30pm, Sunday April 26th, 2026
Rating:  USCF Dual-Rated.
Pairings are based on the April 2026 regular supplemental regular US Chess rating.
Players must have current US Chess Federation membership.
Time Control : 4 round Swiss, G30 d5 (This means you get 30 minutes, your opponent gets 30 minutes, and with 5-second delay before clock starts counting down on each move)
First round starts at 10am . All players should arrive 10 minutes prior to the first round .
Next round starts after the last game finishes in your section (rolling schedule).

Sections:  6 sections based on USCF rating and grade at school

- K-5 Unrated

- K-5 Under 500

- K-5 Under 1000

- K-5 1000+

- Grade 6-12 Under 1000 and Unrated

- Grade 6-12 1000+

We may update event details, like sections and number of rounds, as the tournament date approaches to ensure the best possible experience for all players.

Equipment:  Chess sets, notation sheets and pencils will be provided.
Please bring your own clock if you can.
Prizes : Trophies to top 6 in each section

Registration: https://tinyurl.com/FremontGirls2026Reg
Registration closes once we hit our maximum capacity of 70!

Processed Entries :  https://tinyurl.com/FremontGirls2026

MVP Chess K-12 Quads (FREE for US Chess Members)

Mount Vernon Rec Center

Sunday, April 26, 2026

Event Overview

Date: Sunday, April 26, 2026 at 12:45 PM
Venue: 2017 Belle View Blvd. Alexandria, VA 22307. The rec center has recently been renovated and features state-of-the-art facilities including a gym, two skating rinks, an indoor pool, and a rock-climbing wall.
Organizer: MVP Chess is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Alexandria, Virginia. Our mission is to make chess accessible for everyone and develop growth-minded players. For questions, please email [email protected] .
Register Now: MVP Chess K-12 Quads | April 2026 - Organized by MVP Chess | Chess Nut
Entry & Donations
This tournament is FREE for all US Chess members in grades K–12.
An active US Chess membership is required — you can join or renew here .
The event is limited to 32 players, so please register in advance to secure your spot and help us plan pairings and sections.
We welcome voluntary donations to help cover the cost of room rental, awards, and other tournament-related expenses.
All contributions are tax-deductible and may be made online or onsite at the event.
Format

- 3-round quad (final section may be a small Swiss)

- Time control: G/25; d5 (25 minutes per player, 5-second delay)

- Rated by US Chess

Awards

- 🏆 Trophies for each quad winner

- 🎖️ Medals for all other participants

- 📺 Game Analysis Feature: Select games will be analyzed on the MVP Chess YouTube channel. To be considered, players should submit their scoresheets at the end of the event.

Schedule

- Check-in: 12:45 PM

- Round 1: 1:00 PM

- Rounds begin as soon as prior games finish

- Expected finish: no later than 4:00 PM

Rules & Expectations

- US Chess rules apply

- Notation optional

- Chess sets and clocks provided

- Parents/guardians should stay on-site during the event

- Please show respect for opponents, staff, and the venue

Media Policy
MVP Chess may take photos or short video clips for educational and promotional purposes.
Names will not be published without consent. If you prefer not to be photographed, simply let us or the photographer know.

Alexandria , VA 22307

Dragon Knight Chess Center

Sunday, April 26, 2026

Event Overview

Dragon Knight Chess Center
2000 Bearcat Way
Suite 104, Morrisville, NC  27560
(919) 422-2535
Enhanced Grand Prix
3 round Swiss System
5 sections: Open Section; Under 2000 Section; Under 1800 Section; Under 1600 Section; and Under 1400 Section
Prize Fund:  Open Section: $150-100-50 Guaranteed ($300 Total Guaranteed)
Under 2000 Section: $232 total b/8 entries in Under 2000 Section
Under 1800 Section: $232 total b/8 entries in Under 1800 Section
Under 1600 Section: $232 total b/8 entries in Under 1600 Section
Under 1400 Section: $232 total b/8 entries in Under 1400 Section
